\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Five of the nine cases came back bit for bit unchanged under a block that
rewrote the heating fraction, the ionization channels, the ionized fraction
and two heat returns. \textbf{That is not a statement about the size of the
change; it is the demonstration that the staged default was keeping this
physics switched off in every one of them.} \texttt{wasp\_full}'s $\dot M$ is
quoted here only because it is the golden's own number: it is a du-stop
rather than a Newton finish, and the du-stop's path dependence is several
percent, which is why every quantitative line above uses the
\texttt{\_newton} pair instead.



\section{A segmentation fault that only appeared on more than one thread: a
residual histogram indexed by $\log_{10}$ of a NaN (2026-09-02)}\label{sec:jfnk-nan-histogram}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{The defect.} A molecular run with \texttt{Solver: Newton} died with
SIGSEGV as soon as the steady solver was entered, at the first residual
evaluation after the \texttt{(JFNK) below r\_esc} line, whenever
\texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS} was greater than one. The identical run on one
thread did not crash. \texttt{OMP\_STACKSIZE=1G} changed nothing, so it was
not the size of a thread stack. Reproduced on
\texttt{backup/regression/armD\_D2\_newton} (8 threads), on the same case
with the large stack, and on \texttt{armD\_D2\_LW\_newton} (6 threads).

\textbf{The cause is one bin selector:}
\texttt{src/modules/radiation/ionization\_equilibrium.f90}, the
\texttt{residual\_decade} expression at line 2195 as it stood. Rebuilt with
\texttt{-g -fcheck=bounds,do,mem}, the fault is a bounds violation rather
than a stack overflow, and it names its own line:

\begin{verbatim}
At line 1267 of file src/modules/radiation/ionization_equilibrium.f90
Fortran runtime error: Index '-2147483633' of dimension 1 of array
  'hist_uncv' below lower bound of 0
\end{verbatim}

\texttt{residual\_decade(res)} returned
\texttt{min(15, 16 + int(floor(log10(res))))}. NaN fails every comparison,
so a NaN residual reached that expression; \texttt{int()} of NaN is the
integer indefinite value $-2^{31}$, and the whole expression then evaluates
to exactly $-2147483633$ on this compiler (checked with a standalone
program). The value is used directly as the index of \texttt{hist\_conv} /
\texttt{hist\_uncv} at lines 1264/1267 and 1494/1497, both inside the
OpenMP-parallel cell sweep, so the increment writes about 8.6\,GB below the
array.

\emph{Why the residual is NaN, and only under the steady solver.}
\texttt{jv\_product}
(\texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_newton.f90:679-700}) forms $J v$ by
evaluating the full residual at $Y + \epsilon v$ with no admissibility test
on that state at all, and the line-search trial test
(\texttt{steady\_newton.f90:944-945}) covers only density and pressure
positivity. A probe state can therefore drive a balance row of the
molecular network to NaN, and \texttt{normalized\_reaction\_residual}
returns it. In the marching phase of this case it never happens: the
\texttt{-fcheck} build runs 2002 marching steps and trips on the first JFNK
residual evaluation.

\emph{Why the thread count decides whether it crashes.}
\texttt{hist\_conv} and \texttt{hist\_uncv} are
\texttt{reduction(+:\ldots)} arrays of the parallel sweep, so each thread
increments its own private copy. On a worker thread that copy sits on an
8\,MB pthread stack, and the address 8.6\,GB below it is unmapped, so the
write faults; on the master thread the same wild write does not fault.
Measured with one and the same \texttt{-O3} binary:
\texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=1} completes the JFNK attempt
(\texttt{info=2}) and resumes marching, \texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=8} dies in
\texttt{\_\_ionization\_equilibrium\_MOD\_ioniz\_eq.\_omp\_fn.1}.

\textbf{The fix.} \texttt{residual\_decade} now selects the top bin from the
bracket instead of clamping a computed index, so \texttt{log10} is never
evaluated on a residual that is not finite:

\begin{lstlisting}[language=Fortran,basicstyle=\ttfamily\footnotesize]
if (res .le. 1.0d-16) then
   ib = 0
else if (res .lt. 1.0d-1) then
   ib = 16 + int(floor(log10(res)))
else
   ib = 15
endif
\end{lstlisting}

For every finite residual this returns exactly what the old expression
returned: below $10^{-1}$ the \texttt{min(15,\ldots)} was never binding, and
at or above $10^{-1}$ it always returned 15. NaN and an overflowed residual
now land in the top bin, which is where a residual that large belongs. The
bins are diagnostic counters; no physics reads them.

\textbf{Verification, three things.}
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{The reproduction, 8 threads.} \texttt{armD\_D2\_newton} now
  enters the steady solver, runs its JFNK iterations to the no-descent
  abort, exits \texttt{info=2} (this case does not converge; the criterion
  here is the absence of the crash) and finishes the run.
\item \emph{Serial versus parallel byte-identity}, re-checked after the
  change on the two cases that exercise the atomic and the molecular
  equilibrium path: \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} and \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion},
  each run at \texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=1} and \texttt{=8}.
  \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} and \texttt{Ion\_species.txt} are identical in
  both pairs, and \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion} also reproduces its golden.
\item \emph{The regression matrix.} \texttt{make check}, all nine cases
  byte-identical. A thread-safety repair cannot move a single-threaded
  result, so any movement here would have meant the repair was wrong.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Two things this section does not repair, recorded where they were
found.}

\emph{The steady solver's probe states reach run-level accumulators.} The
species fractions do not leak -- \texttt{jv\_product} and
\texttt{build\_banded\_jac\_full} restore \texttt{f\_sp} from a base copy
before every probe, and the line search adopts \texttt{f\_sp\_j} only for an
accepted trial (\texttt{steady\_newton.f90:959}). But
\texttt{ieq\_nonroot\_streak}
(\texttt{ionization\_equilibrium.f90:189}, written at 2223 and 2227) is
module state that no probe path saves or restores, and its limit
\texttt{error stop}s the run at 1000 consecutive sweeps. Its meaning during
a JFNK phase is not ``consecutive marching sweeps on a non-root'': probe
sweeps both increment it and reset it. The acceptance statistics
(\texttt{ieq\_acc\_n}, \texttt{ieq\_acc\_resmax}, \texttt{ieq\_hist\_conv} /
\texttt{ieq\_hist\_uncv}, the constrained-solve totals and the print budget,
lines 203--210 and 1655--1664) are accumulated the same way, so the
end-of-run report is dominated by states the run never adopted. Measured on
\texttt{armD\_D2\_newton}: not one non-root acceptance in the 2002 marching
steps before the hand-off, and 18339 over the JFNK phase and the eight
marching steps that followed it, largest residual $1.74\times10^{97}$, with
18373 cells promoted to the constrained continuation solve of which 34 were
accepted.

\emph{The pathological case is not serial-versus-parallel byte-identical in
its marching phase either.} \texttt{armD\_D2\_newton} at 1 and at 8 threads
diverges in the last bit at step 1267, well before the steady solver is
reached. It is reproducible at each thread count and it is present in the
code as it stood before this section (built with the same default flags), so
it is not introduced here; the \texttt{-O3 -g} build of the same source does
not show it, which makes it a marginal decision flipping on a rounding
difference rather than a data race. It is not diagnosed here. The regression
cases stay byte-identical, as verification 2 and 3 above show.


\section{He recombination photons had no competing absorber, and an initial
condition that clipped H$_2$ at 1 handed them a cell with no hydrogen
(2026-09-02)}\label{sec:he-rec-absorber}

\textbf{Judgment first.} Two expressions were physically wrong, independently
of each other, and they combined into a runaway.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \texttt{he\_rec\_coupling} implements Draine's (2011) on-the-spot
  treatment: a He\,\textsc{ii} recombination photon above $13.6$~eV is absorbed
  inside the cell that emitted it and ionizes hydrogen. Only the
  $\ge 24.6$~eV ground-capture continuum asked \emph{who} absorbs the photon.
  Every other channel --- four of them in the He\,$2^3S$ branch, the case-B
  cascade in the atomic one --- gave every photon to H\,\textsc{i}
  unconditionally and then divided by $\max(n_{\rm HI}, 10^{-99})$. In a molecular gas that is wrong on the physics
  before it is wrong on the arithmetic: H$_2$ photoionizes from $15.4$~eV with
  a cross section $1.2$--$3.7$ times that of H\,\textsc{i} over the $16$--$25$~eV
  band these photons occupy, so in a molecular layer H$_2$ takes essentially
  all of them, and the share it takes belongs in the H$_2$ photoionization
  rate.
\item \texttt{set\_IC} clipped the initial H$_2$ nucleus fraction at $x_2=1$
  rather than at the element-ratio ceiling
  $q_{\rm H_2} \le 0.5/(0.5 + \mathrm{He/H})$ --- the same silent cap
  \S117 removed from the base particle count, left behind in the initial
  condition. Above $\mathrm{He/H} = 0.0964$, where the solar-composition fit
  exceeds that ceiling (item P26), the clip produced
  \texttt{f\_sp(H\,I)} $= 0$ \emph{exactly}, which is the one input that makes
  (1) diverge.
\end{enumerate}

The rate is now split among the absorbers present, at each channel's own photon
energy, and the H$_2$ share is returned as an H$_2$ photoionization rate; the
initial condition takes its H$_2$ fraction from the same source the inflowing
ghost does. A third defect the same audit turned up --- an EOS-only molecular
base whose ghost silently sits at $\mathtt{ntot\_bc}\times T_0$ --- is refused
at startup from this section on; it is its own subsection below because the
refusal invalidates existing runs and the decision to write it was the user's. The measured consequence is that the ``molecular base runs
supersonic near $\mathrm{He/H}\sim1$--$10$'' window of
\texttt{docs/supersonic\_molecular\_base.md} is not a physical phenomenon: the
same case now relaxes to a subsonic, warm, fully molecular base.

\subsection*{What the defect did}

In the $\mathrm{He/H}=1$ hot-Uranus case the first physical cell was fully
ionized ($f({\rm H\,\textsc{ii}})=1$) after the single \texttt{ioniz\_eq} pass
of step 0. With $n_{\rm HI}=0$ the photon production rate
$P_{\rm add}\sim1.5\times10^{-5}$~cm$^{-3}$\,s$^{-1}$ became a rate coefficient
of $1.5\times10^{94}$~s$^{-1}$, and $x({\rm H\,\textsc{ii}})=1$ is then the
exact root of the hydrogen balance row --- not a failed solve. The energy solve
of the same step took that cell from $1169$~K to the $11.4$~K floor on the
recombination and free-free cooling of the false electron reservoir, the
particle count and hence the pressure jumped by a factor $54$, and the legacy
velocity boundary copied the resulting interior velocity: supersonic base
inflow by step 6.

Three properties made this survive every guard built in \S\S113--117:

\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{the residual test cannot see it.} The acceptance test of \S113
  normalizes each balance row by its own turnover, and the hydrogen row's
  turnover (\texttt{s(1)} in \texttt{System\_HeH\_mol.f90}) is built from the
  same $P_{\rm HI}$. Numerator and denominator both carried the $10^{94}$:
  normalized residual $2.7\times10^{-17}$, raw residual $-1.3\times10^{16}$;
\item \emph{the rate and the heat of one channel disagreed structurally.} The
  heating of the same photons is $n_{\rm HeII}n_e\alpha$ times an energy, a
  volumetric rate, and stayed at a perfectly ordinary
  $2.6\times10^{-10}$~erg\,cm$^{-3}$\,s$^{-1}$. A channel whose rate diverges
  while its heat does not is not a physical channel;
\item \emph{no regression case can reach it.} The five molecular cases run at
  $\mathrm{He/H}=0.0793$, where the fit gives $x_{2,\rm ic}=0.984<1$, the clip
  never engages, and $n_{\rm HI}$ never reaches zero.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{The correction}

For each channel $c$ the photon of energy $E_c$ is divided among the absorbers
whose threshold lies below $E_c$,
\[
  w_s(E_c) = \frac{n_s\,\sigma_s(E_c)}{\sum_{s'} n_{s'}\,\sigma_{s'}(E_c)},
\]
with $s$ over H\,\textsc{i} ($13.6$~eV), H$_2$ ($15.4$~eV) and, for the
$\ge 24.6$~eV ground-capture continuum only, He\,\textsc{i}. Five channels,
each with its own energy:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r l r@{}}
\toprule
channel & $E_c$ [eV] & absorbers & $\sigma_{\rm H_2}/\sigma_{\rm HI}$ \\
\midrule
ground capture continuum          & 24.6   & H\,\textsc{i}, H$_2$, He\,\textsc{i} & 3.66 \\
$2^1P \to 1^1S$ 584\,\AA{} resonance & 21.2   & H\,\textsc{i}, H$_2$ & 3.54 \\
$2^3S \to 1^1S$ line              & 19.8   & H\,\textsc{i}, H$_2$ & 3.46 \\
$2^1S$ two-photon continuum       & 16.110 & H\,\textsc{i}, H$_2$ & 1.20 \\
case-B cascade (atomic branch, lumped) & 19.741 & H\,\textsc{i}, H$_2$ & 3.45 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The H\,\textsc{i} share becomes \texttt{dP\_HI}, the H$_2$ share a new output
\texttt{dP\_H2} that the callers add to \texttt{P\_H2} (which already drives
the H$_2$ destruction row and the H$_2^+$ formation row of the molecular
system), and the He\,\textsc{i} share is excluded from the effective
He\,\textsc{ii} recombination coefficient, which generalizes from
$\alpha_B + y\,\alpha_1$ to $\alpha_B + (w_{\rm HI}+w_{\rm H_2})\,\alpha_1$.
The photoelectron of each share is deposited at its own threshold, $13.6$~eV
for H\,\textsc{i} and $15.4$~eV for H$_2$. Where the cell holds no absorber for
a channel the photon leaves and that channel returns zero, so the
He\,\textsc{ii} recombination reverts to its uncoupled value instead of
dividing by the floor.

Two properties of the implementation are worth recording because they are not
free choices:

\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{the shares are written in the ratio form}
  $w_{\rm HI} = 1/(1 + R_{\rm He}n_{\rm HeI}/n_{\rm HI} +
  R_{\rm H_2}n_{\rm H_2}/n_{\rm HI})$, not as
  $n_{\rm HI}\sigma_{\rm HI}/\sum$. With $n_{\rm H_2}=0$ the added term is
  exactly $0.0$ and $w_{\rm HI}$ is exactly $1.0$, so multiplying an atomic
  run's channel by it is the identity and the three atomic regression cases
  stay byte-identical. Rearranging to the algebraically equivalent
  $P_c\sigma_{\rm HI}/\sum$ would not have been;
\item \emph{the rates stay finite as $n_{\rm HI}\to0$.} Dividing the
  H\,\textsc{i} share by $n_{\rm HI}$ cancels the $n_{\rm HI}$ in
  $w_{\rm HI}$, leaving the trace-particle limit --- the rate a lone
  H\,\textsc{i} atom would see in a sea of H$_2$ --- rather than a divergence.
  The same cancellation gives \texttt{dP\_H2} without dividing by
  $n_{\rm H_2}$. This is the property the earlier form lacked, and it is a
  consequence of writing the physics correctly, not a guard bolted on top.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Approximations, stated at the code site.} The on-the-spot assumption
itself is unchanged and its optical depth is not tested, so a cell thin to
these photons keeps them in the local budget and both the ionization and the
heating are overestimated. The trace metals are not in the absorber
competition (item P34; they were added in section
\ref{sec:he-rec-metal-competition}, where the share they take is measured).
Each channel is collapsed onto one representative photon energy;
for the $2^1S$ two-photon continuum, which is not a line, that energy is the
mean of the in-band photons, $13.598 + $ \texttt{Ee\_2q\_HeI} $= 16.110$~eV.
Its H$_2$-ionizing photon \emph{count} should be the integral of the Drake,
Victor \& Dalgarno (1969) shape over $15.4$--$20.62$~eV rather than the
$13.598$--$20.62$~eV integral \texttt{f\_2q\_HeI} $=0.5564$ the code carries;
that shape is not in the code, only its two integrals, so it cannot be
re-integrated and \texttt{f\_2q\_HeI} is used for H$_2$ as well. This
overestimates one third of one of five channels, on the channel with the
smallest H$_2$/H\,\textsc{i} cross-section ratio.

\subsection*{The initial condition}

\texttt{set\_IC}'s molecular seed now has one rule: \textbf{the initial $x_2$
comes from the same source the ghost does.} When a lower-atmosphere handoff
states the partition (\texttt{base.inp} key \texttt{q\_H2\_base}, or a
profile's value at the matching level),
\texttt{base\_h2\_nuclei\_fraction()} --- the \S117 ghost value --- is used for
the whole column. Otherwise the chemical-equilibrium fit gives the local
$q_{\rm H_2}(p,T_0)$, clipped at \texttt{h2\_mixing\_ratio\_ceiling()} with a
one-line startup notice rather than silently at $x_2=1$. Clipping at the
ceiling still gives $x_2=1$, which is what a fully molecular mixture means, and
with the coupling corrected that is harmless.

This moves the five molecular regression cases: all five carry a handoff, so
their IC H$_2$ fraction changes from the fit's $0.984$ to the handoff's own
value, and their goldens were refreshed for it. \texttt{lower\_profile} does not
solve the molecular network at all, so its seed block never runs and it stays
byte-identical.

\subsection*{A third defect the same audit found, and the decision it needed}

\texttt{Molecular base: True} with \texttt{Molecular chemistry: False} is an
EOS-only molecular base: the H nuclei bound into H$_2$ leave the base particle
count (\texttt{comp\_ntot\_bc}) while the species arrays stay atomic. The
\texttt{ntot\_bc} recomputation at the end of \texttt{ioniz\_eq} that reconciles
the two is gated on the network being solved, so with the network off it never
fires and the base ghost pressure $(\mathtt{ntot\_bc}+\mathtt{dp\_bc})T_0$ sits
on gas that counts one particle per nucleus. \textbf{The isothermal lower
boundary is then not isothermal: it sits at $\mathtt{ntot\_bc}\times T_0$.}
Measured on \texttt{backup/regression/armD\_D1}, $\mathtt{ntot\_bc}=0.768722$
and the ghost is at $876.34$~K where \texttt{Equilibrium temperature: 1140.0}
was asked for. Section 11.5-C of
\texttt{docs/supersonic\_molecular\_base.md} had already written down the
required response --- ``the code must instead refuse a mismatch between that EOS
state and the species state used at the same ghost''.

It was not written immediately, because a startup stop changes what an existing
input file means and the grep said 31 run directories use the combination.
\textbf{The user chose refusal on 2026-09-02}, and \texttt{input\_read} now
stops with the resolved $q_{\rm H_2}$, $x_2$, \texttt{ntot\_bc}, the implied
ghost temperature against the requested $T_0$, and the two ways out: turn the
network on so the H$_2$ the particle count assumes is actually carried, or drop
\texttt{Molecular base: True} and \texttt{q\_H2\_base} if the base is meant to
be atomic.

\textbf{What the refusal invalidates.} \texttt{backup/regression/armD\_D1} (a
diagnostic case, input deliberately left as it was so the refusal reproduces
there) and 30 HD~209458\,b VULCAN handoff runs under \texttt{vulcan\_work/}, all
at $T_0 = 1450$~K:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r r@{}}
\toprule
group & \texttt{ntot\_bc} range & base ghost [K] \\
\midrule
\texttt{hd209\_wind\_response/} (10 runs)      & 0.556--0.994 & 806.2--1441.3 \\
\texttt{pc\_compare\_p1/exhale\_hd209/} (20 runs) & 0.555--0.994 & 804.8--1441.3 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The lowest values come from the deep $10^{-4}$~bar handoffs
($\mathtt{q\_H2\_base}\sim0.80$, $x_2=0.977$) and the highest from the two
shallow chemical-equilibrium-fit cases ($q_{\rm H_2}=0.006$). None has been
re-run --- that is a separate instruction. Each run directory carries an
\texttt{INVALID\_BASE\_TEMPERATURE.md} with its own numbers, the two parent
directories carry the summary tables above, and the seven documents that quote
these runs carry a stale marker at the quoting passage
(\texttt{base\_composition\_handoff\_plan.md} section 11,
\texttt{newton\_scaling\_and\_base\_wall.md}, \texttt{viscosity\_conduction.md}
G3, \texttt{oxygen\_chemistry\_new\_plan.md},
\texttt{vulcan\_photochem\_comparison.md} in two places,
\texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} item (A), and the section~117 passage above, whose two
quoted $q_{\rm H_2}$ values are VULCAN handoff \emph{inputs} and are
unaffected).

\subsection*{A diagnostic for the failure mode}

\texttt{n\_cells\_he\_rec\_photoionization\_dominant} counts cell-steps in
which the coupling's \texttt{dP\_HI} exceeds the direct stellar photoionization
integral \texttt{P\_HI} by more than $1000$. The coupling is a \emph{correction}
to that integral, so three decades of dominance is a statement that the local
photon budget has run away. It is reported at the end of a run only when it is
nonzero, like the positivity counters, and it is zero on every case measured
here.

\subsection*{Verification}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Byte-identical} on the three cases with no molecular hydrogen,
  which are the ones the bitwise property above is designed to protect:
  \texttt{wasp\_full} (He $2^3S$ on, the TR branch of the routine),
  \texttt{wasp\_he23off} (the atomic branch) and \texttt{lower\_profile}.
  \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} and \texttt{Ion\_species.txt} identical to the
  goldens in all three.
\item \textbf{The case, 12000 steps} (\texttt{backup/regression/armD\_D2}, the
  hot Uranus at $\mathrm{He/H}=1$ with \texttt{q\_H2\_base 0.300861},
  \texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=1}): base inflow subsonic throughout at max Mach
  $8.64\times10^{-2}$, zero energy-floor activations, zero activations of the
  new counter, $\log_{10}\dot M = 10.91$. The first physical cell at
  $r=1.000193\,R_p$ holds $n({\rm H_2})=2.49\times10^{13}$,
  $n({\rm H\,\textsc{i}})=2.28\times10^{10}$,
  $n({\rm H\,\textsc{ii}})=1.4\times10^{3}$~cm$^{-3}$ at $1165.7$~K, against
  $n({\rm H\,\textsc{i}})=0$, $n({\rm H\,\textsc{ii}})=5.0\times10^{13}$,
  $132.1$~K before. Two controlled runs, each cutting one defect alone, reach
  the same solution: \texttt{He\_rec\_coupling: False} gives max Mach
  $8.76\times10^{-2}$ and $\log_{10}\dot M = 10.89$, and the IC clip alone
  gives $8.64\times10^{-2}$ and $10.91$.
\item \textbf{The H$_2$ share is real.} In the molecular base of
  \texttt{mol\_diffusion}, where $n_{\rm H_2}/n_{\rm HI}=1.7\times10^{3}$, the
  returned rates are \texttt{dP\_HI} $=3.65\times10^{-23}$ and
  \texttt{dP\_H2} $=1.10\times10^{-22}$~s$^{-1}$ per particle, so H$_2$ absorbs
  $n_{\rm H_2}\,$\texttt{dP\_H2}$/(n_{\rm HI}\,$\texttt{dP\_HI}$)=5.2\times10^{3}$
  times as many of these photons as H\,\textsc{i} does: $99.98\%$ of them. All
  of that used to go to H\,\textsc{i}.
\item \texttt{make check}, 9 of 9. \texttt{wasp\_full},
  \texttt{wasp\_he23off} and \texttt{lower\_profile} pass against the existing
  goldens; the five molecular cases move, for the two reasons above, and their
  goldens were refreshed at the end of this block. \textbf{How far they move},
  measured against the old goldens before the refresh:
  $\log_{10}\dot M$ falls by $0.00$ to $0.02$~dex in every case
  ($10.57\to10.56$, $10.58\to10.58$, $10.58\to10.56$, $10.57\to10.56$,
  $10.58\to10.57$, and $10.54\to10.52$ for \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion}), the sign
  being the same everywhere. In the molecular layer, $r<1.3\,R_p$, the largest
  relative changes are $4$--$7\%$ in $T$, $9$--$14\%$ in density, and up to
  $80\%$ in $n({\rm H_2})$ at the H$_2$ front itself, which moves
  \emph{outward} by $0.0003\,R_p$ ($1.0178\to1.0181$). The outer wind of these
  12000-step snapshots moves more, but they are relaxation snapshots at
  $du\sim3$ rather than converged solutions, and their outer cells are still in
  the cold-start transient.
\item \texttt{run\_fcheck.sh} (bounds/do/mem checking build, one bounded
  HD~209458\,b run): clean, no runtime check fired. It needed two repairs to
  run at all, neither related to this section's physics and both in the script:
  it is the only harness that compiles from scratch, so it was picking up
  whichever \texttt{gfortran} the \texttt{PATH} resolved to (a conda toolchain
  here, whose LAPACK links against a different \texttt{libgfortran} and fails
  with undefined \verb|_gfortran_*@GFORTRAN_1.0|), and its \texttt{-g} build
  hit a linker that cannot read gfortran 13's compressed
  \texttt{.debug\_info}. It now prefers \texttt{/usr/bin/gfortran} when there
  is one and passes \texttt{-gz=none}, and it prints the tail of the build log
  when the build fails instead of only ``BUILD FAILED''.
\end{enumerate}


\section{What the steady solver's probe states were allowed to write, and what
they were allowed to be (2026-09-02)}\label{sec:steady-probe-hygiene}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Two defects, both found while diagnosing the segmentation fault of
section~\ref{sec:jfnk-nan-histogram} and neither repaired there.} They are
numerical hygiene of the steady (JFNK / PTC) solver, not physics: no rate,
cross section or balance is touched, and the marching path is unchanged.

\textbf{(a) The equilibrium sweeps of probe states wrote the run's own
counters.} \texttt{ioniz\_eq} keeps run-wide totals --- the acceptance classes
of section~\ref{sec:ieq-residual-acceptance} and their largest normalized
reaction residual, the residual-decade histograms, the root-validation
counters, the constrained-solve totals, the print budget --- and one array with
authority over the run, \texttt{ieq\_nonroot\_streak}, whose limit
\texttt{error stop}s it. The steady solver calls \texttt{ioniz\_eq} on three
different kinds of state: its current iterate; the finite-difference and Krylov
probes $Y + \epsilon v$ that build the Newton model; and line-search trials,
which are candidates until one is adopted. All three wrote the same counters as
the marching loop.

The species fractions did \emph{not} leak --- \texttt{jv\_product} and
\texttt{build\_banded\_jac\_full} restore \texttt{f\_sp} from a base copy
before every probe, and the line search adopts \texttt{f\_sp\_j} only for an
accepted trial. The counters did. Measured on
\texttt{backup/regression/armD\_D2\_newton} at 8 threads: not one non-root
acceptance in the 2002 marching steps before the hand-off, and 18{,}339 over
the JFNK phase and the eight marching steps after it, largest residual
$1.74\times10^{97}$ --- an end-of-run report dominated by states the run never
adopted. \texttt{ieq\_nonroot\_streak} was worse than noisy: probe sweeps both
raised it and cleared it, so ``consecutive sweeps resting on a non-root'', the
quantity the stop is defined on, counted evaluations that were thrown away in
the next statement.

\textbf{(b) Nothing tested whether a probe state could be described at all.}
The line-search trial test was density and pressure positivity
(\texttt{steady\_newton.f90}, \texttt{minval(Wtry(1,1:N)) > 0 .and.\
minval(Wtry(3,1:N)) > 0}). \texttt{jv\_product} evaluated the full residual at
$Y + \epsilon v$ unconditionally, with $v$ a Krylov direction of no physical
meaning and \texttt{gm = 40} such probes per outer iteration;
\texttt{build\_banded\_jac\_full} probed $Y + \sqrt{\epsilon}\,D$ the same way.
A probe state can drive a balance row of the molecular network to NaN or to
overflow, \texttt{normalized\_reaction\_residual} returns it, and that residual
then entered the Jacobian, the Arnoldi recursion and the merit comparison. The
SIGSEGV of section~\ref{sec:jfnk-nan-histogram} was one symptom; the residual
itself was the disease.

\subsection*{The design}

\textbf{Three ledgers, tagged at the call site.} Each equilibrium sweep is
tagged \texttt{ieq\_state\_marching}, \texttt{ieq\_state\_steady\_iterate} or
\texttt{ieq\_state\_steady\_candidate}
(\texttt{set\_ioniz\_eq\_sweep\_state\_kind}, called from outside any parallel
region), and its totals go to the ledger of that tag. The counters that used to
be a dozen separate module variables are now the fields of one derived type,
\texttt{ioniz\_eq\_ledger}, held in three instances; the end-of-run report
prints one block per instance and stays silent for an instance nothing was
recorded in, so an ordinary marching run prints exactly what it printed before.

The tag also decides two things that are not statistics. A candidate sweep does
not touch \texttt{ieq\_nonroot\_streak} --- it neither increments nor resets
it, and the stop is not evaluated --- so the streak once again counts
consecutive sweeps of a state the run holds. And a candidate sweep's non-root
acceptances are not reported cell by cell and do not spend the print budget: a
probe acceptance is a property of a state the solver invented to differentiate
at, and tens of thousands of them bury the events that matter. They are not
lost; they are in the third ledger, with the class populations and the largest
residual of each.

The line-search trial that \emph{is} adopted was evaluated as a candidate, so
its sweep is counted in the candidate ledger; the next outer iteration
re-evaluates the same state as the iterate and counts it there. The one state
this leaves in the candidate ledger only is the final accepted trial of a
converged solve, which is never re-evaluated.

\textbf{Admissibility, in two layers.}

\emph{The signal.} \texttt{ioniz\_eq} takes an optional
\texttt{sweep\_ledger} argument and returns this sweep's own totals in it,
including three new fields: the number of cells whose accepted state carries a
normalized reaction residual that is \textbf{not a finite number}, the number
of cells at which no starting point stayed inside the element simplex, and the
largest element-budget violation of any iterate that left the simplex (whether
or not a later starting point of the same cell then found a root). Two related repairs went
in with it, both consequences of NaN failing every comparison: a non-finite
\texttt{acc\_res} used to pass the class-3 recheck
(\texttt{acc\_res > ieq\_res\_tol} is false for a NaN) and be recorded as a
\emph{root}, and it used to enter \texttt{acc\_resmax}, where a single
occurrence would have destroyed the largest-residual statistic of the whole
run. A non-finite residual is now class 4 by construction and is kept out of
the maximum. The atomic branch also measures the element violation of the
iterate it rejects, which it previously reported as zero.

\texttt{eval\_residual} combines that signal with a scan of the assembled
residual vector and returns one logical, \texttt{admissible}. Two independent
statements are required because they catch different things: the sweep count
names the cell whose chemistry broke, which is where the diagnosis is; the row
scan catches anything non-finite that reached the residual by another route.
The argument is optional, so the marching path never asks and is not affected.

\emph{The line search.} A trial that is not admissible is rejected ---
$\lambda$ is halved --- exactly as a negative density is, in both
\texttt{solve\_steady\_jfnk} and \texttt{solve\_steady\_ptc}. This is not only
explicitness: a non-finite merit failed the Armijo test by accident of IEEE
ordering rather than by decision, and a trial whose chemistry broke in a few
cells can still produce a finite, smaller merit and be adopted.

\emph{The temperature band was considered and not added.} The only temperature
limit in the code is the $0.01\,T_0$ clamp inside the Newton iteration of
\texttt{energy\_semi\_implicit}, which belongs to the marching energy update
and has no upper counterpart; there is no band in the steady path. The brief
for this work was to use a band if one existed and not to invent one, and none
exists. Positivity of the pressure already excludes a non-positive trial
temperature, and a temperature that breaks the network shows up in the
admissibility signal.

\emph{The element-budget violation is measured and reported, and does not
reject.} The accepted state of every acceptance class is inside the simplex by
construction --- the molecular branch clamps, the atomic branch hands back the
uncoupled balance --- so the violation describes the iterate that was rejected,
not the state returned. Whether a large one should disqualify a trial cannot be
decided without measuring where healthy solves sit, and the healthy cold start
of section~\ref{sec:ieq-residual-acceptance} legitimately clamps. It is
therefore carried in the ledgers and printed, and no threshold is asserted on
it.

\textbf{The probes: sample closer, and never invent the derivative.} A Jacobian
column and a Krylov product are directional derivatives \emph{of the residual
at $Y$}. The point $Y + h v$ at which they are sampled is not physics: $h$ is
ours to choose and $v$ has no physical meaning. So when the sample point leaves
the set of states the code can describe, the honest answer is to sample closer
to $Y$ --- the step is halved and the probe repeated, at most
\texttt{n\_probe\_step\_halvings = 6} times, over which the finite-difference
step falls by 64 and stays far above the round-off floor of the residual.

If even the smallest of those steps is inadmissible, the boundary runs through
$Y$ itself along $v$ and there is no derivative to sample. Then none is
invented:

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{pgmres} stops the cycle at the directions it did build and
returns the step from that subspace. A shorter GMRES cycle is a valid
approximate solve, and the line search judges the step it produces.
\item If not one direction could be sampled, the step is zero and there is no
Newton model at all for that outer iteration. The zero step is then kept
\emph{out of the line search}, and the iteration is recorded as a no-descent
iteration. This is not cosmetic: the non-monotone test compares a trial against
the \emph{worst} merit of the last five iterates, so $Y_{\rm try} = Y$ passes
it whenever the current iterate is not that worst one --- measured on
\texttt{armD\_D2\_newton}, consecutive outer iterations with
\texttt{gm = 0} were being recorded as accepted steps at $\lambda = 1$,
resetting the no-descent counter and letting the solve spin to \texttt{maxit}
instead of aborting. With the zero step rejected the solve reaches its
stagnation abort, which is the honest outcome.
\item \texttt{build\_banded\_jac\_full} leaves the columns of an unresolvable
color at zero. Those columns are a \emph{preconditioner}; zeroing them degrades
the treatment of those unknowns to plain relaxation and costs iterations, not
correctness. If the base point $Y$ itself is inadmissible no column is built at
all.
\end{itemize}

Both events are counted and printed, per solve. Nothing non-finite can reach
the Arnoldi recursion or the band matrix: \texttt{jv\_product} returns
$Jv = 0$ with \texttt{ok = .false.} and the caller is required to stop using
$v$ rather than use the value.

\subsection*{What the code now says, measured}

The verification uses two builds of the \textbf{same source tree} --- the
tree as it stood after section~\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber} went in --- one of them
with this change and one without, so the comparison isolates it. Single thread
unless stated.

\textbf{The regression matrix and the two Newton cases are byte-identical.}
All nine matrix cases plus \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} and
\texttt{wasp\_he23off\_newton}: the data lines of \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} and
\texttt{Ion\_species.txt} agree in all 22 file pairs, and the nine matrix cases
reproduce \texttt{backup/regression/golden/} exactly in both builds.
\texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} is one of the two cases that runs the JFNK to
convergence (\texttt{info = 0}, $\|R\| = 5.615\times10^{-4}$ in 18 outer
iterations), so its identity is the statement that matters: \textbf{no
line-search trial that the new rule rejects was ever adopted by the old code in
that solve.} Its new ledger reads 4241 marching sweeps, 19 steady-solver
iterate sweeps, 388 probe sweeps.

\textbf{Serial versus parallel.} \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} with the final
build at \texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS = 1} and \texttt{= 8}: both output files
identical.

\textbf{The He/H = 1 case, restarted from a healthy state and forced through
the JFNK.} The case of section~\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber}
(\texttt{hotUranus\_diffusion}, He/H = 1, molecular chemistry and He/H
diffusion on) was restarted from its step-168{,}550 state ---
$du = 1.735\times10^{-2}$, monotonically converging --- with
\texttt{Load IC? True}, \texttt{du\_th [PLM,WENO3]: 1.0e9 1.0e-3} and
\texttt{Solver: Newton 100.0}, which puts the solver into the JFNK
immediately. This is a healthy state, so the criterion is the opposite of a
failure report: \textbf{the solve has to converge, and the new hygiene must not
be what stops it.} (The restart was necessary: that marching run does not reach
\texttt{du\_th} by itself --- its $du$ bottoms out at $9.96\times10^{-3}$ at
step 251{,}287 and then rises again.)

At one thread the two builds are \textbf{byte-identical}, output files and JFNK
trace alike. The run marches 2002 steps to $du = 3.1094\times10^{-2}$, enters
the JFNK three times, and every one of them returns \texttt{info = 0}; the last
leaves $\|R\| = 3.264\times10^{-4}$ and the run closes as \emph{converged: JFNK
steady solution}, at
\[
   \log_{10} \dot{M} = 10.32~\mathrm{g\,s^{-1}},
\]
which is the first quotable quantitative He/H = 1 value since P17. Not one
hygiene event fired in the whole run: no GMRES cycle truncated, no Jacobian
color zeroed, no trial rejected as inadmissible. The three ledgers are clean
throughout --- marching 2007 sweeps with 1{,}011{,}495 converged roots, 15
roots without solver convergence and 18 constrained-continuation roots and
\textbf{no non-root acceptance at all}; 22 iterate sweeps, all roots; 396 probe
sweeps, 199{,}584 converged roots and again no non-root, no non-finite residual
and no off-simplex cell in any of the three.

At 8 threads both builds also converged, \texttt{info = 0}, but at
$\log_{10}\dot{M} = 10.35$ (old) and $10.33$ (new) against the serial $10.32$.
The traces separated at the very first JFNK line --- the starting
$\|F_s\|_2$ differed in its third digit, before any hygiene decision can act
--- so that spread was not this change; the serial identity above is what
settles it.

\textbf{It was a defect of its own, and it is now repaired} (item (P37) of
\texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md}, \texttt{docs/supersonic\_molecular\_base.md}
section 12.6). Traced to the constrained element-conserving continuation: its
seed floored the species listed in \texttt{n\_unknown} /
\texttt{species\_of\_unknown}, which are rung-partition state built later in
the same solve, so on entry to a cell they still described whichever cell that
thread had handled last --- and on a thread's first cell they were never
initialized at all. A cell's chemical equilibrium has to be a function of that
cell's state, so the serial answer was order-contaminated in the same way
rather than correct. The seed now uses the cell's own species set and the rung
context is cleared on entry; \texttt{heh1\_jfnk}, \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion}
and \texttt{mol\_metals} are byte-identical at 1 and 8 threads under
\texttt{static}, \texttt{static,1} and \texttt{dynamic,8}, and the He/H = 1
rate is $\log_{10}\dot{M} = 10.32$ at every thread count. The six molecular
matrix cases that promote a cell to the continuation move with it (the three
that do not --- \texttt{wasp\_full}, \texttt{wasp\_he23off} and
\texttt{lower\_profile} --- stay bit for bit); $\log_{10}\dot{M}$ is
unchanged to two decimals in all six and the largest relative profile change is
$2.0\times10^{-2}$. Their goldens are refreshed at the end of the block, not
here.

\textbf{The contamination itself, measured on the old pathological restart.}
The \texttt{backup/regression/armD\_D2\_newton} state --- the pathology that
preceded section~\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber}, a state the code no longer produces
--- is what defect (a) was measured on, at 8 threads. Old code, one report for
the whole run: 20{,}704 non-root acceptances under the relaxation amnesty,
largest residual $1.01\times10^{2}$, longest cell streak 17 sweeps, and
17{,}156 molecular clamps. New code, the same run split by state kind:

\begin{table}[h]
\centering\small
\caption{Acceptance ledgers of one \texttt{armD\_D2\_newton} run (8 threads),
separated by the kind of state the equilibrium sweep was evaluating.}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrr@{}}
\toprule
ledger & sweeps & non-root (max res) & off-simplex cells & non-finite residual\\
\midrule
marching states        & 46{,}047 & \textbf{0} & 0 & 0 \\
steady-solver iterates & 22       & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
steady-solver probes   & 1{,}254  & 21{,}789 ($2.14\times10^{2}$) & 12{,}695 & 9{,}093 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The entire non-root population, and every non-finite reaction residual,
belonged to states the run never adopted; the marching phase it actually walked
is clean, which the merged report had made impossible to see. The JFNK on that
state fails in both builds (\texttt{info = 2} after the 12 no-descent iterations,
then marching resumes and the run ends at the same
$\log_{10}\dot{M} = 17.68$), and the new code says why:
\texttt{probe states without an admissible residual: 0 Jacobian color(s)
zeroed, 14 GMRES cycle(s) truncated}. (That case is not thread-reproducible in
its marching phase, so its counter totals differ from run to run; the JFNK
block and the final mass-loss rate do not.)

\textbf{Why the element-budget violation is not a rejection criterion,
measured.} The healthy matrix cases carry off-simplex iterates of order unity
in their cold start: \texttt{mol\_metals} 27 cells with a largest violation of
\textbf{9.55}, and \texttt{mol\_ir\_bands} 3 cells at \textbf{0.423}, both
reproducing their goldens. There is no threshold that separates those from a
probe excursion --- the same finding, in the same direction, that
section~\ref{sec:ieq-residual-acceptance} made for the residual severity of a
cold start --- so the violation is measured and printed and nothing is decided
on it.

\subsection*{The boundary of this section}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Marching is untouched.} Every new argument is optional or is set
only from the steady solver, and the two default paths of a marching run are
the ones it had. The marching ledger prints the same lines, word for word, that
the old counters printed.
\item \textbf{The state the solver hands back is now consistent in the frozen
background too.} \texttt{f\_sp} is restored with the best iterate and
\texttt{nmol\_eq} / \texttt{nox\_eq} are rebuilt from \texttt{f\_sp} at
the top of every sweep, so those were always consistent. \texttt{bg\_cell} ---
the copy of each cell's coefficients that the carrier transport
(\texttt{diffusive\_photochemistry}) reads --- was not: it is written by every
molecular sweep, probe sweeps included, so on return it described whatever
state was evaluated last, which is a \emph{rejected} line-search trial whenever
the final iteration found no descent, and the best-iterate restore could move
the returned state further still. Both solvers now keep a copy of it at each
state they adopt (\texttt{bg\_cell\_adopted}, \texttt{bg\_cell\_best} in
\texttt{ionization\_equilibrium}) and install the right one before returning,
so the invariant is that every cell state derived from the returned state was
evaluated at the returned state.

\emph{Measured, and the scope is narrower than it looks.} On the converging
He/H = 1 solve the repair is a no-op: all three JFNK phases end on an accepted
trial with no best-iterate restore, so the background the solver was already
leaving matched the adopted state in all 504 cells. On the failing path it is
not: restarted on the old \texttt{armD\_D2\_newton} state, which ends
\texttt{info = 2} after the twelve no-descent iterations, the background the
old code left differed from the adopted state in \textbf{all 504 cells, by up
to a factor 4 in temperature} (largest relative \texttt{T\_K} difference 3.01;
sum over cells $6.90\times10^{5}$ against $7.32\times10^{5}$). \emph{No
consumer saw it}, however: \texttt{EXHALE\_main} calls \texttt{ioniz\_eq} at
the returned state immediately after the solver returns and before the carrier
transport or any resumed marching step, which overwrites \texttt{bg\_cell} in
every cell --- measured, the post-solver sweep and the newly installed
background agree to $3.4\times10^{-5}$ relative. The repair is therefore a
correctness invariant of the solver's own boundary, not a change of any result;
an earlier draft of this section asserted that a molecular run resumed its
transport from the rejected trial, and that was wrong.
\item \textbf{What ``admissible'' covers.} A non-finite normalized reaction
residual in the equilibrium sweep, and a non-finite row of the assembled
residual vector. It does not cover a state that is finite everywhere and
physically absurd; positivity of density and pressure is still the only other
filter, and no temperature band was added because the code has none to use.
\item \textbf{The six halvings are a bound, not a measurement.} Nothing here
measures how often a probe becomes admissible on the second or third halving;
the counters record only how often all six failed. On the healthy He/H = 1 case
that was never; on the old pathological restart it was 14 GMRES cycles and no
Jacobian color.
\end{itemize}


% ===================================================================== %
% ===================================================================== %
\section{H$_2$ self-shielding: the fits were measured against a level-resolved
calculation, and the rate is now a table of it (2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:h2-shield-table}
% ===================================================================== %

\begin{quote}\small\textbf{Superseded in part by Sec.~\ref{sec:lw-cross-section-sources} (2026-09-02).} The rate no longer
multiplies a constant cross section by a shielding factor: the level-resolved
cross section itself is tabulated, and \texttt{sigma\_lw}, \texttt{p\_diss\_lw}
and \texttt{sigma\_lw\_pump} have been removed from the module.\end{quote}

\begin{quote}\small\textbf{Superseded by Sec.~\ref{sec:h2-shield-line-overlap} (2026-09-03).} The tabulated
rate was \textsc{cloudy}'s H2g sub-reservoir and line overlap was absent; both
are fixed there.\end{quote}
\textbf{The judgement first.} Neither closed-form fit reproduces a
level-resolved \textsc{Cloudy} calculation at the temperature of our molecular
layer, and the failure is not an offset that a rescaling would fix: the
calculated $f_{\rm shield}(N_{\rm H_2})$ has a trough near $10^{16}$--$10^{17}$
and a shoulder near $10^{19}$~cm$^{-2}$ that a two-term algebraic form of this
kind cannot carry. Draine \& Bertoldi (1996) runs from $1.85\times$ high at
$900$~K to $2.3\times$ low at $2700$~K over
$10^{18} \le N_{\rm H_2} \le 5\times10^{20}$~cm$^{-2}$; Richings, Schaye \&
Oppenheimer (2014), which section~\ref{sec:h2-shield-richings} adopted, is low
by $3.3$--$4.3\times$ at every temperature of the layer. The physically correct
quantity is the level-resolved calculation, so it is tabulated and the rate
reads the table. \textbf{This reverses the earlier choice, and it does so on
measurement rather than on a re-reading of the papers.}

\subsection{The premise of the earlier section is not what failed}

Richings et al.\ adopted their fit because DB96 overestimates the shielding
factor by about $3$ at $T = 100$~K for $N_{\rm H_2} \gtrsim 10^{17}$~cm$^{-2}$.
That is reproduced here from our own deck --- DB96/\textsc{Cloudy} $=
2.27$--$3.38$ over $10^{17} \le N_{\rm H_2} \le 5\times10^{20}$~cm$^{-2}$ at
$100$~K in interstellar-like conditions --- so the premise stands and the
pipeline is calibrated against the very comparison that motivated the change.
What could not be known then is that \textbf{the sign of the DB96 error
reverses between $100$~K and $900$~K}: a fit built to remove the $100$~K excess
keeps removing it after it has gone, and our layer runs at $865$--$2724$~K.

\subsection{What was calculated}

\textsc{Cloudy} c25.00, \texttt{DATABASE H2}, plane-parallel slab irradiated on
one face: pure H\,+\,He at He/H $= 0.0793$, no dust, no metals, cosmic-ray
background as the only ionization source, constant temperature, thermal Doppler
width. The incident field is flat $F_\lambda$ ($f_\nu \sim \nu^{-2}$), DB96's
own eq.~(24) spectrum, normalized to $F = 343$~erg~cm$^{-2}$~s$^{-1}$ over
$912$--$1110$~\AA, i.e.\ our \texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner} field and
$G_0 = 1.25\times10^{6}$ Habing.

Twenty-seven runs, $T = 700, 900, 1100, 1300, 1600, 1800, 2200, 2700,
3200$~K at $n_{\rm H} = 10^{12}, 10^{13}, 10^{14}$~cm$^{-3}$, each carried to
$N_{\rm H_2} = 5.01\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-2}$. $f_{\rm shield}$ is the
ground-state Solomon dissociation rate divided by the band-integrated field,
normalized to its own value at the illuminated face of the same run.

Two independent checks of the setup, both in
\texttt{docs/h2\_self\_shielding\_cloudy.md}: \textsc{Cloudy}'s own
\texttt{G(TH85)} at the face is $1.25\times10^{6}$, matching the Habing
conversion done by hand, and its band photon flux agrees with $F/\langle h\nu
\rangle$ as \texttt{lyman\_werner.f90} forms it to $0.3\%$.

\subsection{The table}

\texttt{src/modules/lower\_atmosphere/h2\_self\_shielding\_table.f90},
generated by \texttt{src/utils/h2\_shielding\_table\_from\_cloudy.py} from the
decks in \texttt{src/utils/h2\_shielding\_cloudy\_decks/}:
$\log_{10} f_{\rm shield}$ on $39$ columns $\times$ $9$ temperatures $\times$
$3$ densities $=$ \textbf{1053 doubles}, trilinear in
$(\log_{10} T, \log_{10} n_{\rm H}, \log_{10} N_{\rm H_2})$, every axis clamped
rather than extrapolated.

\textbf{The column axis starts at $10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$, not at $10^{16}$.} The
plan was $10^{16}$ with $f = 1$ below it; the calculation says
$f_{\rm shield}(10^{16})$ is $0.067$ at $700$~K and $0.24$ at $3200$~K, so a
table starting there would have needed an invented rule underneath it. At
$10^{12}$ the measured factor is $1.000$ in every run ($0.9989$ in the worst),
which is the optically thin limit, so the bottom clamp asserts only what the
runs show. The cost is $432$ extra doubles.

\subsection{Where the table stops being a value}

\textsc{Cloudy} shields one line at a time ---
\texttt{RT\_continuum\_shield\_fcn} applies the Federman, Glassgold \& Kwan
(1979) function per transition --- so overlap between distinct H$_2$ lines is
absent from it, and overlap is what DB96 \S5.2 say produces ``the rapid falloff
\ldots\ for $N_2 > 10^{20}$~cm$^{-2}$'', suppressing the pumping rates by a
factor $\sim\!10$ at $3\times10^{21}$.

The size of that gap is measured inside the runs rather than assumed. Build the
summed equivalent width of the pumping lines from \textsc{Cloudy}'s own curve
with DB96's eq.~(38) construction,
$A(N) = \sigma_{\rm pump}\int_0^N f_{\rm shield}\,dN'$, using the
\texttt{sigma\_lw\_pump} the module already carries. $A$ is a fraction of the
band and cannot exceed $1$. It does, and the column where it reaches $1$ is
\texttt{h2\_shielding\_overlap\_column(T, n\_H)}:
$1.4$--$1.8\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-2}$ at $700$~K falling monotonically to
$2.5\times10^{20}$ at $3200$~K --- the hotter the gas, the more lines share the
band and the earlier the un-overlapped sum breaks down. \textbf{Above that
column the table is an upper bound on the shielding, hence a lower bound on the
rate. No correction is applied there}: inventing the missing transfer would be
worse than recording its absence. The run reports the crossing once, through
the warning that used to quote the two fits' published ranges.

Our base sits at $N_{\rm H_2} = 4.4\times10^{21}$, i.e.\ above it, so the
deepest cells of a molecular run carry that bound. Extending the grid with a
code that treats line overlap is an open item.

\subsection{What the band share keeps, and why}

$A$ stays on DB96 eq.~(39), and the same calculation is now the reason rather
than the absence of an alternative. Measured off the $1300$~K run, the
band-removal cross section is $\sigma_{\rm pump} = 2.610\times10^{-17}$~cm$^2$
against the $2.557\times10^{-17}$ the module carries --- \textbf{2 per cent}.
The two departures behind it cancel: \textsc{Cloudy}'s dissociation cross
section is $34\%$ above $\sigma_{\rm LW}$ and its $\langle p_{\rm diss}\rangle
= 0.177$ is $31\%$ above the coded $0.135$. So the normalization the equivalent
width rests on is confirmed at our temperature, and the earlier decision to
leave $A$ on DB96 is now measured instead of argued.

Two constants are recorded as measured but \emph{not} changed, because changing
either alters the unattenuated rate rather than its shielding and belongs with
its own verification: $\sigma_{\rm LW} = 3.452\times10^{-18}$~cm$^2$ is
$23$--$60\%$ low against \textsc{Cloudy} over $900$--$2700$~K (mostly a
line-data difference, not temperature --- it is already $37\%$ low at $100$~K),
and $p_{\rm diss}$ is not constant with depth ($0.177$ at the face, $0.217$ at
$N_{\rm H_2} = 5\times10^{21}$).

\subsection{Two axes closed by measurement}

\textbf{Density.} The table carries $n_{\rm H}$ because it can, but the axis is
nearly flat: $f_{\rm shield}$ moves $3$--$7\%$ over
$n_{\rm H} = 10^{12}$--$10^{14}$ below $N_{\rm H_2} = 10^{19}$ and by at most
$40\%$ at $10^{21}$. The absence of a density argument in either fit is not
what is wrong with them.

\textbf{Radiation field, i.e.\ the Elwert axis.} Dropping $F_{\rm LW}$ by four
decades ($G_0$ from $1.25\times10^{6}$ to $125$) moves $f_{\rm shield}$ by at
most $9\%$ anywhere and by under $5\%$ below $N_{\rm H_2} = 10^{20}$. The
earlier section rejected the Elwert exponent by arithmetic; this is the same
conclusion by measurement, and it is why the table has no radiation-field axis.

\textbf{H Lyman lines inside the band}, checked while there: running with
\texttt{Database H-like Lyman pumping off} moves $f_{\rm shield}$ by $2$--$11\%$,
always upward. \texttt{lyman\_werner.f90} \S4 flags their neglect as the least
controlled of the three absorbers it drops; it is a few per cent.

\subsection{What changed in the code}

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{h2\_self\_shielding\_table.f90} is new and generated;
  \texttt{h2\_shielding\_table\_from\_cloudy.py} and the $27$ decks are in
  \texttt{src/utils/} so the table can be rebuilt.
\item \texttt{lyman\_werner\_dissociation\_rate} takes $n_{\rm H}$ and reads
  the table. \texttt{h2\_self\_shielding\_richings} and
  \texttt{h2\_self\_shielding\_draine\_bertoldi} are \textbf{kept and are no
  longer called by the rate}; the header says so. The second is still live for
  the band share.
\item \texttt{fuv\_lw\_photon\_field} takes the total hydrogen nucleus density
  and returns the largest ratio of the star-ward column to
  \texttt{h2\_shielding\_overlap\_column}; the \texttt{f\_shield} column of
  \texttt{output/Lyman\_Werner.txt} is the table's value, i.e.\ still the
  factor the rate actually carries.
\item The extrapolation warning in \texttt{ionization\_equilibrium} and
  \texttt{write\_output} no longer quotes the Richings range, which is no
  longer used; it reports the crossing of $N_{\rm overlap}$ and the DB96 range
  that the band share still rests on. \texttt{NH2\_richings\_max} is gone,
  \texttt{NH2\_db96\_max} stays.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Verification}

\textbf{Two changes share this refresh, and they are separable.} The
section~\ref{sec:steady-probe-hygiene} constrained-continuation seed fix landed
in the tree first and had already moved the six molecular cases off their
goldens; this section's table moves one of them further. Which case moved for
which reason was measured, not inferred: the current tree source was built a
second time with this section's patch reverse-applied, and the six molecular
cases were re-run against it.

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{wasp\_full}, \texttt{wasp\_he23off}, \texttt{lower\_profile} ---
  no Lyman--Werner field; PASS throughout, moved by neither change.
\item \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff}, \texttt{mol\_metals},
  \texttt{mol\_diffusion}, \texttt{mol\_ir\_bands}, \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion} ---
  no Lyman--Werner field; moved by the seed fix, and
  \textbf{byte-identical with and without the table}.
\item \texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner} --- the one case that sets
  \texttt{Stellar LW flux}; moved by both.
\end{itemize}

\noindent That is the structural statement this change should make:
\texttt{F\_LW\_star} defaults to zero and exactly one matrix case supplies it,
so exactly one matrix case can reach the new code at all.

\textbf{The size of the table's own move}, from the pair above (same source,
same $12000$ steps, shielding the only difference; per item P17 these are
relaxation snapshots, so these are not converged change sizes): the H$_2$
front, the largest $r$ with $n_{\rm H_2} > 10^{10}$, goes from $1.165804$ to
$1.149903\,R_p$; the minimum temperature over the molecular cells from
$837.4$ to $806.1$~K; $n({\rm H_2})$ over those cells changes by a factor
$0.0040$ to $1.0714$; \texttt{final} from \texttt{du} $=3.1452$ to $2.5958$ at
the same step count. The sign is the one the measurement predicts --- over the
columns the layer occupies the table shields \emph{less} than Richings, so the
rate is higher, the front is pushed inward, and the outermost molecular cells
lose H$_2$ by up to a factor $250$.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Matrix before the refresh}: the three no-LW cases PASS
  byte-identical, the six molecular cases FAIL --- exactly the split the two
  changes predict.
\item \textbf{Goldens refreshed once}, the previous set preserved at
  \texttt{backup/regression/golden\_blockD\_20260902/} beforehand.
  \texttt{make check} returns \textbf{PASS, all cases byte-identical, 9/9,
  EXIT 0}.
\item \textbf{\texttt{run\_fcheck.sh}: CLEAN}, production build restored, and
  the matrix re-run on that restored binary returns \textbf{PASS 9/9} again.
\item \textbf{The runtime-checked build was additionally run on
  \texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner}}, which the fcheck case (HD~209458\,b, atomic)
  does not reach: the same \texttt{-O1 -fcheck=bounds,do,mem} binary, $1500$
  steps, \textbf{no runtime check fired}. That is the only run in which the
  new table is traversed under bounds checking.
\item \textbf{Unit check of the table against what generated it}: a probe
  program linked against \texttt{h2\_self\_shielding\_table.o} reproduces the
  Python-side value at all $1053$ grid points to $1.2\times10^{-9}$ relative,
  and $N_{\rm overlap}$ at all $27$ to the same, i.e.\ the Fortran
  interpolation returns the \textsc{Cloudy} numbers themselves at the nodes.
  Off the nodes, at the mid-points of the $1300$~K column axis, the table
  reproduces the underlying run to $0.6$--$1.9\%$.
\item \textbf{The warning fires and says the right thing}:
  \texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner} reports the star-ward column reaching
  $4.99\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-2}$, $3.30$ times the column at which the table
  becomes an upper bound.
\item \textbf{Not verified}: nothing was re-run outside the matrix. The stored
  results of \texttt{examples/18\_oxygen\_chemistry/} and
  \texttt{examples/19\_molecular\_ir\_bands/} carry a Lyman--Werner flux and
  now predate this change as well as the earlier one.
\end{itemize}

% ===================================================================== %
% ===================================================================== %
\section{The heating dump left the oxygen carriers' hydrogen out of the
ionized fraction, and the H/He nucleus totals are now one routine
(2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:nuclei-one-routine}
% ===================================================================== %
Section~\ref{sec:sec-ion-molecular} fixed what the ionized fraction handed to the
photoelectron partition is --- the \emph{total} free electron density over the
hydrogen and helium \textbf{nuclei}, the quantity Dalgarno, Yan \& Liu (1999)
section~7 define --- and made the sites that build it agree. The oxygen
chemistry (sections~\ref{sec:oxychem-kinetics} and~\ref{sec:oxychem-beam})
then introduced two further carriers of hydrogen nuclei, OH and H$_2$O, and
one of those sites was not taught about them.

\subsection{What was different}

\texttt{ionization\_equilibrium} builds the nucleus totals as
%
\begin{align*}
n_{\rm H}  &= n({\rm H\,I}) + n({\rm H\,II})
   + 2\left[n({\rm H_2}) + n({\rm H_2^+})\right] + 3\,n({\rm H_3^+})
   + n({\rm HeH^+}) + n({\rm OH}) + 2\,n({\rm H_2O}) , \\
n_{\rm He} &= n({\rm He\,I}) + n({\rm He\,II}) + n({\rm He\,III})
   + n({\rm HeH^+}) ,
\end{align*}
%
while \texttt{write\_heat\_breakdown\_eq}, the diagnostic that writes
\texttt{output/Heating\_breakdown.txt}, stopped at the molecular carriers: OH
and H$_2$O were absent from its $n_{\rm H}$. The dump is not short of the
information --- it fills its \texttt{nox} array from \texttt{f\_sp\_in} twenty
lines earlier, because it needs those densities for the FUV photolysis heating
channel --- it simply did not count their nuclei. So its $n_{\rm H}$ was too
small in exactly the cells the oxygen chemistry populates, which is the
molecular base.

Two quantities inside the dump read that $n_{\rm H}$, and neither of them is
part of the solved state:

\begin{itemize}
\item $x_{\rm ion} = n_e/(n_{\rm H} + n_{\rm He})$, which the photoelectron
  partition of every photoheating channel reads, so every \texttt{heat\_*}
  column of the dump carries it;
\item the hydrogen nucleus density handed to \texttt{fuv\_lw\_photon\_field},
  which is the density argument of the H$_2$ self-shielding table of
  section~\ref{sec:h2-shield-table}, so the \texttt{heat\_H2\_LW} column
  carries it as well.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{One definition, not one more copy}

The remedy is the standing rule that a quantity is defined in exactly one
place. \texttt{hydrogen\_helium\_nuclei\_density} is new in \texttt{utils}
(\texttt{src/modules/functions/utilities.f90}), beside \texttt{calc\_ne} and
\texttt{calc\_ntot}, and every carrier is counted with its nucleus
multiplicity: H$_2$ and H$_2^+$ two H, H$_3^+$ three, HeH$^+$ one H and one
He, OH one H, H$_2$O two, CO none. Its molecular and oxygen arguments are
optional, so a caller that does not track those carriers omits them rather
than writing a shorter sum of its own.

Four sites now call it and no site builds the totals itself:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\hline
site & carriers passed \\
\hline
\texttt{ionization\_equilibrium} & molecular, oxygen \\
\texttt{write\_heat\_breakdown\_eq} (\texttt{util\_ion\_eq.f90}) & molecular, oxygen \\
\texttt{post\_process\_adv}, before the advection sweep & none \\
\texttt{post\_process\_adv}, after it & none \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The two post-process sites pass neither, which is the composition
that pass already had and its module header already states: the advection
correction carries only the H/He columns, so the molecular and oxygen carriers
are not available to it. What they gain is the same statement order as the
other two.

\subsection*{Verification}

\textbf{Byte-identity, and where it deliberately stops.} The four sites now
evaluate the same statements in the same order, so the change is
arithmetically inert everywhere except the two places it is meant to move.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{\texttt{make check}: PASS, 9/9, all cases byte-identical.} No
  matrix case runs the oxygen chemistry, so no matrix case can reach the
  corrected term at all; what the matrix proves is that the refactor of the
  other three sites did not move anything.
\item \textbf{The oxygen case was run explicitly}, since the matrix does not
  cover it: \texttt{examples/18\_oxygen\_chemistry/} (HD~209458\,b, molecular
  and oxygen chemistry with a Lyman--Werner flux), $2000$ steps,
  single-threaded, the same source built with and without the patch.
  \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} and \texttt{Ion\_species.txt} are
  \textbf{byte-identical} and the marching trace agrees step for step, i.e.\
  the solved state does not see this.
\item \textbf{What did move, in that run}, all of it inside the diagnostic:
  $n_{\rm H}$ at the base ($r = 1.0002$) was low by $2.55\times10^{-4}$ and is
  corrected upward; $x_{\rm ion}$ there was high by $2.35\times10^{-4}$ and is
  corrected downward; the \texttt{heat\_HI}, \texttt{heat\_HeI},
  \texttt{heat\_HeII} and \texttt{heat\_H2} columns move by up to
  $9.4\times10^{-6}$ relative, downward; \texttt{heat\_H2\_LW} by up to
  $1.27\times10^{-5}$; \texttt{heat\_metals} by up to $1.9\times10^{-7}$; and
  \texttt{heat\_total} by up to $1.1\times10^{-9}$. The sign is the one the
  correction predicts: adding hydrogen nuclei lowers the ionized fraction, and
  a less ionized gas gives the photoelectron less of its energy as heat. The
  size is set by how much hydrogen the oxygen carriers hold at a solar oxygen
  abundance, which is $2.5\times10^{-4}$ of the nuclei even where H$_2$O
  peaks --- this is a diagnostic reading corrected by a fraction of a per mil,
  not a physics change waiting to be found.
\item \textbf{\texttt{Cooling\_breakdown.txt} and \texttt{Lyman\_Werner.txt}
  are byte-identical} in the same run; neither builds the nucleus totals.
\item \textbf{The \texttt{\_adv} files move at round-off}, by at most
  $1.8\times10^{-14}$ relative (\texttt{Ion\_species\_adv.txt}), because the
  post-process previously summed
  $n({\rm He\,I}\ {\rm singlet}) + n({\rm He\,II}) + n({\rm He\,III})$ and
  added the triplet last, and now adds the two He\,\textsc{i} populations
  first, as the other three sites do. The two orders are the same sum; nothing
  else about that pass changed.
\end{itemize}

% ===================================================================== %
% ===================================================================== %
\section{The ladder, converged: He/H from 0.0793 to 30 on one hot Uranus
(2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:heh-ladder}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Judgment first. Every rung of the He/H ladder has a Newton-converged
solution, the JFNK returns \texttt{info = 0} on all of them, and the ladder is
monotonic and undramatic: raising He/H from 0.0793 to 30 thins the molecular
layer, pulls the hydrogen ionization front inward, heats the wind and leaves
the mass-loss rate almost unchanged. There is no window and no crossing
anywhere on the ladder, which is what section~\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber}
predicted when it removed the two defects that had made the He/H${}\sim1$ case
look supersonic. The full account, with the convergence recipe and the run
ledger of each rung, is \texttt{docs/supersonic\_molecular\_base.md}
section~13; this section is its record here.}

The planet is the hot Uranus of the Tier-2 gate (0.0457\,$M_J$, 0.49\,$R_J$,
$T_{\rm eq} = 1140$\,K, 0.048\,au, power-law spectrum), metals off, no
\texttt{opacity.inp}, \texttt{Secondary\_ionization} at its STAGED default,
\texttt{He\_diffusion: True} except where noted. Each rung changes
\texttt{He/H number ratio} and the \texttt{base.inp} \texttt{HeH\_base} /
\texttt{q\_H2\_base} and nothing else, \texttt{q\_H2\_base} being set to hold
the H$_2$ nucleus fraction at $x_2 = 0.9251143$ on every rung so that the
ladder varies He/H alone. Every \texttt{q\_H2\_base} is below its element-ratio
ceiling $0.5/(0.5 + {\rm He/H})$, by 8 to 13\%.

\subsection{The rungs}

Seven \texttt{info = 0} states (the six rungs plus the second
He/H${}=0.0793$ rung that carries the case's \texttt{He\_diffusion}),
\texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=8}:

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrrr}
\hline
He/H & 0.0793 & 0.0793 (diff.) & 0.3 & 1 & 3 & 10 & 30 \\
\hline
$\log_{10}\dot M$ [g/s] & \textbf{10.42} & \textbf{10.49} & \textbf{10.35}
   & \textbf{10.32} & \textbf{10.36} & \textbf{10.42} & \textbf{10.39} \\
final JFNK residual & 9.89e-4 & 9.16e-4 & 7.97e-4 & 6.57e-4 & 6.02e-4
   & 9.21e-4 & 4.95e-4 \\
H$_2$ front $f_{\rm H_2}=0.5$ [$R_p$] & 1.1012 & 1.1200 & 1.0681 & 1.0469
   & 1.0467 & 1.0357 & 1.0250 \\
H$_3^+$ peak [$R_p$] & 1.0226 & 1.0200 & 1.0167 & 1.0014 & 1.0017 & 1.0015
   & 1.0027 \\
ioniz.\ front $x_{\rm HII}=0.5$ [$R_p$] & 2.573 & 2.755 & 2.040 & 1.593
   & 1.396$^*$ & 1.333$^*$ & 1.241$^*$ \\
$T$ maximum [K] & 2751 & 2698 & 3642 & 4967 & 5864 & 6328 & 6660 \\
boundary outflow speed [km/s] & 8.97 & 8.97 & 8.28 & 7.34 & 6.85 & 6.74
   & 6.61 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent$^*$ measured before the coupling repair of
section~\ref{sec:he-rec-thin}; the corrected values are in
section~\ref{sec:he-rec-thin}.

Read across, the structure is monotonic in everything: more helium means a
thinner molecular layer, a hotter wind, an ionization front closer to the
planet and a slower outflow, which is the sign helium's extra opacity and its
24.6\,eV photoelectrons predict.

\textbf{The rate is the exception: it is flat.} $\log_{10}\dot M$ spans 10.32
to 10.49 over a factor 378 in He/H, and it is not even monotonic --- it has a
shallow minimum at He/H${}=1$. The 0.17\,dex spread includes the 0.07\,dex the
\texttt{He\_diffusion} switch alone moves the 0.0793 rung, so the He/H
dependence of the rate over this range is at most a factor 1.5 and probably
less.

\textbf{What converges the rungs} is not the marching. Every rung reaches
$du = 2\times10^{-2}$ on its own and the staged secondary ionization fires
there, so the wind has to cross the switch a second time; the JFNK entered at
that second crossing fails (\texttt{info = 2}) on every rung that got there
inside 250,000 steps, and three rungs never got there. What converges all six
is a restart of the marched state with \texttt{Load IC? True},
\texttt{du\_th [PLM,WENO3]: 1.0e9 1.0e-3} and \texttt{Solver: Newton 100.0},
which arms the hand-off immediately and gives the solver the state instead of
making it march to the state. Five of six converge on the first such restart,
in under two minutes each, against hours of marching.

\subsection{Marching does not leave the converged solution}

The He/H${}=1$ state was restarted with the JFNK hand-off put out of reach
(\texttt{Solver: Newton 1.0e-30}) and marched \textbf{50,000 steps with no
steady solve at all}. \texttt{du} has one excursion --- from
$2.58\times10^{-4}$ up by a factor 20 at step 3968 and back --- and then holds
between $2.58$ and $2.63\times10^{-4}$ for the last 30,000 steps. \textbf{The
steady residual ends below where the JFNK left it}, $2.07\times10^{-4}$ against
$6.57\times10^{-4}$, $\log_{10}\dot M$ is 10.32 at step 50,000, and handing the
marched state back to the JFNK closes it immediately at \texttt{info = 0}. The
cells that move during the excursion are at $r = 2.12$--$2.19\,R_p$, not at the
base; below $1.1\,R_p$ nothing moves by more than 0.5\%.

This answers the two-solution question of item (P17) for this case: the marching
branch and the JFNK branch are not two steady solutions. It does not show that
no second solution exists elsewhere.

\subsection{The P23 gate does not pass}

Compared against Koskinen et al.\ (2022) Model~A --- whose mass, gravity at the
escape base, orbital distance, base temperature and XUV flux all match ours to
within a few percent --- and Frelikh \& Murray-Clay (2026), both read from the
publisher PDFs in \texttt{references/}:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{agreeing}: the rate (10.42 against their 10.28, a factor 1.4),
  the outflow speed (8.97 against 9.8\,km/s), and the wind being mostly
  neutral --- $n({\rm H\,I})$ exceeds $n({\rm H\,II})$ out to $2.57\,R_p$,
  which is the property both papers single out;
\item \textbf{disagreeing}: our H$_2$ is truncated (four decades between 1.10
  and $1.27\,R_p$) where theirs ``remains significant at all altitudes''; our
  H$_3^+$ is base-confined, nine decades over half a planetary radius, where
  theirs is present throughout; and we are colder, 2751\,K peak against their
  4400\,K at $3\,R_p$.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{The explanation P23 proposed for the disagreement is refuted by this
measurement.} P23 reasoned that the difference from an H-and-He-only model was
most likely the metal electrons our metals-on gates carry. This ladder is
metals-off and converged, and H$_3^+$ is still base-confined, so composition is
not the explanation. Nor is temperature, which is the mechanism Frelikh give
for their own result: our H$_2$ front sits at 765\,K against the 48,350\,K
barrier of the thermal-dissociation reaction both codes take from Baulch et
al.\ (1992), so \textbf{our H$_2$ is not being thermally dissociated; it is
being removed by something else, at a temperature where their argument says it
should survive.} Which channel that is --- H$_2$ photoionization at 15.4\,eV,
the H$_2^+ \to$ H$_3^+ \to$ dissociative-recombination route, or charge
exchange with H$^+$ --- is the next measurement, and it is not one this
campaign made. Lyman--Werner photodissociation is not a candidate: it is off in
these runs and Koskinen's Table~1 does not carry it either.

\subsection{Ledger}

None of the six converging runs admitted any base inflow --- the
\texttt{base boundary:} line, printed whenever a run has one, is absent from
all six logs --- and none activated the energy floor. Root acceptance is clean
for He/H${}\le10$: zero non-root acceptances, zero non-finite reaction
residuals, zero projected or handback roots. \textbf{He/H${}=30$ is not clean}:
34 non-root states accepted under the relaxation amnesty, $153+6+52$
projected/handback roots, and 165 cells with no in-simplex starting point.
Every printed non-root cell sits at $r = 2.12$--$2.22\,R_p$ at 5700--5820\,K
--- the ionized outer wind, which is where the defect of
section~\ref{sec:he-rec-thin} lived. The largest element-budget violation grows
along the ladder: none at 0.0793, 1.2e-3 at 0.3, 2.1e-1 at 1, 1.5e-1 at 3,
2.8 at 10, 1.1e1 at 30.

Item (P17) may be lifted for the six converged states, with the asterisked
front and $x_{\rm HII}$ entries taken from section~\ref{sec:he-rec-thin} and
the He/H${}=30$ row carrying its ledger.

% ===================================================================== %
% ===================================================================== %
\section{The He recombination photons are now only as absorbed as the cell is
thick (2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:he-rec-thin}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Judgment first. The expression was physically wrong, and the divergence
item (P40) reported is that wrongness showing itself rather than a numerical
accident. The on-the-spot assumption of section~\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber} ---
every He recombination photon above 13.6\,eV is absorbed inside the cell that
emitted it --- is a statement that the cell is optically thick to those
photons. It was never tested, and in the thin outer wind of a helium-rich run
it is false by 160 orders of magnitude: a cell holding no hydrogen and
$2.1\times10^{-151}$\,H$_2$ molecules per cm$^3$ has a cell optical depth of
$10^{-160}$ at 16--21\,eV and keeps none of its photons, while the code handed
all of them to the H$_2$ residue and returned a photoionization rate of
$2.6\times10^{100}$\,s$^{-1}$. The repair is not a floor on the absorber
density. It is the closure the assumption was standing in for: the cell keeps
the fraction $1 - e^{-\tau_c}$ of each channel's photons and the rest leave.}

Opened as items (P33) (the untested optical depth) and (P40) (the divergence it
produces); both are closed here. Item (P34), the trace metals missing from the
absorber competition, is untouched here and is closed in section
\ref{sec:he-rec-metal-competition}.

\subsection{The closure}

For each channel $c$, emitting at its representative energy $E_c$ into the
absorbers whose threshold lies below $E_c$,
%
\begin{align*}
\tau_c &= \Big(\sum_s n_s \sigma_s(E_c)\Big)\, \Delta r_j , &
f_{\rm abs} &= 1 - e^{-\tau_c} , &
w_s &= \frac{n_s \sigma_s(E_c)}{\sum_{s'} n_{s'} \sigma_{s'}(E_c)} ,
\end{align*}
%
and the rate per particle of absorber $s$, its heating, and the effective
He\,\textsc{ii} recombination coefficient become
%
\begin{align*}
{\rm d}P_s &= \frac{P_c\, f_{\rm abs}\, w_s}{n_s}
   \;=\; P_c\, \sigma_s(E_c)\, \Delta r_j\,
         \frac{1 - e^{-\tau_c}}{\tau_c} , \\
H_c &= P_c\, f_{\rm abs} \sum_s w_s \left(E_c - E_{{\rm th},s}\right) , \\
\alpha_{\rm eff} &= \alpha_B + \alpha_1 \left(1 - f_{\rm abs} w_{\rm HeI}\right)
   \qquad\left[\text{TR branch: } \alpha_1
   \left(1 - f_{\rm abs} w_{\rm HeI}\right) + 0.25\,\alpha_B\right] .
\end{align*}

\textbf{The second form of ${\rm d}P_s$ is the one that shows there is no
singularity anywhere.} The bracket is 1 at $\tau\to0$ and $1/\tau$ at
$\tau\to\infty$, so the rate runs from the optically thin limit
$P_c \sigma_s \Delta r_j$ --- what a single absorber in a transparent cell
sees, which is finite whether that absorber exists or not --- to the thick
limit $P_c \sigma_s / \sum n\sigma$, which is exactly the expression
section~\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber} wrote. \textbf{The thick limit is the old
expression, so the correction is a physical closure of it, not a replacement of
it.} The He recombination coefficient changes for the same reason the rates do:
a ground-capture photon that leaves the cell does not re-ionize helium either,
so only the He\,\textsc{i} share of the photons that \emph{stay} is excluded
from the net recombination.

\paragraph{Implementation.} \texttt{he\_rec\_coupling} in
\texttt{src/modules/radiation/util\_ion\_eq.f90} keeps
section~\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber}'s ratio form for the shares $w$ and
multiplies each channel by its own $f_{\rm abs}$; the five channels have five
different optical depths, because they have five different energies and (for
the $\ge24.6$\,eV ground-capture continuum alone) different absorber sets.
$f_{\rm abs}$ comes from a new module function
\texttt{absorbed\_photon\_fraction(tau)}, which uses the series
$\tau\left[1 - \tfrac{\tau}{2}\left(1 - \tfrac{\tau}{3}\right)\right]$ below
$\tau = 10^{-4}$, where $1 - e^{-\tau}$ loses all but a few digits to
cancellation, and returns zero for a non-positive $\tau$ (the ionization solve
can hand it a small negative trace density). The recombination coefficient is
written $\left(1 - f_{\rm abs}\right) + f_{\rm abs}\left(w_{\rm HI} +
w_{\rm H_2}\right)$ rather than $1 - f_{\rm abs} w_{\rm HeI}$ so that
$f_{\rm abs} = 1$ reproduces section~\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber} bit for bit.
$\Delta r_j$ is the cell width of the code's own grid, defined on the ghost
cells as well, and \texttt{sigma} returns $10^{-18}$\,cm$^2$, the unit the
stellar optical depth of \texttt{PH\_heat\_HHe} also carries.

\paragraph{Where the two forms actually differ.} $f_{\rm abs}$ is exactly 1.0
in double precision for $\tau > 37$, so wherever the cell is that thick the
returned numbers are unchanged to the last bit. Measured on the existing
goldens:

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\hline
case & $\tau$ at the base cell (gnd / casc)
     & $f_{\rm abs} < 1$ from & $f_{\rm abs}$ at the outer boundary \\
\hline
\texttt{wasp\_full}, \texttt{wasp\_he23off} (WASP-121\,b, atomic)
   & 16.5 / 20.2 & the base cell & 2.0e-3 / 2.4e-3 \\
\texttt{mol\_sec\_ion} (hot Uranus, molecular)
   & 174 / 240 & $r = 1.102$ / $1.116\,R_p$ & 7.0e-4 / 7.7e-4 \\
\texttt{mol\_base\_handoff}
   & 174 / 240 & $r = 1.106$ / $1.119\,R_p$ & 8.1e-4 / 8.9e-4 \\
\texttt{lower\_profile} (HD\,209458\,b, profile handoff)
   & 327 / 403 & $r = 1.037$ / $1.041\,R_p$ & 7.6e-7 / 1.1e-6 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{The molecular base is thick and is not touched; the atomic base is not
thick.} The hot Uranus keeps its photons out to 1.10--$1.12\,R_p$ and
HD\,209458\,b to $1.04\,R_p$, but WASP-121\,b's base cell has $\tau = 16.5$ in
the ground-capture channel, so no cell of the two atomic cases was ever
optically thick to these photons and the coupling there was overestimated
everywhere --- by a factor 2 at $1.15\,R_p$, 10 at $1.25\,R_p$ and 500 at
$1.5\,R_p$.
