%=============================================================================
\section{The Newton direction at the hand-off state points uphill, and the
solver had no direction that uses the gradient (2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Judgment first. The suspected cause was wrong and the real one is
simple. The WENO3 smoothness weights are not what makes the JFNK hand-off fail
on the He/H\,=\,0.3 case: the inner Newton model already freezes them, and
freezing them in the line search too changes the merit at the rejected step by
seven parts in ten thousand --- the step still ascends. What ascends is the
Newton/PTC direction itself, at every damping including the
$\Delta\tau\to0$ limit, because the scaled Jacobian is indefinite there
($s^{T}As<0$); and \texttt{solve\_steady\_jfnk} had only that one direction, so
backtracking shortened an uphill step twenty times, the pseudo-time floor made
the next iteration identical, and the solve counted to twelve and gave up. The
merit gradient is not zero there --- $\|A^{T}s\| = 12.6$ --- and the damped
Gauss--Newton (Levenberg--Marquardt) step built from the transpose of the
banded Jacobian, which is a descent direction for every damping by
construction, cuts the merit in half in one step. With that escape the hand-off
closes at \texttt{info = 0} where it used to abort. What it does NOT do is
reproduce the state the restart trick reaches, and
section~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open} says so with numbers: the two
\texttt{info = 0} states differ by 24\% in the $L_2$ norm of $(\rho,v,p)$ and
by 0.22\,dex in the rate, and the code's convergence measure rates the worse
one better. That is a defect of the measure, and it is left open, not papered
over.}

Opened as item (P41) of \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md}, which is closed here except
for the part promoted to a new item.

\subsection{The state, and how it is reached in ten seconds}

The hot Uranus of the Tier-2 gate at He/H\,=\,0.3 with
\texttt{He\_diffusion: True} and \texttt{Secondary\_ionization: Immediate},
restarted from its own archived output with \texttt{Load IC? True}. The failing
hand-off is reproduced with no marching at all by the direct steady route,
%
\begin{lstlisting}[language=bash]
EXHALE_PTC=1 EXHALE_PTC_JFNK=1 EXHALE_PTC_DTAU0=1.0 ./EXHALE.x
\end{lstlisting}
%
which lands on $\|R\| = 1.259\times10^{-2}$, merit
$\|F/D\|_2 = 5.140363464\times10^{-1}$, worst cell $j = 304$ at $r = 1.3412$ in
the mass row, and returns \texttt{info = 2} --- the in-run failure to every
printed digit. Every measurement below is made at that point, on the first
outer iteration.

\subsection{The direction report}

The merit is $f_2 = \|F/D\|_2$ over the whole domain, the quantity the line
search minimizes. \texttt{weno\_mode = 0} recomputes the smoothness weights at
the trial state (what the line search does); \texttt{weno\_mode = 2} reuses the
weights stored at $Y$ (what the Jacobian probes and the Krylov products do).
Entries are $(f_2^{\rm trial}-f_2)/f_2$, so \textbf{positive is uphill}.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{llrr}
\toprule
direction & step & weights recomputed & weights frozen at $Y$ \\
\midrule
Newton/PTC (GMRES, $\Delta\tau_0=1$) & $\lambda = 1$      & $\mathbf{+2.2249\times10^{-2}}$ & $\mathbf{+2.2242\times10^{-2}}$ \\
                                     & $\lambda = 0.5$    & $+9.1531\times10^{-3}$ & $+9.1528\times10^{-3}$ \\
                                     & $\lambda = 0.1$    & $+1.5086\times10^{-3}$ & $+1.5091\times10^{-3}$ \\
                                     & $\lambda = 10^{-2}$& $+1.4355\times10^{-4}$ & $+1.4361\times10^{-4}$ \\
                                     & $\lambda = 10^{-4}$& $+1.4275\times10^{-6}$ & $+1.4281\times10^{-6}$ \\
                                     & $\lambda = 10^{-6}$& $+1.4274\times10^{-8}$ & $+1.4280\times10^{-8}$ \\
\midrule
scaled steepest descent, Cauchy point & $\lambda = 1$      & $\mathbf{-3.1886\times10^{-5}}$ & $-2.6393\times10^{-5}$ \\
                                      & $\lambda = 0.5$    & $-2.0839\times10^{-5}$ & $-1.9783\times10^{-5}$ \\
                                      & $\lambda = 10^{-2}$& $-5.1275\times10^{-7}$ & $-5.2475\times10^{-7}$ \\
                                      & $\lambda = 10^{-6}$& $-5.1471\times10^{-11}$& $-5.2735\times10^{-11}$ \\
                                      & $\lambda = 10$     & $+1.4369\times10^{-3}$ & \\
                                      & $\lambda = 100$    & $+1.7001\times10^{-1}$ & \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Auxiliary numbers at the same point: $\|A^{T}s\| = 1.2563\times10^{1}$ (the
merit gradient in the scaled space, from the banded Jacobian), Cauchy step
length $t = \|g\|^2/\|Ag\|^2 = 8.8215\times10^{-8}$,
$|\delta Y_{\rm Newton}|/|Y| = 1.5322\times10^{-3}$,
$|\delta Y_{\rm Cauchy}|/|Y| = 4.1409\times10^{-8}$.

\textbf{Three things follow, and the first one kills the hypothesis this
section was opened to test.}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The WENO weights are not involved.} The two columns agree to four
significant figures at every $\lambda$. The suspicion was that the nonlinear
weights make $F$ non-smooth at the fixed point and that the finite-difference
directional derivatives cross the kink; they do not, and in any case the inner
model has frozen weights already (\texttt{weno\_mode = 1} stores them at $Y$,
the Jacobian colors and the Krylov products reuse them at
\texttt{weno\_mode = 2}; section~\ref{sec:steady-probe-hygiene} and
\texttt{newton\_scaling\_and\_base\_wall.md} section~10 record why the line
search deliberately does not). Freezing the line search too, the one part that
was still free, moves the rejected step by $7\times10^{-4}$ relative and leaves
it uphill.

\item \textbf{The Newton direction is uphill in the limit, not merely
overshooting.} The excess merit falls linearly with $\lambda$ over six decades
and never changes sign, so the directional derivative is strictly positive.
Backtracking cannot fix a direction; it can only make an uphill step short.

\item \textbf{A descent direction exists.} The scaled steepest-descent
direction $-A^{T}s$ descends, its measured directional derivative
($-2.65\times10^{-5}$ per unit $\lambda$, read at $\lambda = 10^{-6}$) matches
the value $-t\|g\|^2/\|s\|$ the banded Jacobian predicts to 2\%, and the Cauchy
point is close to the minimum along that ray ($\lambda = 10$ is already back
uphill). The gradient is therefore accurate and nonzero, and the solve simply
never built anything from it.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Why the Newton/PTC direction can point uphill at all}

The solve minimizes $m(x) = \tfrac12\|s\|^2$ with $s = F/D$ and $Y = Dx$; its
gradient is $A^{T}s$ with $A = D^{-1}JD$. The step it takes solves
$(I/\Delta\tau + A)\,\delta Z = -s$, which is an implicit Euler step of the
pseudo-transient continuation and is not a minimizer of $m$. In the
$\Delta\tau\to0$ limit that step is $\delta Z = -s$, whose directional
derivative is $-s^{T}As$; the heavily damped step at
$\Delta\tau_0 = 1.36\times10^{-4}$ (the CFL value) raises the merit, so
$s^{T}As<0$ at this state and even the shortest pseudo-time step climbs.
Tightening the GMRES tolerance from $10^{-1}$ to $10^{-4}$
(\texttt{gm} $1\to4$) gives a better-resolved solution of the same wrong
problem and still climbs, to $+1.771\times10^{-2}$. Nothing in the family
$(I/\Delta\tau + A)\,\delta Z = -s$, over any $\Delta\tau$, is guaranteed to
descend when $A$ is indefinite.

The damped Gauss--Newton (Levenberg--Marquardt) step is
%
\begin{equation*}
\big(A^{T}A + \mu\,\mathrm{diag}(A^{T}A)\big)\,\delta Z = -A^{T}s .
\end{equation*}
%
The matrix is symmetric positive definite for every $\mu>0$, so
$\nabla m^{T}\delta Z = -g^{T}(\cdot)^{-1}g < 0$ \textbf{for any damping} ---
descent is a property of the family, not of a lucky parameter.
$\mu\to\infty$ recovers the Cauchy direction and $\mu\to0$ the Gauss--Newton
step, so $\mu$ is the trust parameter, and choosing it is a one-dimensional
search along a curve rather than along a ray. Measured on this state (relative
merit change, weights recomputed):

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrrrr}
\toprule
$\mu$ & $10^{2}$ & $10^{1}$ & $10^{0}$ & $10^{-1}$ & $10^{-2}$ & $10^{-3}$ & $\mathbf{10^{-4}}$ & $10^{-6}$ \\
\midrule
$(f_2-f_2^0)/f_2^0$ & $-4.69$e$-5$ & $-3.64$e$-4$ & $-1.88$e$-3$ & $-1.15$e$-2$ & $-7.65$e$-2$ & $-3.21$e$-1$ & $\mathbf{-4.93\text{e}-1}$ & $+4.25$e$-2$ \\
$|\delta Y|/|Y|$    & $2.7$e$-8$ & $2.4$e$-7$ & $1.3$e$-6$ & $4.5$e$-6$ & $1.5$e$-5$ & $3.0$e$-5$ & $\mathbf{7.5\text{e}-4}$ & $4.7$e$-3$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

One step at $\mu = 10^{-4}$ takes the merit from 0.514 to 0.260. The curve
falls monotonically to that point and rises again below it, which is what a
trust parameter passing through its optimum looks like.

\subsection{What changed}

All of it in \texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_newton.f90} except the last
item.

\textbf{(a) The transpose the solver never had.}
\texttt{band\_matvec\_transpose} computes $J^{T}x$ from the band-stored
Jacobian, and \texttt{normal\_equations\_band} forms $J^{T}J$ (half-bandwidth
$2\,\texttt{kl\_jac} = 16$, LAPACK general-band layout, leading dimension
\texttt{ldab\_normal} $= 49$). Both act on the ALREADY SCALED band \texttt{ab}
that the outer iteration builds, so what they return is $A^{T}s$ and $A^{T}A$
in the scaled space with no further bookkeeping.
\texttt{levenberg\_marquardt\_step} adds $\mu\,\mathrm{diag}$ and solves by one
banded LU. The cost is one factorization of a 16-wide band per $\mu$, against
17 full residual evaluations for the Jacobian itself, so the escape is cheap
next to the iteration that calls it.

\textbf{(b) The escape.} \texttt{levenberg\_marquardt\_descent} sweeps $\mu$
down by decades from $10^{2}$, measures every candidate with the TRUE residual
(weights recomputed, exactly as the line search does), stops when the merit
turns back up, and returns the best step. It is called from
\texttt{solve\_steady\_jfnk} when the pseudo-time step is at its floor
($\Delta\tau \le \Delta\tau_0$) and either the backtracking search rejected
every step, or it accepted one that did not lower the true merit. The second
case is the non-monotone window: the test compares a trial against the WORST of
the last five iterates, so a sideways step passes it, and on this state 487 of
500 iterations were such acceptances before the escape covered them. The
$\Delta\tau \le \Delta\tau_0$ guard is what makes the escape a repair rather
than a change of algorithm: while the pseudo-time step is still above its
floor, reducing it does change the next iteration, and the PTC ramp is left
alone.

\textbf{(c) The bit-identical repetitions are gone.} When the line search fails
at $\Delta\tau = \Delta\tau_0$, \texttt{dtau = max(dtau*0.25d0, dtau0)} returns
$\Delta\tau_0$, so the preconditioner, the Krylov direction and the search
repeat exactly --- eleven times, before \texttt{n\_no\_descent\_max = 12}
fired. Now the escape is taken at the first such iteration, and if it too finds
nothing the solve stops there and prints $\|\nabla m\|$, which is the number
that says whether the point is stationary or the model is wrong. That path was
exercised during development, when a band-layout error made every
Levenberg--Marquardt solve fail: the solve aborted at iteration 1 reporting
$\|\nabla m\| = 1.256\times10^{1}$ instead of repeating eleven identical
iterations.

\textbf{(d) The hand-off is no longer given up for the rest of the run.}
\texttt{src/EXHALE\_main.f90}: a failed hand-off records the step, holds the
next attempt for \texttt{N\_stall} steps of further marching, and disables the
Newton finish only after \texttt{n\_newton\_attempt\_max = 3} attempts. The
failure is a property of the state the solver was handed, not of the run. No
input key is added.

\subsection{What was measured}

Everything single-threaded where byte-identity is claimed,
\texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=8} otherwise.

\textbf{Which source each item was run on.} The archived hand-off states of
items 1, 2, 5 and 6 are fixed points of the source that produced them, which is
this tree minus the two files section~\ref{sec:he-rec-thin} changed
(\texttt{util\_ion\_eq.f90}, \texttt{ionization\_equilibrium.f90}); loaded
into the current code they are no longer near-steady and the failure this
section repairs cannot be posed. Those four items were therefore run on that
snapshot plus this change, with the same before/after comparison on both sides.
Items 3 and 4, which are the byte-identity claims, were run on the current
tree, and \texttt{make check} on the tree passes 9 of 9 against the goldens
refreshed for section~\ref{sec:he-rec-thin}.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The control that reproduced the failure now converges.} The
He/H\,=\,0.3 case restarted single-stage (\texttt{Reconstruction scheme: WENO3},
no PLM step), marching to the hand-off at step 105: before, \texttt{info = 2}
at $\|R\| = 1.258\times10^{-2}$ after eleven bit-identical iterations at
$\lambda = 9.54\times10^{-7}$; after, \texttt{info = 0} at
$\|R\| = 5.614\times10^{-4}$ in 38 outer iterations, 36 of which took the
escape, in 16\,s.

\item \textbf{The two rungs whose hand-off never engaged converge, and the
escape is not what does it.} The He/H\,=\,3 and He/H\,=\,30 marched states
(250,000 steps, ended at $du = 3.9\times10^{-2}$ and $4.4\times10^{-2}$ with
the hand-off never fired), restarted single-stage: \texttt{info = 0} at
$\|R\| = 6.042\times10^{-4}$ and $3.157\times10^{-4}$, $\log_{10}\dot M$ 10.35
and 10.40 against the ladder's 10.36 and 10.39. Before and after are
byte-identical and the escape never fires --- those rungs were never blocked by
an ascending direction, only by a $du$ that stayed above the switch.

\item \textbf{The two atomic Newton cases are byte-identical.}
\texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} and \texttt{wasp\_he23off\_newton},
\texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=1}: \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} and
\texttt{Ion\_species.txt} identical to the same tree without this change,
\texttt{info = 0} at $\|R\| = 5.536\times10^{-4}$ and $6.341\times10^{-4}$,
$\log_{10}\dot M$ 13.21 and 13.22, escape count 0.

\item \textbf{The regression matrix of nine is byte-identical} to the goldens,
and the escape fires in none of them. \textbf{Note what that does and does not
guard:} \texttt{wasp\_full} and \texttt{wasp\_he23off} carry no
\texttt{Solver:} key --- they stop on $du < du_{\rm th}$ and never reach the
JFNK at all --- and the seven molecular cases are fixed-step relaxation
snapshots that do not reach it either. The Newton guards for this change are
the two \texttt{*\_newton} cases of item 3 and the restarts of items 2 and 5.

\item \textbf{The He/H\,=\,1 reference is unmoved}: $\log_{10}\dot M = 10.32$,
output byte-identical, escape count 0.

\item \textbf{The retry of (d) works, and it is what shows the escape has not
stalled.} The same control run with \texttt{Resid tol: 1.0e-8}, a target it
cannot meet, makes three hand-offs 2000 marching steps apart and reaches
$\|R\| = 2.324\times10^{-5}$, $1.271\times10^{-5}$ and $7.697\times10^{-6}$
before the finish is given up, against $1.258\times10^{-2}$ where the old code
aborted. So the escape does not merely move the iterate off the repeat: it goes
on reducing the residual by three further decades. What that does NOT buy is
the next subsection.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{What is NOT repaired: two \texttt{info = 0} states the convergence
measure cannot tell apart}
\label{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open}

The other half of item (P41) was that the restarts of the ladder converge only
because \texttt{in\_plm\_stage = (du\_th\_plm .gt. du\_th)} is evaluated
without reference to \texttt{do\_load\_IC}, so every two-stage restart takes
one PLM step before switching to WENO3, and that step is what unblocks the
solve. Making the restart honest --- letting a loaded state whose flux spread
is already below \texttt{du\_th\_plm} continue in WENO3 --- was implemented,
measured, and \textbf{held back}, because the measurement says the accident is
doing something the escape does not.

On the same case, from the same wind:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
 & one PLM step & no PLM step, & the same, driven \\
 & (restart as it is today) & escape only & to $\|R\| = 7.7\times10^{-6}$ \\
\midrule
final $\|R\|$ & $8.818\times10^{-4}$ & $5.614\times10^{-4}$ & $7.697\times10^{-6}$ \\
$\log_{10}\dot M$ & $\mathbf{10.34}$ & $\mathbf{10.56}$ & 10.46 \\
flux spread of $\rho v r^2$, $r>1.2\,R_p$ & $\mathbf{1.134\times10^{-2}}$ & $\mathbf{1.132\times10^{-1}}$ & $\mathbf{1.203\times10^{-1}}$ \\
flux spread, $r>2\,R_p$ & $3.540\times10^{-3}$ & $2.521\times10^{-3}$ & $2.470\times10^{-3}$ \\
$T$ maximum [K] & 3650 & 3398 & 3492 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The state handed to the solver has a flux spread of 1.129 over $r>1.2\,R_p$ and
$2.0\times10^{-2}$ over $r>2\,R_p$: the marching flattened the escaping wind
and left the region between 1.2 and 2\,$R_p$ an order of magnitude from steady.
The PLM-kicked solve flattens that region by a factor 100; the escape flattens
it by a factor 10 and stops, because it has reached the floor of the merit
basin it started in and $\|R\|$, which is measured over $[j_{\min}:N]$, i.e.\
$r>r_{\rm esc}$ only, is by then $5.6\times10^{-4}$ and the run is declared
converged. The two solutions differ by 24\% in the $L_2$ norm of $(\rho,v,p)$
(20\% for the third column), and the ladder's own value for this rung, 10.35,
is the PLM-kicked one.

\textbf{The third column is the decisive one.} Driving $\|R\|$ down by a
further factor 73, through three hand-offs, moves the inner flux spread not at
all --- it ends at $1.20\times10^{-1}$, no better than the $1.13\times10^{-1}$
the loose tolerance reached. $\|R\|$ and the state of the wind between 1.2 and
2\,$R_p$ are simply not measuring the same thing, and no amount of the former
fixes the latter.

\textbf{So the convergence measure is the next defect, not the restart rule.} A
descent method cannot leave a merit basin, and the PLM step is a perturbation
that leaves it; removing the perturbation before $\|R\|$ can see the region it
repairs would silently replace the ladder's rates with the rates of a state
that is not a steady wind between 1.2 and 2\,$R_p$. The restart rule is
therefore left as it is and the pair is recorded as a new open item.



\section{The convergence measure now covers the whole column: what the wind
does below the escape radius is part of $\|R\|$ (2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:whole-column-residual}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Judgment first. The measure was wrong, and it was wrong in the one way
that matters for a steady wind: it did not look at most of the wind. $\|R\|$
was a relative residual over $[j_{\min}:N]$ alone, i.e.\ over $r>r_{\rm esc}$,
so the column between the base and the escape radius --- for the hot Uranus of
the ladder, everything below $2\,R_p$, which is 391 of 500 cells and where the
molecular layer, the H$_2$ front and the transonic acceleration all live ---
was controlled by nothing. A steady state is steady in every physical cell or
it is not a steady state; measuring it in a fifth of them is not a tolerance
choice, it is the wrong quantity. $\|R\|$ is now the larger of two relative
residuals, one over the wind and one over the layer below the escape radius,
each taken on the scale that region's own physics sets. The two solves of
section~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open} that the old measure could not tell
apart are now separated by a factor 5.7 in $\|R\|$, in the right direction:
re-scored on the same converged states, the one with a flux spread of
$7.6\times10^{-2}$ above $1.2\,R_p$ goes from $4.93\times10^{-4}$ to
$4.00\times10^{-3}$, while the one with a spread of $3.0\times10^{-3}$ stays at
$6.97\times10^{-4}$. The nine-case matrix is byte-identical,
\texttt{run\_fcheck.sh} is clean, and both WASP-121b Newton cases still
converge --- one of them from a state whose layer the old measure had left at
12\% of $\rho g$ while reporting $\|R\| = 6.9\times10^{-4}$.}

This closes item (P42).

\subsection{Where the window came from: it was inherited, not chosen}

$j_{\min}$ is upstream ATES's: \texttt{define\_grid.f90} sets it to the first
cell with $r \ge r_{\rm esc}$, and \texttt{ATES/ATES-Code-main/ATES\_main.f90}
lines 286--298 use \texttt{mom(j\_min:N)} for the marching \texttt{du} and
\texttt{dtu} monitors, because $r_{\rm esc}$ is where ATES expects
$\rho v r^2$ to have become constant. The steady residual inherited that range
on the day it was written: \texttt{git show
10c248a:src/modules/time\_step/steady\_residual.f90} (2026-06-11, the commit
that introduced it) already carries the comment ``max relative residual rate
over the wind \texttt{[j\_min:N]}'', and \texttt{resid\_relnorm} in
\texttt{steady\_newton.f90} says in its own header that it uses ``the same
definition the marching monitor uses''. So the window is not a repair of
anything; it is the marching monitor's range, adopted without the question
being asked.

\textbf{It was asked once, on 2026-08-15, and answered on a scale that has
since been replaced.} Section~\ref{sec:below-escape-residual} measured the
layer's residual on $|u|$ for all three rows, found converged states reading
0.2 to 10 there, and concluded that widening the window on that norm would
report \texttt{info = 2} for every configuration that converges. That
conclusion was correct for that norm and is void for this one: section 62.3,
the same series, replaced the momentum row's $|\rho v|$ --- which collapses in
a layer moving at 10\,cm/s --- by the gravitational force density, and
re-measured the same converged states at $10^{-5}$ to $1.4\times10^{-4}$ of
$\rho g$. The obstacle was removed and the criterion was never revisited.

\textbf{What was NOT the reason: a base null mode.} The 2026-08-11 and
2026-08-13 experiments recorded in \texttt{solve\_steady\_jfnk} went the other
way --- they narrowed the line-search \emph{merit} to $[j_{\min}:N]$ and broke
two solves that converge with the whole-domain merit. The merit has covered
every physical cell $1..N$ since it was written; it was never windowed in
space, and nothing in it was a work-around for the base. The counter printed as
\texttt{window-only accepts} was about the Grippo non-monotone window in
\emph{time} --- acceptances that beat the worst merit of the last five iterates
without beating the current one --- and had nothing to do with a spatial range.
It is now printed as \texttt{non-monotone accepts}, so the name cannot be read
as the other thing.

\subsection{The change}

\textbf{(a) One definition of the row scale.}
\texttt{residual\_row\_scale(k, j, u)} in
\texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_residual.f90} is now the only place in
the code that says how a residual row is made dimensionless:
%
\begin{itemize}
\item mass and energy rows, everywhere: $|u(k,j)|$. Both are positive definite
      and collapse nowhere, so $|R|/|u|$ is that cell's fractional drift rate,
      in $1/t_s$.
\item momentum row at $r \ge r_{\rm esc}$: $|u(2,j)| = |\rho v|$, the momentum
      density the row transports.
\item momentum row at $r < r_{\rm esc}$:
      $|u(1,j)|\,|G\phi_i(j)-G\phi_i(j-1)|/dr_j(j)$, the gravitational force
      density discretized exactly as the momentum source term is
      (\texttt{Source.f90} line 33). The layer is quasi-hydrostatic, so this is
      the balance the row expresses there and the ratio is the fractional
      violation of hydrostatic balance.
\end{itemize}
%
This is the expression section 62.3 introduced for the below-escape print. It
is not a new scale; it moved from a print-only routine into the measure, and
\texttt{resid\_relnorm\_below\_escape} now reads it from the same place instead
of carrying its own copy.

\textbf{(b) One norm, evaluated on two regions.}
\texttt{relnorm\_over\_cells(Res, u, ja, jb, volume\_weighted, rc)} computes the
relative residual of each row over a cell range, volume-weighted
($V = r^2\,dr$, the default) or as a ratio of maxima. \texttt{residual\_norms},
\texttt{residual\_norms\_vol} (both in \texttt{steady\_residual.f90}) and
\texttt{resid\_relnorm} (the steady solver's convergence measure,
\texttt{steady\_newton.f90}) each call it twice --- once on $[j_{\min}:N]$,
once on $[1:j_{\min}-1]$ --- and return the componentwise \textbf{maximum} of
the two.

\textbf{Why the maximum and not a sum.} The two regions' rows are made
dimensionless by different physics, so their numbers are not addends of one
quantity. Each is already a dimensionless statement whose target is ``small'',
and the maximum says that every part of the column is steady on the scale its
own physics sets. A volume- or cell-count-weighted sum would not: on the ladder
grid the region above $2\,R_p$ carries most of $\sum r^2\,dr$, which is exactly
how a wind an order of magnitude from steady between 1.2 and $2\,R_p$ came to
be scored better than one that was not.

\textbf{One number to read with care.} The criterion is stated on the
volume-weighted form, which is the default (\texttt{resid\_vol}) and the one
the JFNK tests. The legacy L-inf form --- a ratio of maxima --- is selected by
its own key, \texttt{Resid norm: Linf} (\texttt{Resid norm: vol} is the
default); it is \emph{not} a fourth word of \texttt{Resid tol:}, whose parser
reads only the number and silently drops anything after it. Over the layer the
L-inf form inherits the $1/dr$ bias its own header already warns about: the
smallest cells sit at the base, so on the hot Uranus of the ladder a converged
state reads $1.3\times10^{-2}$ on it against $7.0\times10^{-4}$
volume-weighted. \textbf{How much that costs is planet-dependent}, because it
depends on whether the L-inf maximum falls in the layer or in the wind: on
WASP-121b the layer carries it and the two forms differ by about a factor 20
($4.66\times10^{-1}$ L-inf against $2.30\times10^{-2}$ volume-weighted on the
\texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} state), while on HD\,189733\,b the wind carries it
and the L-inf number is the \emph{smaller} of the two ($7.50\times10^{-3}$
against $2.63\times10^{-2}$ on the \texttt{jfnk\_hd189} state, both re-read in
PLM, the scheme that state was converged in). Neither ratio is a property of
the state; both are properties of the L-inf norm on that grid, and they are why
the volume-weighted form is the default.

\textbf{(c) Everything else is comments and one diagnostic.} The
\texttt{EXHALE\_NEWTON\_TEST=1} self-test compared $\max|F|/\max|u|$ over
$[j_{\min}:N]$ against the \texttt{EXHALE\_RESIDUAL=1} numbers by open-coding
the old formula; it now packs $F$ into the residual array and calls
\texttt{residual\_norms}, so the two sides of the self-test cannot drift apart
again. The stale comments in \texttt{solve\_steady\_jfnk} that explained the
merit/\texttt{rnorm} region mismatch are rewritten: the two now cover the same
cells and remain different functionals (a 2-norm of $F/D$ with $D$ the cell's
own signal scale, against a maximum of volume-weighted ratios on the physical
scales), which is still why the iterate with the smallest $\|R\|$ need not be
the last one.

\textbf{What is deliberately NOT changed.} The marching \texttt{du} is still
the flux spread of $\rho v r^2$ over $[j_{\min}:N]$. It is ATES's and CETIMB's
flux-based stop, its threshold is calibrated against that range, and every
golden case stops on it; moving it is a separate change with its own
rebaseline. The consequence is recorded here: a run that stops on \texttt{du}
alone still says nothing about the column below $r_{\rm esc}$, and only the
Newton finish does.

\subsection{The two states of section~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open},
re-scored}

Both states re-read with \texttt{EXHALE\_RESIDUAL=1} (volume-weighted, the
default), same binary for the row, so the only difference is the measure:

\begin{tabular}{lrrr}

state (He/H\,=\,0.3 case) & flux spread, $r>1.2\,R_p$ & old $\|R\|$ & new $\|R\|$ \\
\midrule
two-stage restart (one PLM step) & $3.02\times10^{-3}$ & $6.97\times10^{-4}$ & $6.97\times10^{-4}$ \\
single-stage restart (no PLM step) & $7.59\times10^{-2}$ & $\mathbf{4.93\times10^{-4}}$ & $\mathbf{4.00\times10^{-3}}$ \\

The old measure rated the second state the better of the two while its inner

\subsection{What the two paths do under the new measure}

The hand-off state of section~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open}, restarted the
two ways, on the current tree before and after this change
(\texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=8}). The \emph{before} column is not identical to
section~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open}'s, because that measurement was made
before section~\ref{sec:he-rec-thin} and the \texttt{q\_H2\_base}
ghost-composition change and the archived state is no longer the same fixed
point; the defect reproduces at 0.16\,dex instead of 0.22.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
\toprule
 & two-stage & two-stage & single-stage & single-stage \\
 & before & after & before & after \\
\midrule
\texttt{info} of the finish & 0 & \textbf{0} & 0 & \textbf{1, three attempts} \\
final $\|R\|$ & $4.540\times10^{-4}$ & $5.642\times10^{-4}$ & $4.927\times10^{-4}$ & $1.601\times10^{-3}$ (best) \\
$\log_{10}\dot M$ & 10.31 & \textbf{10.27} & 10.47 & 10.43 (marched stop) \\
flux spread, $r>1.2\,R_p$ & $3.02\times10^{-3}$ & $\mathbf{2.456\times10^{-3}}$ & $7.59\times10^{-2}$ & $5.115\times10^{-3}$ \\
flux spread, $r>2\,R_p$ & $2.76\times10^{-3}$ & $2.455\times10^{-3}$ & $2.53\times10^{-3}$ & $2.510\times10^{-3}$ \\
$T$ maximum [K] & 3641 & 3707 & 3439 & 3475 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{The measure now does its job, and it exposes a second thing that it is
not.} The two-stage path converges and its solution is flat over the whole
column --- the spread above $1.2\,R_p$ equals the spread above $2\,R_p$ to
three digits, which is what a steady wind looks like. The single-stage path no
longer converges: all three Newton attempts return \texttt{info = 1}
($2.076\times10^{-3}$, $1.677\times10^{-3}$, $1.601\times10^{-3}$ against a
target of $10^{-3}$), the run falls back to the \texttt{du} stop, and it
reports a marched state at 10.43. That is the honest outcome --- the state is
not steady and the code now says so instead of reporting \texttt{info = 0} on
it --- but it is not convergence, and the two paths still do not meet: they
differ by 33\% in the $L_2$ norm of $(\rho,v,p)$, against 22\% before.

\textbf{What blocks the single-stage solve is measured, and it is not the
base.} The term the merit is dominated by --- the largest $|F/D|$ over the
whole column, which \texttt{solve\_steady\_jfnk} prints on every outer
iteration --- is the \textbf{energy row} in 493 of the 500 iterations of the
third attempt, and it sits at $j = 198$ or 199, $r = 1.090$, in 485 of them;
the base cell $j=1$ holds it 7 times. Driving the same state directly with
\texttt{EXHALE\_PTC=1 EXHALE\_PTC\_JFNK=1} and 3000 iterations instead of 500
does not change the answer: $\|R\|$ falls $4.00\times10^{-3}$ (start)
$\to 2.27\times10^{-3}$ (201) $\to 1.89\times10^{-3}$ (601)
$\to 1.74\times10^{-3}$ (1001) $\to 1.62\times10^{-3}$ (1601), and ends at
\texttt{info = 1}, $1.437\times10^{-3}$, after 3000 iterations of which 2994
were non-monotone acceptances --- each damped Gauss--Newton step buying about
one part in ten thousand of the merit, and the
worst cell walks slowly down from $r = 1.134$ to $r = 1.066$ --- i.e.\ onto the
H$_2$ front of this case, which sits at $1.0681\,R_p$. It is a slow mode of the
energy equation at the molecular front, not a null mode of the base contact or
of the ghost temperature, and it is asymptotic rather than budget-limited: no
practical iteration count reaches $10^{-3}$ from there. Repairing it is solver
work in the line of item (P41), and the measure is not what stands in its way.

The restart rule of (P41)(c) --- letting a loaded state whose flux spread is
already below \texttt{du\_th\_plm} continue in WENO3 instead of silently taking
one PLM step --- is still not applied. The reason for holding it back has
changed: it is no longer that nothing would notice, because the measure now
does; it is that the path it would take is the one that does not converge.

\section{The molecular carriers are transported without the oxygen chemistry,
and H$_2$ is the only one that needs to be (2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:molecular-carrier-transport}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Judgment first. EXHALE solved H$_2$ in local chemical equilibrium, and
section 13.6 of \texttt{docs/supersonic\_molecular\_base.md} measured that
closure to be violated on its own solution: across the H$_2$ front of the
converged He/H\,=\,0.0793 hot Uranus the omitted advection term is 44 to 117
times the whole net chemical rate. The transport operator that closes that gap
existed, but ran only with the oxygen chemistry on, which the case does not
have. It now runs on the molecular network alone, with H$_2$ as its one
carrier. It is \emph{default off} for a molecular-only run: the transported
problem has a front that is still propagating when the steady solver is handed
it, so whether a steady transported solution exists on that planet is not yet
answered, and the default does not change until it is.}

Both comparison papers carry the term. Koskinen et al.\ (2022) Appendix~B
equation~(B1) is a continuity equation for each species, with an advection and
a diffusion velocity, and they attribute their H$_2$-at-all-altitudes to it:
``outflow brings fresh H$_2$ up from deeper layers of the atmosphere and
primarily balances the total loss rate''. Frelikh \& Murray-Clay (2026) plot
``advection of H$_2$'' as a term of their Figure~7. Neither balances H$_2$
chemically; we did, because that was all the closure could do.

\subsection{H$_2$ is the only carrier that needs transporting, and that is
measured}

The transported set is a property of the run, so ``which species'' has to be
answered with numbers. Evaluated on the converged He/H\,=\,0.0793 state,
against the flow time $r/|v|$:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}
\toprule
$r$ [$R_p$] & $\tau$(H$_2^+$) & $\tau$(H$_3^+$) & $\tau$(HeH$^+$) & $r/v$ &
$\tau$(H$_3^+$)$/(r/v)$ & $3n$(H$_3^+$)$/n_{\rm H}$ \\
\midrule
1.02 & $2.1\times10^{-5}$ & $9.1\times10^{1}$  & $2.7\times10^{-5}$ & $7.5\times10^{8}$ & $1.2\times10^{-7}$ & $1.9\times10^{-8}$ \\
1.10 & $9.1\times10^{-4}$ & $7.9\times10^{-1}$ & $9.1\times10^{-4}$ & $1.2\times10^{8}$ & $6.9\times10^{-9}$ & $2.5\times10^{-9}$ \\
1.15 & $6.1\times10^{-3}$ & $2.8\times10^{-1}$ & $4.4\times10^{-3}$ & $1.1\times10^{7}$ & $2.7\times10^{-8}$ & $1.7\times10^{-10}$ \\
1.25 & $1.3\times10^{-1}$ & $4.8\times10^{-1}$ & $1.2\times10^{-1}$ & $4.0\times10^{5}$ & $1.2\times10^{-6}$ & $5.1\times10^{-12}$ \\
2.00 & $1.1\times10^{0}$  & $1.3\times10^{0}$  & $4.8\times10^{0}$  & $2.5\times10^{4}$ & $5.1\times10^{-5}$ & $3.7\times10^{-13}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The three molecular ions are local by four to seven decades everywhere in the
domain and hold at most $2\times10^{-8}$ of the H nuclei. H$_2$'s own ratio,
from the section 13.6 table, is 0.02 to 1.3 over the same radii. So the carrier
is H$_2$ and the molecular ions stay local --- the same statement the module
header already made for HD~209458\,b, now measured on the planet the gate is
about. \texttt{n\_carrier} is therefore a run-time count (1, or 4 with the
oxygen cycle) set once by \texttt{carrier\_set\_init}, with
\texttt{n\_carrier\_max} dimensioning the arrays; the oxygen path is unchanged
and byte-identical.

\subsection{The key was named for the wrong thing}

\texttt{Oxygen transport} switched an operator whose first carrier is H$_2$ and
which runs with or without the oxygen cycle. It is renamed
\texttt{Molecular carrier transport: True|False}, and the old key is
\emph{refused at startup with a message}, not silently aliased: a stored input
file that says \texttt{Oxygen transport} describes a switch that no longer
exists, and reading it as if it did would hide that. No \texttt{input.inp} in
the repository carried the key and no regression case sets it, so nothing
stored breaks.

The default is not a constant. Left unstated it is \texttt{thereis\_oxychem}:
the oxygen cycle exists to compute a base partition a local steady state cannot
produce, so it turns the transport on, exactly as before; a molecular run
without it keeps the closure it has always had.

\subsection{The base face of an inflowing carrier}

Design decision D6 gave the carrier partition a zero-flux base, on the argument
that the split of an element among its carriers is what the oxygen option
exists to compute and imposing it would make that option's own gate circular.
That argument holds exactly when nothing upstream states the partition. When a
handoff does --- \texttt{base.inp}'s \texttt{q\_H2\_base}, or a profile at the
matching level --- the partition is incoming data, and section 117 already pins
it on the ghosts of the ionization sweep; leaving the base cell free while the
ghost below it is pinned puts the defect section 117 removed one cell higher
up.

So where the handoff speaks and the base face is an \emph{inflow}, the
advective term at that face carries the ghost's composition. Only the advective
term: face 0 still carries no diffusive flux, because the handoff supplies the
composition of the gas that flows in, not a mixing rate across a boundary whose
gradient is set by the ghost spacing and by a $K_{zz}$ that describes an
unresolved region. The two branches cannot both apply --- decision D7 refuses
\texttt{q\_H2\_base} while the oxygen chemistry is on.

Measured on \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff} (HD~209458\,b, 12000-step snapshot,
$v=+97.7$\,cm\,s$^{-1}$ at the base, \texttt{q\_H2\_base}\,=\,0.75):

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
\toprule
 & $x_2$ ghost & $x_2$ base cell 1 & jump & $f({\rm H_2})=0.5$ at & $\log_{10}\dot M$ \\
\midrule
transport off            & 0.925114 & 0.999674 & 0.0746 & 1.15467 & 10.56 \\
on, D6 zero flux         & 0.925114 & 0.999052 & 0.0739 & 1.15862 & 10.55 \\
\textbf{on, handoff Dirichlet} & 0.925114 & \textbf{0.939813} & \textbf{0.0147} & 1.15813 & 10.57 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{It closes 80\% of the jump and it does not pin the cell, and it
cannot.} This is a condition on the \emph{face}, not on the cell: the remaining
0.0147 is the cell's own chemistry rebuilding H$_2$ faster than the inflow
sweeps it out. Pinning cell 1 itself would take a physical cell out of the
solution. Both numbers are reported by every run, so the size of the remaining
jump is visible rather than assumed.

\textbf{Whether the base face is an inflow is decided by the mass flux the wind
carries, not by the base cell's velocity, and that distinction was forced by a
measurement.} On the converged hot Uranus the base cell's $v$ is
$-250$\,cm\,s$^{-1}$ and its cell-centred $\rho v r^2$ is 196 times the wind's
flux inward --- while the face flux the scheme actually transports there,
reconstructed by integrating its own steady mass residual down from the smooth
wind, is $+0.36$ to $+0.98$ times the wind flux, \emph{outward}, in every
converged configuration measured (\texttt{docs/p44\_base\_sawtooth.md}). The
cell-centred velocity at that base is a collocated odd-even mode, not infall:
$\rho$, $p$ and $T$ are monotone through the same cells, the layer carries 288
cells per scale height, and no dissipative remedy tried --- Shapiro filter,
Low-Mach damping, \texttt{Base velocity: massflux}, a continuous ghost
temperature --- changes $v(1)$ by more than 3\,cm\,s$^{-1}$. A condition gated
on $\mathrm{sign}(n_{\rm tot}v(1))$ reads the mode; one gated on the wind's
flux reads the state. The ghost velocity is not usable either: the
$+0.94$\,cm\,s$^{-1}$ it carries in the converged state is exactly the softplus
floor of the smooth valve.

So \texttt{carrier\_base\_state} computes $\sum \rho v r^2$ over
$[j_{\min}:N]$ --- the same constant and the same average
\texttt{Base velocity: massflux} uses for the ghost velocity, seeded in
\texttt{init.f90} and updated each step in \texttt{EXHALE\_main.f90} --- and its
sign decides both the composition condition and the advective direction of cell
1. In a steady spherical wind that flux is one number at every face, so using it
at the base face states the steady state rather than approximating it. The
interior keeps the cell-velocity upwind, for the reason its own header gives
(the element operator's frozen helium hole); only cell 1 is decided on the face,
and only because the measurement says the cell velocity there is not a flux.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
\toprule
20000 marching steps, hot Uranus & $x_2$ ghost & $x_2$ cell 1 & jump & $f=0.5$ & $10^{-4}$ \\
\midrule
transport off                        & 0.925114 & 0.998668 & 0.0736 & 1.1008 & 1.2698 \\
on, condition on $\mathrm{sign}(n_{\rm tot}v(1))$ & 0.925114 & 0.998518 & 0.0734 & 1.1016 & 1.3072 \\
\textbf{on, condition on the wind flux} & 0.925114 & \textbf{0.957446} & \textbf{0.0323} & 1.1017 & 1.3073 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The condition now fires on this planet, where the cell-centred test left it
permanently off, and it closes 56\% of the composition jump. It does not move
the front ($1.1016 \to 1.1017$), which is the right outcome: this is a boundary
condition on the partition, not on the wind. On \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff},
where the cell-centred velocity happens to agree in sign, the case is nearly
unchanged and slightly better --- the jump goes from 0.0147 to 0.0090 --- because
the cell-centred test also flipped transiently during the run and the flux test
does not.

\textbf{On the oxygen option it is not a no-op, and that is the point.} With
the transport on and no handoff, cell 1's advective term used to be taken from
cell 2 whenever $n_{\rm tot}v(1) < 0$, and on
\texttt{examples/18\_oxygen\_chemistry} that quantity is $1.5\times10^{6}$ times
the wind flux inward --- the same mode, worse. With the direction taken from the
face, the base cell's H$_2$ partition moves from 0.2593 to 0.3411 of the H
nuclei ($+32\%$), base H$_2$O by $+120\%$, and $\log_{10}\dot M$ by $+0.02$ dex
over a 2000-step snapshot. The base partition is what A2 exists to compute, so
the correction lands on its own subject. Both states are 2000-step snapshots
from a cold start, so this is a direction and an order of magnitude, not a
result.

The base cell's own velocity, and what it is, are \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md}
item~(V).

\subsection{A defect the transported problem found: two definitions of the same
budget}

\texttt{carrier\_source} closed atomic H by sharing the element with the frozen
ion stages,
\[
  n_{\rm HI} = n_{\rm H,free} - n_{\rm HII} - 2n_{\rm H_2^+} - 3n_{\rm H_3^+}
             - (\text{what the carriers hold}),
\]
while \texttt{limit\_to\_element\_budget} let the carriers take the whole of
$n_{\rm H,free}$. The two disagreed by exactly the H sitting in the frozen
ions, and that gap is what the transported hot Uranus walked into: 80 of 500
cells between 1.032 and 1.156\,$R_p$ reached $2n({\rm H_2})/n_{\rm H}=1$, the
write-back's remainder for H\,I, H\,II, H$_2^+$ and H$_3^+$ went to zero, $n_e$
collapsed to 3.7\,cm$^{-3}$, and the next ionization sweep stopped with
``persistent non-root chemical equilibrium'' at $r=1.112$.

The two sites now call one function,
\texttt{hydrogen\_available\_to\_carriers}. The comment that permitted the
looser bound has been corrected where it stood: ``the next sweep re-solves the
stages'' is true of the sweep and false of the step in between, because this
step's write-back does not re-solve H\,I, H\,II, H$_2^+$ and H$_3^+$ --- it
rescales them in proportion to what they already held.

\textbf{Measured effect on the oxygen option: none, and the reason is measured
too.} On \texttt{examples/18\_oxygen\_chemistry} (2000 steps) all twelve output
files are byte-identical, because the carriers there reach only 0.358 of the
hydrogen available to them and no cell has $n({\rm H_3^+})=0$. The fix bites
only where the transported H$_2$ approaches the whole hydrogen budget, which on
that planet it does not. On the hot Uranus it removes the electron collapse
($n_e$ $3.7 \to 1.8\times10^{4}$\,cm$^{-3}$) and cuts the saturated cells from
80 to 54.

\subsection{A scale for the carrier row, beside the others}

The steady solver never sees the carrier equation: it holds the partition fixed
and solves the wind, and an outer Picard iteration relaxes the carriers at that
wind. Their common fixed point is a steady state of both, but only the
hydrodynamic half of it is in $\|R\|$. \texttt{carrier\_steady\_residual}
reports the other half --- the same residual the transport step assembles, with
the time term switched off --- made dimensionless by
\texttt{carrier\_row\_scale}, which lives beside \texttt{residual\_row\_scale}
in \texttt{steady\_residual.f90} so that every row scale in the code has one
definition site.

The scale is $n_{\rm H}(|v|+c_s)/\Delta r$, the flux divergence a cell would
carry if its whole hydrogen inventory moved at its own fastest signal speed.
The unknown $n({\rm H_2})$ cannot be its own scale for the same reason
$|\rho v|$ cannot be the momentum row's in the quasi-hydrostatic layer: it
falls four decades across the front, and $|R|/n({\rm H_2})$ would then be large
wherever the carrier is scarce whether or not the state is right.

\subsection{What the steady route does with it, and why the default is off}

On the converged He/H\,=\,0.0793 state with the transport on, the outer loop
does not converge, and the measurements say why.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The wind solve is not the blocker.} The first JFNK converges,
      \texttt{info\,=\,0}, $\|R\| = 8.7\times10^{-4}$ --- the same grade as
      with the transport off.
\item \textbf{The relaxation then moves the composition by order unity, at the
      front.} Outer drift 0.536, worst at cell 247, $r=1.168$; carrier steady
      residual $1.06\times10^{-2}$ at $r=1.129$. That is not a numerical
      artefact: it is the size of the correction the closure was missing.
\item \textbf{Bounding the pass does not bound the move.} Capping how far one
      pass may advance the carriers at 1.0 and at 0.1 of a cell flow time gave
      drifts of 0.536 and 0.533. At the front, one tenth of a flow time is
      about sixty cell crossings; the front is advected, and advection is not
      slow on any scale such a bound can be written in. The bound was therefore
      \emph{not} kept --- a bound that controls nothing reads as a control to
      the next person.
\item \textbf{The front propagates outward at the gas speed, pass after pass.}

      \begin{center}\small
      \begin{tabular}{lrrrrrr}
      \toprule
      outer pass & $f=0.5$ & $10^{-2}$ & $10^{-4}$ & $n({\rm H_3^+})>1$ to &
      cells with $n({\rm H_3^+})=0$ & $x_2$ at $1.5\,R_p$ \\
      \midrule
      1 & 1.1664 & 1.2257 & 1.2921 & 1.2211 & 52 & $2.44\times10^{-5}$ \\
      2 & 1.2482 & 1.3122 & 1.4051 & 1.3053 & 33 & $1.89\times10^{-5}$ \\
      \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}
      \end{center}

      0.082\,$R_p$ per pass of 0.1 flow times is about
      2050\,cm\,s$^{-1}$ against a gas speed of 3000\,cm\,s$^{-1}$ there. The
      far wind (1.5, 2.0\,$R_p$) does not move, and the saturated cell count
      \emph{falls} as the front leaves them. This is a front filling a region,
      not a runaway.
\item \textbf{A real feedback reinforces it, and the frozen background is the
      conservative side of it.} Within one relaxation pass He$^+$, $n_e$, $T$
      and the photoionization rates are frozen ---
      \texttt{relax\_photochemical\_composition} never calls \texttt{ioniz\_eq}
      and \texttt{carrier\_write\_back} never writes a helium index --- so the
      pass advances the front using the \emph{old}, larger He$^+$. Between
      passes the sweep re-solves it, and where H$_2$ has arrived it collapses:

      \begin{center}\small
      \begin{tabular}{lrrr}
      \toprule
      $r$ [$R_p$] & $n$(He\,II) entry & after pass 1 & after pass 2 \\
      \midrule
      1.100 & $1.23\times10^{3}$ & $9.56\times10^{4}$ & $1.05\times10^{4}$ \\
      1.150 & $1.77\times10^{6}$ & $2.25\times10^{6}$ & $\mathbf{1.85\times10^{4}}$ \\
      1.200 & $1.07\times10^{7}$ & $8.35\times10^{6}$ & $\mathbf{1.99\times10^{5}}$ \\
      1.250 & $1.32\times10^{7}$ & $1.11\times10^{7}$ & $2.85\times10^{6}$ \\
      \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}
      \end{center}

      A factor 50 to 100 at 1.15--1.20\,$R_p$, where section 13.6 measured
      He$^+$\,+\,H$_2$ to be 95\% of the whole net H$_2$ loss. So the sink that
      would stop the front is removed by the front itself. Whether that makes
      two steady states or one slow approach is \emph{not} settled here: the
      front had not stopped after two passes.
\item \textbf{The blocking mode is the front's energy row, and it moves with
      the front.} Over all JFNK iterations after the first relaxation the worst
      row is the energy row in 674 to 765 of about 1030, at
      $r=1.113$--$1.137$ when the front is at 1.15--1.28 and at
      $r=1.162$--$1.195$ when the front is at 1.17--1.25. With the transport
      off that mode is not the worst cell at all --- the base is, row $k=2$,
      $r=1.000$ --- and the solve converges. This is the slow mode of
      section~\ref{sec:whole-column-residual}, enlarged by the transport and no
      longer at a fixed radius.
\item \textbf{Marching does not fail.} 20000 marching steps with the transport
      on, from the same state, run clean (no \texttt{ERROR STOP}) and move the
      front outward monotonically: $f({\rm H_2})=10^{-4}$ from 1.2698 to
      1.3072\,$R_p$, $n({\rm H_3^+})>1$ from 1.1810 to 1.1976\,$R_p$,
      $\log_{10}\dot M = 10.40$ either way. What fails is asking a
      steady-state routine to follow a propagating front.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Hence the default.} \texttt{Molecular carrier transport} stays off for
a molecular-only run until a marching run long enough to stop the front says
where it stops, and a steady solve started from that state returns
\texttt{info\,=\,0}. Nothing above is a converged solution and nothing above is
quoted as a rate.

\subsection{What was checked}

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{make check}, nine cases, \texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=1}:
      \textbf{9/9 byte-identical}. The transport is off in all of them, which
      is what the default says.
\item \texttt{examples/18\_oxygen\_chemistry}, 2000 steps, the transport
      \emph{on}: byte-identical against the pre-change binary through the
      headroom change, and then deliberately \emph{moved} by the base-face
      condition, by $+32\%$ in the base H$_2$ partition and $+0.02$ dex in the
      rate. The two were measured separately so that each is attributable.
\item \texttt{backup/regression/run\_fcheck.sh}:
      \texttt{-fcheck=bounds,do,mem} rebuild and the bounded HD~209458\,b case.
\item The six molecular regression cases were additionally run pairwise against
      the pre-change binary outside the harness, at four separate stages of this
      change (carrier count, gates and key, base condition, headroom):
      identical every time.
\item NOT checked: \texttt{mol\_diffusion} with the transport \emph{on}, i.e.\
      the helium element operator and the carrier operator in the same split
      step. They are ordered \texttt{element\_diffusion\_step} then
      \texttt{photochemical\_transport\_step}, and the second reads
      \texttt{ntot}, \texttt{T\_K} and the rate coefficients from the
      \texttt{bg\_cell} the sweep \emph{before} the diffusion left, so it lags
      by one operation on the marching path (not on the Picard path, where
      \texttt{ioniz\_eq} runs between them). Nothing measures the size of that
      lag yet.
\end{itemize}

\section{The trace metals now compete for the He recombination photons, and
nitrogen at depth notices (2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:he-rec-metal-competition}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Judgment first. The expression was physically incomplete, and the size
of what it left out was never measured. A He recombination photon of energy
$E_c$ is absorbed by every species whose ionization threshold lies below
$E_c$, in proportion to $n_s\sigma_s(E_c)$. Sections
\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber} and \ref{sec:he-rec-thin} wrote that
competition with H\,\textsc{i}, H$_2$ and (above 24.6\,eV) He\,\textsc{i} in
it, and gave the metals' share to hydrogen. The metals are $10^{-4}$ to
$10^{-3}$ of the gas by number, but their cross sections in the 16--25\,eV
band are \emph{larger} than hydrogen's --- 11.9 (O\,\textsc{i}), 12.2
(N\,\textsc{i}) and 4.9 (C\,\textsc{ii}) against 1.24 for H\,\textsc{i} at
24.6\,eV --- and in the ionized wind the H\,\textsc{i} that used to take those
photons is itself a trace. Measured before the change: the metal share of the
absorption coefficient runs from $3\times10^{-3}$ at the base to
$2.8\times10^{-2}$ at 2.8\,$R_p$. That is a share of the photons, and it was
going to hydrogen.} Item (P34), opened with section
\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber}, is closed here.

\subsection{The size, measured first}

For each channel $c$ the metal share of the absorption coefficient is
\[
  \frac{\sum_m n_m\sigma_m(E_c)}
       {n_{\rm HI}\sigma_{\rm HI}+n_{\rm H_2}\sigma_{\rm H_2}
        +n_{\rm HeI}\sigma_{\rm HeI}},
\]
evaluated on the pre-change solutions with the same \texttt{sigma\_*}
functions the code uses. The five channels are the ground-capture continuum
(24.6\,eV), the 584\,\AA\ resonance (21.2), the 2$^3$S line (19.8), the
2$^1$S two-photon continuum (16.110) and the case-B cascade average (19.741).

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrl}
\toprule
case and radius & 24.6 & 21.2 & 19.8 & 16.11 & 19.74 & who \\
\midrule
\texttt{wasp\_full\_newton}, 1.00\,$R_p$    & $4.4\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $3.6\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $2.8\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $1.1\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $2.8\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & O\,\textsc{i}, 84\% \\
\texttt{wasp\_full\_newton}, 1.61\,$R_p$    & $\mathbf{2.2\!\times\!10^{-2}}$ & $2.3\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $1.7\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $6.9\!\times\!10^{-4}$ & $1.7\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & C\,\textsc{ii}, 89\% \\
\texttt{wasp\_he23off\_newton}, 1.61\,$R_p$ & $\mathbf{2.2\!\times\!10^{-2}}$ & $2.3\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $1.7\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $6.9\!\times\!10^{-4}$ & $1.7\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & C\,\textsc{ii}, 89\% \\
\texttt{mol\_metals}, 1.00\,$R_p$           & $3.2\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $2.9\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $2.4\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $3.2\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $2.4\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & O\,\textsc{i}; C\,\textsc{i} at 16.11 \\
\texttt{mol\_metals}, 4.81\,$R_p$           & $6.0\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $4.4\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $3.5\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $1.4\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $3.4\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & O\,\textsc{i}, 54\% \\
\texttt{lower\_profile}, 1.00\,$R_p$        & $4.7\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $4.8\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $4.0\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $2.0\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & $3.9\!\times\!10^{-3}$ & O\,\textsc{i} \\
\texttt{lower\_profile}, 2.82\,$R_p$        & $\mathbf{2.8\!\times\!10^{-2}}$ & $5.8\!\times\!10^{-4}$ & $4.7\!\times\!10^{-4}$ & $2.1\!\times\!10^{-4}$ & $4.6\!\times\!10^{-4}$ & C\,\textsc{ii}, 98\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{It is above $10^{-3}$ everywhere, in every channel, in every metals-on
case.} The threshold the measurement was to be judged against was $10^{-3}$,
so the metals belong in the competition and were implemented.

Two features of the table are worth reading. The ground-capture channel is the
one that grows outward, because it is the only channel whose H\,\textsc{i}
competitor thins out while a metal ion that can still absorb at 24.6\,eV ---
C\,\textsc{ii}, threshold 24.38\,eV --- does not. And the two-photon channel
at 16.110\,eV is the one the molecular cases pick out, because C\,\textsc{i}
(threshold 11.26\,eV, $\sigma=13.4$ there against H\,\textsc{i}'s 4.0) is
neutral in a molecular layer.

\subsection{The change}

\texttt{he\_rec\_coupling} (\texttt{src/modules/radiation/util\_ion\_eq.f90})
now runs the competition over H\,\textsc{i}, H$_2$, He\,\textsc{i}
\emph{and} every photo-ionizable metal ion of \texttt{species\_table} whose
\texttt{mion\_ethr} lies below the channel energy:
\begin{align*}
  \tau_c &= \Big(n_{\rm HI}\sigma_{\rm HI}+n_{\rm H_2}\sigma_{\rm H_2}
            \;[+\,n_{\rm HeI}\sigma_{\rm HeI}]
            +\textstyle\sum_m n_m\sigma_m\Big)\,\Delta r_j, \\
  w_s    &= n_s\sigma_s(E_c)\big/\textstyle\sum_{s'}n_{s'}\sigma_{s'}(E_c), \\
  \delta P_m &= P_c\,f_{\rm abs}\,w_m/n_m
              = P_c\,\sigma_m(E_c)\,\Delta r_j\,[1-e^{-\tau_c}]/\tau_c, \\
  H_c    &= P_c\,f_{\rm abs}\textstyle\sum_s w_s\,(E_c-E_{{\rm th},s}),
            \qquad E_{{\rm th},m}=\texttt{mion\_ethr}(m), \\
  \alpha_{\rm eff} &= \alpha_B+\alpha_1\big[(1-f_{\rm abs})
            +f_{\rm abs}(w_{\rm HI}+w_{\rm H_2}+\textstyle\sum_m w_m)\big].
\end{align*}

The metals enter in four places and each one is the same statement: they take
a share of the photons. They add opacity to the cell optical depth, so the
cell keeps more of them; they take a share out of the H\,\textsc{i} and H$_2$
shares; the share they take ionizes them, and is returned in a new output
\texttt{dP\_m} that the callers add to the metal photoionization rate
\texttt{P\_m}; and the share they take is not available to re-ionize helium,
so it enters the effective He\,\textsc{ii} recombination coefficient with the
other absorbed shares.

\textbf{The shares stay in the ratio form of section
\ref{sec:he-rec-absorber}}, $w_{\rm HI}=1/(1+R_{\rm He}n_{\rm HeI}/n_{\rm HI}
+R_{\rm H_2}n_{\rm H_2}/n_{\rm HI}+\sum_m R_m n_m/n_{\rm HI})$ with
$R_m=\sigma_m(E_c)/\sigma_{\rm HI}(E_c)$ evaluated once at entry, and the
metal rate is $P_c f_{\rm abs} w_{\rm HI} R_m/n_{\rm HI}$ so that the metal
density of the share cancels rather than appearing in a denominator --- the
same property that makes \texttt{dP\_H2} finite as $n_{\rm H_2}\to0$. A run
with no metals adds \emph{exactly} $0.0$ to every one of those sums, which is
why it is bitwise unchanged; and \texttt{metal\_photoion\_sigma} returns zero
below an ion's own threshold, so an ion that cannot absorb a channel drops out
of it with no test.

The ions that participate are the 17 photo-ionizable stages, i.e.\ every stage
but the inert top one of each element. At 24.6\,eV that is 15 of them
(O\,\textsc{ii} at 35.12\,eV and N\,\textsc{ii} at 29.60\,eV are above the
edge); at 16.110\,eV it is 12.

\subsection{One place that says what column of the cross-section table is
which}

Adding the metals meant evaluating their cross sections at the five channel
energies, which are not on the \texttt{e\_v} grid the \texttt{sigma\_tab}
table lives on. The 17 fits were listed once, by hand, in
\texttt{set\_energy\_vectors}. A second hand-kept list in
\texttt{he\_rec\_coupling} would be a copy that can drift, so the ordering was
moved into one function instead: \texttt{metal\_photoion\_sigma(k,E)} in
\texttt{Cross\_sections} dispatches on the photo-table column index $k$, and
\texttt{set\_energy\_vectors} fills \texttt{sigma\_tab} through it in a loop.
The ordering now exists in one place, and the coupling reads the same function
the table does.

This is a refactor with no intended physics change, and it is byte-identical
on a metals-\emph{on} case: \texttt{wasp\_full} run with this change alone
reproduces its golden \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} and \texttt{Ion\_species.txt}
exactly.

\subsection{What moved}

\texttt{make check}, nine cases, \texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=1}: \textbf{the four
metals-off cases are byte-identical} (\texttt{mol\_base\_handoff},
\texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner}, \texttt{mol\_diffusion}, \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion})
and the five metals-on cases move.

$\Delta\log_{10}\dot M$ is the outer-cell mass flux $r^2\rho v$, re-measured

\textbf{Approximations, unchanged or newly stated at the code site.} The
photoelectron of a metal share is deposited entirely as heat, at
$E_c-\texttt{mion\_ethr}(m)$, without passing through the Shull \& van
Steenberg secondary-ionization partition the stellar photoelectrons go through
--- the same treatment the H\,\textsc{i} and H$_2$ shares of these photons
already had. The ions that actually carry the metal share leave 11.0\,eV
(O\,\textsc{i}), 10.1 (N\,\textsc{i}), 8.4 (Fe\,\textsc{ii}) and 0.2
(C\,\textsc{ii}) at the ground-capture channel and 4.9 (C\,\textsc{i}) at the
two-photon one; the largest of the set, 20.3\,eV for K\,\textsc{i}, belongs to
an ion whose cross section there is 0.048 against H\,\textsc{i}'s 1.24 and
which therefore carries almost none of it. The $\sigma_m$ are the same
single-shell Verner et al.\ (1996) fits \texttt{sigma\_tab} carries, with the
Fe\,\textsc{i} caveat already recorded at \texttt{sigma\_FeI}. The metal cross
sections are evaluated at the channel energy with their (small) $kT$
dependence neglected, as the H\,\textsc{i}, H$_2$ and He\,\textsc{i} ones
already were.

\section{Dissociative photoionization of H$_2$ is the second product channel of
a cross section the code already had, and the branching comes from the
measurement rather than from a summary of it (2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:h2-dissoc-photoion}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Judgment first. The photon channel
$\mathrm{H_2} + h\nu \to \mathrm{H} + \mathrm{H^+} + e^-$ (threshold
$18.076$~eV) was missing, and it was missing on both sides: from the primary
photoionization and from the secondary-electron partition of
Sec.~\ref{sec:sec-ion-molecular}. That is not a small omission dressed
up as a large one, and it is not a new opacity either. \texttt{sigma\_H2} is
the \emph{total} photoionization cross section, so the channel was already
inside the H$_2$ destruction rate the code applied --- it was simply all being
credited to H$_2^+$. In the shielded molecular base that is the wrong ion: the
dissociative channel makes a proton and an H atom, does not feed the H$_3^+$
chain (R8), and is the dominant photon-driven proton source there, $39$ times
the H\,\textsc{i} photoionization at $1.004\,R_p$ on the converged
He/H\,$=0.0793$ hot Uranus.} Item (P31), opened with
Sec.~\ref{sec:sec-ion-molecular}, is closed here.

\subsection{The two channels}

\begin{align}
  \text{(a)}\quad \mathrm{H_2} + h\nu &\;\to\; \mathrm{H_2^+} + e^-,
    & E_{\rm th} &= 15.4~\text{eV},\\
  \text{(b)}\quad \mathrm{H_2} + h\nu &\;\to\; \mathrm{H} + \mathrm{H^+} + e^-,
    & E_{\rm th} &= 18.076~\text{eV}.
\end{align}

Both consume one H$_2$. Since (b) is a share of the same \texttt{sigma\_H2},
the H$_2$ destruction rate, the opacity and the absorbed energy are unchanged;
what moves is the product and the threshold each channel is charged. The code
carries the whole rate as \texttt{P\_H2} and the dissociative part as
\texttt{P\_H2\_di}, a \textsc{subset} of it, and the coupled molecular system
reads row (4), H$_2$: the whole \texttt{P\_H2}, as before; row (5), H$_2^+$:
\texttt{P\_H2 $-$ P\_H2\_di}; row (1), H$^+$: $+\,$\texttt{P\_H2\_di}$\,n_{\rm
H_2}$. The H atom of the pair is supplied by the H-nucleus closure
$n_{\rm HI} = (1 - x_1 - x_4 - x_5 - x_6 - x_7)\,n_{\rm H}$, exactly as the two
Lyman--Werner fragments are, so no row was added.

The photoelectron of (b) carries $h\nu - 18.076$~eV, not $h\nu - 15.4$: the
$2.68$~eV between the thresholds goes into breaking the bond and is not
available as heat, the rule every other absorber in \texttt{PH\_heat\_HHe}
follows. It is therefore its own absorber in the secondary-ionization energy
grid (\texttt{iabs\_H2\_di}, \texttt{n\_abs\_fixed} $5\to6$), because its
photoelectron lands elsewhere in the Dalgarno energy table and thermalizes a
different share.

\subsection{The secondary side is one sentence of the source}

Dalgarno, Yan \& Liu (1999), the paragraph after their Eq.~(10): ``The
production of H$^+$ ions from dissociative ionization of H$_2$ is given by a
mean energy per ion of $22W_m(\mathrm{H_2^+})$. The harmonic mean of
$22W_m(\mathrm{H_2^+})$ and $W_m(\mathrm{H^+})$ is the mean energy for the
production of H$^+$ ions in the gas mixture.'' A mean energy $22$ times larger
is a yield $22$ times smaller, and the harmonic mean makes the two H$^+$
sources \textsc{add} rather than share, so the fast electrons make one
dissociative proton for every $22$ H$_2^+$ ions they make. The $4.5\%$ is not
deducted from the Shull \& van Steenberg amplitude the module borrows for the
ionization budget, because Dalgarno et al.'s $W$ is the primary energy divided
by the number of ions and already contains every loss of the degradation;
deducting it would double-count.

\subsection{The branching, and a correction to the summary we would otherwise
have used}
\label{sec:h2-di-branching}

The obvious source is the paper the cross section itself comes from. Yan,
Sadeghpour \& Dalgarno (1998), ApJ 496, 1044, Sec.~4: ``The cross section for
dissociative ionization, $\mathrm{H_2} + h\nu \to \mathrm{H} + \mathrm{H^+} +
e^-$, is complicated by the contribution of resonance states \dots Its ratio to
the total photoionization cross section increases from zero at the threshold of
18.08 eV to 0.284 at 76 eV and then decreases slowly to 0.258 at 124 eV.''

\textbf{Those two numbers are not the ratio to the total.} They are the
H$^+$/H$_2^+$ column of Chung, Lee, Masuoka \& Samson (1993), J.\ Chem.\ Phys.\
99, 885, Table~II, whose caption reads ``The partial cross sections
$\sigma(\mathrm{H^+})$, $\sigma(\mathrm{H_2^+})$, and the ratio
H$^+$/H$_2^+$ for dissociative photoionization of H$_2$'': a ratio to the
H$_2^+$ \emph{partial} cross section. The ratio to the total is $r/(1+r)$,
which is $0.221$ at $76$~eV and $0.205$ at $124$~eV. An implementation built on
the quoted sentence --- which is what this work first built, and ran ---
overstates the channel by a factor $1.26$--$1.28$ above $70$~eV; and because
the real curve rises to a $0.02$ plateau within $0.03$~eV of threshold instead
of ramping linearly from it, the same implementation understates it by up to a
factor $20$ below $20$~eV and misses the $Q_1$ Rydberg autoionization resonance
entirely.

The code therefore reads Chung et al.'s Table~II directly, as
$f_{\rm di}(E) = \sigma(\mathrm{H^+})/[\sigma(\mathrm{H^+}) +
\sigma(\mathrm{H_2^+})]$ at their $69$ energies from $18.076$ to $124$~eV,
linearly interpolated. Two checks were run on the transcription: their two
partial columns reproduce their own ratio column to better than $0.5\%$ at
every row, and the partial columns sum to their $\sigma({\rm abs})$ column
exactly except at the ten rows carrying their footnote~b ($33$--$41$~eV),
where the photoionization yield is below unity and the deficit is their
Table~I neutral cross section ($1.29 - 1.20 = 0.09$ against their $0.092$ at
$37$~eV).

 50   & 0.1537 & 0.1565 & 1.02 \\
 60   & 0.1982 & 0.2055 & 1.04 \\
 74   & 0.2219 & 0.2742 & 1.24 \\
 76   & 0.2212 & 0.2840 & 1.28 \\
110   & 0.2096 & 0.2656 & 1.27 \\
124   & 0.2048 & 0.2580 & 1.26 \\
$>124$ & 0.2048 & 0.2580 & 1.26 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The flux-weighted branching of an unattenuated $E^{-1}$ power law over
$15.5$--$1240$~eV is $0.0239$ against the ramp's $0.0224$: the two agree in the
mean and disagree everywhere in detail, which is exactly the case in which a
mean-preserving error survives a coarse test.

\textbf{Uncertainty, as the source states it.} ``An estimate of the total
uncertainty in the data is about $\pm4\%$--$5\%$''; the ionization yields used
over $18$--$28$~eV are unity ``within an accuracy of about $\pm5\%$''. Against
other determinations Chung et al.'s H$^+$ data lie $0\%$--$5\%$ below Backx,
Wight \& van der Wiel over $18$--$33$~eV, growing to $26\%$ at $70$~eV; they
agree within $5\%$ with Kossmann et al.\ over $25$--$75$~eV and lie
$11\%$--$20\%$ below them over $75$--$110$~eV.

\textbf{Above $124$~eV}, the top of the measured range, $f_{\rm di}$ is held at
its $124$~eV value, $0.2048$. The source quotes no higher-energy data. The
curve is nearly flat over its last $50$~eV ($0.2219$ at $74$~eV to $0.2048$ at
$124$~eV), so this is a mild extrapolation --- but it is an extrapolation, and
it is the value the whole X-ray grid uses.

\subsection{Two things the branching carries that its name does not}

Both are stated by the source, both are recorded at the code site, and both
are carried as open items --- (P31b) and (P31c) of \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md},
which give the size of each and what removing it would take.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Double ionization.} Chung et al.'s Eqs.~(3)--(4) note that ``the
  branching ratio H$^+$/(H$^+$ $+$ H$_2^+$) is understood to include both
  single and double ionization where appropriate'', and their discussion of
  Fig.~4 that ``by 80 eV about 20\% of $\sigma(\mathrm{H^+})$ comes from double
  ionization. This percentage remains fairly constant towards higher
  energies.'' Their $\sigma(\mathrm{H^+})$ counts \textsc{protons}, and a
  double ionization yields two, so using $f_{\rm di}$ as a share of the H$_2$
  ionization rate gives the \textsc{proton} source rate correctly; what it
  mis-assigns is the co-product, since those events leave no H atom and no
  H$_2^+$. Above $80$~eV that is about $4\%$ of the H$_2$ ionizations, in a
  band where \texttt{sigma\_H2} is already two decades below its threshold
  value.
\item \textbf{Neutral dissociation over $33$--$41$~eV.} \texttt{sigma\_H2}
  follows Samson \& Haddad's \textsc{absorption} cross section there --- it is
  $1.76$ against Chung et al.'s $\sigma({\rm abs})$ $1.74$ and their ionization
  sum $1.699$ at $34$~eV --- so the H$_2$ destruction rate the code applies in
  that band includes $\mathrm{H_2} + h\nu \to \mathrm{H} + \mathrm{H}$, up to
  $7\%$ of it at $37.5$~eV, and the $1 - f_{\rm di}$ branch hands that share to
  H$_2^+$. This is a property of the cross-section fit, which predates this
  change, not of the branching.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Not split, deliberately: the He recombination photons.}
\texttt{dP\_H2\_hrc} (\texttt{he\_rec\_coupling}) sits at $19.8$--$24.6$~eV,
where $f_{\rm di}$ is $1.9\%$--$2.3\%$. Splitting off that much of a channel
that is itself a correction would be well inside the $\pm4$--$5\%$ the
branching carries, so the whole of it still makes H$_2^+$, and the code says so
where it is applied.

\subsection{What moved}

\textbf{The three atomic cases are byte-identical.} \texttt{wasp\_full},
\texttt{wasp\_he23off} and \texttt{lower\_profile} carry no H$_2$, so
\texttt{nh2} is never passed, \texttt{s\_h2\_di} is allocated and never read,
and every H$_2$ term is identically zero. Their \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} and
\texttt{Ion\_species.txt} reproduce the pre-change tree bit-for-bit. They do
\emph{not} reproduce the goldens, and neither did the tree before this change:
Secs.~\ref{sec:molecular-carrier-transport} and \ref{sec:he-rec-metal-competition} moved
five of the nine cases and the goldens are refreshed once at the end of the
series, so the comparison that means anything is against the tree's own output
immediately before the change, which is what the table below is.

The six molecular cases move. Each is a fixed-step relaxation snapshot, not a
converged solution, so a per-cell extreme is noisy; the entry below is the
largest relative change over the cells where that species is within three
decades of its own peak.

The signature is the one the physics predicts: \textbf{H$_2$ barely moves} (the
total destruction rate is unchanged by construction), \textbf{H$_2^+$ falls},
\textbf{H$_3^+$ falls with it} because R8 is fed by H$_2^+$, and
\textbf{H$^+$ rises}. The H$_2$ front moves inward in the fifth decimal, i.e.\
not at all. The largest temperature change of the six is $4.2\%$
(\texttt{mol\_ir\_bands}) and the smallest $5.7\times10^{-4}$
(\texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner}). \texttt{mol\_ir\_bands} and \texttt{mol\_metals}
carry the opposite sign at their extreme cell; both are the same hot-Uranus
gate at $12000$ fixed steps with a base that is still breathing, and neither
case is converged.

\textbf{Where the channel actually matters, measured with the diagnostic
build.} On \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion}, $P_{\rm H_2,di}/P_{\rm H_2}$ is $4.67\%$ in
the shielded base and rises to $6.5\%$ at the top of the molecular layer as the
surviving spectrum hardens ($8.5\%$ on the He/H\,$=0.0793$ run) --- the $4.5\%$
order the secondary side of Dalgarno et al.\ predicts, arrived at independently
through the photon branching. The proton source ratio
$P_{\rm H_2,di}n_{\rm H_2}/(P_{\rm HI}n_{\rm HI})$ is $20.5$ at $1.004\,R_p$,
$3.1$ at $1.04$, and falls through unity at $1.064\,R_p$; on the converged
He/H\,$=0.0793$ run the same ratio is $38.9$ at $1.004\,R_p$ and crosses unity
at $1.036$. Inside the molecular layer this channel, not the H\,\textsc{i}
photoionization, is what the protons come from.

\subsection{What was checked, and what was not}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Byte-identity of the atomic path}, against the tree's own

  \texttt{lower\_profile}, both files. This is the guard that

  secondary-ionization energy grid, which it would have done silently.
\item \textbf{The six molecular cases}, table above.
\item \textbf{Runtime checks.} An \texttt{-O1 -g -fcheck=bounds,do,mem} build
  run on \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion} for $1200$ steps: clean, no trap. Run in a
  scratch copy of the tree rather than through \texttt{run\_fcheck.sh}, which
  begins with a \texttt{make distclean} in the repository and would have
  collided with the other work in flight; and that script's own case is
  HD~209458\,b, which is atomic and would not have entered this code at all.
\item \textbf{Thread determinism.} \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion} at
  \texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=8} reproduces the single-threaded run bit-for-bit,
  which is what the three new \texttt{!\$OMP PRIVATE} entries are for.
