\section{What the below-escape rows are measured against, a ``PLM+WENO3'' that
could not reconstruct, and a residual gate that switched off every other stop
(2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:layer-row-scales}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Judgment first, in three parts.}

\textbf{(1) The layer's energy and mass rows are measured against the wrong
thing, and neither of the two proposed replacements survives measurement.} The
claim this item was opened on --- that $|u(3,j)|$ collapses in the
quasi-hydrostatic layer the way $|\rho v|$ does --- is \textbf{refuted}:
$u(3,j)$ is the energy \emph{density}, not an energy flux, and it collapses
nowhere (in the layer it is 0.16 of $|{\rm heat}|+|{\rm cool}|$ on WASP-121b
and 69 times it on HD\,189733\,b). What is nevertheless wrong is real:
$|R|/|u|$ is a fractional drift \emph{rate} in units of the code's global time
$t_s$, and near the base the cell's own timescale is three to four orders
shorter than $t_s$, so a layer that is steady to one part in $10^{7}$ of its
own terms reads $10^{-3}$ on that rate. Measured on the converged
\texttt{jfnk\_hd189} state, the layer holds $\|R\|$ at $9.915\times10^{-4}$
while the wind is at $1.836\times10^{-6}$ --- a factor 540 --- and 806 of the
solve's outer iterations go into the layer alone.
\textbf{Candidate (a), $|{\rm heat}| + |{\rm cool}|$, is disqualified}: on the
hot Uranus the radiative terms are not the dominant balance (layer
$|{\rm heat}|+|{\rm cool}| = 9.4\times10^{-5}$ against
$|{\rm d}F_3| = 8.7\times10^{-5}$), and converged states read
$2.3\times10^{-2}$ to $5.4\times10^{-1}$ on it.
\textbf{Candidate (b), $|p\,{\rm div}\,v| + |\rho v g|$, is disqualified}: both
terms carry $v$ and collapse in the layer exactly as $|\rho v|$ does; converged
states read $1.8\times10^{-1}$ to 1.9 on it.
\textbf{The one scale that survives} is the signal-speed transport bound
$|u(k,j)|\,(|v_j| + c_{s,j})/dr_j$, the same construction
\texttt{cell\_state\_scales} uses for the momentum unknown and
\texttt{carrier\_row\_scale} for the carriers; on it every converged state
above reads $7\times10^{-9}$ to $4\times10^{-6}$ in both regions and both rows.
\textbf{It is not applied, because applying it is a re-calibration of a
user-facing tolerance and, measured, it costs section~\ref{sec:whole-column-residual}.}
With the layer's mass and energy rows on that bound, \texttt{jfnk\_hd189\_tight}
reaches \texttt{info = 0} easily (its binding row becomes the layer momentum
row at $1.8\times10^{-7}$) --- and the two hot-Uranus states of
section~\ref{sec:whole-column-residual} swap places again: the wind rows become
the maximum, and the state whose inner flux spread is $7.6\times10^{-2}$ scores
$4.8\times10^{-4}$ against $7.0\times10^{-4}$ for the one whose spread is
$3.0\times10^{-3}$. The discrimination itself is scale-independent (the bad
state is 5.7 times worse than the good one in the layer energy row on
\emph{every} candidate); what the re-scaling changes is whether the layer is
ever the larger half. \textbf{So the two goals cannot both be met by one
max-combined residual with one threshold, and the resolution is a design
decision, proposed in section 131.4 and not taken here.}

\textbf{(2) ``PLM+WENO3'' with an empty PLM stage crashed on the first step.
Fixed.} The parser left \texttt{rec\_method} at the input word
\texttt{'PLM+WENO3'}, which is the name of a two-stage recipe and not of a
reconstruction; when the stage-1 threshold did not exceed the stage-2 one,
\texttt{EXHALE\_main}'s \texttt{in\_plm\_stage} was false, the string was never
normalized, and the first \texttt{Reconstruct} fell through to
\texttt{case default} and aborted with \texttt{unknown reconstruction scheme:
PLM+WENO3}. \texttt{rec\_method} is now always \texttt{'PLM'} or
\texttt{'WENO3'}; the two-stage intent travels in \texttt{recon\_two\_stage}
alone; and an empty PLM stage resolves to single-stage WENO3 with a message
saying so. Three regression cases were affected ---
\texttt{wasp\_hybrid\_finish}, \texttt{crit\_warm} and
\texttt{wasp\_localdt\_cont}, all with \texttt{du\_th [PLM,WENO3]: -1.0 ...}
--- and all three now run.

\textbf{(3) A \texttt{Resid tol} gate switched off every other stop, including
the stall net. Fixed.} With \texttt{resid\_th > 0} the marching loop set
\texttt{is\_stalled = .false.} unconditionally, so a run that could not reach
its residual gate marched to \texttt{count\_max = 1e6}. Measured:
\texttt{jfnk\_cold} reaches $du = 1.5\times10^{-4}$ and \texttt{ptc\_warm}
$du = 5.5\times10^{-5}$ --- flux-converged by any ordinary standard --- and
neither crossed its gate in 40,000 steps. A residual gate is one more stop
condition, not a licence to remove the others; the plateau detector now stays
live under \texttt{Resid tol}, and the stop it produces is reported as what it
is, a stall with the residual target unmet.

\subsection{What the layer rows actually measure}

$R(3,j) = {\rm d}F(3,j) - ({\rm heat}_j - {\rm cool}_j)$ --- the source
$S(3,:)$ is identically zero, the gravity work being folded into the energy
flux (\texttt{RK\_rhs.f90}) --- so the energy row has exactly two terms.
Volume-weighted sums over the layer, in code units, on four states
(\texttt{EXHALE\_RESIDUAL=1} on the converged output, WENO3 except
HD\,189733\,b which is re-read in the PLM it was converged in):

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
\toprule
layer sums & WASP-121b & HD\,189733\,b & hot U, two-stage & hot U, single-stage \\
\midrule
$|{\rm d}F_3|$ & $1.404\times10^{-1}$ & $1.964\times10^{-4}$ & $8.720\times10^{-5}$ & $1.349\times10^{-4}$ \\
$|{\rm heat}|$ & 1.054 & $1.083\times10^{-3}$ & $8.141\times10^{-5}$ & $9.384\times10^{-5}$ \\
$|{\rm cool}|$ & $9.138\times10^{-1}$ & $1.522\times10^{-3}$ & $1.302\times10^{-5}$ & $7.488\times10^{-5}$ \\
$|{\rm heat}-{\rm cool}|$ & $1.399\times10^{-1}$ & $5.310\times10^{-4}$ & $8.416\times10^{-5}$ & $1.577\times10^{-4}$ \\
$|R_3|$ & $1.161\times10^{-3}$ & $5.664\times10^{-4}$ & $1.015\times10^{-5}$ & $9.130\times10^{-5}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{Which term dominates is planet-dependent.} On WASP-121b the radiative
pair is an order above the flux divergence; on the hot Uranus it is not
($|{\rm heat}|+|{\rm cool}| = 9.4\times10^{-5}$ against
$|{\rm d}F_3| = 8.7\times10^{-5}$). That is why $|{\rm heat}| + |{\rm cool}|$
cannot serve as the scale: it is not a bound on the row's terms where the layer
is cold and shielded. The ratio
$(|{\rm heat}|+|{\rm cool}|)/(E\,(|v|+c_s)/dr)$ over the layer has median
$5.1\times10^{-3}$ (WASP), $7.1\times10^{-5}$ (HD\,189733\,b),
$1.1\times10^{-4}$ and $3.4\times10^{-6}$ (hot Uranus) and never exceeds 0.15,
so the radiative pair never dominates the signal-speed transport bound either.

Read down the columns: $/(h{+}c)$ ranges over four decades and is worst on the

regions, which is what a scale that bounds its own row looks like.

\subsection{Why this cannot simply be adopted}

\texttt{jfnk\_hd189\_tight} (\texttt{Resid tol: 1.0e-4}) is blocked by the
layer, and by both rows, not only the energy one: at convergence of the
$10^{-3}$ run the layer reads mass $7.183\times10^{-4}$, momentum$/\rho g$
$1.845\times10^{-7}$ and energy $9.915\times10^{-4}$, so re-scaling the energy
row alone leaves the mass row at $7.2\times10^{-4}$ and the $10^{-4}$ target
still out of reach. Re-scaling both makes the layer's binding row the momentum
one at $1.8\times10^{-7}$, and the target is met with room to spare.

But the same re-scaling removes what section~\ref{sec:whole-column-residual}
was written for. The discrimination between the two hot-Uranus states is
present on every candidate --- the single-stage state is 5.7 times worse than
the two-stage one in the layer energy row and 2.4 times worse in the layer mass
row, on $|u|$ and on the signal-speed bound alike --- yet $\|R\|$ is a maximum,
so what decides the verdict is which half is larger:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrl}
\toprule
policy & hot U two-stage & hot U single-stage & ordering \\
\midrule
section~\ref{sec:whole-column-residual} as it stands & $6.97\times10^{-4}$ & $4.00\times10^{-3}$ & correct \\
energy row re-scaled in the layer only & $6.97\times10^{-4}$ & $1.06\times10^{-3}$ & correct \\
mass and energy re-scaled in the layer & $6.97\times10^{-4}$ & $4.76\times10^{-4}$ & \textbf{inverted} \\
every row re-scaled, both regions & $4.68\times10^{-6}$ & $3.12\times10^{-6}$ & \textbf{inverted} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\subsection{The proposal, not implemented}

Separate the two statements the one number is being asked to make.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Steadiness of the equations} $\to$ $\|R\|$ on the signal-speed
bound in both regions and all three rows, with the layer's momentum row keeping
the gravitational force density of section 62.3 (it is that row's
dominant-term bound). Every row is then divided by a bound on its own largest
term, the number is dimensionless everywhere, and the two regions become
commensurable --- which would also retire the ``not addends of a common
quantity'' caveat that section~\ref{sec:whole-column-residual} had to make for
the maximum. \texttt{Resid tol} would need a new default: converged states
measure $7\times10^{-9}$ to $4\times10^{-6}$, so $10^{-5}$ is the natural
equivalent of today's $10^{-3}$, and every existing \texttt{Resid tol} in the
repository changes meaning.
\item \textbf{Constancy of the mass flux} $\to$ a separate gate on the radial
spread of $\rho v r^2$ over the \emph{whole} column rather than over
$[j_{\min}:N]$, which is the quantity that actually separates the two
hot-Uranus states ($3.0\times10^{-3}$ against $7.6\times10^{-2}$, a factor 25,
against 1.9 to 5.7 in any residual norm) and which item (P42) named in the
first place.
\end{enumerate}

That is a change to the meaning of a user input, so it is proposed and not
taken.

\subsection{What was checked}

\begin{itemize}

\section{The Lyman--Werner rate is now the level-resolved cross section itself,
one pump has two branching ratios, and the $2.0$~eV of the heat return is
computed instead of adopted (2026-09-02)}
\label{sec:lw-cross-section-sources}
% ===================================================================== %

\begin{quote}\small\textbf{Superseded in part by Sec.~\ref{sec:h2-shield-line-overlap} (2026-09-03).} The
tabulated rate was \textsc{cloudy}'s H2g sub-reservoir and line overlap was
absent; both are fixed there. The absolute cross section, the two branching
ratios and the computed heat return all stand; the table they are read from
was rebuilt.\end{quote}
\textbf{Judgment first. The two Lyman--Werner band constants did not disagree
with the \textsc{cloudy} calculation of Sec.~\ref{sec:h2-shield-table} for
the reason that note recorded. The line data agree: rebuilt from
\textsc{cloudy}'s own Abgrall, Roueff \& Drira (2000) files, the band-averaged
dissociation cross section for a thermal H$_2$ population at $100$~K is
$3.479\times10^{-18}$~cm$^2$ against the $3.4520\times10^{-18}$~cm$^2$ the
module took from Draine \& Bertoldi (1996) --- $0.8$ per cent --- and the pump
cross section agrees to $0.02$ per cent. The factor $1.15$--$1.37$ between
them is \textsc{line trapping} of the fluorescent decay photons, which
\textsc{cloudy}'s converged pass carries and DB96's unshielded tables do not.
The defect was the mixture: an untrapped constant multiplied by a shielding
factor whose own normalization is trapped. The rate now comes from the
absolute cross section, tabulated.} Item (P39) is closed here.

\subsection{What the measurement was}

\textsc{cloudy} does not write the untrapped branching out --- its Solomon
rate carries the escape probability inside $D/(D + \sum A_{ul} P_{\rm loss})$.
A four-line diagnostic was added to a scratch build of c25.00 to print, at
full precision, the fresh pump rate of the H$_2$g population, the dissociation
rate that pump gives with $D/(D + \sum A_{ul})$, the rate it gives with
\textsc{cloudy}'s own branching, and the band field. The patch is in
\texttt{src/utils/h2\_shielding\_cloudy\_decks/} and it is inert: the 27 decks
re-run with it reproduce the unpatched $f_{\rm shield}$ curve with a maximum
relative difference of exactly zero, and the table built from them is
byte-identical to the one Sec.~\ref{sec:h2-shield-table} installed.

With it the attribution is a measurement. At the illuminated face of the
$1300$~K run the single-pump branching is $0.1466$ \emph{on both passes} ---
there is no escape probability in it, so it cannot move --- while the
effective one goes $0.1466 \to 0.1771$ between the first pass and the
converged one. At fixed $T = 1300$~K the converged face cross section moves
$13$ per cent between $n_{\rm H} = 10^{12}$ and $10^{14}$~cm$^{-3}$ while the
untrapped value is identical to five digits, and atomic data cannot depend on
density.

\subsection{One absorption, three counts}

\begin{tabular}{@{}l p{0.72\linewidth}@{}}
\hline
$\sigma_{\rm diss}$ & dissociations per unit \textsc{incident} band photon
  fluence [cm$^2$]; self-shielding and trapping both inside it --- the
  \textsc{rate}.\\
$p_{\rm single}$ & dissociations per \textsc{pump} with every fluorescent
  photon free to escape, $D/(D + \sum A_{ul})$ --- the \textsc{heat return}.\\
$p_{\rm eff}$ & dissociations per photon \textsc{removed from the beam}, i.e.\
  per fresh pump, $D/(D + \sum A_{ul} P_{\rm loss})$ --- the \textsc{photon
  ledger}.\\
\hline
\end{tabular}

\medskip

$p_{\rm single}$ and not $p_{\rm eff}$ is what the fluorescence heat needs,
because the trapping cancels out of that count exactly. Per fresh pump the
chain ends in dissociation with probability $p_{\rm eff}$ and contains
$(D+A)/(D + A P_{\rm loss})$ pump events, so
\begin{equation}
  \text{pumps per dissociation} \;=\; \frac{D+A}{D} \;=\; \frac{1}{p_{\rm single}},
\end{equation}
independent of $P_{\rm loss}$, and the decays per dissociation are
$(1-p_{\rm single})/p_{\rm single}$. Physically, a trapped decay and the
re-absorption that follows it move one molecule down and another up and
deposit nothing. \textsc{cloudy}'s own bookkeeping says the same: the return
flux into $X(v'',J'')$ is $\mathrm{Pop}_{\rm up} A_{ul} P_{\rm loss}$ and the
excited-state population is $\dot{n}_{\rm in}/(D + \sum A_{ul} P_{\rm loss})$,
so the arrivals in vibrationally excited $X$ per dissociation are $A_+/D$,
with no escape probability in them. The beam photon count is the other one:
only fresh pumps take photons out of the stellar beam, so
\texttt{write\_output}'s \texttt{ph\_lw} divides by $p_{\rm eff}$. The two
differ by $20$--$40$ per cent through the layer.

\subsection{What the table carries now}

\texttt{h2\_self\_shielding\_table.f90} holds three cubes on the same
$39\times9\times3$ grid in $(\log N_{\rm H_2}, \log T, \log n_{\rm H})$ ---
$\log_{10}\sigma_{\rm diss}$, $\log_{10} p_{\rm single}$,
$\log_{10} p_{\rm eff}$ --- generated by the same script from the same 27
decks. \texttt{h2\_self\_shielding\_level\_resolved} survives as the ratio
$\sigma_{\rm diss}(N)/\sigma_{\rm diss}(N_{\min})$, a diagnostic, which is
what \texttt{output/Lyman\_Werner.txt} reports. At $n_{\rm H} = 10^{13}$
cm$^{-3}$:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r r r@{}}
\hline
$N({\rm H_2})$ [cm$^{-2}$] & $\sigma_{\rm diss}$ ($1300$~K) & $p_{\rm single}$ & $p_{\rm eff}$\\
\hline
$10^{12}$            & $4.630\times10^{-18}$ & $0.147$ & $0.177$\\
$10^{17}$            & $3.806\times10^{-20}$ & $0.225$ & $0.293$\\
$4.3\times10^{18}$   & $1.060\times10^{-21}$ & $0.175$ & $0.238$\\
$4.8\times10^{20}$   & $9.844\times10^{-23}$ & $0.147$ & $0.220$\\
$5.0\times10^{21}$   & $3.105\times10^{-23}$ & $0.151$ & $0.215$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\subsection{The $2.0$~eV of the heat return is now computed}

Burton, Hollenbach \& Tielens (1990) Appendix A read: ``the effective heating
per pump, $E_*$, has been taken as 2.0 eV'', an adopted value with no
derivation, and their Eq.~(A1) multiplies it by the collisional de-excitation
rate of a UV-excited pseudolevel, not by the pump rate and not by the
dissociation rate. Black \& van Dishoeck (1987), pp.~412--413, supply only the
branching --- ``fluorescence to the vibrational continuum of the ground state
with a typical average probability of 0.10 \dots The remaining 90\% of the
fluorescent transitions populate various bound excited vibration-rotation
levels of the ground state'' --- not a mean energy.

The same quantity is computable. Summing the Abgrall, Roueff \& Drira (2000)
transition probabilities over every decay of every in-band pump, weighted by
the $X(v'',J'')$ energy the decay lands on, gives the mean landing energy per
\textsc{bound} fluorescence:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r r r r r@{}}
\hline
$T$ [K] & $700$ & $1300$ & $1800$ & $2700$ & $3200$\\
\hline
$E_{\rm bound}$ [eV] & $2.060$ & $2.085$ & $2.102$ & $2.121$ & $2.129$\\
per pump [eV]        & $1.769$ & $1.779$ & $1.786$ & $1.795$ & $1.799$\\
against $2.0$~eV     & $+3.0\%$ & $+4.3\%$ & $+5.1\%$ & $+6.1\%$ & $+6.4\%$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\texttt{h2\_energy\_per\_bound\_fluorescence\_eV(T)} replaces the constant, a
quadratic reproducing the nine points to $0.03$ per cent and clamped at
$700$--$3200$~K. The form stored is per \textsc{bound} fluorescence, not per
pump, because it then belongs to the cascade alone and not to the branching of
whatever excited the molecule: the Lyman--Werner path multiplies by
$(1-p_{\rm single})$, the photoelectron path by its own state-resolved
$(1-p_{{\rm diss},B})$, $(1-p_{{\rm diss},C})$ ($0.27$, $0.036$). The sixth of
the bound fluorescences that land back on $v''=0$ and leave only rotational
energy is already inside these means and must not be discounted a second time.

\subsection{Three constants removed}

With the rate and both branchings on the table, \texttt{sigma\_lw},
\texttt{p\_diss\_lw} and \texttt{sigma\_lw\_pump} entered no number the code
produced. They are gone from \texttt{lyman\_werner.f90}; the values (DB96
Table~1--2, $\chi = 1$, the $T_r = 100$~K row: $F = 1.208\times10^{7}$
cm$^{-2}$~s$^{-1}$, $\zeta_{\rm pump} = 3.09\times10^{-10}$~s$^{-1}$,
$\langle p_{\rm diss}\rangle = 0.135$, hence
$\sigma_{\rm diss} = 3.452\times10^{-18}$ and
$\sigma_{\rm pump} = 2.557\times10^{-17}$~cm$^2$) are stated in the
\texttt{h2\_band\_equivalent\_width} header as what DB96's Eq.~(39) is
normalized to, since that fit is still what computes the band share $A(N)$ the
H$_2$O and OH continua see. The band share itself is unchanged.

\subsection{What moved}

Nine matrix cases, single-threaded, against the same tree without this change:
\textbf{seven byte-identical}; \texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner} and
\texttt{mol\_sec\_ion} move, and nothing else does. In
\texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner} the unattenuated rate rises by $1.274$ at the base
($1.15$--$1.37$ was the predicted band), the H$_2$ half-abundance radius moves
inward from $1.13116$ to $1.12652\,R_p$, and \texttt{heat\_H2\_LW} integrates
$1.16$ times higher from the rate and a further $1.040$ from $E_{\rm bound}$;
\texttt{heat\_total} moves by $3$ per cent. \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion} is the only
case in which the photoelectron fluorescence channel is live, and there
$E_{\rm bound}$ moves \texttt{heat\_total} by $0.05$ per cent integrated.

\subsection{Where it stops being a value}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The trapping inside $\sigma_{\rm diss}$ and $p_{\rm eff}$ is
  slab geometry.} \textsc{cloudy} computes it from escape probabilities in a
  plane-parallel slab illuminated on one face and closed on the other. Our
  layer has the same thick-inward side, which is the side that matters, but it
  is spherical and open outward, and the size of the enhancement depends on
  the column \emph{behind} the point --- a property of the run, not of H$_2$.
  $p_{\rm single}$ is free of this.
\item \textbf{$E_{\rm bound}$ is an unshielded average.} With shielded weights
  the same sum gives $2.17$--$2.25$~eV at
  $N({\rm H_2}) = 10^{18}$--$10^{21}$~cm$^{-2}$, $+4$ to $+9$ per cent,
  because self-shielding removes the strongest lines first and the survivors
  land higher. The face value is used, so the term is a lower bound inside the
  shielded layer by about as much as the correction it applies.
\item \textbf{Above \texttt{h2\_shielding\_overlap\_column} everything here is
  an upper bound}, for the line-overlap reason
  Sec.~\ref{sec:h2-shield-table} gives. That item is unchanged.
\item Sources and arithmetic: \texttt{docs/p39\_lw\_cross\_section\_sources.md}.
\end{itemize}



\section{Two gates: the residual on each row's own largest term, and the mass
flux on the wind (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:two-gates}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Judgment first. One number was being asked to say two things, and it
could say neither well.} $\|R\|$ is a statement that nothing is changing; the
constancy of $\rho v r^2$ is a statement that the wind carries one mass flux at
every altitude. They are not the same statement --- the two solves of
section~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open} differ by a factor 25 in the flux
spread and by only 1.9 to 5.7 in every residual norm that was tried --- and
section~\ref{sec:layer-row-scales} measured that no single max-combined
residual with one threshold can make both. \textbf{They are now two gates, and
a steady solve is accepted only when BOTH are met.} The residual's row scale
becomes, at every cell and in every row, a bound on that row's own largest
term: the cell's state scale times the rate at which a signal crosses the cell,
$D_k(j)\,(|v_j| + c_{s,j})/dr_j$. That is the same $D_k$ the line-search merit
uses, so the merit and the acceptance test are now the same scaling of the same
residual, differing only by each cell's signal-crossing time.
\texttt{Resid tol} therefore changes meaning by a measured factor $10^{-2}$ and
every value in the repository is renormalized. The result is what the pair was
for: the two restarts of section~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open} now land on
the same wind --- $\log_{10}\dot M$ 10.30 and 10.32 against 10.47 and 10.27 ---
and \texttt{jfnk\_hd189}, which used to spend 806 iterations on a layer the
measure was mis-scaling, converges on both gates.

This closes item (P42).

\subsection{The residual row scale, and what the measurement chose}

Section~\ref{sec:layer-row-scales} left one candidate standing,
$|u(k,j)|\,(|v|+c_s)/dr_j$, and one question: whether the momentum row's
gravitational scale of section 62.3 should be replaced by it or combined with
it. The question is settled by measuring which of the two collapses, on the
four converged states of section~\ref{sec:layer-row-scales}, volume-weighted,
in each region:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
momentum-row candidate & layer, four states & wind, four states \\
\midrule
$|R_2| / \rho|d\Phi/dr|$ (section 62.3) & $1.5\times10^{-6}$--$2.5\times10^{-4}$ & $9.0\times10^{-7}$--$1.3\times10^{-2}$ \\
$|R_2| / |\rho v|(|v|+c_s)/dr$ & $4.4\times10^{-5}$--$2.5\times10^{-3}$ & $5.2\times10^{-10}$--$6.8\times10^{-5}$ \\
$|R_2| / \rho(|v|+c_s)^2/dr$ & $\mathbf{1.9\times10^{-8}}$--$\mathbf{1.5\times10^{-6}}$ & $\mathbf{2.5\times10^{-10}}$--$\mathbf{1.0\times10^{-5}}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The literal reading of $|u(2,j)| = |\rho v|$ collapses in the layer exactly as
it always did --- it is 40 to 120 times smaller than the gravitational scale
there --- so it cannot be the bound. What does not collapse anywhere is
$\rho(|v|+c_s)$, which is \texttt{cell\_state\_scales}' own momentum scale,
times the signal-crossing rate. \textbf{Measured, it exceeds the gravitational
scale at every cell of every state: by a factor 20.8 at the tightest cell and
21 to 3600 in the volume-weighted sums.} So gravity never wins, and the maximum
is kept only so that the bound is a bound by construction rather than by
measurement on four states.

The row scale is therefore, with no region switch at all,
%
\begin{align*}
 s_k(j) &= D_k(j)\,\bigl(|v_j| + c_{s,j}\bigr)/dr_j,\qquad
 D = \bigl(\rho,\ \rho(|v|+c_s),\ E\bigr) \\
 s_2(j) &= \max\Bigl( s_2(j),\ \rho_j\,|G\phi_i(j) - G\phi_i(j-1)|/dr_j \Bigr).
\end{align*}
%
$D_k$ now lives in one place, \texttt{state\_scales\_of\_cell} in
\texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_residual.f90}, and
\texttt{cell\_state\_scales} in the solver calls it. The convergence measure is
the merit's own scaling of the same residual, multiplied by the cell's
signal-crossing time: the merit is a rate, the acceptance test the
dimensionless fraction of the row's largest term.

The two-region maximum of section~\ref{sec:whole-column-residual} stays, but
its justification changes. It was there because the wind's and the layer's
numbers were not commensurable; they are now. It is kept because the outer
region carries almost all of $\sum r^2\,dr$, so any single volume-weighted norm
would let it average the inner column away.

\subsection{The flux gate}

New key, parsed in \texttt{input\_read.f90}, defaulted in
\texttt{parameters.f90}:
%
\begin{lstlisting}
Flux spread tol: <tol> [<r_flux [R_p]>]      default 5.0e-3, 1.2
\end{lstlisting}
%
\texttt{flux\_spread\_of\_state} (\texttt{steady\_residual.f90}) returns
$(\max F - \min F)/|\overline{F}|$ with $F = \rho v r^2$ over
$[j_{\rm flux}:N]$, i.e.\ over $r \ge r_{\rm flux}$; $j_{\rm flux}$ is set in
\texttt{define\_grid} beside $j_{\min}$ and carries the same empty-window
guard. \texttt{steady\_gates\_met} in \texttt{steady\_newton.f90} is the only
acceptance test either solver uses, and it is $\|R\| <$
\texttt{resid\_tol} AND spread $<$ \texttt{flux\_spread\_th}. A tolerance
$\le 0$ disables the flux gate. When a solve ends unaccepted the log names the
gate that is left:
%
\begin{lstlisting}
 (JFNK) the residual gate is met; the FLUX gate is the one left: spread 1.874E-02 >= 5.000E-03
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{Why the window is not $[1:N]$, measured.} Mass conservation does make
$\rho v r^2$ constant everywhere in a steady state, but the base boundary
condition deliberately admits a small inflow through the smooth valve, and just
above it the wind is still being launched at $|v| \sim 1$--$10$\,cm/s, eight
orders below the wind speed. On a hot Uranus state that is flat everywhere
else, the spread over all cells is $\mathbf{9.9\times10^{2}}$ and $F$ changes
sign, so $\max/\min$ is not even defined; over $r \ge 1.03$ it is
$7.5\times10^{-2}$, over 1.05 $4.6\times10^{-2}$, over 1.10
$3.3\times10^{-3}$ and over 1.20 $2.5\times10^{-3}$. Including the launch
region would measure the base boundary condition, not the wind.

\textbf{Why the defaults are $5\times10^{-3}$ and $1.2\,R_p$.} Over
$r \ge 1.2$ every converged state in hand is flat: $2.4\times10^{-3}$ (hot
Uranus, two-stage restart), $2.4\times10^{-3}$ (He/H\,=\,0.0793),
$2.6\times10^{-3}$ (He/H\,=\,1), $2.9\times10^{-3}$ (He/H\,=\,30),
$4.8\times10^{-4}$ (WASP-121b, both Newton cases). The state
section~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open} showed the old measure could not
reject reads $7.6\times10^{-2}$ there. A threshold of $5\times10^{-3}$ clears
the worst converged state by 1.7 and rejects the bad one by 15. $1.2\,R_p$ is
the smallest fixed radius at which all of them are flat --- at 1.10 the
He/H\,=\,30 rung reads $2.1\times10^{-2}$ --- and it is the inner edge of the
region sections~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open}
and~\ref{sec:whole-column-residual} identified as the one the old measure could
not see.

where they used to sit at $4.9\times10^{-4}$ to $9.9\times10^{-4}$. The old

Fifteen lines in fourteen canonical files, each with a
\texttt{\# Resid tol renormalized 2026-09-03, Update\_EXHALE.md section 133

places in \texttt{docs/EXHALE\_user\_manual.tex}. \textbf{932 further
\texttt{input.inp} files under \texttt{LHS1140b/exhale/} were NOT changed}:
they are stored records of past runs, paired with the outputs those tolerances
produced, and rewriting them would make each directory inconsistent with its
own result. Re-running one of them now asks for a tolerance 100 times looser
than intended, which is recorded here rather than repaired silently.

\subsection{What was measured}

Every steady solve below is the JFNK with both gates; the flux spread quoted is
the gate's own, at the accepted iterate.

\textbf{1. \texttt{jfnk\_hd189} reaches both gates.} \texttt{Resid tol: 1.0e-5}
(renormalized), direct PTC/JFNK route: \texttt{info = 0} at
$\|R\| = 9.340\times10^{-7}$ and flux spread $4.645\times10^{-3}$, in 520 outer
iterations. Under section~\ref{sec:layer-row-scales} the same state took 806
iterations to reach $9.915\times10^{-4}$ and its flux spread was
$2.1\times10^{-2}$ --- the solve now keeps working until the flux is flat, and
the extra work is what flattens it.

\textbf{2. \texttt{jfnk\_hd189\_tight} reaches the residual gate and not the
flux gate.} \texttt{Resid tol: 1.0e-6}: $\|R\|$ falls to
$2.830\times10^{-7}$, a factor 3.5 inside the target, and stops improving at
iteration $\sim$1500; the flux spread ends at $1.874\times10^{-2}$ and the
solve returns \texttt{info = 1} with the log naming the flux gate. \textbf{The
two gates pull apart at that depth on this planet}: the state that satisfies
the residual to $2.8\times10^{-7}$ is four times \emph{less} flux-flat than the
one that satisfies it to $9.3\times10^{-7}$. That is a property of

makes visible.

\textbf{3. The two restarts of section~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open} land

\subsection{The state the gates accept is the state that is written; the
file's ghost rows are what differed}
\label{sec:written-state-ghost-rows}

Section 133.5 recorded that the flux spread the solve accepted
($4.6\times10^{-3}$ on HD\,189733\,b) did not match the spread computed from
the written \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} ($1.0\times10^{-2}$), and left it open.
\textbf{The cause is not a state change. It is that the output file carries
ghost cells and the offline measurement counted them.}

\textbf{Nothing between the solve's return and the write touches \texttt{u}.}
Traced, file:line:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lp{7.4cm}}
\toprule
step & what it does to \texttt{u} \\
\midrule
\texttt{EXHALE\_main.f90:1593} \texttt{solve\_steady\_jfnk}
 (or \texttt{:1596} \texttt{solve\_steady\_ptc}) & returns the accepted \texttt{u} \\
\texttt{:1599} \texttt{U\_to\_W(u,W)}; \texttt{:1600} \texttt{rho,v,p,E} re-read
 & reads \texttt{u}; \texttt{rho}, \texttt{v} are \emph{derived from it} \\
\texttt{:1601} \texttt{get\_species\_densities}, \texttt{:1603}
 \texttt{comp\_T\_from\_p}, \texttt{:1604} \texttt{excited\_H\_update},
 \texttt{:1605} \texttt{ioniz\_eq}, \texttt{:1606}
 \texttt{get\_species\_densities} & composition, \texttt{heat}, \texttt{cool},
 \texttt{T}, \texttt{eta} only \\
\texttt{:1608}/\texttt{:1609} exit (no diffusion, no carriers) & --- \\
\texttt{:1169}--\texttt{:1171} \texttt{is\_mom\_const},
 \texttt{newton\_finished} & --- \\
rest of the marching-loop body to \texttt{:1260} & only the NaN scan reads
 \texttt{u(k,j)} \\
\texttt{:1262}--\texttt{:1449}
 (\texttt{contact\_mode\_dissipation\_magnitude},
 \texttt{excited\_H\_update}, \ldots) & read \texttt{u}; no assignment \\
\texttt{:1445} \texttt{write\_output(rho,v,p,\ldots)} & writes what
 \texttt{U\_to\_W(u)} gave \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

There is no hydro step after the Newton finish --- the RK stages are at
\texttt{:592}--\texttt{:760}, before it --- so $\rho v r^2$ cannot move, which
is what the physics says too.

\textbf{What did differ.} \texttt{write\_output.f90:101} writes
\texttt{do j = 1-Ng, N+Ng}: the file has $N+4$ rows with $N_g = 2$
\textbf{ghost cells at each end}. The upper two are filled by
\texttt{Apply\_BC} from a zero-gradient / WENO3 extrapolation, so their
$\rho v r^2$ is a boundary value, not part of the solution, and an offline
$r \ge 1.2$ selection over the raw file picks them up. Dropping them reproduces
the gate exactly:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
state & all file rows, $r\ge1.2$ & physical cells & the gate's value \\
\midrule
\texttt{jfnk\_hd189} & $1.0486\times10^{-2}$ & $\mathbf{4.6447\times10^{-3}}$ & $4.6447\times10^{-3}$ \\
\texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} & $2.3148\times10^{-3}$ & $\mathbf{1.8581\times10^{-3}}$ & $1.8581\times10^{-3}$ \\
He/H\,=\,1 reference & $3.5434\times10^{-3}$ & $\mathbf{3.5434\times10^{-3}}$ & $3.5434\times10^{-3}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The factor is state-dependent --- 2.3 on HD\,189733\,b, 1.25 on WASP-121b, 1.00
on the hot Uranus --- which is why it looked like a state change on the one case
it was first noticed on. \texttt{examples/exhale\_io.py} has no ghost handling
either, so every Python consumer of these files has the same trap.

\textbf{Both halves are closed, in the two places they belong.}

\emph{The file now says which rows are physical.} \texttt{write\_output} emits a
third \texttt{\#} header line,
%
\begin{lstlisting}
# rows 504: 2 ghost cells at each end; physical cells are rows 3 to 502
\end{lstlisting}
%
It is a comment, so no numeric parse and no golden changes
(\texttt{run\_check.sh} compares with \texttt{grep -v '\^{} *\#'}).

\emph{The run now asserts that the written state is the accepted one.}
\texttt{assert\_written\_state\_is\_the\_accepted\_one}
(\texttt{EXHALE\_main.f90:1545}) is called immediately after both final
\texttt{write\_output} calls --- \texttt{:475} on the direct steady route and
\texttt{:1450} on the marching route --- and re-measures the flux gate on the
state as written, printing it beside the value the solve accepted and warning
loudly if they differ:
%
\begin{lstlisting}
 (EXHALE_main) flux gate: accepted 4.6447E-03   as written 4.6447E-03
\end{lstlisting}
%
The table above is that line on the three states; none of them raised the
warning. The check is an assertion rather than a correction: the trace says the
two are the same object, and the line is what makes that a measured statement
on every run instead of a claim in a document. It costs one pass over the wind
window.

\textbf{What is asserted and what is not.} The flux gate is a function of
\texttt{u} alone, so the assertion is exact. $\|R\|$ is not: it depends on
\texttt{u} \emph{and} on the equilibrium composition, and \texttt{ioniz\_eq} is
called once more at \texttt{:1605} after the solve returns. That call re-solves
the same equilibrium at the same $(T,\rho)$, so the residual of the written
state is the accepted one to the ionization solver's own tolerance rather than
bit for bit. It is not re-evaluated here, because doing so costs a full extra
residual evaluation and would mutate \texttt{f\_sp} after the state has been
written.

\textbf{Checked.} \texttt{make check}, nine cases, single-threaded: 9/9
byte-identical --- the header line is a comment and the assertion is output
only. The three reference solves above were re-run end to end on this build:
\texttt{jfnk\_hd189} \texttt{info = 0}, \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton}
$\log_{10}\dot M = 13.21$, He/H\,=\,1 reference $\log_{10}\dot M = 10.31$, all
unchanged from section 133.4. \textbf{Not changed:}
\texttt{examples/exhale\_io.py} still returns the ghost rows to its callers.
Fixing it would change what every notebook and the transit tool see, which is
its own change with its own verification.

Files: \texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_residual.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_newton.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/init/parameters.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/init/define\_grid.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/input\_read.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/write\_setup\_report.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/write\_output.f90},
\texttt{src/EXHALE\_main.f90}.
Documentation: \texttt{docs/input\_schema.md}, \texttt{README\_HOWTO.md},
\texttt{docs/EXHALE\_user\_manual.tex}, \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} item (P42).



\section{The transported H$_2$ front was being carried by the scheme:
second-order limited advection, and a Lyman--Werner flux the run computes for
itself (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:carrier-second-order}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{Judgment first. The runaway H$_2$ front of
section~\ref{sec:molecular-carrier-transport} had two causes and the larger one
was ours. First-order donor-cell advection gave the carrier operator a
numerical diffusivity 8 to 22 times the molecular one at the front, and it was
pushing the front outward; second-order limited advection removes it and buys,
on a 500-cell grid, what doubling the grid bought. The missing Lyman--Werner
sink is real and is the second cause --- it is the \emph{dominant} sink where
the front now sits --- and it is no longer optional to know it: a run with a
numerical spectrum integrates its own band flux. With both fixed the front is
grid-converged to 0.2\% and nearly stationary. It is \emph{not} a steady state
yet, and the carrier transport stays default off until it is.}

\subsection{What was measured before anything was changed}

Two candidates were separated by controlled runs.

\textbf{The grid.} Two refinements were tried and only one of them is a test.
Refining the base region (\texttt{Base grid [dr,cells]: 1.0e-4 100}) halves the
smallest cell, which halves the global CFL step --- measured,
$\min \Delta r/(|v|+c_s)$ goes from 2.382\,s to 1.180\,s, a ratio 0.495 --- so
equal step counts are no longer equal physical times. Doubling the \emph{total}
cell count (\texttt{Grid cells: 1000}) leaves the base spacing alone: 2.428\,s
against 2.382\,s, ratio 1.019, so step counts \emph{are} comparable. That is
the test:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
\toprule
100000 steps, cold start, LW off & $f=0.5$ & $10^{-2}$ & $10^{-4}$ & $n({\rm H_3^+})>1$ \\
\midrule
first order, 500 cells   & 1.1658 & 1.2979 & \textbf{1.3967} & 1.2979 \\
first order, 1000 cells  & 1.1594 & 1.2211 & \textbf{1.2689} & 1.2252 \\
\textbf{second order, 500 cells} & 1.1641 & 1.2269 & \textbf{1.2468} & 1.2267 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The first-order 500-cell front sits $0.15\,R_p$ outside the resolved one, and
the second-order scheme on the coarse grid lands where the fine grid does. The
mechanism is not inferred: donor-cell carries $D_{\rm num} = |v|\Delta r/2$,
and against the molecular diffusivity of H$_2$ that is

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
 & $r=1.15$ & 1.30 & 1.50 \\
\midrule
$D_{\rm num}/D_{\rm H_2}$, 500 cells  & 8.5 & 20 & 22 \\
$D_{\rm num}/D_{\rm H_2}$, 1000 cells & 0.74 & 5.3 & 7.5 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

with $K_{zz}=0$ in these runs, so the molecular value is the whole of the
physical transport coefficient.

\textbf{Lyman--Werner.} It was off in every section-\ref{sec:molecular-carrier-transport}
run, and Frelikh \& Murray-Clay carry it always on. Switched on it roughly
halves the advance, but on the first-order grid it does not stop it. Its size
depends on where the front is, and that is why the first measurement of it was
misleading: in the \emph{runaway} states LW is 25--34\% of the He$^+$ channels,
because the front has reached low density where He$^+$ is abundant; in the
states where the front holds at $1.22\,R_p$ it is the dominant sink by 4 to 12
times.

\subsection{Second-order limited advection, by deferred correction}

The residual now carries, for $v \geq 0$,
\[
  \left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial r}\right|_j
   = \frac{f_j - f_{j-1}}{h} + \frac{\sigma_j - \sigma_{j-1}}{2},
\]
and its mirror image for $v<0$, with $\sigma$ a limited slope. On a linear
profile the two slopes cancel; on a quadratic they cancel the donor-cell
truncation term exactly. \textbf{With $\sigma = 0$ this is exactly the
first-order operator the module had}, on the same non-uniform spacing, so the
correction is attributable on its own.

$\sigma$ is \textbf{van Leer}, $2ab/(a+b)$, zero when the one-sided differences
disagree in sign. Not minmod, and the reason is about this solver rather than
about accuracy in general: minmod has a kink wherever $|a|=|b|$, and a kink in
the source of a Newton residual is the defect section~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape-open}
spent a campaign on, while van Leer is differentiable except at the sign change
--- and it is the less diffusive of the two.

\textbf{The correction is deferred}: $\sigma$ is frozen over one Newton solve
and refreshed at every transport step. That keeps the Jacobian
block-tridiagonal --- the correction reaches $j-2$ and $j+2$, which
\texttt{block\_thomas} cannot carry --- and keeps the residual smooth inside a
solve. At the fixed point of the marching loop, and of the fixed-wind
relaxation, consecutive steps agree, so the state the code converges to is the
second-order one. \texttt{block\_thomas} is untouched. Cell 1 keeps the
face-flux upwind of section~\ref{sec:molecular-carrier-transport} and carries no
correction.

\textbf{Order of accuracy, measured.} A Gaussian mixing ratio on the code's own
spacing convention, the discrete derivative against the analytic one in $L_1$
over the pulse, using the module's own \texttt{carrier\_slope}:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{rrrrr}
\toprule
$N$ & $L_1$ first order & $L_1$ corrected & $p$ first order & $p$ corrected \\
\midrule
 100 & $1.070\times10^{-1}$ & $1.834\times10^{-2}$ & --- & --- \\
 200 & $5.356\times10^{-2}$ & $4.786\times10^{-3}$ & 0.998 & \textbf{1.938} \\
 400 & $2.679\times10^{-2}$ & $1.229\times10^{-3}$ & 0.999 & \textbf{1.962} \\
 800 & $1.340\times10^{-2}$ & $3.122\times10^{-4}$ & 1.000 & \textbf{1.976} \\
1600 & $6.699\times10^{-3}$ & $7.886\times10^{-5}$ & 1.000 & \textbf{1.985} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The test lives in the campaign scratch directory as \texttt{unit/adv\_order.f90};
it is written in centimetres because \texttt{carrier\_slope} floors its spacing
at 1\,cm, the code's own units, and a test on a unit-length grid measures the
floor instead of the scheme.

\subsection{The Lyman--Werner band flux is now computed, not remembered}

H$_2$ photodissociation is not an option of the physics: the band exists
whenever the star does. What was optional was our knowing the number, and a run
with a numerical spectrum knows it.
\texttt{lyman\_werner\_band\_flux\_from\_sed} integrates the SED over
912--1110\,\AA{} and \texttt{input\_read} uses it when the run carries a
spectrum and states no \texttt{Stellar LW flux}. \textbf{A stated key always
wins}: it is the more specific statement, and a band-integrated measurement can
be better than a trapezoid over whatever grid the file happens to have.

\textbf{No dilution is applied, and that is not an omission.} EXHALE's own SED
file is at the planet --- \texttt{read\_sed}'s header says so --- while the
$(R_\star/a)^2$ step of the documented prescription belongs to the
stellar-surface files the value used to be produced from by hand. Both routes
were checked against each other: Gueymard's solar spectrum integrated over
91.2--111.0\,nm at the stellar surface and diluted to 0.048\,AU behind a
$1.155\,R_\odot$ star gives 328.96\,erg\,cm$^{-2}$\,s$^{-1}$ against the 343.0
the molecular cases carry, i.e.\ \textbf{the prescription reproduces its own
number to 4\%}. And the new routine against an independent integral of the
LHS~1140\,b spectrum: $5.980\times10^{-1}$ from the code against
$5.9796\times10^{-1}$, four significant figures.

With neither a key nor a spectrum the flux stays zero and the setup report says
what that means, because a silently absent channel is what the runaway was
partly made of.

\subsection{The two together, and what is left}

Cold start on the hot Uranus, the H$_2$ front at $f({\rm H_2}) = 10^{-4}$, with
the advance per 20000 steps in brackets:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
step & second order, LW off & 2nd order, LW on, 500 & 2nd order, LW on, 1000 \\
\midrule
 20000 & 1.2186 (0.0092) & 1.2134 ($-0.0141$) & 1.2157 ($-0.0065$) \\
 60000 & 1.2304 (0.0052) & 1.2168 (0.0034) & 1.2148 (0.0025) \\
100000 & 1.2458 (0.0091) & 1.2223 (0.0024) & 1.2199 (0.0023) \\
150000 & --- & \textbf{1.2300 (0.0034)} & \textbf{1.2275 (0.0033)} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{The front is grid-converged.} At 150000 steps the two grids put it at
1.2300 and $1.2275\,R_p$, 0.2\% apart, and they drift at the same physical
rate, 0.0034 against $0.0033\,R_p$ per 20000 steps. A residual motion that does
not change when the grid is halved is not a discretization artefact; it is the
state still relaxing, which $du$ agrees with at $3.1$--$3.3\times10^{-2}$ and
falling. LW's own share: at 100000 steps it holds the front $0.024\,R_p$
further in and cuts the advance rate by 3.8.

The sinks where the front now sits, on the final states
[cm$^{-3}$\,s$^{-1}$]:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrrr}
\toprule
run & $r$ & $T$ & $n({\rm H_2})$ & R17 & R20 & LW & LW/(R17+R20) \\
\midrule
LW on, 500  & 1.15 & 1029 & $1.93\times10^{11}$ & $2.62\times10^{2}$ & $2.80\times10^{1}$ & $1.75\times10^{3}$ & 6.0 \\
LW on, 500  & 1.22 & 986  & $5.18\times10^{8}$  & $5.49\times10^{2}$ & $7.46\times10^{1}$ & $5.26\times10^{3}$ & 8.4 \\
LW on, 1000 & 1.22 & 1046 & $3.45\times10^{8}$  & $5.40\times10^{2}$ & $5.27\times10^{1}$ & $7.00\times10^{3}$ & 11.8 \\
LW on, 500  & 1.30 & 925  & $5.38\times10^{5}$  & $7.74\times10^{0}$ & $1.54\times10^{0}$ & $3.72\times10^{1}$ & 4.0 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{What is not closed, and why the option stays off.} The front is nearly
stationary at about $1.23\,R_p$ but it is not stationary: 0.85 to 1.26 cells
per 20000 steps on the coarse grid, which is \emph{at} the stopping criterion
rather than below it. The wind is not steady either, and the steady solver
cannot finish it: restarted from the 150000-step state with
\texttt{Secondary\_ionization: Immediate} (the STAGED default reloads a
different state --- $du$ jumps from 0.03 to 9), the JFNK stalls at
$\|R\| = 2.78\times10^{-2}$ and exits \texttt{info = 2} with no descent along
either the Newton or the damped Gauss--Newton direction, and its worst cell is
\emph{the energy row at $r = 1.186$, inside the H$_2$ front}. That is the slow
mode of section~\ref{sec:whole-column-residual}, and neither change removes it.
It is now \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} item~(Y).

\subsection{What was checked}

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{make check}, nine cases: byte-identical. The carrier transport is
      off in all of them and no regression case carries a
      \texttt{Spectrum file}, so neither change can reach them --- which is why
      \texttt{backup/regression/mol\_carrier} now exists.
\item \texttt{examples/18\_oxygen\_chemistry}, 2000 steps, the transport
      \emph{on}: moved, as it must be. The base cell's H$_2$ partition goes
      from 0.5634 to 0.3634 of the H nuclei, base H$_2$O falls by about half,
      and $\log_{10}\dot M$ moves $+0.03$ dex. Eleven of twelve output files
      change; \texttt{IC\_dump.txt} does not.
\item The order-of-accuracy test above, and the two independent checks of the
      band integral.
\item NOT checked: the second-order operator on a \emph{converged} oxygen
      state. The \texttt{examples/18} comparison is a 2000-step snapshot from a
      cold start, so it is a direction and an order of magnitude.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{One line that belongs to every profile file, carried in one place.}
The row-layout header of section~133.6 --- \texttt{\# rows N: Ng ghost cells at
each end; physical cells are rows a to b} --- was written by
\texttt{Hydro\_ioniz(\_adv).txt} alone, which made it a property of one file
rather than of the convention, while \texttt{Ion\_species}, the cooling and
heating breakdowns, \texttt{Excited\_H}, \texttt{Lyman\_Werner},
\texttt{OI\_levels}, \texttt{Oxygen\_chemistry} and \texttt{FUV\_bands} span
the same ghost rows and said nothing. It is now
\texttt{write\_row\_layout\_header} in \texttt{utils}, called by all nine
writers and defined once. \texttt{residual\_profile.txt} and
\texttt{diffusion\_pass\_profiles.txt} do \emph{not} get it, because they write
$1{:}N$ and the sentence would be false there. The regression strips
\texttt{\#} lines, so this is byte-identical by construction and measured to
be.

Files: \texttt{src/modules/lower\_atmosphere/diffusive\_photochemistry.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/radiation/sed\_read.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/input\_read.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/write\_setup\_report.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/init/parameters.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/functions/utilities.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/write\_output.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/radiation/util\_ion\_eq.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/radiation/excited\_hydrogen.f90}.
Regression: \texttt{backup/regression/mol\_carrier}.
Documentation: \texttt{docs/molecular\_hydrogen\_treatment.tex},
\texttt{docs/input\_schema.md}, \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} items (P43) and (Y).
\section{The H$_2$ Lyman--Werner table was a rate for a sub-reservoir of
H$_2$ and it left out line overlap; the two errors had opposite signs and hid
each other (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:h2-shield-line-overlap}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{The judgement first.} Two independent errors sat in the H$_2$
photodissociation rate. The first made it too small, the second too large,
they crossed near $N_{\rm H_2} = 2\times10^{20}$~cm$^{-2}$, and below that
column they very nearly cancelled --- which is why neither showed up when the
table was built (Sec.~\ref{sec:h2-shield-table}) or when it was turned into an
absolute cross section (Sec.~\ref{sec:lw-cross-section-sources}). Both are now
gone: the table is rebuilt from a line-by-line calculation in which every
Lyman and Werner line absorbs every other line's beam, and it is a rate for
\textbf{all} H$_2$ rather than for the part of it \textsc{cloudy} calls H2g.

\subsection{Error one: the tabulated rate belonged to a sub-reservoir}

\textsc{cloudy} splits H$_2$ into two chemical species at
\texttt{ENERGY\_H2\_STAR}, set to \textbf{$4100$~cm$^{-1}$} ($5899$~K) where
the H$_2$ model is constructed (\texttt{h2.cpp:10},
\texttt{diatomics h2("h2", 4100., ...)}): \textbf{H2g} is $v = 0$, $J \le 8$
--- the top of it, $(0,8)$, is at $4051.9$~cm$^{-1}$ --- and \textbf{H2s} is
every level above. \texttt{H2\_Solomon\_rate} accumulates the dissociation of
the two separately and divides each by its \textbf{own} density
(\texttt{mole\_h2\_etc.cpp:60-92},
\texttt{Solomon\_dissoc\_rate\_g /= SDIV(H2\_den\_g)}), and the
\texttt{Shield(H2)} column that Sec.~\ref{sec:h2-shield-table} tabulated is
\texttt{Solomon\_dissoc\_rate\_g/G(TH85)} (\texttt{mole\_h2\_io.cpp:1580}).
EXHALE carries one H$_2$ species and applied that rate to all of it.

The two are not interchangeable at depth. The H2s lines start from levels
$100$ to $1000$ times less populated, are therefore far less saturated, and
keep dissociating long after the H2g lines have gone black:
\texttt{Solomon\_dissoc\_rate\_s/}\allowbreak\texttt{Solomon\_dissoc\_rate\_g}
reaches
\textbf{$165$ ($1300$~K) and $615$ ($900$~K) at
$N_{\rm H_2} = 10^{19}$}. Weighting the two by their densities --- read from
the runs, not assumed --- raises the tabulated factor by

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r r r r@{}}
\hline
$N_{\rm H_2}$ [cm$^{-2}$] & $900$~K & $1300$~K & $1800$~K & $2700$~K\\
\hline
$10^{17}$          & $1.24$ & $1.94$ & $2.98$ & $4.16$\\
$10^{18}$          & $2.15$ & $3.94$ & $6.16$ & $9.27$\\
$10^{19}$          & $2.43$ & $4.15$ & $6.89$ & $11.10$\\
$10^{20}$          & $1.60$ & $2.42$ & $3.51$ & $5.34$\\
$10^{21}$          & $1.23$ & $1.49$ & $1.78$ & $2.34$\\
$4.4\times10^{21}$ & $1.12$ & $1.27$ & $1.42$ & $1.73$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{At the illuminated face the correction is $+0.02$ per cent ($700$~K)
rising to $+12.7$ per cent ($3200$~K)}, so the $0.5$ per cent agreement with
Draine \& Bertoldi's Table~1--2 normalization that
Sec.~\ref{sec:lw-cross-section-sources} rests on --- measured at $100$~K,
where H2s is empty to five digits --- is untouched. It is the depth dependence
that was wrong.

\textbf{How it was found.} Two calculations that shield one line at a time,
the Meudon PDR code with \texttt{f\_ShieldAlgo = 0} and a line-by-line
calculation written for the purpose, agreed with each other to $15$--$35$ per
cent at $100$~K and at $1300$~K and both sat $5$--$9\times$ \textbf{above} the
table over $10^{19} \le N_{\rm H_2} \le 10^{21}$. The reservoir split accounts
for essentially all of it: with the weighting undone the table reproduces the
line-by-line no-overlap branch to \textbf{$1$--$4$ per cent up to
$N_{\rm H_2} = 10^{17}$} and $28$--$36$ per cent at $10^{18}$.

\subsection{Error two: line overlap, which is the dominant term at our
columns}

\textsc{cloudy} applies the Federman, Glassgold \& Kwan (1979) shielding
function to each transition using that transition's own optical depth; nothing
couples one line to another. Draine \& Bertoldi's sec.~5.2 say overlap is what
produces ``the rapid falloff \ldots\ for $N_2 > 10^{20}$~cm$^{-2}$'', and at
the columns of a molecular base it is not a correction. Two calculations
differing \textbf{only} in whether the lines absorb each other's beam give

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r r r r@{}}
\hline
$N_{\rm H_2}$ [cm$^{-2}$] & $900$~K & $1300$~K & $1800$~K & $2700$~K\\
\hline
$10^{19}$          & $0.73$   & $0.62$   & $0.47$    & $0.30$\\
$10^{20}$          & $0.45$   & $0.33$   & $0.22$    & $0.096$\\
$10^{21}$          & $0.080$  & $0.042$  & $0.019$   & $0.0040$\\
$4.4\times10^{21}$ & $0.0047$ & $0.0016$ & $0.00056$ & $0.000048$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

i.e.\ a factor $24$ at $10^{21}$ and $630$ at the $4.4\times10^{21}$ of the
base, at $1300$~K. Sec.~\ref{sec:h2-shield-table} knew the table was an upper
bound above \texttt{h2\_shielding\_overlap\_column} and said so; what it could
not know is that the boundary was about a decade optimistic --- at the column
that function returned, the table already stood $7$ to $10$ times above the
overlapping-line answer.

\subsection{What the table is now}

The table is now \texttt{h2\_self\_shielding\_table.f90} in
\texttt{src/modules/}\allowbreak\texttt{lower\_atmosphere/}, generated by the
new \texttt{h2\_shielding\_table\_}\allowbreak\texttt{line\_by\_line.py} in
\texttt{src/utils/}. Same three quantities on the same grid ($39$ columns $\times$ $9$ temperatures
$\times$ $3$ densities), same axes, same accessors ---
\texttt{h2\_lw\_dissociation\_}\allowbreak\texttt{cross\_section},
\texttt{h2\_lw\_dissociation\_}\allowbreak\texttt{per\_pump},
\texttt{h2\_lw\_dissociation\_}\allowbreak\texttt{per\_absorbed\_photon},
\texttt{h2\_self\_shielding\_}\allowbreak\texttt{level\_resolved}. The physics
behind each number changed:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{$\sigma_{\rm pump}$ and $p_{\rm single}$ are line-by-line, with
  overlap.} Plane-parallel slab, normally incident beam, flat $F_\lambda$
  normalized to $F = 343$~erg~cm$^{-2}$~s$^{-1}$ over $912$--$1110$~\AA,
  $\tau(\nu, N) = N \sum_i x_i \sigma_i(\nu)$ summed over every Lyman and
  Werner transition between $911.75$ and $1200$~\AA\ on a
  $4\times10^{5}$-point frequency grid, Voigt profiles with
  $b = (2kT/m_{\rm H_2})^{1/2}$, LTE populations. The line data are Abgrall,
  Roueff \& Drira (2000) --- the same measurements \textsc{cloudy}'s
  \texttt{dissprob\_*}/\texttt{transprob\_*} files and the Meudon PDR code
  carry, so no line-list difference enters.
\item \textbf{The fluorescent trapping is still \textsc{cloudy}'s.}
  $p_{\rm eff}/p_{\rm single}$ is read node by node from the same $27$ runs
  and multiplied in. Reimplementing \textsc{cloudy}'s escape probabilities
  would be a second, unvalidated version of the same thing. \textbf{Its
  geometry is plane-parallel, illuminated on one face and closed on the
  other}; our layer has the same thick-inward side, which is the side that
  matters, but it is spherical and open outward. That is the one ingredient of
  the table carrying a geometry our layer does not have, and it is a new item
  of \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md}.
\item \textbf{\texttt{h2\_shielding\_}\allowbreak\texttt{overlap\_column} is
  gone}, and with it the
  \texttt{h2\_shield\_}\allowbreak\texttt{log\_col\_overlap} plane. There is no longer a
  column above which the value stops meaning anything, because overlap is
  inside it. \texttt{h2\_shield\_max\_column()} replaces it: the top of the
  tabulated column axis, $5.0\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-2}$, above which the edge
  value is returned. The two run-time warnings that quoted the old boundary
  now report that extrapolation instead.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Verification}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The line-by-line calculation against a published
  overlap-including curve.} At $100$~K it reproduces the Draine \& Bertoldi
  (1996) self-shielding function to \textbf{$2$--$9$ per cent over
  $10^{16} \le N_{\rm H_2} \le 10^{21}$}, and its no-overlap branch departs
  from DB96 exactly where DB96 say overlap sets in ($3.3\times$ at $10^{21}$,
  $12\times$ at $4.4\times10^{21}$).
\item \textbf{Against a second code that carries overlap.} The Meudon PDR code
  (Le Petit et al.\ 2006) run with \texttt{f\_ShieldAlgo = 1}, its exact UV
  line transfer --- $30$ H$_2$ levels in full transfer, $20$ global
  iterations, pure H/He at $n_{\rm H} = 10^{13}$~cm$^{-3}$ --- agrees to
  \textbf{$5$--$22$ per cent over $10^{19} \le N_{\rm H_2} \le 10^{21}$} at
  $900$, $1300$ and $1800$~K.
\item \textbf{Absolute quantities.} $\sigma_{\rm pump}$ at the bottom of the
  column axis is $2.59\times10^{-17}$ ($700$~K) to $2.88\times10^{-17}$~cm$^2$
  ($3200$~K) against DB96's own
  $3.4520\times10^{-18}/0.135 = 2.557\times10^{-17}$ ($1$--$13$ per cent);
  $p_{\rm single}$ there is $0.1425$ to $0.1592$, and at $1300$~K it is
  $0.1475$ against \textbf{$0.1465$} from the \textsc{cloudy} runs ($0.7$ per
  cent); $\sigma_{\rm diss}$ there agrees with the H2g-corrected
  \textsc{cloudy} table to \textbf{$1.3$--$3.6$ per cent}, which is the
  statement that the two differ in the shielding and not in the normalization.
\item \textbf{The trapping factor that came from \textsc{cloudy}} is
  $1.13$--$1.38$ at the \emph{bottom} of the column axis
  ($N_{\rm H_2} = 10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$, the optically thin end) across the whole
  grid, reproducing the $1.15$--$1.37$
  Sec.~\ref{sec:lw-cross-section-sources} records at the illuminated face, and
  it rises to $1.25$--$3.07$ at the top of the axis,
  $5\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-2}$.
\item \textbf{Fortran against Python} at all $1053$ grid points: max relative
  difference \textbf{$3.1\times10^{-9}$} on $\sigma_{\rm diss}$,
  $8.4\times10^{-10}$ on $p_{\rm single}$, $9.6\times10^{-10}$ on
  $p_{\rm eff}$.
\item \textbf{Regression, both stages, in a scratch copy of the tree first.}
  The baseline reproduces the goldens 9/9 byte-identical. With the H2g
  weighting alone, and again with the overlapping-line table, \textbf{exactly
  one case moves, \texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner}, and the other eight are
  byte-identical} --- which is the structural statement the change should
  make, since \texttt{F\_LW\_star} defaults to zero and one matrix case
  supplies it. Sizes ($12000$-step relaxation snapshots, so not converged
  change sizes):
\end{itemize}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.36\linewidth} r r r@{}}
\hline
quantity & golden & H2g weighting & $+$ overlapping lines\\
\hline
H$_2$ front, largest $r$ with $n_{\rm H_2} > 10^{10}$
  & $1.146163\,R_{\rm p}$ & $1.142513$ & $1.144327$\\
$f_{\rm shield}$ at the deepest cell
  & --- & $8.165\times10^{-6}$ & $1.716\times10^{-7}$\\
$n({\rm H_2})$ over the golden molecular cells
  & $1$ & $0.150$--$1.0005$ & $0.147$--$1.013$\\
\texttt{final} du
  & $2.6075$ & $2.7629$ & $2.7689$\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\medskip

\noindent The front barely moves while the deepest cell's shielding falls
$48\times$, because the front sits at moderate columns where the two errors
nearly cancel and the deep cells are already almost fully molecular.

\medskip

\noindent \textbf{Which gate these were measured on.} The four rows above are
the 9~microbar hot-Uranus gate, the one the goldens were written against.
Re-running the matrix in the tree afterwards gives a larger move --- H$_2$
front $1.064744\,R_{\rm p}$, $N_{\rm H_2}$ reaching $2.877\times10^{20}$
rather than $4.296\times10^{21}$ --- and none of that difference is the table:
section~136 re-pinned the \texttt{base.inp} of the six hot-Uranus cases to
\texttt{p\_base 1.0e-06}, \texttt{q\_H2\_base 0.84}, i.e.\ a 1~microbar base,
and the molecular layer above a 1~microbar gate is an order of magnitude
thinner to begin with. The two sets of numbers are therefore not to be
compared with each other, and neither needs re-running: this section's are the
change in the table at fixed gate, and the tree's are the same table on the
gate section~136 installed.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Goldens were NOT refreshed.} \texttt{make check} reports FAIL on
  \texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner} by design; the refresh is a separate decision.
\item \textbf{\textsc{cloudy} was patched a second time} to make the reservoir
  weighting possible: four more columns of \texttt{save h2 rates}
  (\texttt{pump\_s}, \texttt{diss\_single\_s}, \texttt{den\_g},
  \texttt{den\_s}), the H2s counterparts of the four
  Sec.~\ref{sec:lw-cross-section-sources} added. The $27$ decks were re-run
  with it; nothing else about them changed.
\end{itemize}

Files:

\section{The base level was stated twice and the two statements disagreed
everywhere; \texttt{p\_base} now fixes it, and the hot-Uranus gate moves to
$1$~$\mu$bar (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:base-level-one-source}
% ===================================================================== %
\textbf{The judgement first.} The lower boundary is one level, and EXHALE let
two inputs state it independently: \texttt{Log10 lower boundary number density}
in \texttt{input.inp}, and \texttt{p\_base} in a \texttt{base.inp} handoff.
Nothing compared them. Every one of the $52$ \texttt{base.inp} files in this
tree that carries \texttt{p\_base} disagreed with its own density key --- the
hot-Uranus gate by $10\%$, the He/H ladder by $1.4$--$55\%$, the
\texttt{vulcan\_work} HD~209458\,b runs by factors of $7$ to $32$. The key had
never actually located the base level anywhere. \texttt{p\_base} now fixes the
level, the pair is refused when it disagrees by more than $1\%$, and the
hot-Uranus gate moves to the $1$~$\mu$bar level its own base radius already
corresponded to.

\subsection{What was wrong}

\texttt{docs/p44\_base\_sawtooth.md} (Secs.~8 and 9 there) arrived at this from
the other end. The hot-Uranus gate carries a base velocity artifact at cell~1
($v(1) \approx -250$~cm\,s$^{-1}$, a first-order-in-$dr$ boundary
discretization error) whose effect on the base-face mass flux scales with the
base density: $-21$, $-203$ and $-589$ times the wind flux at base pressures of
$1$, $9$ and $28$~$\mu$bar. On the default $9$~$\mu$bar base the converged
molecular layer is not even reproducible across restart cycles --- three
\texttt{info = 0} states of the same configuration put the H$_2$ front anywhere
in $1.053$--$1.089\,R_{\rm p}$. At $1$~$\mu$bar the same configuration
reproduces the front to five digits, converges from a cold start in
$27$~minutes where the $9$~$\mu$bar base did not converge in $1$~h~$41$~m, and
leaves $\log_{10}\dot M$ where it was.

And $1$~$\mu$bar is where that gate's boundary belongs. Koskinen et al.\ (2022,
ApJ 929, 52, Sec.~3.2) state their lower boundary as

\begin{quote}
``The lower boundary of the model is at r0 = 1.34Rp (p0 = 10$^{-6}$ bar,
T0 = 1,140 K) where the boundary conditions are consistent with our models of
the lower and middle atmosphere''
\end{quote}

\noindent and $1.34\,R_{\rm 1bar} = 3.425\times10^{9}$~cm with their
$R_{\rm 1bar} = 2.5559\times10^{9}$~cm is the gate's own
\texttt{Planet radius: 0.49 R\_J} $= 3.4256\times10^{9}$~cm, to $0.2\%$. The
gate had the right radius and the wrong pressure at it, because $n_0 = 10^{14}$
was chosen by hand.

The earlier reading, that $T_0 = 1140$~K was a $1$~$\mu$bar value applied nine
times deeper along a falling profile, is \textbf{withdrawn}: the same paper's
Sec.~2.2 says their lower and middle atmosphere is isothermal at the effective
temperature, so $1140$~K is their number at any depth below their boundary. The
inconsistency was never the temperature.

\subsection{What changed}

\textbf{\texttt{input\_read.f90}.} A \texttt{base.inp} carrying \texttt{p\_base}
is a handoff written \textsc{at} that pressure --- its composition, its $q_{\rm
H_2}$ and its temperature all refer to that level --- so the level is the
handoff's to state, and
%
\begin{equation}
n_0 = \frac{p_{\rm base}}{k_{\rm B} T_0\, n_{\rm tot,bc}},
\end{equation}
%
the relation \texttt{Base BC: pressure} already used. Three refusals go with it:
%
\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{Log10 lower boundary number density} is now \textbf{optional}.
      Given alongside \texttt{p\_base}, the two must agree to $1\%$; otherwise
      startup stops and prints both pressures, the ratio, the $n_0$ each
      implies, $n_{\rm tot,bc}$, and the two ways to fix it (delete one or the
      other).
\item \texttt{p\_base} and \texttt{Base BC: pressure} together must name the
      same level to round-off, or startup stops.
\item Neither given: startup stops and lists the three keys that can state it.
\end{itemize}
%
A lower-atmosphere \textbf{profile} sets \texttt{p\_base\_bar} from its own
matching pressure, so a profile run owns the level itself and is outside the
rule (\texttt{lower\_profile} stays byte-identical).

\textbf{\texttt{write\_setup\_report.f90}} gained one line naming the source and
both numbers:
%
\begin{lstlisting}[basicstyle=\ttfamily\footnotesize]
 - Base level: p =  1.0000E-06 bar (from base.inp p_base) -> n0 =  1.1690E+13 cm^-3
 - Base level: n0 =  3.0903E+12 cm^-3 (from the density key) -> p =  1.0069E-06 bar
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{The gate and the diagnostic cases.} The six molecular regression cases and the
sixteen diagnostic cases now carry \texttt{p\_base 1.000e-06} with the density
key deleted from \texttt{input.inp}, and the gate's \texttt{q\_H2\_base} becomes
\textbf{$0.84$} --- the same paper's value at the same level (Sec.~3.2: ``The
volume mixing ratio of H2 at the lower boundary is about q0 = 0.84 while H is a
minor species with q0 = 0.026''), which sits at $97.3\%$ of the ceiling
$0.5/(0.5 + {\rm He/H}) = 0.863110651$ this He/H can supply. The He/H ladder
keeps its own rule --- hold the fraction of H nuclei bound into H$_2$ fixed and
vary only He/H --- so its values were recomputed from
$x_2 = 2q(1+{\rm He/H})/(1+q) = 0.985447826$ (it was $0.925114286$):

\begin{center}

\subsection{What it moves}

\texttt{make check}: \texttt{wasp\_full}, \texttt{wasp\_he23off} and
\texttt{lower\_profile} \textbf{PASS, data identical} --- they carry no
\texttt{p\_base}, so the code path is untouched, and this was also confirmed
directly by building the same source snapshot with and without the change and
running all three cases with both binaries. The six molecular cases
\textbf{FAIL, i.e.\ move}, which is the point; the row count is unchanged
($504$), so the goldens are re-snapshotted rather than restructured, and there
is no NaN in any of them.

The base is $8.6$ times lighter, the H$_2$ column falls to $7$--$10\%$ of what
it was, the front moves in by $0.08$--$0.09\,R_{\rm p}$, and $\dot M$ falls by
$0.04$--$0.16$~dex. All of it follows from putting the base nine times higher;
no physics changed.

The $12000$-step snapshot convention survives the move: at the same $12000$
steps the retargeted gate reaches a \emph{smaller} $du$ ($2.56$ against $3.75$
on \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff}, $2.23$ against $4.68$ on \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion})
and runs faster ($5$~m~$35$~s against $6$~m~$59$~s single-threaded), so the
lighter base costs it no physical time.

\subsection{What this does not fix, and one thing it exposes}

The cell-1 velocity artifact itself is unchanged in magnitude --- it is a
first-order-in-$dr$ discretization error and only base refinement removes it.
What the lighter base removes is its \emph{consequence}: the base-face
mass-flux error falls with $\rho_{\rm bc}$, from $203$ to $21$ times the wind
flux.

The $30$ \texttt{base.inp} files under \texttt{vulcan\_work/} were \textbf{not}
retargeted --- they are records of past VULCAN comparison runs, not part of the
matrix --- but each of them states a \texttt{p\_base} that is wrong by a factor
of $7$ to $32$ against the level its density key actually used, and each will
now be refused if it is re-run. That is a finding about those runs.

\section{The output readers returned the file's ghost rows as solution cells;
the transit depths move by up to $3.8$ per cent (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:python-ghost-rows}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{The judgement first.} Every Python consumer of an EXHALE
profile was reading the file's boundary rows as if the solver had converged
them, and that is wrong whatever it costs: the two rows at each end are a fixed
base state below and a zero-gradient / WENO3 extrapolation above, both written
by \texttt{Apply\_BC}. Sec.~\ref{sec:written-state-ghost-rows} closed the
Fortran half of this by making the file say which rows are physical; this
closes the Python half. \texttt{examples/exhale\_io.py} now returns the
physical cells and takes \texttt{ghost=True} for the file as written, and
\texttt{EXHALE\_transit.py} and \texttt{EXHALE\_plots.py}, which bypassed the
reader with their own \texttt{np.loadtxt} calls, go through it. Item (P48) of
\texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} closes with this.

\subsection{The rule, and why the fallback is not a legacy path}

\texttt{exhale\_io.physical\_cell\_rows} has two ways of knowing, in order.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The header, which is the contract.} Since
  Sec.~\ref{sec:written-state-ghost-rows} the writer emits
  \texttt{\# rows 504: 2 ghost cells at each end; physical cells are rows 3 to
  502} (1-based, inclusive). It is a comment, so no numeric parse changes.
\item \textbf{The layout}, for a file written before that header existed --- the
  regression goldens and every saved \texttt{output*/} directory.
  $N_{\rm g} = 2$ is a Fortran \texttt{parameter} and every writer loops
  \texttt{1-Ng..N+Ng}, so two rows at each end are ghosts unconditionally, for
  every grid type. What the file can still be asked is whether it has that
  layout at all, and the base radius answers it: \texttt{define\_grid} puts a
  cell center exactly at $r = 1$ and that center is a \emph{ghost} ---
  \texttt{r(1-Ng) = 1} for the \texttt{Uniform} and \texttt{Stretched} grids,
  \texttt{r(2-Ng) = 1} for \texttt{Mixed} --- so $r = 1$ falls on row 1 or row 2
  and never later. A file whose radius column increases monotonically and
  equals 1 to roundoff at row 1 or row 2 has the ghost layout, and two rows come
  off each end. Checked against all $9214$ profile files in this working copy:
  every one satisfies it. A file that satisfies neither rule is returned whole
  with a warning, which is the pre-2026-09 behavior.
\end{enumerate}

The two routes were checked against each other on
\texttt{backup/regression/mol\_}\allowbreak\texttt{diffusion/output/Hydro\_ioniz.txt},
which has the header: with the header line removed the layout rule returns the
same $(2, 502)$ and the same $500$ rows.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The fallback is not a legacy path.} \texttt{write\_output}
emits the \texttt{\# rows} header for \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz(\_adv).txt}
\emph{only}; \texttt{Ion\_species}, \texttt{Cooling\_breakdown},
\texttt{Heating\_breakdown}, \texttt{Excited\_H}, \texttt{Lyman\_Werner} and
\texttt{OI\_levels} carry no such line even in a run made today, so they take
rule 2 on every read. Giving the other writers the same header is a one-line
change per file in \texttt{write\_output.f90} / \texttt{util\_ion\_eq.f90} /
\texttt{excited\_hydrogen.f90} and is left as an open item --- the Fortran was
not touched here.

\subsection{What it changes, measured}

The mechanism is at the top of the domain. The transit integrates chords out to
$R_{\rm ib} = \min(r_{\rm last}, R_\star/R_{\rm p})$, so dropping the two upper
ghost rows shrinks the outermost annulus, and the area lost is
$(r_{\rm top,phys}/r_{\rm top,ghost})^2 - 1$: $-1.04$ per cent on WASP-121b,
$-4.6$ per cent on HD~189733~b and $-3.6$ per cent on the hot Uranus. That is
the size of the effect, not a prediction of it: a line opaque all the way to the
boundary loses the whole annulus, one that is not loses part of it, and the
lower-level column densities change with the same two rows.

\noindent \texttt{backup/regression/jfnk\_hd189} is the state

\noindent\textbf{Largest single move: the hot Uranus Ly$\alpha$ line center,
$-3.81$ per cent.} Two further numbers the run prints move by more than the
depths do: the peak $n = 2$ hydrogen density of the hot Uranus falls from
$1.794\times10^{5}$ to $2.693\times10^{4}\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$ (a factor $6.7$ ---
the maximum sat in the lower ghost row, in the fixed base state, behind the
planetary disk, which is why the H$\alpha$ depth barely notices), and the
He 10830 red-peak depth of the same state goes from $8.989$ to $8.812$ per
cent. \texttt{EXHALE\_plots.py} on the same states shows the change as an axis
range: the radial axis now starts at the first physical cell, and on the hot
Uranus the ion-density panel loses the two decades of empty base ghost that
used to set the bottom of its logarithmic scale. The curves themselves lie on
top of each other.

\noindent \texttt{mdot\_log10} was fixed at the same time and for the same
reason. The Fortran evaluates the mass-loss rate at the physical cell
$j = N - 20$ (\texttt{EXHALE\_main.f90:1514}); the reader evaluated it at index
\texttt{len(r) - 20} of an array that still held the ghost rows, i.e.\ three
cells further out. It is now \texttt{len(r) - 1 - j\_from\_top} of the
ghost-free array, the same cell the run reports. On the WASP-121b state both
give $\log_{10}\dot{M} = 13.2224$ --- the mass flux is flat there, which is what
the convergence gate asserts --- so this is a correctness fix with no measured
effect on that state.

\subsection{Every consumer, and the two that would have double-counted the fix}

Eighteen files besides the reader itself name \texttt{exhale\_io}; seventeen
import it (\texttt{LHS1140b/make\_memo\_figures.py} only mentions it in a
comment). Going through the reader, they pick the change up automatically ---
but two of them cut the ghost rows a second time and one mixed the two
conventions:

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{src/utils/collisional\_validity.py} held its own
  \texttt{N\_GHOST = 2} and applied \texttt{slice(N\_GHOST, -N\_GHOST)} to what
  \texttt{load\_run} returned. Both the constant and the slice are gone; the
  Knudsen diagnosis now runs on the $500$ cells it meant to. Its
  $\log_{10}\dot{M}$ for the WASP-121b state reads $13.222$, the run's own
  value.
\item \texttt{LHS1140b/exhale/metastable\_step\_diagnosis/knudsen\_scale.py}
  sliced with \texttt{CV.N\_GHOST} for the same reason; removed.
\item \texttt{LHS1140b/heh\_series/audit\_checks.py} read \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz},
  \texttt{Ion\_species} and the two breakdown files with a bare
  \texttt{np.loadtxt} and compared them column by column with the ion densities
  \texttt{exhale\_io.load\_ions} returned. After the change those are $504$ rows
  against $500$ and its charge-neutrality check raises \texttt{IndexError}; it
  now reads all four through \texttt{exhale\_io.loadtxt\_cells}, and runs.
\item \texttt{poster/make\_poster\_figs.py} read one
  \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz\_adv.txt} directly while importing the reader for
  everything else; it goes through \texttt{loadtxt\_cells}.
\end{itemize}

Not changed, deliberately: \texttt{LHS1140b/make\_memo\_figures.py} reads
profiles with about twenty bare \texttt{np.loadtxt} calls and never imports the
reader, so nothing there breaks and nothing there is corrected either --- its
figures still include the ghost rows. Whether to convert it is tied to re-making
the LHS~1140~b memo figures, which is its own decision.

\subsection{What was checked, and what was not}

Checked: the two selection routes against each other and against all $9214$
profile files in the working copy; the three transit runs above, end to end,
before and after; \texttt{EXHALE\_plots.py} on two of them;
\texttt{src/utils/collisional\_validity.py} and
\texttt{LHS1140b/heh\_series/audit\_checks.py} run to completion after the fix.

Not checked, and not run: \texttt{examples/make\_figures.py} and the figures
under \texttt{docs/figures/}, every notebook, and the paper and poster figure
scripts. All of them read through the reader
(\texttt{make\_poster\_figs.py} now included), so their output \emph{will} move
by the amounts tabulated above the next time they are made; nothing under
\texttt{docs/figures/} was regenerated here. No Fortran source was touched, so
\texttt{make check} and the goldens are untouched by this change.
