\section{The Newton direction at the H$_2$ front pointed uphill because the
residual is discontinuous there: the positivity guard was a switch, and it is
now a limiter (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:continuous-positivity-limiter}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{The judgement first, and it retires item (Y) by contradicting
both of the causes that item proposed.} The energy row at the front is smooth
in the temperature: its finite-difference directional derivative converges to
six digits over four decades of step size, a two-sided scan of it is
antisymmetric down to $h = 10^{-9}$, and the residual's effective
$\mathrm{d}\ln\mathrm{cool}/\mathrm{d}\ln T$ there is $0.26$, not an
exponential. What has no descent direction is the state as a whole, because
$F(Y)$ is genuinely \emph{discontinuous} at the iterate. The WENO3
reconstruction at the face of cell 273 ($r = 1.2324\,R_{\rm p}$) returned a left
density of $2.50\times10^{-15}$ against cell averages of $10^{-4}$ --- eleven
orders below, and still positive by a hair --- so the iterate sat exactly on the
switching surface of \texttt{positivity\_limited\_faces}. Raising the density of
the neighbouring cell by one part in $10^{9}$ tipped that face through zero, the
guard replaced the whole face pair by the first-order cell averages, the face
density jumped by a factor $1.7\times10^{9}$, and the merit jumped from $202.5$
to $945.1$ --- by the \emph{same} factor $4.67$ at every step size from
$10^{-2}$ to $10^{-9}$, which is what a jump looks like and what a slope does
not. Every direction the solver could build put its largest scaled component at
that face, so every one of them ascended: the Newton/PTC step at all six decades
of damping and all ten damped Gauss--Newton steps, by factors $4.7$ to $27.8$.
The escape of Sec.~\ref{sec:jfnk-ascent-escape} was not defeated by an indefinite
Jacobian; it was asked to descend a function that is not continuous. The guard
is now the continuous limiter of Zhang \& Shu (2010), and a trial state whose
chemistry the equilibrium sweep could not certify is refused the way
Sec.~\ref{sec:steady-probe-hygiene} refuses one it cannot describe at all. On the
reproduction case the abort is gone: it is printed once in a whole run instead
of ending every hand-off, and the solve that used to stop at
$\lVert R\rVert = 2.775\times10^{-2}$ having excavated a $65\,000$~K hole in the
layer now meets the residual gate at $2.95\times10^{-6}$ and is held only by the
flux gate.

\medskip
This closes item (Y) of \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md}. The full measurement is
\texttt{docs/}\allowbreak\texttt{p49\_front\_energy\_mode.md}.

\subsection{What the measurement found, and what it ruled out}

Everything below is on the hot Uranus of Sec.~\ref{sec:carrier-second-order}
--- 500 cells, second-order carrier advection,
\texttt{Stellar LW flux: 343.0}, 150\,000 marching steps, restarted with
\texttt{Secondary\_ionization: Immediate} and \texttt{Solver: Newton 4.0e-2} ---
reproduced to every printed digit of item (Y): \texttt{info = 2} at
$\lVert R\rVert = 2.775\times10^{-2}$, worst cell $j = 255$,
$\lVert\nabla\,\mathrm{merit}\rVert = 4.583\times10^{11}$, 46 non-monotone
accepts.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The blocking row, term by term.} At the abort the worst
\emph{scaled} energy residual is cell 259, $r = 1.1952$, at $|R|/D = 67.6$. Its
row is $R_3 = \mathrm{d}F_E - (\mathrm{heat} - \mathrm{cool})$ with
$\mathrm{cool}$ at $97.7\%$ of $|R_3|$; from \texttt{Cooling\_breakdown.txt} at
that state, $93\%$ of that cooling is H$_3^+$ infrared emission at
$65\,173$~K, from an $f(\mathrm{H_3^+}) = 4.5\times10^{-3}$ the chemical solve
did not certify (acceptance class 4, reaction residual $2.4\times10^{-3}$).
H$_3^+$ does not survive at $65\,000$~K. Cells 256--259 sit exactly at the
radiative/advective transition, $E/|\mathrm{heat}-\mathrm{cool}|$ over
$\mathrm{d}r/|v|$ = $0.75$, $0.65$, $0.97$, $0.63$; from cell 260 outward the
class-4 acceptance sets $n(\mathrm{H_3^+}) = x(\mathrm{H\,II}) = 0$ exactly, the
cooling collapses by five orders and the ratio is $715$ to $2319$.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Candidate (a) of item (Y), the temperature entering through
$n_{\rm tot}$: real, and not the blocker.} Scanning the energy unknown of cell
259 alone in steps of $10^{-3}$ relative, the accepted composition does jump
between two branches at isolated points --- $x(\mathrm{H\,II}) = 0$ exactly,
$f(\mathrm{H_3^+})$ a factor 38 lower, the reaction residual from
$3.2\times10^{-3}$ to $1.4\times10^{-5}$ --- and returns in between, which is
seed-dependent root selection rather than a threshold. The energy row does not
notice: \texttt{cool} reads $1.0859\times10^{-2}$ on the jumped points against
$1.0857\times10^{-2}$ on the trend.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Candidate (b), the H$_3^+$ and H$_2$ rates: measured, and it is
the residual that cannot see them.} On the same scan \texttt{cool} has
$\mathrm{d}\ln\mathrm{cool}/\mathrm{d}\ln T = 0.263$ while the composition's own
$f(\mathrm{H_3^+})$ has $1.728$. Both cannot belong to a rate that is exactly
proportional to $n(\mathrm{H_3^+})$, and they do not: within one
\texttt{ioniz\_eq} the molecular densities the cooling uses are built at the top
of the routine from the composition handed \emph{in}
(\texttt{ionization\_equilibrium.f90:570--573}), \texttt{eval\_cool} is called
with them, and the per-cell sweep that changes the composition runs afterwards.
So the residual's temperature derivative carries the emissivity's $0.26$ and
none of the density's $1.728$ --- about one seventh of the self-consistent
response. That lag is not a defect and is not corrected
(Sec.~\ref{sec:limiter-open}).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Candidate (c), the frozen-radiation Jacobian: not the blocker
either.} The matrix-free $J v$ of the full residual along the energy unknown of
cell 259 converges to six digits from $h = 10^{-4}$ to $10^{-10}$, and a
two-sided merit scan on cells 255, 259 and 260 is antisymmetric to nine digits
with the WENO weights recomputed and frozen alike. Descent directions along the
front's energy rows exist.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{What does block it.} A forward-difference gradient of the merit
itself over cells 244--274 has one component that \emph{is} the whole norm ---
cell 272, the mass row, $7.43\times10^{8}$ against $10^{0}$--$10^{3}$ everywhere
else. Stepping along $+g$ changes the merit by $+3.6668$ at every step size from
$10^{-2}$ to $10^{-9}$, constant to seven digits. Dumping both sides at
$h = 10^{-9}$: every cell's temperature, class, heating, cooling and composition
is identical to every printed digit, and what changes is the reconstruction ---
faces dropped to first order $2 \to 3$, the left density at face 273
$2.50\times10^{-15} \to 4.16758\times10^{-6}$, the mass-row residual of cell 273
$|R|/D$ $9.50 \to 918.3$.

\subsection{The positivity repair is continuous}

\texttt{positivity\_limited\_faces}
(\texttt{src/modules/states/}\allowbreak\texttt{Reconstruction.f90}) no longer
swaps a face pair between two schemes. Each face state is scaled toward
\emph{its own} cell average by the largest factor that keeps $\rho$ and $p$
above a floor,
\begin{equation*}
  W_{\rm face} \;\leftarrow\; W_{\rm avg} + \theta\,(W_{\rm rec} - W_{\rm avg}),
  \qquad
  \theta = \min_{\rho,\,p}\;
  \frac{q_{\rm avg} - \varepsilon}{q_{\rm avg} - q_{\rm rec}},
\end{equation*}
which is the positivity-preserving limiter of Zhang \& Shu (2010, J.\ Comput.\
Phys., 229, 8918; \texttt{doi:10.1016/j.jcp.2010.08.016}). The publisher PDF is
not in \texttt{references/}, so only the bibliography is recorded. Two functions
carry the arithmetic, \texttt{positivity\_scaling} and
\texttt{positive\_variable\_scaling}.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The floor.} The switch this replaces tested $q > 0$, so its own
floor was zero, and zero is what the change was asked to keep. It cannot be:
with $\varepsilon = 0$ the scaling puts the face value at exactly zero and hands
\texttt{Num\_Fluxes} a $\sqrt{\gamma p/0}$. The floor used is the smallest one
that is not a chosen number --- one unit in the last place of the cell average,
$\varepsilon = \texttt{epsilon(1.0d0)}\,q_{\rm avg}$. No dimensional constant and
no tuning enter, and the residual jump that survives at the crossing is
$2.2\times10^{-16}$ of the cell average against the factor $1.7\times10^{9}$ the
switch made.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Byte-identity.} A face with $\theta = 1$ is left untouched
rather than rewritten as $W_{\rm avg} + 1\cdot(W - W_{\rm avg})$, which is not
bitwise $W$. Every run in which the guard never fires is therefore unchanged to
the bit, and Sec.~\ref{sec:limiter-regression} measures that on eight of the ten
matrix cases. The counter now counts face \emph{states}, not face pairs, because
the limiter scales the offending side only.

\subsection{A trial whose chemistry is not certified is refused}

\texttt{eval\_residual}
(\texttt{src/modules/time\_step/}\allowbreak\texttt{steady\_newton.f90}), inside
the admissibility of Sec.~\ref{sec:steady-probe-hygiene}. A state whose
equilibrium sweep accepted a cell as class 4 (the relaxation amnesty) or class 5
(the constrained continuation) is a residual computed on a composition the
chemistry does not describe, and its value says nothing about how far the hydro
is from steady. The count and the worst reaction residual are reported by the
solve, separately from the \texttt{ioniz\_eq} ledgers.

Two properties of the test, both forced by measurement rather than chosen.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{It is a comparison, not a threshold.} Refusing any trial with an
  uncertified cell was written first and measured: on this state the
  \emph{iterate} carries 11 such cells, so all 17 Jacobian colours and every
  Krylov direction were refused, the solve had no Newton model at all
  ($\lVert\nabla\,\mathrm{merit}\rVert = 0$) and aborted at iteration 1 with
  $\lVert R\rVert$ unchanged. A rule that rejects the neighbourhood of the point
  it stands on cannot be used to leave that point. The test is
  $n_{\rm uncert}(\text{trial}) \le n_{\rm uncert}(\text{iterate})$, the
  reference refreshed from the iterate at the top of every outer iteration; at a
  fully certified iterate it is the same rule as the absolute one.
\item \textbf{It applies to states that could be adopted, not to derivative
  samples.} With the comparison in place the solve ran 18 iterations and stopped
  again with 13 of 17 colours zeroed: the refusal had moved onto the
  finite-difference probes. A Jacobian colour and a $J v$ sample are points
  where the residual is read, never states anyone keeps, and a model built from
  an imperfect derivative is still a model. \texttt{eval\_residual} takes
  \texttt{may\_be\_adopted} (default \texttt{.true.});
  \texttt{build\_banded\_jac\_full} and \texttt{jv\_product} pass
  \texttt{.false.}
\end{enumerate}

ended the hand-off. What holds the second solve is the flux gate at

and that is the propagating front of
\texttt{docs/supersonic\_molecular\_base.md} Sec.~13.7, not a solver failure:
the carrier pass moves the composition by $0.553$ and leaves a carrier steady

follows the flux spread grows monotonically from $1.24\times10^{-1}$ at step

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The three-layer table is not produced and nothing is quoted for
it.} The first solve's state meets both gates, but the carrier pass overwrites
it before anything is written, and there is no key that caps the Picard outer
passes --- the bound is \texttt{merge(20, 1, ...)} at
\texttt{EXHALE\_main.f90:1628}. Capturing it needs either an output write at the
accepted return or that bound made settable, and both are changes of their own.
Until then the rule of item (Y) still applies to the \emph{carrier-relaxed}
molecular wind: it is quoted on the marching criterion, and the fact is stated
where it is quoted. What has changed is that the wind solve itself is no longer
the obstacle.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The lagged cooling is judged, not corrected.} At the fixed point
the composition the cooling uses and the composition the sweep returns are the
same object, so the lag is a property of the iteration and not of the solution,
and re-evaluating \texttt{eval\_cool} after the sweep would change no converged
answer. What it costs is the Newton model --- the factor 7 above --- and adding
the analytic $\mathrm{d}\ln\mathrm{cool}/\mathrm{d}\ln T$ of the dominant channel
to the banded Jacobian's energy diagonal is the repair for that. It is not done
here; it is held until the two changes above are shown to be insufficient.

\section{The carrier/wind alternation was pointing the wrong way, its
convergence measure understated the imbalance by 64, and the two are now solved
together (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:coupled-carrier-solve}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{The judgement first, in three parts.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(a) The alternation of Sec.~\ref{sec:molecular-carrier-transport}
does not converge because it cannot.} Its drift gate of $10^{-3}$ stands
\emph{below} the smallest move the transport operator can make: one step at a
cell's own crossing time moves the largest H$_2$ mixing ratio by
$1.1\times10^{-2}$, measured. A gate that cannot fire reads as a control to the
next person, so it is gone. What replaces it is the test the wind is already
held to --- is the row steady on the scale of its own largest terms.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(b) That test could not be applied, because the carrier row's
scale was not its own largest term.} \texttt{carrier\_row\_scale},
$n_{\rm H}(|v|+c_s)/\mathrm{d}r$, is a \emph{bound} on the row; measured against
the sum of the terms the row actually balances it is $10^{2.7}$ to $10^{6.4}$
too large. A wind the steady solver accepted at \texttt{info = 0} reported a
carrier residual of $1.6\times10^{-4}$ while carrying \textbf{0.60 of its own
terms} at the H$_2$ front and $1.07\times10^{-2}$ volume-weighted --- a factor
64 on the volume-weighted measure and 1850 on the worst cell.
Sec.~\ref{sec:two-gates} already made ``a bound on that row's own largest term''
the principle for every hydrodynamic row; the carrier row now follows it, using
the quantity \texttt{carrier\_residual} has always computed for its own Newton.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(c) The splitting was not merely slow --- it had the sign
wrong.} The alternation moves the H$_2$ front \textsc{outward} about one cell in
each pass, at 83 per cent of the local gas speed. Solving the carriers and the
wind \emph{together}, from the same state, moves it \textsc{inward}:
$f(\mathrm{H_2}) = 0.5$ from $1.1421$ to $1.0618\,R_{\rm p}$,
$f(\mathrm{H_2}) = 10^{-2}$ from $1.2192$ to $1.1488$. The reason is a feedback
a fixed wind cannot see, and it closes exactly: H$_2$ costs particles, fewer
particles at the wind's own pressure means a hotter cell, and a hotter cell
destroys H$_2$. At the front the predicted temperature from the particle count
alone is $1915$~K against $1915$~K measured, and $1958$ against $1961$.

\medskip
\texttt{Molecular carrier transport} and \texttt{Coupled carrier solve} both
stay \textsc{default off}. Nothing below is a converged solution and nothing
below is quoted as a rate.

\subsection{What was measured, before anything was changed}

Reproduction is cheap and that is worth recording: the alternation's failure
does not need the $64\,000$-step hand-off of
Sec.~\ref{sec:continuous-positivity-limiter}. The \textsc{first} steady solve of
that run, at marching step 2, already returns \texttt{info = 0}, and the carrier
pass that follows it throws $\lVert R\rVert$ from $5.0\times10^{-4}$ to
$8.2\times10^{-2}$. Dumping that accepted wind and restarting from it reproduces
the failure in three seconds.

\medskip
On that state, one fixed-wind carrier pass, undamped:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}rrrrr@{}}
\toprule
$r$ [$R_{\rm p}$] & $x_2$ entry & $x_2$ exit & $f_c(\mathrm{H_2})$ entry & $f_c(\mathrm{H_2})$ exit \\
\midrule
1.050 & 0.9425 & \textbf{1.0000} & 7.75e$-$1 & 8.22e$-$1 \\
1.150 & 0.4447 & \textbf{1.0000} & 2.60e$-$1 & 5.84e$-$1 \\
1.200 & 0.0963 & \textbf{1.0000} & 4.67e$-$2 & 4.85e$-$1 \\
1.227 & 6.3e$-$4 & \textbf{1.0000} & 2.90e$-$4 & 4.63e$-$1 \\
1.400 & 5.9e$-$5 & 4.4e$-$5 & 2.75e$-$5 & 2.05e$-$5 \\
1.835 & 2.7e$-$5 & 1.1e$-$5 & 1.24e$-$5 & 5.07e$-$6 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent $x_2 = 1.0000$ is not a rounding: \textbf{123 of 500 cells between
1.047 and 1.227 $R_{\rm p}$ sit exactly on the hydrogen element ceiling} that
\texttt{limit\_to\_element\_budget} imposes (entry: none). The state the pass
returns is pinned by the limiter over a quarter of the grid, which is a solution
of nothing. The far wind moves by $7\times10^{-6}$ in $f_c$, four decades below.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The drift measure was not the problem, and that was checked.}
It normalizes by the largest H$_2$ mixing ratio anywhere on the grid --- one
number, not the cell's own value --- so it is already absolute. On the
\textsc{late} hand-off, where Sec.~\ref{sec:limiter-open} reported the worst
drift ``in the wind'' at $1.795\,R_{\rm p}$, the H$_2$ mixing ratio there goes
from $0.252$ to $0.507$: a quarter of the gas to a half. There is no
trace-species artefact; the wind is molecular to the top of the domain, which is
the runaway itself.

\subsection{The alternation, repaired as far as it can be}

Two changes, both to what the outer loop does with a pass.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The under-relaxation blend is gone.} It is measurably worse
than either state it interpolates: carrier steady residual $1.6\times10^{-4}$ at
entry, $2.2\times10^{-3}$ at the relaxed exit, $\mathbf{8.6\times10^{-3}}$ for
the $\omega = 0.5$ blend, which then threw $\lVert R\rVert$ to
$6.7\times10^{-2}$ against $1.9\times10^{-2}$ for the relaxed state handed over
whole. A blend of two states solves neither equation. Reducing $\omega$ does not
help and is measured to hurt ($\omega = 1.8\times10^{-3}$ gave
$2.0\times10^{-1}$).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{A composition trust region replaces it.} The pass advances the
carriers and stops as soon as it has moved the composition by
\texttt{carrier\_trust}, and that state is handed over whole.
Sec.~\ref{sec:molecular-carrier-transport} tried a bound in \textsc{flow times}
and measured that it controls nothing; a bound on the \textsc{composition} does,
because the operator's smallest step is already $1.1\times10^{-2}$ of it. Where
the boundary is, measured on the same hand-off:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r l@{}}
\toprule
bound on one pass & passes returning \texttt{info = 0} & $\lVert R\rVert$ handed on \\
\midrule
the full relaxation, blended at $\omega = 0.5$ (old) & 0 & 6.7e$-$2, abort \\
the full relaxation, whole & 0 & 1.9e$-$2, abort \\
0.4 & 1 & 6.7e$-$4 then 8.2e$-$3, abort \\
0.2 & 8+ & 2.8e$-$4 \\
0.05 & 19 & 2.4e$-$4 \\
$\mathbf{10^{-2}}$ \textbf{(adopted)} & \textbf{20 of 20} & \textbf{2.4e$-$4 to 3.1e$-$4} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent So \texttt{carrier\_trust} $= 10^{-2}$ stands a factor 20 inside the
measured boundary. \textbf{And the alternation still does not reach a fixed
point}: with it, the drift creeps $1.13\times10^{-2}$ to $1.34\times10^{-2}$
over 20 passes while the front walks from $1.203$ to $1.250\,R_{\rm p}$, one
cell in each pass. Each pass is one transport step at the cell's own advective
crossing time --- \texttt{dt\_phys} equals $\mathrm{d}r/|v|$ exactly there,
$799$~s at $1.227\,R_{\rm p}$ --- and $0.047\,R_{\rm p}$ in 20 such steps is
$1.03\times10^{4}$~cm\,s$^{-1}$ against a gas speed of $1.24\times10^{4}$. The
alternation is time integration wearing a fixed point's clothes.

\subsection{The measure, and the floor that a steady evaluation had killed}

\texttt{carrier\_steady\_residual} now divides by \texttt{row\_terms}, the sum
of the row's own term magnitudes, and reports the volume-weighted ratio of sums
over the layer and the wind separately, combined by the larger --- the same
construction \texttt{relnorm\_over\_cells} uses for the hydrodynamic rows. The
retired scale is still computed and printed beside it while the two are being
compared.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{A defect found on the way.} \texttt{carrier\_residual}'s
absolute floor, $10^{-20}$ of the element, was converted to the row's units by
dividing by the step. The steady evaluation substitutes
$\mathrm{d}t = 10^{30}$ to kill the time term, and the floor went with it: the
far wind was being measured with no floor at all. It is now converted by
$\max(1/\mathrm{d}t, (|v|+c_s)/\mathrm{d}r)$ --- the same statement written
without a step, so it survives $\mathrm{d}t \to \infty$ and agrees with the step
form whenever the step is the cell's own crossing time, which is what the
relaxation uses.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The gate is \texttt{carrier\_resid\_th} $= 10^{-3}$ and it is
\textsc{not} \texttt{Resid tol}.} Sec.~\ref{sec:two-gates} renormalized
\texttt{Resid tol} against a row scale that \textsc{bounds} each hydrodynamic
row's largest term rather than being it, so the two numbers are not on the same
footing. What this one says is the plain statement: the carrier row balances to
a thousandth of the terms it is made of.

\subsection{The coupled solve: $n(\mathrm{H_2})$ as a fourth Newton unknown}

\texttt{Coupled carrier solve: True|False}, default false, meaningless without
\texttt{Molecular carrier transport: True}.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Unknowns} are four per cell, $(\rho, \rho v, E,
  n(\mathrm{H_2})/n_0)$, the last in the code's own density units and not in
  cm$^{-3}$: the Krylov step size is $\sqrt{\epsilon}(1+\lVert Y\rVert)/\lVert
  v\rVert$, a norm of the whole vector, so a component thirteen decades from the
  others would set that step by itself.
\item \textbf{The chemistry coupling already existed.} With the carrier
  transport on, \texttt{ioniz\_eq} holds H$_2$ fixed at the partition it is
  handed and solves everything else around it --- that is what made the
  splitting possible. The coupled solve changes only where that number comes
  from: the Newton unknown instead of the last transport step. So the particle
  count, the temperature that follows from it, and every heating and cooling
  term are functions of the carrier unknown, and the Jacobian sees it.
  \textbf{No new chemistry was written.}
\item \textbf{The limited slope is frozen inside the model}, on
  \texttt{weno\_mode} --- the switch Sec.~\ref{sec:steady-probe-hygiene} already uses for
  the WENO3 weights, and for the same reason: it reaches $j-2$ and $j+2$, which
  the banded stencil does not carry.
\item \textbf{The element budget is a \textsc{constraint}, not a row.} A trial
  whose $n(\mathrm{H_2})$ leaves the hydrogen its cell has is refused where
  \texttt{admissible} is asked for, the way the positivity of $\rho$ and $p$ is
  refused in the line search. It is not clamped: a clamp puts a kink in the
  residual, which is the defect Sec.~\ref{sec:continuous-positivity-limiter}
  removed, and it is exactly what made the fixed-wind relaxation return a state
  pinned on the ceiling. The test is a \textsc{comparison} against how many
  cells the \textsc{iterate} leaves outside, for that section's reason: a rule
  that rejects the neighbourhood of the point it stands on cannot be used to
  leave that point.
\item \textbf{Band geometry} is set at run time: $|\mathrm{row}-\mathrm{col}|
  \le 4\times2+3 = 11$, so $k_l = k_u = 11$ and 23 colours against 8 and 17. The
  carrier row itself reaches only $\pm1$ --- its second-order correction is a
  frozen source --- so the WENO3 reach still sets the bandwidth and the fourth
  variable only widens the stride.
\item \textbf{Acceptance is a \textsc{third gate}, not a row of $\lVert
  R\rVert$}, and that is Sec.~\ref{sec:two-gates}'s own judgement applied again:
  one number cannot say two things. \texttt{Resid tol} was renormalized there
  against a row scale that \textsc{bounds} each hydrodynamic row's largest term,
  and converged states sit at $10^{-6}$ on it; the carrier row is measured
  against the terms \textsc{themselves}, where a converged row sits near
  $10^{-3}$. Folding it into $\lVert R\rVert$ was tried first and holds the
  carrier row to a tolerance meant for a different scale --- on the 1 microbar
  gate the solve then works against a target it cannot reach. So a steady solve
  is accepted on three gates: $\lVert R\rVert <$ \texttt{Resid tol}, the flux
  spread, and the carrier row below \texttt{carrier\_resid\_th} ($10^{-3}$), and
  the log names whichever is left. \texttt{carrier\_resid\_th} lives in
  \texttt{parameters.f90} and the outer loop reads the same number.
\item \texttt{solve\_steady\_ptc} \textbf{refuses} the coupled unknown and says
  so: it builds its Jacobian from \texttt{frozen\_residual}, which does no
  equilibrium sweep and so has no carrier row.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Three defects of the coupled formulation, each found by measurement}

\noindent\textbf{(i) One scale vector cannot scale both the carrier row and its
unknown.} The solver scales rows and columns with the same $D$, which is right
when the residual has the units of the unknown over a time --- true of every row
here. It is still not enough, because the carrier row is \textsc{stiff}: its
natural rate is the chemical one, about $10^{3}$ per code time at the front
against the hydrodynamic rows' $10^{-6}$.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r l@{}}
\toprule
carrier scale used for both & merit at the hand-off & outcome \\
\midrule
$n(\mathrm{H_2}) + \mathrm{row\_terms}/((|v|+c_s)/\mathrm{d}r)$ (state-like) & \textbf{89.8} & abort at iteration 2 \\
$\mathrm{row\_terms}\times(R_0/v_0)$ (the row's own terms) & 2.51 & abort at iteration 2 \\
\textbf{row terms for the \textsc{row}, state-like for the \textsc{column}} & 2.51 & runs \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent With the state-like scale on the row the line search sees nothing but
the carrier and lands on a state whose chemistry cannot be certified; with the
row scale on the column the Newton proposes carrier steps \textbf{84 times the
cell's own $n(\mathrm{H_2})$} and the line search cuts to
$\lambda = 4.9\times10^{-4}$. The fix is a two-sided scaling,
\texttt{cell\_row\_scales} beside \texttt{cell\_state\_scales}.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(ii) The constraint was moving with the trial it constrained.}
The element headroom depends on the very unknown it bounds
(\texttt{n\_H\_free} counts H$_2$'s own two nuclei). Refreshed at every state
that is not a Jacobian probe, the last line-search trial leaves its own headroom
behind and the Gauss--Newton escape then finds the \textsc{iterate} outside it:
every backtracked step is refused down to $\lambda = 5\times10^{-4}$ and the
solve aborts holding a descent direction. It is now frozen at the outer iterate.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{(iii) The Gauss--Newton escape had no line search, and with the
carrier row it needs one.} The escape used to evaluate the full step and nothing
else, which suffices while the only way it can fail is to ascend. With the
carrier unknown a second failure mode appears: the full step \textsc{lowers} the
merit ($2.28 \to 1.50$) and puts 73 cells' molecular equilibrium outside the
physical simplex, so the trial is refused and the solve aborts with a descent
direction in hand. It now backtracks up to 12 times. \textbf{The three-unknown
route keeps the single evaluation it has always had.}

\subsection{(P51): the best iterate stops moving, and the search keeps accepting}
\label{sec:grippo-stagnation}

The non-monotone (Grippo) line search compares a trial against the \textsc{worst}
merit of the last five iterates, so it accepts sideways steps. That is what lets
the solve leave a bad neighbourhood, and it is also what lets it circle: on the
coupled hand-off the best iterate is reached at outer iteration 10 and
\textbf{490 further iterations produce no improvement at all} while the search
accepts 61 sideways steps.

\medskip
So when the best iterate has not improved for \texttt{n\_stall\_best}
iterations the solve \textsc{goes back to it} and switches to a monotone Armijo
acceptance; if that buys nothing in another \texttt{n\_stall\_best}, it stops and
says it \texttt{STAGNATED}, which is a different statement from ``no descent
direction exists''.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Where 20 comes from.} Over every solve of this campaign that
ended \texttt{info = 0} on a configuration that survived measurement, the largest
gap between two improvements of the best iterate is \textbf{6} outer iterations
(both WASP-121\,b Newton cases); on the coupled hot Uranus it is 3. Two accepted
solves show gaps of 68 and 85 and both are configurations that were measured and
rejected. So 20 stands a factor 3.3 above anything a surviving route has needed,
and 40 --- where the solve gives up --- stands a factor 6.7 above it and below
every stall observed (tails of 278 to 729). Measured effect on the coupled
hand-off: the solve now stops at \textbf{49 iterations} instead of running to its
500-iteration limit, with the same best iterate and an explicit reason.

\subsection{What the coupled solve does, and where it stops}

From the accepted wind ($\lVert R\rVert = 1.454\times10^{-4}$ on three rows),
with the carrier row in the unknowns and in $\lVert R\rVert$, and both gates:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r l@{}}
\toprule
 & at entry & at exit \\
\midrule
$\lVert R\rVert$ with the carrier row folded in (the form first tried) & 1.221e$-$2 & \textbf{4.073e$-$3} \\
carrier row, worst cell / own terms & 6.04e$-$1 & \textbf{1.36e$-$1} \\
carrier row, volume-weighted & 7.72e$-$3 & 4.07e$-$3 \\
\texttt{info} & --- & 2, \texttt{STAGNATED} at 49 iterations \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent $\lVert R\rVert$ at entry is $1.221\times10^{-2}$ rather than
$1.454\times10^{-4}$ because the carrier row is now in it: the wind that solve
accepted was steady in three rows and not in the fourth.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{It does not converge, and where it stops is not where the
alternation stopped.} The binding row is the carrier row, and resolving its
volume-weighted sum by radius says the imbalance is \textbf{spread through the
molecular layer}, not concentrated at the front the alternation could not move:
the wind above $2\,R_{\rm p}$ reads $1.17\times10^{-4}$, the layer
$6.5\times10^{-3}$, and the single largest contributor is the \textsc{base} cell
at $r = 1.000$ with 19 per cent of the layer's numerator. Excluding the launch
region the way the flux gate does makes the number worse, not better
($1.97\times10^{-2}$ over $r \ge 1.03$), because the denominator is dominated by
the same cells: the layer is 0.6 to 4 per cent out of carrier balance
throughout, against a 0.1 per cent gate.

\medskip
The front, and the three layers, against the state the solve was handed.
\textbf{The returned state is four times the carrier tolerance, so this is a

\subsection{Cost}

Both from the same hand-off, 20 outer iterations, \texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=8}:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r r@{}}

\midrule

\subsection{What was checked}

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{make check}, \textbf{10 of 10 byte-identical} ---
  \texttt{wasp\_full}, \texttt{wasp\_he23off}, \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff},
  \texttt{mol\_metals}, \texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner}, \texttt{mol\_diffusion},
  \texttt{mol\_ir\_bands}, \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion}, \texttt{mol\_carrier},
  \texttt{lower\_profile} --- run twice, once with the alternation change alone
  and once with the coupled route on top of it. \textbf{And that had to be
  worked for.} The two-sided row scaling is the \textsc{same} arithmetic when
  there is no carrier row --- \texttt{Drow} holds exactly $D$'s values --- but
  not the same instruction sequence, and a reduction summed in a different order
  differs in its last bits: without a branch, \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} and
  \texttt{wasp\_he23off\_newton} moved by $1.2\times10^{-9}$ and
  $4.0\times10^{-8}$ relative, with $\log_{10}\dot M$ unchanged to six decimals
  and, on the first, an identical iteration log. \textbf{The run-time band
  geometry is not the cause and that was tested}: a build with \texttt{kl\_jac}
  and the rest back at compile time is bit-identical to the run-time one. Every
  site that divides by the row scale therefore branches on \texttt{nvar\_jac},
  with the \textsc{original} expression character for character in the
  three-unknown branch.
\item The carrier arrays are allocated only when the coupled route is on, and
  \texttt{Drow} last and on its own, so every array the three-unknown solve has
  always had keeps the address it has always had.
\item \textbf{NOT checked}: the coupled route on any planet but the
  He/H $= 0.0793$ hot Uranus, on any state but that hand-off, or with helium
  diffusion also on.
\item \textbf{NOT checked}: whether the band half-width 11 is exact rather than
  sufficient. It is derived, and no column-by-column comparison against a dense
  Jacobian was made.
\item \textbf{The 1 microbar gate (\texttt{mol\_carrier}) was run, and it does
  not produce a quotable steady state either --- for a reason that is about the
  case, not about the solver.} That case is a $12\,000$-step relaxation
  \textsc{snapshot}, not a converged wind: restarted from its own output with the
  coupled solve on, the marching takes $21\,000$ further steps to reach the JFNK
  hand-off and the solve then stagnates at
  $\lVert R\rVert = 2.30\times10^{-3}$ with the carrier row binding at
  $2.30\times10^{-3}$ and, decisively, a \textbf{flux spread of $0.244$ against a
  gate of $5\times10^{-3}$}. The wind is not carrying one mass flux at every
  altitude, so no gate can be met and no three-layer table from it would
  describe a steady state. A quotable coupled solution needs a converged wind on
  that planet first, which is the same thing item (P43) has been waiting for.
\item \textbf{NOT checked}: the E1d hand-off in the tree. It is a 9 microbar
  state whose \texttt{base.inp} and \texttt{Log10 lower boundary} disagree, and
  Sec.~\ref{sec:base-level-one-source} made \texttt{p\_base} authoritative, so
  the tree would set up a different base than the campaign's pre-136 working
  copy did; the comparison would not be like-for-like.
\end{itemize}

\section{Six ways a run could not say why it stopped, and an acceptance test
that existed in two versions (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:stop-reasons-and-one-acceptance-test}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{The judgement first, in three parts. (1) The marching loop's
\texttt{Resid tol} stop wrote its verdict into the \emph{du} flag, so a run
that stopped on the residual printed \texttt{converged: momentum constant (du <
du\_th)} at $du = 3.156\times10^{-3}$ with $du_{\rm th} = 10^{-3}$: the
reported reason and the reason that fired were different statements and only
one of them was true. (2) There were two definitions of an accepted steady
state --- \texttt{steady\_gates\_met} (the residual \emph{and} the flatness of
the mass flux, Sec.~\ref{sec:two-gates}) inside the JFNK, and the residual
alone in the marching loop --- so for the same \texttt{Resid tol} key the
marching accepted a WASP-121\,b state whose flux spread was
$9.879\times10^{-2}$, twenty times the default threshold, while the JFNK was
refusing $1.874\times10^{-2}$. (3) A key stated twice was resolved by file
order with nothing saying so, and one file in the repository was stated twice.
All three are fixed; the acceptance test now exists once, in
\texttt{steady\_residual.f90}, and every route that may stop a run on ``the
equations are satisfied'' calls it.}

\medskip
This closes item (P52) of \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md}.

\subsection{The stop that was reported was not the stop that fired}

\texttt{EXHALE\_main.f90} carried three stop flags --- \texttt{is\_mom\_const},
\texttt{is\_zero\_dt}, \texttt{is\_stalled} --- and printed a fixed sentence for
each. The \texttt{Resid tol} branch had no flag of its own and borrowed the
first, \texttt{is\_mom\_const = is\_resid\_ok}, so the run's own log said
$du < du_{\rm th}$ about a stop that had nothing to do with $du$. Measured on
\texttt{resid\_on} (WASP-121\,b, \texttt{Resid tol: 1.0e-4},
\texttt{du\_th [PLM,WENO3]: 0.5 1.0e-3}) before the change, the loop stopped at
step 14\,000 printing

\begin{verbatim}
     -> converged: momentum constant (du < du_th)
     final: count=14000  du= 3.1560E-03  dtu= 2.4942E-05
\end{verbatim}

\noindent with $du$ three times its own threshold, because what had happened
was $\lVert R\rVert = 8.066\times10^{-5} < 10^{-4}$.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Every stop condition now has its own flag and its own line},
and the flags are named for what they measure rather than for the order they
were added in:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l p{0.62\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
flag (\texttt{parameters.f90}) & the condition it holds \\
\midrule
\texttt{mass\_flux\_converged}    & $du < du_{\rm th}$: the radial spread of $\rho v r^2$ over the wind \\
\texttt{step\_change\_converged}  & $dtu < dtu_{\rm th}$: the largest relative change of $u$ in one step \\
\texttt{du\_plateaued}            & $du$ settled on a plateau (the stall net) \\
\texttt{steady\_gates\_converged} & \emph{both} steady gates met on the marched state \\
\texttt{hit\_max\_steps}          & the \texttt{EXHALE\_MAXSTEPS} cap \\
\texttt{newton\_finished}         & the JFNK finish returned \texttt{info = 0} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent \texttt{newton\_finished} used to set \texttt{is\_mom\_const} to
leave the loop; it is now a stop condition of the loop in its own right, so
nothing has to borrow a flag to exit. The report tests the flags in the order
the loop leaves on them, with the NaN scan first because a NaN invalidates any
convergence a flag may also be carrying.

\subsection{One acceptance test, in one place}

\texttt{steady\_gates\_met} --- $\lVert R\rVert < \texttt{resid\_tol}$
\emph{and} the mass-flux spread over $r \ge r_{\rm flux}$ below
\texttt{flux\_spread\_th}, Sec.~\ref{sec:two-gates} --- was a private function
of \texttt{steady\_newton.f90}, so only the steady solvers could call it and the
marching loop's \texttt{Resid tol} stop tested the residual alone. \textbf{The
two routes were reading the same user key and applying different acceptance
criteria.} On \texttt{resid\_on} the state the marching accepted at step
14\,000 had a gate-window flux spread of $9.879\times10^{-2}$ --- the
diagnostic line was already printing it --- against a default
\texttt{Flux spread tol} of $5.0\times10^{-3}$ and against the
$1.874\times10^{-2}$ the JFNK is on record refusing on
\texttt{jfnk\_hd189\_tight}.

\medskip
The function moves to \texttt{steady\_residual\_mod}
(\texttt{steady\_residual.f90}), beside the residual and the flux functional it
combines, because neither solver owns the definition.
\texttt{steady\_newton.f90} imports it; the marching monitor calls it at the
same \texttt{N\_resid} cadence it already used, in place of its bare
\texttt{flux\_spread\_of\_state} call. Where a \texttt{Resid tol} run stops
without meeting the pair, the log names the gate that is left, in the same
terms the JFNK uses:

\begin{verbatim}
     -> stopped: du plateau detected (stalled 500 steps) with the steady gates NOT met
        the residual gate is met: ||R|| 7.153E-05 < 1.000E-04
        the FLUX gate is the one left: spread 4.218E-02 >= 5.000E-03
\end{verbatim}

\subsection{The step cap is a stop, and now says so}

\texttt{EXHALE\_MAXSTEPS=N} leaves the loop from inside the body, so none of
the three flags was set and the \texttt{count\_max} branch tested only the hard
$10^6$ cap: a run that ended on the cap printed no stop line at all, going
straight from \texttt{Time integration done.} to \texttt{final: count=...}.
Every fixed-step case in the regression matrix ends this way, and so does
\texttt{wasp\_localdt\_cont}. The exit now sets \texttt{hit\_max\_steps} and
the report prints \texttt{-> stopped: reached EXHALE\_MAXSTEPS = 12000 steps
WITHOUT convergence}, with the unmet gates listed after it when the run asked
for \texttt{Resid tol}. The \texttt{Do only PP} exit and the NaN exit likewise
now name themselves.

\subsection{A key states one quantity}

The parser resolved a repeated key to its \textsc{last} occurrence. That is a
rule about file order, not about intent: the run proceeds on a value nobody
chose and nothing in its log says a choice was made.
\texttt{backup/}\allowbreak\texttt{regression/}\allowbreak\texttt{valve\_sens/}\allowbreak\texttt{eps5/}\allowbreak\texttt{input.inp}
carried \texttt{Resid tol} twice, and its own stored \texttt{run.log} shows the
parser echoing both and the solve taking the second
(\texttt{tol = 1.00E-03}, then \texttt{tol = 1.00E-04}).

\medskip
\texttt{refuse\_duplicate\_keys} (\texttt{input\_read.f90}) now stops the run
before any line is consumed, printing both line numbers and both values. Each
non-blank, non-\texttt{\#} line is attributed to the \textsc{longest} key it
matches, because the key set is not prefix-free (\texttt{Lower atmosphere} is a
prefix of \texttt{Lower atmosphere profile}, \texttt{Wind-AE seed} of
\texttt{Wind-AE seed out}) and the longest match is the key the parser itself
consumes. The same routine covers \texttt{base.inp}. \texttt{metals.inp} gets
its own check, keyed on the \textsc{quantity} rather than on the token, because
there the labels alias: \texttt{C} and \texttt{CI} both set \texttt{X\_C}, so a
token-level test would miss the pair that matters.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The repository was swept for the same defect.} All 1889
settings files under the repository were attributed key by key with the
parser's own matching rule (1126 \texttt{input.inp}, 650 \texttt{base.inp},
113 \texttt{metals.inp}, including the 942 stored \texttt{LHS1140b/} inputs and
the 32 under \texttt{vulcan\_work/}). \textbf{Exactly one file carried a
duplicate}, the \texttt{valve\_sens/eps5} above, and it is repaired here. Which
of its two values was meant is settled by its own run log, not by preference:
the solve ran on the second, $10^{-4}$ on the pre-Sec.~\ref{sec:two-gates}
scale, which the renormalization there makes $10^{-6}$.

\subsection{The direct steady route printed none of the run's counters}

\texttt{EXHALE\_PTC=1} solves from the initial condition and stops. The
run-counter ledger --- the ionization-solver acceptance report, the
energy-floor, positivity-limiter and $dt$-bisection counts, the base-inflow
Mach, the He-recombination coupling warning, the low-Mach damping magnitude ---
sat inline in the marching route below its stop line, so this route reported
none of it. It is now one contained routine,
\texttt{write\_run\_counter\_report}, and both routes call it: the marching
loop where the block used to be, and the direct route before its \texttt{stop}.
Measured on a WASP-121\,b PTC/JFNK solve from the \texttt{ptc\_warm} initial
condition, the same build with and without the call: the outputs are
byte-identical and the run gains 846 equilibrium sweeps' worth of acceptance
statistics it was discarding.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{A second diagnostic-only defect travels with it.}
\texttt{write\_heat\_breakdown\_eq} (\texttt{util\_ion\_eq.f90}) called
\texttt{PH\_heat\_HHe} without \texttt{f\_vibq} / \texttt{e\_vibq}, the two
arrays carrying the collisional quench fraction of an H$_2$ vibrational
excitation and the internal energy a B/C fluorescence leaves behind. They are
optional arguments, so their absence switched the two H$_2$ vibrational heat
channels off silently and only in the dump --- the solver's own call in
\texttt{ionization\_equilibrium.f90} has always passed them. Measured on
\texttt{mol\_base\_handoff}, the dump's photoheating total rises by up to a
factor $1.97$ (at $r = 1.0002\,R_{\rm p}$), with \texttt{heat\_H2} nearly
doubling there, and by $0.49\%$ volume-integrated.
\texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} and \texttt{Ion\_species.txt} are untouched.

\subsection{Regression-directory hygiene, and the numbers of
Sec.~\ref{sec:layer-row-scales}}
\label{sec:regression-directory-hygiene}

\texttt{backup/regression/valve\_sens/eps4} holds two output files and no
\texttt{input.inp}, so it is not a case any harness can run; nothing in
\texttt{run\_check.sh} or in \texttt{docs/} refers to it. It is left as found
with a \texttt{NOTE.txt} recording that, checked 2026-09-03. Three pairs of case
directories are the same case under two names, with byte-identical
\texttt{input.inp} and \texttt{metals.inp}:
\texttt{crit\_warm} $=$ \texttt{wasp\_hybrid\_finish},
\texttt{ptc\_wasp} $=$ \texttt{resid\_on},
\texttt{solver\_newton\_cold} $=$ \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton}. Each of the six
gets a \texttt{NOTE.txt} recording the identity; none is deleted or merged,
because which name to keep is a judgement about what the stored outputs are
records of.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The rates quoted in Sec.~\ref{sec:layer-row-scales} are
corrected.} They were 30-step probes reported as though they were the cases'
results. Run to their own stopping criteria:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l l r@{}}
\toprule
case & stop & $\log_{10}\dot M$ \\
\midrule
\texttt{wasp\_hybrid\_finish} $=$ \texttt{crit\_warm} & $du = 9.9997\times10^{-4} < du_{\rm th}$, step 22\,935 & 13.23 \\
\texttt{wasp\_localdt\_cont} & the 40\,000-step cap, $du = 4.97\times10^{-5}$ & 13.36 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The second row is not a converged rate, and until this section its
run printed no line saying so.

\subsection{What was checked}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The ten regression cases are byte-identical, and to two
  references.} The tree was being edited concurrently, so the comparison is an
  A/B between two builds made from \emph{one} frozen snapshot of it: the
  snapshot as it stood, and the same snapshot with the six files of this
  section changed and nothing else. All ten agree with the control bit for bit
  in \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} and \texttt{Ion\_species.txt}, and all ten agree
  with \texttt{backup/regression/golden/} as well. What changed is the stop
  line: \texttt{wasp\_full} and \texttt{wasp\_he23off} now print
  \texttt{converged: mass flux rho*v*r\^{}2 constant over the wind
  (du= 9.999E-04 < du\_th 1.000E-03)}, and the eight fixed-step cases print
  \texttt{stopped: reached EXHALE\_MAXSTEPS = 12000 steps WITHOUT convergence}
  where they used to print nothing at all.
\item \textbf{\texttt{resid\_on} no longer stops at step 14\,000, and what it
  does instead is worth having.} With both gates it marches on, and the staged
  secondary-ionization flip --- which fires on the first stop condition the
  loop reaches --- now fires at step 37\,500 on a state with
  $\lVert R\rVert = 3.808\times10^{-6}$ and a flux spread of
  $4.793\times10^{-3}$, i.e.\ on a state that meets \emph{both} gates, instead
  of at step 9500 on one that meets the residual alone. The run then reaches
  the 40\,000-step cap and reports it. Over the 80 monitor evaluations the
  residual gate is met at 52 and the pair at exactly one; the flux spread at
  those 52 ranges over $4.793\times10^{-3}$ to $1.290\times10^{-1}$, so
  \textbf{the residual gate on this planet says nothing about whether the mass
  flux is flat}. $\log_{10}\dot M$ is 13.26 either way: the premature stop was
  not costing accuracy here, it was costing the statement.
\item \textbf{The other two \texttt{Resid tol} cases, both under a
  40\,000-step cap.} \texttt{ptc\_warm} stops on the cap with
  $\lVert R\rVert = 1.653\times10^{-5} \ge 10^{-5}$ and spread
  $1.070\times10^{-2} \ge 5\times10^{-3}$ ($\log_{10}\dot M = 13.23$);
  \texttt{jfnk\_hd189} with $3.865\times10^{-5}$ and $2.304\times10^{-1}$
  ($9.93$). Neither reaches both gates by marching alone, and both now say so
  in one line each.
\item \textbf{The duplicate-key refusal, on all three file kinds.} The
  unrepaired \texttt{eps5} stops naming lines 33 and 36; a second
  \texttt{T\_base} in a \texttt{base.inp} stops naming lines 32 and 38; a
  \texttt{CI} line beside an existing \texttt{C} line stops on \texttt{X\_C},
  which is the alias case a token-level check would miss. The repaired
  \texttt{eps5} parses and reports \texttt{tol = 1.00E-06}.
\item \textbf{The heat-breakdown dump, and what it does NOT close.} Its own
  closure stays exact ($\max|\sum\mathrm{channels}/\mathrm{heat\_photo}-1| =
  1.8\times10^{-15}$). What the fix does \emph{not} do is make the dump agree
  with the \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt} heat column on the molecular gates: that
  ratio is $0.23$ on \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff} before \emph{and} after,
  because those cases are 12\,000-step relaxation snapshots and the dump
  re-solves the equilibrium at the final $(T,\rho)$ while the heat column is
  the marching state's own. On the converged \texttt{wasp\_full} the same
  measurement gives $1.0000$ at every cell, which is what the dump's header
  already claims (``up to convergence''), so a $1.000$ closure on a molecular
  case has to be measured on a converged one.
\item \textbf{Runtime checks.} A \texttt{-fcheck=bounds,do,mem} rebuild of the
  changed tree and a 1500-step bounded HD 209458\,b run: \textbf{clean},
  $\log_{10}\dot M = 9.60$, and the run now prints
  \texttt{stopped: reached EXHALE\_MAXSTEPS = 1500 steps WITHOUT convergence}.
\item \textbf{NOT checked}: whether any \texttt{Resid tol} case reaches both
  gates given more than 40\,000 marching steps (all three were capped); the
  remaining \texttt{Resid tol} cases (\texttt{jfnk\_cold},
  \texttt{jfnk\_hd189\_tight}, \texttt{tpm\_*}); \texttt{ifort} / \texttt{ifx}
  builds; and the 932 stored \texttt{LHS1140b/exhale/} inputs, which were
  scanned for duplicate keys and have none but were not re-run.
\end{itemize}

\section{The adiabatic index of the molecular layer, and the chemical heat the
network releases (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:caloric-eos-and-reaction-heat}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{The judgement first, in two parts. (1) The code carried a
two-part equation of state whose halves disagreed: the thermal half has been
composition exact for a long time, $p = (n_{\rm tot}+n_e)kT$ with the species
count of the cell, but the caloric half, $e = p/(\gamma-1)$, used the monatomic
$\gamma = 5/3$ everywhere. That asserts that every particle stores
$\tfrac{3}{2}kT$; H$_2$ at 400--1300\,K stores about $\tfrac{5}{2}kT$, so where
the gas is 80 per cent H$_2$ the specific heat was wrong by a factor 1.67.
(2) Looking for the thermal H$_2$ dissociation-energy sink that
\texttt{lyman\_werner.f90} records as an open item turned up something larger:
none of the COLLISIONAL reactions of the H$_2$/He network deposits its chemical
energy, and on the converged He/H = 0.0793 rung that sum is 81 per cent of the
total heating rate at 1.02\,$r_{\rm base}$. Both are fixed. The caloric EOS is
structural, so an atomic run is byte-identical; the reaction heat defaults ON,
because in a molecular gas the ionization energy comes back to the GAS through
dissociative recombination instead of leaving as a photon.}

\medskip
This closes item (Z) of \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} and opens item (AB).
The census of every place $\gamma$ entered the code, the sizing experiment and
the design are in \texttt{docs/p53\_h2\_adiabatic\_index.md}.

\subsection{The rename}

The polytropic index was the single-letter global \texttt{g}
(\texttt{parameters.f90}), in a module almost every other module \texttt{use}s
whole, and five routines already declared a local or dummy \texttt{g} that
shadowed it: the merit gradient of \texttt{levenberg\_marquardt\_step} (whose
\texttt{mu} shadowed the global hydrogen-atom mass as well), a Jacobian entry
in \texttt{charge\_exchange}, the local gravitational acceleration and mean
molecular weight in \texttt{lower\_column}, a rate-coefficient function result
in \texttt{h2\_vibrational\_relaxation} and a table abscissa in
\texttt{h2\_self\_shielding\_table}. None was a bug, but this is the shadowing
class that cost hours twice before (\texttt{t0}/\texttt{T0},
\texttt{G2s}/\texttt{g2s}).

The global is now \texttt{gamma\_ad} and the five locals are named for what
they hold: \texttt{grad\_merit}, \texttt{mu\_damp}, \texttt{dR\_dn},
\texttt{grav\_accel}, \texttt{mu\_mean}, \texttt{gamma\_deex}, \texttt{axis}.
The whole regression matrix is byte-identical across the rename.

\subsection{The caloric equation of state}
\label{sec:caloric-eos-module}

\texttt{src/modules/states/caloric\_eos.f90} holds the map between internal
energy density, pressure and temperature for a mixture in which every atom, ion
and free electron carries $\tfrac{3}{2}k$ and H$_2$ carries its own
rovibrational heat capacity:
%
\begin{equation}
  e = \tfrac{3}{2}(n_{\rm tot}+n_e)kT + n({\rm H_2})\,k\,u_{\rm rv}(T),
  \qquad
  \gamma_{\rm eff} = 1 + \frac{n_{\rm tot}+n_e}
        {\tfrac{3}{2}(n_{\rm tot}+n_e) + n({\rm H_2})\,c_{\rm rv}(T)} .
\end{equation}

$u_{\rm rv}$ and $c_{\rm rv}$ are evaluated from the COMPLETE bound
rovibrational ladder of H$_2$ $X\,^1\Sigma_g^+$ --- 302 levels up to
51\,966\,K, the 4.478\,eV dissociation limit --- which the code already carried
in \texttt{molecular\_infrared\_data} (Roueff et al.\ 2019, A\&A 630, A58,
table 2, via VizieR J/A+A/630/A58). Using the observed ladder is not a
refinement for its own sake: it is the only H$_2$ level data in the tree, so
there is no second copy of the spectroscopic constants to drift, and a rigid
rotor plus a harmonic oscillator gives $c_v({\rm H_2})/k$ smaller by 1.4 per
cent at 200--900\,K, 2.3 per cent at 1300\,K and 7.3 per cent at 3000\,K.
Because the sum runs over one partition function with the nuclear-spin weights
inside it, this is the ortho/para EQUILIBRIUM mixture; a frozen $3\!:\!1$
mixture agrees to four decimals at and above 300\,K.

H$_2^+$, H$_3^+$ and HeH$^+$ are counted with $\tfrac{3}{2}k$ each. Measured
over every cell where H$_2$ exceeds $10^{-3}$ of the particle count
($r = 1.000$ to $1.101\,r_{\rm base}$), the largest ratios to H$_2$ are
$1.7\times10^{-7}$, $1.2\times10^{-7}$ and $3.2\times10^{-8}$, so giving all
three the full H$_2$ heat capacity would move $C_V$ by less than $10^{-6}$.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The table, and why the inverse is solved rather than lagged.}
The 302-level sum costs one exponential per level per evaluation, so
$u_{\rm rv}$ is tabulated once on a 4096-point logarithmic grid from 1\,K to
$5\times10^4$\,K and interpolated by a CUBIC HERMITE in $\ln T$ built on exact
nodal values of both $u_{\rm rv}$ and ${\rm d}u_{\rm rv}/{\rm d}\ln T$, so the
interpolant is $C^1$ and its own derivative is exact at the nodes. Against the
direct sum over 200--5000\,K the largest relative error is $10^{-12}$ in
$u_{\rm rv}$ and $9\times10^{-10}$ in $c_{\rm rv}$. With the vibrational ladder
in $c_v$ the map from internal energy to temperature is a genuinely nonlinear
scalar equation; it is inverted to full precision at every conversion by a
bisection-safeguarded Newton on the bracket $0 < T \le u/1.5$, NOT lagged at a
previous temperature, because a residual that depended on the previous state
would blur the fixed point of the steady solver and the finite-difference
Jacobian alike. The round trip $T \to u \to T$ is exact to $1.1\times10^{-15}$
over 24\,000 points and six H$_2$ fractions.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Where the local index is used, and where it is not.} Every
$E \leftrightarrow p$ conversion: \texttt{UW\_conversions}, \texttt{Source},
the HLLC and Lax--Friedrichs total energies and the physical flux in
\texttt{Num\_Fluxes}, the low-Mach dissipation pressure, the heating/cooling
temperature update in \texttt{energy\_semi\_implicit}, the heat capacity of the
conduction tridiagonal and the two energy rebuilds in
\texttt{viscous\_conduction}, the JFNK state scales in
\texttt{steady\_residual}, and the post-process energy equation
\texttt{T\_equation}. The sound speeds of \texttt{eval\_dt}, the base Mach
diagnostic of \texttt{Apply\_BC} and the carrier-row signal rate of
\texttt{diffusive\_photochemistry} use each cell's own $\gamma_{\rm eff}$.

The reconstruction needs no index: it works in primitive variables. Each face
state's energy and sound speed are built with the heat capacity of the cell it
was reconstructed from, which is well defined because both stored composition
quantities are ratios of number densities to $\rho$ --- functions of the mass
fractions alone --- and so are unchanged by the density difference between a
cell average and its face value. The one place a single index is still needed
is the Roe average $a_{\rm avg} = \sqrt{(\gamma-1)(H_{\rm avg}-v_{\rm avg}^2/2)}$
and the adaptive $p_\star$ estimate of \texttt{speed\_estimate\_ROE}, both
derived for one ideal gas on both sides; they are given the arithmetic mean of
the two face values. That is a WAVE-SPEED ESTIMATE, not a definition of the
steady state: the converged solution is the root of a residual assembled from
the conservative fluxes, and those carry each side's own EOS. The HLLC branch
needs no such average, its Davis--Einfeldt speeds taking one sound speed per
side already.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{One module was deleted on the way.}
\texttt{speed\_estimate\_HLLC} (Toro's adaptive $p_\star$ estimate) was
\texttt{use}d by \texttt{Num\_Fluxes} and never called. It has been removed
with its \texttt{use} and its \texttt{SRC} line; nothing links to it, so the
change is byte-identical.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Byte identity is structural, never a limit of the formula.}
With $n({\rm H_2}) = 0$ the mixture expression evaluates $1 + 1/1.5$, which is
not the same double as $5/3$. Two gates: a run with molecular chemistry off
leaves every map on the legacy expression verbatim, and inside a molecular run
a cell with exactly zero H$_2$ takes the same legacy expression.

\texttt{Load IC? True}, \texttt{Solver: Newton 100.0},
\texttt{du\_th [PLM,WENO3]: 1.0e9 1.0e-3},

\noindent\textbf{Reading.} The caloric EOS alone is small and confined to the
layer: $\dot M$ moves by $+0.003$\,dex (0.7 per cent) and $T$ by at most 18\,K,
warmer at the base and cooler by 1.4 per cent through 1.10--1.30, with the
H$_2$ front unmoved to 0.02 per cent. \textbf{The term that responds is the
advection term}, exactly as item (Z) predicted: $p\,{\rm div}\,v$ rises by 5 per
cent at 1.06 to 26 per cent at 1.01, while the advection term, which carries
$u = e/\rho$, changes SIGN over 1.03--1.06 (at 1.04, from $+4.7\times10^{-9}$
to $-2.5\times10^{-8}$). Above the front, where $\gamma_{\rm eff}$ is $5/3$ to

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Against the sizing experiment.} A whole-domain $\gamma = 7/5$
put $\log_{10}\dot M$ at $10.30 \to 10.23$ (a factor 0.85) and $T$ down by up
to 97\,K, and was called an upper bound. The local treatment is inside that
bound by a factor 20 in $\dot M$ and 5 in $T$, and \emph{it does not even share
its sign for} $\dot M$. The bound held; the extrapolation from it did not,
because the wind's energetics are set at and above the sonic transition, where
$\gamma_{\rm eff}$ is exactly $5/3$, so a global hack moves a region the
correct treatment leaves alone.

\subsection{The chemical heat the molecular network releases}
\label{sec:molecular-reaction-heat}

\noindent\textbf{What the code already deposited.}
\texttt{ionization\_equilibrium} adds the photoelectric heating of
H\,\textsc{i}, He\,\textsc{i}, He\,\textsc{ii}, He($2^3$S), H$_2$ and the
metals; the Balmer photoelectric heating of H($n=2$); the He-recombination
coupling; the He($2^3$S)+H Penning exothermicity (6.2\,eV); the
He($2^3$S)+H$_2$ Penning exothermicity (4.4\,eV); the Lyman--Werner fragment
kinetic energy (0.4\,eV per pair) and the fluorescence heat; and the FUV
photolysis heat of H$_2$O and OH. \texttt{eval\_cool} carries the
radiative-recombination and collisional-ionization sinks. \textbf{No
collisional reaction of the molecular network deposited anything.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Why that is not a small omission, and why the default is ON.}
Follow one closed cycle a photon drives:

\begin{verbatim}
H2 + hv  -> H2+ + e     photon pays I(H2) = 15.43 eV; the photoelectron keeps
                        hv - I(H2), which PH_heat_HHe already deposits
H2+ + H2 -> H3+ + H     + 1.70 eV
H3+ + e  -> H2 + H      + 9.25 eV, DISSOCIATIVE: into the fragments, not a
                        photon
\end{verbatim}

\noindent The cycle returns to H$_2$ having turned one H$_2$ into H\,+\,H and
left $I({\rm H_2}) - D_0({\rm H_2}) = 15.43 - 4.48 = 10.95$\,eV in the gas.
There is no photon anywhere in it to carry that away, and that is exactly what
differs from the atomic case, where the ionization energy leaves as the Lyman
photon of a radiative recombination and is therefore correctly absent from the
heating. Sized on the converged constant-$\gamma$ state, the sum of the
collisional reaction heats is 2.37 times the whole photoelectric heating rate
over 1.00--1.05\,$r_{\rm base}$, crossing 1 at 1.053 and falling to 1 per cent
by 1.10; solved self-consistently, the run's own
\texttt{Heating\_breakdown.txt} puts the new \texttt{heat\_mol\_chem} column at
\textbf{81 per cent of the total heating rate} at 1.02\,$r_{\rm base}$,
55 per cent at 1.05, 5 per cent at 1.10 and 1 per cent above. So
\texttt{Molecular reaction heat:} defaults to \texttt{True} and the key exists
to turn the term OFF for A/B work; an atomic run is gated out
(\texttt{thereis\_mol}) and is byte-identical either way.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The 4.478\,eV term alone would not have been right.} Sized on
the same state, $D_0({\rm H_2})\times$(three-body formation $-$ collisional
dissociation) is 1.06 times the whole photoelectric heating in the molecular
base, and every other molecular channel is 4 to 45 per cent of it by rate
(R8 0.45, R7 0.44, R6 0.19, R9 0.17, R20 0.15, R13 0.13, R19 0.12, R18 0.046,
R17 0.039), so the term the open item asked for is not separable from the rest
of the network.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{How it is built.}
\texttt{src/modules/lower\_atmosphere/molecular\_reaction\_heat.f90} computes
the heat from ONE table of species enthalpies --- the energy to build each
species out of ground-state H, ground-state He and free electrons at rest ---
so that the heat of $A+B \to C+D$ is $h(A)+h(B)-h(C)-h(D)$ and a cycle that
returns to its starting species releases exactly zero. A reaction-by-reaction
list has no such property. Excluded, so that nothing is counted twice: the
photon-driven reactions (H$_2$ photoionization and its dissociative branch,
Lyman--Werner photodissociation, the H and He photoionizations), the radiative
recombinations of H$^+$ and He$^+$, the collisional ionizations of H and He,
the Penning channels, and the H/He charge exchange. The three-body association
carries Hollenbach \& McKee's (1979, ApJS 41, 555, p.~586) collisional
branching $(1+n_{\rm cr}/n)^{-1}$, evaluated by the module that owns
$n_{\rm cr}$; in this layer that factor is 1 to a part in $10^3$.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l l p{0.46\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
constant & value & checked against \\
\midrule
$D_0({\rm H_2})$ & 36118.11\,cm$^{-1}$ & not repeated: read through
  \texttt{mol\_rates}, the code's single definition (Huber \& Herzberg 1979) \\
$I({\rm H})$  & 13.598434599702(12)\,eV & NIST Atomic Spectra Database \\
$I({\rm He})$ & 24.587389011(25)\,eV    & NIST Atomic Spectra Database \\
$I({\rm H_2})$& 15.42593(5)\,eV         & NIST Chemistry WebBook \\
$D_0({\rm H_3^+}\!\to\!{\rm H_2}+{\rm H^+})$ & $35\,076\pm2$\,cm$^{-1}$
  $=4.3489$\,eV & read in the PUBLISHED text of Mizus, Polyansky,
  McKemmish \& Tennyson (2019), Mol.\ Phys.\ 117, 1663
  (\texttt{references/Mizus\_2019MP\_117\_1663.pdf}) \\
$D_0({\rm HeH^+}\!\to\!{\rm He}+{\rm H^+})$ & 14882.16\,cm$^{-1}$ &
  DERIVED from the published text of Coxon \& Hajigeorgiou (1999),
  J.\ Mol.\ Spectrosc.\ 193, 306
  (\texttt{references/Coxon\_1999JMS\_193\_306.pdf}): their Table~9
  $D_e({}^4{\rm HeH^+}) = 16448.84$ minus their Table~8
  $G_0({}^4{\rm HeH^+}) = 1566.6764$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent $D_0({\rm H_3^+})$ is a 0\,K dissociation energy and deliberately not
the proton affinity of H$_2$, which NIST gives as 422.3\,kJ\,mol$^{-1}$ =
4.377\,eV at 298\,K --- the wrong quantity for a 0\,K ledger, and 0.028\,eV
away from the right one.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The HeH$^+$ constant had to be corrected, and that is why the
citation matters.} Coxon \& Hajigeorgiou determine a $D_e$, never a $D_0$:
$16456.24\pm0.1$\,cm$^{-1}$ for the Born--Oppenheimer potential and $16448.84$
for the $^4$HeH$^+$ isotopomer. The value 14874.215\,cm$^{-1}$ that the
secondary literature attributes to them appears nowhere in the paper. What the
paper supports is $D_0 = D_e - G_0$ with $G_0 = 1566.6764$\,cm$^{-1}$ from
their Table~8, i.e.\ $14882.16$\,cm$^{-1}$, and their own sentence fixes the
channel: ``Since the dissociation limit of the ground state of HeH$^+$ is
He\,$+$\,H$^+$''. The difference from the quoted number is 7.95\,cm$^{-1}$
($9.9\times10^{-4}$\,eV, 0.053 per cent); it moves $h({\rm HeH^+})$ and the
four HeH$^+$ reaction heats by that much, which is bitwise visible and was
folded in before the golden refresh. The converged measurement of
Sec.~\ref{sec:caloric-eos-measurement} was re-run with the corrected constant
and did not move: \texttt{info = 0}, the same $\lVert R\rVert$, flux spread,
$\log_{10}\dot M$, layer temperature minimum and H$_2$ front, and the same
$\Delta T$ against the control to 0.1\,K at every radius in the table.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{What it does, on the converged rung} (column C above). The
photoheating rate at 1.02\,$r_{\rm base}$ goes from $5.6\times10^{-8}$ to
$1.9\times10^{-7}$\,erg\,cm$^{-3}$\,s$^{-1}$, a factor 3.3; the layer
temperature minimum rises 410\,$\to$\,525\,K; 1.15 to 1.50\,$r_{\rm base}$
falls by 74 to 212\,K; $\log_{10}\dot M$ rises by 0.046\,dex; the H$_2$ front
moves out from 1.0418 to 1.0429\,$r_{\rm base}$ and the H$_3^+$ peak density
falls by 17 per cent. The run converges to \texttt{info = 0} with a flux spread
BETTER than the control's ($2.1\times10^{-3}$ against $3.0\times10^{-3}$).
Neither change is a candidate for the Koskinen temperature gap in the direction
it needs: the caloric EOS moves the layer minimum by $+7$\,K, and the reaction
heat moves it by $+115$\,K while taking 1.15--1.50\,$r_{\rm base}$ DOWN by
74--212\,K, so it is a redistribution rather than a closing of the gap.

\subsection{A lag the constant index was hiding}
\label{sec:base-ghost-composition-lag}

The steady residual fills the ghosts (\texttt{Apply\_BC}) BEFORE its ionization
sweep runs, so the ghost conservative state it writes carries the composition of
the previous sweep while the fluxes assembled afterwards carry this one. Under
a constant index the primitive-to-conservative round trip returns the pressure
the boundary condition asked for and the two cannot disagree; under the caloric
EOS they can, by as much as the ghost composition moved in one sweep. The gap
vanishes at the fixed point and is largest during relaxation.

It is not repaired here. The obvious fix --- a second \texttt{Apply\_BC(u)}
after the last composition refresh --- is not free, because \texttt{Apply\_BC}
is not idempotent even today: its interior round trip evaluates
\texttt{0.5*W(1)*W(2)**2} where the input was \texttt{0.5*u(2)*u(2)/u(1)}, and
those are not the same double, so a second call perturbs every interior cell at
the last bit and moves the whole atomic regression matrix --- the byte-identity
gate this change is accepted on. The lag is stated at the head of
\texttt{caloric\_eos.f90} and recorded as \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} item (AB).
\texttt{n\_part\_cell1} already had the same lag and the code already said so;
what changed is that it now reaches the ghost pressure itself. The marching
loop does not have it: there \texttt{Apply\_BC} follows the refresh.

\subsection{The golden refresh}

Both columns come from the SAME binary: the right-hand one is the default, the
left-hand one is that binary with \texttt{Molecular reaction heat: False}
appended to each input, i.e.\ stage 2 alone. Each entry is
$\Delta\log_{10}\dot M$ / max $|\Delta T|/T$ over the physical cells / the
largest $\Delta T$ below $1.2\,r_{\rm base}$, against the goldens in place
before this change (preserved as
\texttt{backup/regression/golden\_blockG\_20260903}).

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l l l@{}}
\toprule
case & stage 2 only & default (stage 2 + reaction heat) \\
\midrule
\texttt{wasp\_full}        & byte-identical & byte-identical \\
\texttt{wasp\_he23off}     & byte-identical & byte-identical \\
\texttt{lower\_profile}    & byte-identical & byte-identical \\
\texttt{mol\_base\_handoff} & $+0.0143$ / 3.5e-1 / $-65$\,K & $+0.0168$ / 3.7e-1 / $-65$\,K \\
\texttt{mol\_metals}       & $+0.0159$ / 1.9e-1 / $-73$\,K & $+0.0183$ / 2.0e-1 / $-73$\,K \\
\texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner}& $-0.0349$ / 4.4e-1 / $-40$\,K & $-0.0323$ / 4.5e-1 / $-39$\,K \\
\texttt{mol\_diffusion}    & $+0.0143$ / 3.5e-1 / $-65$\,K & $+0.0168$ / 3.7e-1 / $-65$\,K \\

\noindent The largest relative temperature change always falls at the
OUTERMOST cells, where the two builds sit at different points of the same
transient; the layer column is the one that means something.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The two columns are close only because of what these cases
are.} Every \texttt{mol\_*} case is a pinned-step relaxation snapshot, so it
stops long before a change in the heating rate can restructure the layer. The
reaction heat is 81 per cent of the base heating rate on a CONVERGED state and
moves that state's layer temperature minimum by $+115$\,K
(Sec.~\ref{sec:molecular-reaction-heat}); here it adds about $+0.003$\,dex and
no measurable $\Delta T$. These numbers are the golden refresh, not the physics.

\subsection{What was checked, and what is still open}

Regression: \texttt{wasp\_full}, \texttt{wasp\_he23off} and
\texttt{lower\_profile} are byte-identical against the previous goldens both
with the reaction heat on and with it off (\texttt{lower\_profile} never sets
\texttt{Molecular chemistry: True}, so the module-level gate never opens); the
seven \texttt{mol\_*} cases move and their goldens were refreshed, with the
previous block preserved as
\texttt{backup/regression/golden\_blockG\_20260903}. Neither the Roe nor the
Lax--Friedrichs branch is in the matrix --- every case runs HLLC --- so
\texttt{wasp\_full} was run for 300 steps under each against the pre-change
build: byte-identical on both output files for both, which is also the test of
the deleted module. The Roe branch was then run for 400 steps on
\texttt{mol\_base\_handoff}, where the two face values genuinely differ: clean,
no NaN. A \texttt{-fcheck=bounds,do,mem} build ran 600 steps each of
\texttt{wasp\_full}, \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff} and \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff}
with the reaction heat off, with no trap.

Still open: nothing on the constants --- both dissociation energies were read in
the publisher PDFs --- except that $D_0({\rm HeH^+})$ is DERIVED from its paper
rather than printed in it, so a later determination would mean redoing the
derivation; the associative
branch of the He($2^3$S) ionizations, He($2^3$S)+H $\to$ HeH$^+$+e (8.1\,eV),
left out because the metastable density in the layer is $2\times10^{-7}$
cm$^{-3}$, which makes the channel $10^{-13}$ of the sum; the
O($^1$D)+H$_2$ $\to$ OH+H exothermicity, already recorded as an omission
elsewhere; item (AB) above.
% ===================================================================== %
\section{P51: the coupled solve's step ascends because the pseudo-transient
term puts it there, and the flux gate cannot see how far the non-flatness
reaches (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:p51-pseudo-time-and-flux-windows}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{The judgement first, in four parts. (1) Of the three things
item (P51) left open, two are excluded by measurement.} The banded model's
missing non-local column coupling is REAL --- perturbing $n({\rm H_2})$ in one
front cell changes the residual of every cell BELOW it, 215 of them, far
outside the band half-width 11 --- and it is not the obstruction: that tail
carries 0.53 per cent of the response, its largest entry outside the band is
$3.5\times10^{-4}$ of the diagonal one, and the matrix-free $J v$ has it
already. The Krylov cycle reaches its tolerance in 1 to 2 directions at
${\rm rtol}=10^{-1}$ and 2 to 4 at $10^{-3}$, never truncating; tightening it
changes neither the direction nor where the solve stops. The frozen limited
slope is not the obstruction either: refreshing it at every residual evaluation
leaves the same sign change at the same outer iteration, and along the Newton
ray the inner model's residual and the true one agree to 5--6 significant
figures. \textbf{(2) The stagnating iterates are not stationary points}: the
merit falls along $-\delta Y$, 0.9287 to 0.8717 at $t=-0.1$, and along the ray
it is smooth over eight decades of $t$ with no kink and no noise, so this is
not the non-differentiable residual of \S\ref{sec:continuous-positivity-limiter}
either. \textbf{(3) The pseudo-transient term is what makes the step ascend.}
An exactly solved Newton system gives ${\rm slope}=-f_2$ whatever the Jacobian
is; this solver solves $(I/\Delta\tau + J)\,\delta Y = -F$ under the two-sided
scaling of \S139.5(i), and
%
\begin{equation}
  \left.\frac{{\rm d}f_2}{{\rm d}t}\right|_0
  \;=\; -f_2 \;-\; \frac{1}{\Delta\tau}\,
        \frac{\sum_k g_k\,(D_k/D^{\rm row}_k)\,x_k}{f_2},
  \qquad g = F/D^{\rm row},
\end{equation}
%
whose second term carries no fixed sign once $D$ and $D^{\rm row}$ differ.
\textbf{(4) A rule that raises $\Delta\tau$ until the slope is negative was
built, measured and NOT adopted}: it resolves every predicted ascent and
converges neither solve, because the arc over which the raised direction
descends is far shorter than the step. \textbf{The controlling quantity is the
step LENGTH, not the pseudo-time.} What did go into the code is one reporting
line --- the mass-flux spread over $r\ge1.03$ and $r\ge1.10$ printed beside the
gate's own window --- which changes no number and immediately found two things.

\medskip
\noindent The full measurement is \texttt{docs/p51\_coupled\_stagnation.md} and
\texttt{docs/p23\_transport\_on\_state.md}. \texttt{Molecular carrier
transport} and \texttt{Coupled carrier solve} stay default off and nothing here
is quoted as a rate.

\subsection{The three candidates, closed}

Everything is measured on the 1 microbar gate --- \texttt{mol\_carrier} plus
\texttt{Coupled carrier solve: True}, \texttt{Secondary\_ionization:
Immediate}, \texttt{Solver: Newton 4.0e-2} --- from one state marched 36{,}001
steps past the golden snapshot, because \S139.9 records that the E1d hand-off
cannot be reproduced in the tree. The directional derivative of the merit along
the Newton step, in units of $-f_2$ (an exact Newton direction gives $-1$):

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrrrrr}
\toprule
outer iteration & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 8 & 10 & 12\\
\midrule
the code's own cycle, ${\rm rtol}=10^{-1}$ & $-0.502$ & $-0.120$ & $-0.019$ & $-0.003$ & $\mathbf{+0.018}$ & $+0.043$ & $+0.487$ & $+0.631$ & $+0.858$\\
tightened, ${\rm rtol}=10^{-3}$, $m=120$   & $-0.503$ & $-0.118$ & $-0.016$ & $\mathbf{+0.001}$ & $+0.021$ & $+0.042$ & $+0.494$ & $+0.604$ & $+0.817$\\
the limited slope refreshed                & $-0.506$ & $-0.119$ & $-0.017$ & $\mathbf{+0.001}$ & $+0.025$ & $+0.009$ & $+0.065$ & $+0.280$ & $+0.908$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\noindent Two things at once: the direction is never a good Newton direction
--- it delivers half the descent an exact one would even at iteration 1 --- and
it changes sign at iteration 4 or 5 in every run regardless of how the Krylov
step is solved or whether the limiter is frozen. All three end at the same
place, carrier row $1.02$--$1.03\times10^{-2}$ against a $10^{-3}$ gate.

\subsection{The pseudo-time step, measured}

The slope the linear model itself predicts, from the same $J v$ the Krylov
space is built from, beside the $\Delta\tau$ the SER ramp was holding:

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\small

outer iteration & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 8 & 10 & 12\\
\midrule
$\Delta\tau_0=1$ (the hand-off's own), $\Delta\tau$ & 1.00 & 1.17 & 1.21 & 1.17 & 1.12 & 1.54 & 0.498 & 0.856\\

measured slope & $-0.928$ & $-0.211$ & $-0.031$ & $-0.004$ & $+0.025$ & $+0.547$ & $+0.657$ & $+0.797$\\

\noindent The model slope and the measured slope agree to three or four digits
at every iteration --- the model is right about the function and wrong about
the direction --- and the $\Delta\tau_0$ rows say why: with the
pseudo-transient term made negligible the SAME Jacobian, the SAME
preconditioner and the SAME frozen model give a descent direction at every one
of those iterations.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The escalation rule, measured and not adopted.} Raise
$\Delta\tau$ by 100 and re-solve whenever the model says the step ascends,
until the slope is negative or $\Delta\tau$ reaches the ramp's ceiling
$10^{14}\Delta\tau_0$. Its directional derivative is free: \texttt{pgmres} can
return $A_z x$ from its own Arnoldi relation
$A_z M^{-1} V_k = V_{k+1}\bar H_k$, so no residual is evaluated.

\midrule
