\noindent It helps one state and loses the other, and the reason is measured:
after a raise the line search still cuts to $\lambda=9.5\times10^{-7}$. Capping
the raised step at the ascending one's length is necessary and not sufficient.
So the repair belongs at the step length --- a trust region sized by the arc the
ray scan measures --- and that is \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} item (P51
continuation).

\subsection{What went into the code: the spread at three radii, not one}

The gate is the mass-flux spread over $r\ge r_{\rm flux}$, $1.2\,R_p$ by
default (\S133.2), and it cannot show how far the non-flatness reaches.
\texttt{flux\_spread\_above\_radius} takes the same spread over any inner
radius, FOR REPORTING ONLY; \texttt{flux\_spread\_of\_state} and
\texttt{steady\_gates\_met} are untouched, so the acceptance test is the same
test and no golden can move on this.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{It earned itself immediately.} On the 1 microbar hot Uranus the
gate's whole $1.70\times10^{-1}$ comes from its own window's inner edge ---
every cell above $1.4\,R_p$ is flat to 1 per cent. Run past its \texttt{du}
plateau stop, that run falls to a gate-window minimum of
$\mathbf{1.015\times10^{-2}}$ at 180{,}500 further steps and \textbf{turns
around}, reaching $4.417\times10^{-2}$ by the time it converges on its own
criterion at 212{,}706 further steps ($\texttt{du}=9.9998\times10^{-4}$ against
$\texttt{du\_th}=10^{-3}$, with $\|R\|$ at $3.5\times10^{-6}$, below its own
gate); meanwhile $r\ge1.10$ moves only $3.1\to2.5\to2.9\times10^{-1}$ and
$r\ge1.03$ $7.8\to6.9\to7.3\times10^{-1}$. So on this planet the marching's own
convergence criterion and the flux gate are anti-correlated over the last third
of the trajectory: \textbf{the state the run calls converged is not the
flattest one it passed through, and neither meets the flux gate.} This is a
finding about the \texttt{du} plateau detector and the \texttt{du} stop, not a
proposal to move $r_{\rm flux}$.

\subsection{A reporting defect the same measurement exposed}

The coupled Newton from either of those states meets the residual gate for the
first time --- $\|R\| = 1.547\times10^{-6}$ and $1.383\times10^{-6}$ against
$10^{-5}$ --- and returns \texttt{info = 2} on the other two. The old report
then printed \texttt{the CARRIER gate is the one left}, which is wrong: the
flux gate was also unmet, at $2.447\times10^{-2}$ against $5\times10^{-3}$. The
chain tested the residual and the flux gate TOGETHER first and only then fell
through to the carrier row, so a state that met the residual gate and missed
the other two named one of the two it missed; nothing before had met the
residual gate with the carrier row in the unknowns. It is now one line per
unmet gate, each asked separately.

\subsection{What was checked}

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{make check}, \textbf{10 of 10 byte-identical} against the goldens
      as refreshed for \S\ref{sec:caloric-eos-and-reaction-heat}. Only log
      lines change, and no golden carries them.
\item Four \texttt{Solver: Newton} cases --- \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton},
      \texttt{wasp\_he23off\_newton}, \texttt{solver\_newton\_cold},
      \texttt{newton\_rsw01} --- byte-identical to the same cases run with the
      unpatched binary. The escalation rule, measured on the same fourteen
      before it was set aside, never once predicted an ascent in them.
\item The Arnoldi slope against a direct $J v$ along the same step:
      \textbf{54 of 56} comparisons agree in sign, $1.5\times10^{-7}$ relative
      at iteration 1. The two that disagree are where the merit turns over
      inside the probe step, which is the same curvature again.
\item NOT checked: any planet but the ${\rm He/H}=0.0793$ hot Uranus and the
      WASP-121b of the matrix; whether the band half-width 11 is exact rather
      than sufficient; whether $r_{\rm flux}=1.2$ is the right window edge on
      this planet.
\end{itemize}

\section{Every conservation row is measured against the largest term it
contains (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:row-scales-own-terms}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{Judgement first. The residual's row scale was a bound on the
wrong quantity, and the error is exactly quantifiable on each row.} Dividing
the mass residual by $\rho(|v|+c_s)/\Delta r$ gives identically the fractional
change of the mass flux across the cell TIMES the local Mach number ---
verified to one per cent at ten radii --- so a quasi-hydrostatic layer at
${\rm Ma}=5\times10^{-5}$ was invisible by a factor $2\times10^{4}$. The
momentum row's two terms are a near-cancellation that is $4.4\times10^{5}$
times the wind's mass flux in the same layer, so a row reading $10^{-8}$ on
that scale was still displacing the wind measurably per crossing time. The
energy row of the layer was out by one part in a thousand of the terms it
balances, and cell~1 by 99 per cent, while both read $10^{-8}$ to $10^{-4}$.
\textbf{Each row is now divided by the largest term it itself contains} --- the
flux it differences, the source it is balanced against, and for the energy row
the two radiative terms it is the difference of --- all of which
\texttt{RK\_rhs} and the ionization sweep already produce. The 1~microbar
hot-Uranus gate rung, accepted before at $\|R\|=2.9\times10^{-6}$ with a mass
flux 30 per cent out at $1.03\,R_{\rm p}$, now converges to a flux flat to
$1.0\times10^{-4}$ from $1.01\,R_{\rm p}$ outward and to residuals of
$5\times10^{-9}$ to $5\times10^{-6}$ on every row above the first cell, in 14
JFNK iterations against 5, with $\log_{10}\dot M$ unchanged at 10.34. The
Newton system and the line-search merit keep the state scales, deliberately.

\medskip
\noindent Full measurement: \texttt{docs/p54\_base\_layer\_mass\_flux.md} (the
mass row and the census), \texttt{docs/p55\_base\_mode.md} (the momentum row
and the marching departure), \texttt{docs/p54g23\_row\_scale\_scan.md} (all
three rows compared). This closes item (AA) for the mass flux and opens
(AD) and (AE) in \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md}.

\subsection{What the old scale measured}

Section~\ref{sec:two-gates} made every row's scale a bound on that row's own
largest term, the cell's state scale times the rate at which a signal crosses
the cell, $D_k(j)\,(|v_j|+c_{s,j})/\Delta r_j$. It is a bound, but on the wrong
quantity: nothing in any of these rows moves at $c_s$.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Mass.} The row has no source (\texttt{Source.f90},
$S_1=0$), so it is
%
\begin{equation}
  R_1(j) \;=\; \frac{F_{j+1/2}\,r_{j+1/2}^2 - F_{j-1/2}\,r_{j-1/2}^2}{\Delta V_j},
\end{equation}
%
and nothing else. Writing $\Delta V_j \simeq r_j^2\,\Delta r_j$ and
$F\simeq\rho v r^2$,
%
\begin{equation}
  \frac{R_1}{s_1} \;\simeq\;
  \frac{\Delta(F r^2)}{F}\,\frac{|v|}{|v|+c_s}
  \;\simeq\; \frac{\Delta F}{F}\;{\rm Ma}.
\end{equation}
%
\emph{Measured} on the converged 1~microbar hot Uranus, the ratio of
$|R_1|/s_1$ to $(\Delta F/F)\,{\rm Ma}$ is 1.109, 1.004, 1.015, 1.007, 1.008,
1.010, 1.006, 0.979, 0.908, 0.656 at $r=1.001$, 1.004, 1.010, 1.023, 1.032,
1.048, 1.093, 1.177, 1.329, 2.119 --- one per cent everywhere the flow is
subsonic. The flux change per cell that a tolerance of $10^{-5}$ still passed:

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
$r$ & ${\rm Ma}$ & $\Delta F/F_0$ carried & $\Delta F/F_0$ passed at $10^{-5}$\\
\midrule
1.001 & $3.9\times10^{-5}$ & $1.5\times10^{-2}$ & $2.6\times10^{-1}$\\
1.010 & $5.2\times10^{-5}$ & $3.8\times10^{-3}$ & $1.9\times10^{-1}$\\
1.031 & $1.5\times10^{-4}$ & $9.9\times10^{-4}$ & $6.7\times10^{-2}$\\
1.093 & $4.5\times10^{-3}$ & $1.9\times10^{-3}$ & $2.2\times10^{-3}$\\
1.329 & $1.1\times10^{-1}$ & $2.1\times10^{-5}$ & $8.7\times10^{-5}$\\
2.119 & $5.4\times10^{-1}$ & $4.5\times10^{-6}$ & $1.9\times10^{-5}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\noindent\textbf{Momentum.} In a quasi-hydrostatic layer the row is the
near-cancellation of a flux divergence and gravity, both enormous beside the
wind's mass flux: $\max(|{\rm d}F_2|,|S_2|)/F_0$ is $4.41\times10^{5}$ at
$1.005\,R_{\rm p}$, $1.12\times10^{5}$ at 1.03, $4.46\times10^{3}$ at 1.10 and
$1.92\times10^{2}$ at 1.20 on the hot Uranus ($7.69\times10^{3}$,
$2.24\times10^{3}$, $1.08\times10^{2}$, $1.71\times10^{1}$ on WASP-121b). A
residual $\epsilon$ of that row therefore displaces the mass flux by
$\epsilon\,(|{\rm d}F_2|/F_0)$ of the wind per crossing time, and
\texttt{docs/p55\_base\_mode.md} \S4 predicts the measured departure rate of an
accepted state from exactly that product to \textbf{9 per cent}.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Energy.} Same construction, same result: the accepted state's
row reads $1.72\times10^{-3}$ at $1.03\,R_{\rm p}$ and $4.68\times10^{-3}$ at
1.05 against its own terms while reading $3\times10^{-9}$ to
$4\times10^{-8}$ against $E(|v|+c_s)/\Delta r$.

\subsection{It is not a diagnostic artifact}

Before changing the measure, the obvious alternative was checked: that the
cell-centred $\rho v r^2$ the diagnostics print is not what the finite-volume
scheme conserves, and that the scheme's own face flux is flat. It is not.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{lrr}
\toprule
$r\ge$ & spread, cell centre & spread, Riemann face\\
\midrule
1.002 & $3.247\times10^{-1}$ & $3.282\times10^{-1}$\\
1.030 & $3.105\times10^{-1}$ & $3.137\times10^{-1}$\\
1.100 & $2.920\times10^{-2}$ & $3.041\times10^{-2}$\\
1.200 & $2.460\times10^{-3}$ & $2.513\times10^{-3}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\noindent The two agree to within one to four per cent at every window above
$1.002\,R_{\rm p}$. The one place they differ is cell~1, where the centred
product is $-21\,F_0$ --- negative, 21 times the wind flux --- while both of
its faces carry $+1.75$ and $+1.92\,F_0$; that is the odd-even mode of
\texttt{docs/p44\_base\_sawtooth.md}, and it is why the face flux is single
signed over the whole column where the cell-centred one changes sign. There is
no mass source that could produce the rest: $S_1=0$, and the Shapiro filter,
the low-Mach damping, the element diffusion, the carrier transport, the viscous
and conduction operators and the semi-implicit energy step were each checked
and none writes $u(1,:)$.

\subsection{The change}

\texttt{residual\_row\_scale} now dispatches to three functions, each named for
the physics it scales:
%
\begin{align}
  s_1(j) &= \max\!\left(|F_{j-1/2}|\,r_{j-1/2}^2,\;
                        |F_{j+1/2}|\,r_{j+1/2}^2\right)\big/\Delta V_j
            & &\texttt{mass\_flux\_row\_scale}\\
  s_2(j) &= \max\!\left(|{\rm d}F_2(j)|,\;|S_2(j)|\right)
            & &\texttt{momentum\_row\_scale}\\
  s_3(j) &= \max\!\left(|{\rm d}F_3(j)|,\;|S_3(j)|,\;
                        {\rm heat}(j),\;{\rm cool}(j)\right)
            & &\texttt{energy\_row\_scale}
\end{align}
%
plus the operator-split viscous and conduction sources where those are active.
$\Delta V_j$ is the volume \texttt{RK\_rhs} divides the flux difference by, so
$R_1/s_1$ is exactly the fractional change of the mass flux across the cell.
There is no fallback and no second definition: the terms are those
\texttt{assemble\_residual} has just had \texttt{RK\_rhs} and the sweep
produce, and a caller asking about a state they do not describe gets the
Riemann solve done on the spot (\texttt{refresh\_row\_terms}). That path cannot
rebuild \texttt{heat}/\texttt{cool}, which do not come from $u$; the states that
reach it are the solver's trial and finite-difference probes --- \emph{measured},
15 of order $10^5$ scale requests on the hot Uranus and 45 on WASP-121b, none
of them a state the run adopts --- and the code says so where it happens. The
face-limiter ledger is restored across such a rebuild, because a measurement of
a state is not a step of the run.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The \S62.3 gravitational bound is no longer a special case.}
It existed because the old momentum scale could not see gravity; $s_2$ now
takes gravity from $S_2$, the same expression the residual subtracts, so the
two are one term and not two.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The Newton system is NOT rescaled with any of this.}
\texttt{cell\_state\_scales} keeps $D_k$. Rescaling the merit and the scaled
Jacobian by these quantities as well was tried on the mass row --- it varies by
a factor 9 across the first two cells --- and the hot-Uranus solve then ground
from $2.2\times10^{-2}$ to a plateau at $7.8\times10^{-4}$, spent most of 179
iterations in damped Gauss-Newton escapes, and aborted on \texttt{no descent
direction exists for the banded model at this state} at 8238 residual
evaluations against 115 for the baseline. So \S133's statement that the merit
and the acceptance test are one expression apart now holds for neither, and
that is the measured choice.

\medskip
\noindent\texttt{Resid tol} changes meaning on all three rows, in the direction
that makes it stricter: on the states measured the rows read 58 to 4000 times
larger than before. No repository value is renormalized --- the states that
pass the new measure pass at the existing $10^{-5}$ --- but \emph{every golden
that runs a steady solve or a residual gate moves}, and that is a deliberate
refresh, not a byte-identical change. A run that stops on \texttt{du} alone is
byte-identical.

\subsection{What it does to the cases}

All 34 named cases were run under both binaries --- the 10-case
\texttt{run\_check.sh} matrix, every \texttt{backup/regression/} case carrying
\texttt{Solver: Newton}, and the three \texttt{Resid tol} cases --- from copies
of their inputs, each keeping its own \texttt{maxsteps} and otherwise capped at
60{,}000 steps. Full table: \texttt{docs/p54g23\_census.md}.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Seven goldens move; twenty-seven are byte-identical.} The
seven are \texttt{arm\_heh1\_x2matched}, \texttt{newton\_rsw01},
\texttt{newton\_rsw05}, \texttt{ptc\_warm}, \texttt{solver\_newton\_cold},
\texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} and \texttt{wasp\_he23off\_newton} --- exactly the
cases that reach their answer through a steady solve or the residual gate. A
run that stops on \texttt{du}, on \texttt{maxsteps}, or on a JFNK that aborts
before its first accepted step never reads a row scale, and is unchanged: that
is the check on the change, and it is why the default regression matrix is
10/10 identical.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{The rate does not move.}
$|\Delta\log_{10}\dot M|\le0.01$ on every case that converged under both. The
single exception is \texttt{arm\_heh1\_x2matched} at $-0.19$, and it is an
improvement: that case does not converge at all under the old measure ---
60{,}000 steps and no acceptance --- and under this one it converges, in 106
iterations against 40 and at 89 residual evaluations against 1127, i.e.\
twelve times cheaper. Its old number was an unconverged state's rate.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{No case that converged stops converging.} Three cases fail
under this measure --- \texttt{armD\_D2\_LW\_newton}, \texttt{armD\_D2\_newton},
\texttt{armD\_D2\_newton\_bigstack} --- and all three fail under the old one
too, at the same iteration and for the same reason (\texttt{no descent
direction exists for the banded model at this state}, at flux spreads of 21 to
34, i.e.\ states nowhere near steady). The failure list is a strict subset of
the old one; \texttt{docs/p54g23\_nonconvergent.md} records which row and which
cell blocks each.

\noindent Two and a half to eight times the residual evaluations where the old

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{What the accepted states look like.} Every case that converges
under this measure ends with its mass flux flat to $5\times10^{-5}$ to

over $r\ge1.03$, where before it was $2.0\times10^{-4}$ to

\noindent\textbf{Cell 1 does not move, on either planet, under any variant

the norm is volume weighted and that cell's volume is negligible. That is item
(V), and these are the sharpest numbers it has.

\subsection{The marching stop and the flux gate measure the same quantity
through different windows (decision pending, not implemented)}

This is a separate finding of the census and it is \textbf{not implemented}:
the code keeps \texttt{du} as it is. It is recorded because the census makes it
unavoidable.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\toprule
 & marching \texttt{du} & flux gate\\
\midrule
window     & $[j_{\min}\!:\!N]$, $r\ge r_{\rm esc}$ & $[j_{\rm flux}\!:\!N]$, $r\ge r_{\rm flux}=1.2$\\
functional & $(\max|F|-\min|F|)/\min|F|$ & $(\max F-\min F)/|\overline{F}|$\\
sign       & absolute value & signed\\
threshold  & \texttt{du\_th}, $10^{-3}$ & \texttt{flux\_spread\_th}, $5\times10^{-3}$\\
stops      & the marching loop, the JFNK hand-off & the acceptance of a steady solve\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\noindent $r_{\rm esc}$ is $2.0\,R_{\rm p}$ on the hot Uranus and 1.5 on
WASP-121b, so \texttt{du} is a statement about the outer wind only and says
nothing about $1.2\le r\le r_{\rm esc}$ --- a region the flux gate does cover.
Not hypothetical: \texttt{wasp\_full}, a matrix golden, stops as ``converged''
on $\texttt{du}=9.999\times10^{-4}<10^{-3}$ at an $r\ge1.2$ spread of
$3.13\times10^{-2}$, six times the flux gate's own threshold and 1.37 at
$r\ge1.01$; P51's transport-on hot Uranus stopped the same way at
$4.4\times10^{-2}$. The census makes the same point on the other side:
\texttt{du} and the gate's spread are uncorrelated on the states these cases
stop at --- every \texttt{armD\_*}/\texttt{armHeH\_*} snapshot ends with
\texttt{du} between 1.1 and 28 and a gate spread between 0.77 and 35.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Recommendation, physics first (a decision, not a change).} A
steady state has one mass flux at every altitude, not one mass flux above
$2\,R_{\rm p}$. Two definitions of the same statement, differing in window and
in functional, is what the naming rule forbids: one kind of quantity, one rule.
The \texttt{du} window should become the gate's window and the functional the
gate's functional, so that \texttt{du\_th} and \texttt{flux\_spread\_th} become
one number. \textbf{This is a user decision and it is not in the code.} It is a
different change with a different blast radius: it moves where every marching
run stops, hence every golden that stops on \texttt{du} --- which is most of
them --- for a reason independent of the row scale.

\subsection{What is not settled}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The first two cells.} No measure change moves them; they pass
      because the norm is volume weighted. Item (V).
\item \textbf{The marching attractor.} A state this measure accepts is a zero
      of the steady residual and is not a fixed point of the marching loop.
      Reloaded and marched 5000 steps, the hot Uranus's departure is halved by
      the mass row's scale alone (peak-to-peak of $F(1.03)/F_0$ $1.127\to0.509$)
      and then moves only to 0.495 when the momentum and energy rows are added,
      while WASP-121b's three roots --- residuals spanning four orders of
      magnitude --- all depart identically (4.277, 4.291, 4.292). \emph{The
      departure is not controlled by the part of the residual this section
      removes}; it is a restart kick and a cell-1 problem
      (\texttt{docs/p55\_base\_mode.md} \S7(2) and \S7(3)). New item (AD).
\item \textbf{The energy half of (AA)}, the factor-2 gap in
      ${\rm heating}={\rm cooling}+p\,{\rm div}\,v+{\rm advection}$ below
      $1.08\,r_{\rm base}$. This section is a statement about how a row is
      measured, not about what it contains.
\end{itemize}

\texttt{mass\_flux\_row\_scale}, \texttt{momentum\_row\_scale},
\texttt{energy\_row\_scale}, \texttt{store\_row\_terms},
\texttt{refresh\_row\_terms}; \texttt{residual\_row\_scale} dispatches),
\texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_newton.f90} (comment only).
Documentation: \texttt{docs/p54\_base\_layer\_mass\_flux.md},
\texttt{docs/p55\_base\_mode.md}, \texttt{docs/p54g23\_row\_scale\_scan.md},
\texttt{docs/input\_schema.md} (K35, K35b),
\texttt{docs/newton\_scaling\_and\_base\_wall.md} (\S2 and \S3),
\texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} ((AA) closed for the mass flux, (V) extended,
(AD) and (AE) opened).

\section{P55: the accepted root, the marching fixed point, and what a restart
must carry (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:p55-restart}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{Judgement first. A state the steady solver accepts is not a
fixed point of the marching loop, and the reason is mostly in the STATE, not in
the operator.} The spatial operator is the same by construction ---
\texttt{assemble\_residual} calls the same \texttt{Reconstruct} and
\texttt{RK\_rhs} the marching calls --- and the departure is not an
instability: it starts at step~1 at a finite size and grows \emph{linearly} in
step number, at a rate the accepted state's own residual predicts to nine
percent. Two things produce it, both measured; one is now fixed, and the other
is what \S\ref{sec:row-scales-own-terms}'s item (AD) is about.

\noindent Full account and figures: \texttt{docs/p55\_base\_mode.md},
\texttt{docs/p55\_base\_mode.png}, \texttt{docs/p55\_operator\_terms.png},
\texttt{docs/p55\_reload.png}.

\subsection{The departure is a residual being integrated, not a mode growing}

On the two \texttt{EXHALE\_CONT\_SCALE=gate} solutions of
\S\ref{sec:row-scales-own-terms} (the $1\,\mu$bar hot Uranus and WASP-121b),
reloaded and marched with \texttt{Solver:} removed:

\begin{itemize}
\item the flux at $r=1.03$ moves \textbf{linearly in step number} for the first
      twenty steps --- $4.71\times10^{-4}$ of $F_0$ per step on the hot Uranus,
      against a state the solve left flat to $1.04\times10^{-4}$ over
      $r\ge1.01$. \textbf{One step undoes 4.5 times the flatness the solve
      achieved.}
\item the state's own momentum-row residual there predicts
      $4.31\times10^{-4}$ per step. Nine percent agreement, no free parameter.
      In a quasi-hydrostatic layer the momentum row is the near-cancellation of
      two terms worth $1.1\times10^{5}$ times the wind's mass flux, so one part
      in $10^{5}$ of that row displaces the mass flux by order the wind itself.
\item judged by its own largest term instead of by $\rho(|v|+c_s)/\delta r$,
      the accepted hot-Uranus state's energy row is out by $1.2\times10^{-3}$ at
      $r=1.03$ and $6.0\times10^{-3}$ at 1.05, its momentum row by
      $2.5\times10^{-5}$, and cell~1 by $1.4\times10^{-1}$ and
      $9.9\times10^{-1}$. That is what \S\ref{sec:row-scales-own-terms}'s row
      scales are for.
\end{itemize}

\noindent\emph{Not a discrete instability}: quartering the time step changes the
excursion by 3 percent at equal model time; first-order reconstruction at the
base leaves WASP-121b unchanged and makes the hot Uranus 12 times worse; the
Shapiro filter removes 8 percent on WASP-121b and multiplies the hot Uranus by
\textbf{42}; freezing the first 20 cells does nothing on WASP-121b.
\emph{Not a physical instability} either: the rise is linear, and the same
operator started from a state the marching itself produced departs 3 to 41 times
less.

\subsection{A restart did not run the physics its state was converged under}

WASP-121b's input sets no \texttt{Secondary\_ionization:} key, so the
SvS85/Dalgarno coupling is STAGED. The run that WROTE the state armed it at step
2242 and the JFNK finished with it on --- and every written state is a
coupling-on state, because the post-loop arming precedes \texttt{write\_output}.
The run that RESTARTED it re-staged it, and the flip never fired again in 3000
steps. \textbf{Every marching experiment on WASP-121b in this series was
therefore run at a photoionization rate the state was not converged under.} The
first ionization sweep moved the particle count by $8.1\times10^{-3}$ instead of
$2.6\times10^{-4}$.

The state cannot carry that by itself, so the file now says it.
\texttt{write\_coupling\_state\_header} (\texttt{utilities.f90}) adds one
\texttt{\#} line to \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt}, which is the file a restart is fed
as \texttt{Hydro\_ioniz\_IC.txt}:

\begin{quote}\ttfamily\small
\# coupling: sec\_ion=T sec\_ion\_step=2242 valve= 1.00000E-04 recon=WENO3
fluxconst=-1.00000E+00
\end{quote}

\noindent It is the census of every switch \texttt{EXHALE\_main} changes
\emph{inside} the marching loop:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.30\linewidth}p{0.42\linewidth}p{0.20\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
switch & what changes it & field \\
\midrule
\texttt{sec\_ion\_active} and the step it was armed at &
the du-convergence flip, the pre-hand-off flip, the unconditional post-loop
arming & \texttt{sec\_ion}, \texttt{sec\_ion\_step} \\
\texttt{valve\_eps} & the JFNK hand-off adopts $10^{-4}$ when the input left the
valve off & \texttt{valve} \\
\texttt{rec\_method} & the \texttt{PLM+WENO3} stage switch at
$du<du_{\rm th,PLM}$ & \texttt{recon} \\
\texttt{base\_flux\_const} & the 100-step average behind
\texttt{Base velocity: massflux} & \texttt{fluxconst} \\
\texttt{du\_stop\_armed}, \texttt{du\_newton\_armed} & the first descending $du$
crossing & already keyed to \texttt{do\_load\_IC} \\
\texttt{weno\_mode} & frozen inside the JFNK, restored on exit & not run state
outside the solver \\
\texttt{*\_active} (viscosity, conduction, transport, low-Mach, caloric, CX) &
nothing: pure functions of input parameters & not run state \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\texttt{load\_IC} parses the line and the run starts the coupling where
the file says it was; \texttt{valve} and \texttt{recon} are properties of the
run, which \texttt{input.inp} states, so they are reported when they disagree and
never overridden. \textbf{A file with no \texttt{\# coupling:} line starts staged
exactly as it did before}, because nothing else can be inferred about it --- and
that is not a formality: on \texttt{jfnk\_hd189}, whose IC predates the line,
arming it blindly makes the composition mismatch \emph{worse}
($4.12\times10^{-3}\to6.26\times10^{-3}$) and produces a $du=1.0\times10^{2}$
transient by step 5500. \texttt{write\_setup\_report} prints which of the three
cases the run is in.

Measured, 3000 steps from the WASP-121b solution, peak-to-peak of
$\Delta(Fr^2)/F_0$:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccc@{}}
\toprule
 & $r{=}1.005$ & 1.03 & 1.10 & 1.20 & $v(1)$ end & $du$ end \\
\midrule
before                        & 7.9689 & 4.2961 & 1.1976 & 0.6349 & 5.766e-03 & 1.178e-02 \\
composition equilibrated      & 8.0041 & 4.3197 & 1.1970 & 0.6341 & 5.880e-03 & 1.130e-02 \\
\textbf{with the header}      & \textbf{0.0382} & \textbf{0.0174} & \textbf{0.0051} & \textbf{0.0040} & \textbf{3.150e-03} & \textbf{5.187e-05} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent $du$ ends at $5.187\times10^{-5}$ against the $5.03\times10^{-5}$ the
accepted state carries: \textbf{with the restart running the physics the state
was converged under, the JFNK root IS a fixed point of the marching on
WASP-121b}, to one part in 250 of what the re-staged run does. The hot Uranus is
unchanged to five digits, as it must be: its input sets
\texttt{Secondary\_ionization: Immediate}.

\subsection{A restart did not start from its own equilibrium composition}

The marching step ends with
${\rm RK3}\to T=p/(n_{\rm tot}+n_e)\to\texttt{ioniz\_eq}\to p=(n_{\rm
tot}+n_e)T$, whose last stage rewrites the pressure at the particle count the
sweep just produced. On any step of a relaxed run that is a rate. On the FIRST
step of a restart it is a \textbf{projection of fixed size}, because the
composition it corrects came from the file. The same first step at four time
steps, as $\Delta E_{\rm chem}/E$:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccc@{}}
\toprule
 & CFL 0.6 & 0.06 & 0.006 & 0.0006 \\
\midrule
WASP-121b $r{=}1.10$, before & -6.2295e-03 & -6.2297e-03 & -6.2297e-03 & -6.2297e-03 \\
WASP-121b $r{=}1.10$, after  & \textbf{-3.2041e-06} & -3.2067e-07 & -3.2070e-08 & -3.2072e-09 \\
hot Uranus $r{=}1.03$, before & 5.4549e-07 & 5.5078e-07 & 5.5131e-07 & 5.5136e-07 \\
hot Uranus $r{=}1.03$, after  & \textbf{-5.8808e-09} & -5.8712e-10 & -5.8546e-11 & -5.6966e-12 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent Four decades of $\delta t$ and four identical values is a projection;
one factor of ten per decade is a rate. Before the fix the jump reaches
$6.2\times10^{-3}$ of the cell energy in one step, twelve times that step's
entire hydro contribution.

\texttt{equilibrate\_loaded\_composition} (\texttt{EXHALE\_main.f90}) holds
$\rho$, $v$ and $p$ --- the primitive state the file carries --- and iterates the
composition to the fixed point of $f_{\rm sp}\leftarrow\texttt{ioniz\_eq}(\rho,T)$
with $T=p/(n_{\rm tot}+n_e)$, using the same sweep the marching loop and the
steady residual call, with the same secondary-ionization arming. It runs on the
marching route and on the \texttt{EXHALE\_RESIDUAL} route, capped at 64 sweeps,
stopping at $10^{-10}$ (the floor the cell solve's own \texttt{xtol} sets, not a
target). \texttt{EXHALE\_RELOAD\_EQ=0} reproduces a run of the previous code bit
for bit.

\textbf{Writing the files with more digits would not have helped.} They are
written with list-directed output, i.e.\ full double precision already
(\texttt{0.99980405732338939}), and the written triple is self-consistent to
$10^{-8}$ at most radii. The gap is four to five orders above anything the
format could cause.

Every named Load-IC case starts more than four parts in a thousand from the
equilibrium of its own state; \texttt{armD\_D2\_newton} starts
$7.127\times10^{-1}$ away and \texttt{armD\_D2\_LW\_newton}
$5.000\times10^{-1}$ (contracting at only 0.69 per sweep, needing 54). The bytes
move; the answer does not: \texttt{armD\_D2\_LW\_newton} at its 2100-step cap
gives $du$ $1.5463\times10^{1}\to1.5493\times10^{1}$ and $\log_{10}\dot M=8.88$
either way, and at a matched step 40000 \texttt{armD\_D2\_newton} is 1.2 percent
apart and \texttt{jfnk\_hd189} 0.34 percent.

\subsection{The temperature column belonged to a composition one sweep behind it}

The refresh after the steady solve computed $T$ from the particle count BEFORE
its final \texttt{ioniz\_eq} and never recomputed it, so the $T$ column of a file
written from there was not the temperature of the species columns beside it. One
line closes it (\texttt{call comp\_T\_from\_p(p,n\_tot,ne,T)}); $p$ is untouched,
so $(p,T,f_{\rm sp})$ becomes a consistent triple. Isolated on a converging
hot-Uranus JFNK run, \textbf{only the $T$ column moves, by at most
$1.770\times10^{-5}$} (at $r=1.0488$); $r$, $\rho$, $v$, $p$, heat, cool and all
of \texttt{Ion\_species.txt} are bit-identical and $\log_{10}\dot M$ is 10.34
either way. It cannot touch the ten default goldens: that code is reached only
from the JFNK hand-off, and \emph{none of the ten ever reaches one}.

\subsection{Does the new root fix the departure? No}

The hot Uranus was re-solved with the tree as it now stands
(\S\ref{sec:row-scales-own-terms}'s row scales plus this section's restart
handling), giving $\texttt{info}=0$, $\|R\|=9.958\times10^{-6}$, gate flux
spread $2.501\times10^{-4}$, $\log_{10}\dot M=10.34$ --- and the new root's own
flux is still $3.433\times10^{-3}$ out over $r\ge1.03$, fourteen times the
gate's number. Marched 3000 steps from it with the tree binary:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccc@{}}
\toprule
root & p2p at 1.005 & 1.03 & 1.10 & 1.20 & $du$ end \\
\midrule
mass row only                        & 1.5476 & 0.5336 & 0.0710 & 0.0125 & 6.387e-04 \\
mass row $+$ this section's restart handling & 1.5473 & 0.5296 & 0.0705 & 0.0126 & 6.389e-04 \\
\textbf{all three rows, tree binary} & 1.5481 & \textbf{0.5333} & 0.0719 & 0.0132 & \textbf{3.363e-04} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{The departure is unchanged to 0.06 percent.} Making the
momentum and energy rows honest halves $du$ at the end
($6.39\times10^{-4}\to3.36\times10^{-4}$) and moves the excursion not at all. So
on the hot Uranus the two remaining causes of item (AD) are neither the restart
(fixed here) nor the row measure: what is left is the layer's own imbalance in
the terms those rows contain, and cell~1.

\subsection{What is not settled}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The hot Uranus root is still not a fixed point of the marching},
      by the same excursion as before either change. Item (AD) stands, narrowed:
      it is not the restart and not the row scale.
\item \textbf{The first two cells.} Untouched here; item (V).
\item \textbf{The reloaded WASP-121b residual} improves 14 to 17 times in the
      hydro rows (mass $L^\infty$ $4.406\times10^{-5}\to2.604\times10^{-6}$,
      momentum $1.023\times10^{-4}\to7.295\times10^{-6}$) but its energy row
      still reads $1.0\times10^{-5}$ against the $3.138\times10^{-6}$ the solve
      accepted. Not chased.
\item \textbf{heat and cool are now one sweep behind the corrected $T$} in a file
      written from the steady solve; they are diagnostic columns, and running
      the full composition fixed point in that refresh was not done.
\item \textbf{The $du$ window} is measured over $r\ge r_{\rm esc}$ while the flux
      gate measures $r\ge r_{\rm flux}$; the measurement of that mismatch is
      \texttt{docs/p55\_du\_window\_census.md} in the P55 scratch tree.
\end{itemize}

\noindent Files: \texttt{src/EXHALE\_main.f90} (new
\texttt{equilibrate\_loaded\_composition}; the arming rule reads the restart
header; \texttt{comp\_T\_from\_p} after the post-solve sweep;
\texttt{sec\_ion\_armed\_step} bookkeeping),
\texttt{src/modules/functions/utilities.f90} (new
\texttt{write\_coupling\_state\_header}),
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/load\_IC.f90} (new
\texttt{parse\_coupling\_header}),
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/write\_output.f90} (emits the line),
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/write\_setup\_report.f90} (reports the restore),
\texttt{src/modules/init/parameters.f90} (\texttt{sec\_ion\_armed\_step}).
Documentation: \texttt{docs/p55\_base\_mode.md} (+ three figures),
\texttt{docs/input\_schema.md}, \texttt{docs/EXHALE\_user\_manual.tex},
\texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} ((AD) narrowed, the \texttt{roundtrip} broken IC
opened). Regression: 10/10 data identical; \texttt{run\_fcheck.sh} CLEAN.

\section{Acceptance measures what the code conserves: face mass flux, cellwise
residual, one marching-stop label, the update-map diagnostic, provenance
(2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:acceptance-conserved}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{Judgement first. Both halves of the acceptance test were
measuring something other than what they were described as measuring.} The flux
gate read the cell-centred $\rho v r^2$, which is not the quantity the
finite-volume scheme conserves; on a state whose conserved face flux is a single
double-precision number over three hundred cells it reported $2.5\times10^{-4}$.
The residual norm was either a volume-weighted ratio of sums or a ratio of two
maxima taken in different cells; neither is $\max_j |R_j|/s_j$, which is what the
routine's own comment says it is, and under it two accepted states carried cells
218 times above the tolerance. Both are now what they say. Neither change moves a
mass-loss rate.

\noindent Measurements: \texttt{docs/p55\_base\_mode.md} \S11,
\texttt{docs/p55\_update\_map.md}, \texttt{docs/p55\_du\_window\_census.md}.

\subsection{The flux gate reads the Riemann face mass flux}

\texttt{flux\_spread\_of\_state} and \texttt{flux\_spread\_above\_radius} now
both call one implementation, \texttt{flux\_spread\_over\_faces}, which takes the
spread of $F_{j+1/2}r^2$ --- SIGNED, so a window in which the flow reverses is a
large spread and not a small one --- over the interior faces bounding the
window's cells. The cached face flux is the one \S\ref{sec:row-scales-own-terms}'s
\texttt{refresh\_row\_terms} maintains, so there is no second staleness rule and
no second Riemann solve.

$R_1/s_1$ is exactly the fractional change of the face flux across a cell, so
summing it bounds that flux's total variation. On the hot-Uranus root of
\S\ref{sec:p55-restart}:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
window & face-flux spread & $\sum R_1/s_1$ (bound) & cell-centred (what the gate read) \\
\midrule
$r\ge1.03$ & 1.21e-08 & 9.33e-08 & \textbf{3.433e-03} \\
$r\ge1.10$ & 0 (one value over 300 cells) & 4.38e-09 & 2.375e-03 \\
$r\ge1.20$ & 0 & 3.17e-10 & 2.501e-04 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The wind carries one mass flux to the last bit and the gate was
reporting $2.5\times10^{-4}$: the number was the difference between two
functionals, not a failure of conservation, and it was wrong by six orders. It
also removes the cell-1 artifact for free.

\textbf{This settles a comparison \S\ref{sec:p55-restart} got wrong.} The
$1.043\times10^{-4}$ of P54b and the $3.433\times10^{-3}$ of
\S\ref{sec:p55-restart} are the same state measured by the two different
functionals, not a change between P53 and now: the pre-P53 root's cell-centred
spread is $3.523\times10^{-3}$, within 3 percent of the current root's. On the
conserved functional the newer root is better by four orders.

\subsection{The threshold, re-derived for that definition}

\texttt{flux\_spread\_th} was $5.0\times10^{-3}$, calibrated against the
cell-centred product; on the face flux it is not a gate. Face spread at
$r\ge r_{\rm flux}$ over every state available:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\toprule
population & measured \\
\midrule
accepted by the JFNK & 1.02e-10, 3.89e-08, 3.97e-06, 3.83e-06 \\
stopped on $du$ only & 1.14e-04, 1.04e-03, 3.17e-02, 3.18e-02 \\
marching, 600 steps & 4.00 to 1.38e+01 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The two populations are separated by the interval $4\times10^{-6}$ to
$1.1\times10^{-4}$; the new default is its geometric middle to one digit,
$\mathbf{2.0\times10^{-5}}$, five times above the loosest accepted state and six
times below the tightest $du$ stop. \textbf{No canonical input sets
\texttt{Flux spread tol}} (checked over every \texttt{input.inp} outside
\texttt{LHS1140b/exhale/}), so the default is the whole change. A value
$\ge10^{-3}$ draws a warning, not a refusal. One case is refused that used to be
accepted, and is meant to be: \texttt{arm\_heh1\_x2matched} at
$1.14\times10^{-4}$.

\subsection{The residual norm is the maximum over cells of a cell's own scaled
residual}

\texttt{relnorm\_over\_cells} had two forms and neither was the local relative
infinity norm the comments describe: a volume-weighted ratio of sums, and a
ratio of two maxima taken in different cells (since $s\sim1/\delta r$ is largest
in the smallest cells at the base). There is now one form,
$rc(k)=\max_j |R_{kj}|/s_{kj}$, and \texttt{resid\_vol}, the \texttt{Resid norm}
key and \texttt{residual\_norms\_vol} are gone with the second form they
selected.

What the old norm hid, on the two roots of \S\ref{sec:p55-restart}, both accepted
at $\|R\|\sim10^{-5}$: the hot Uranus carried 7 cells above $10^{-5}$, all in
cells 1--3 (mass $3.10\times10^{-5}$, energy $2.17\times10^{-3}$, 218 times the
accepted number); WASP-121b carried 70, fifty of them in the \emph{wind} between
1.30 and 2.00 $R_p$. \textbf{It is not the layer that was hidden}: between
$r=1.03$ and 1.30 not one cell of either row exceeds $10^{-5}$ on the hot Uranus.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccc@{}}
\toprule
 & hot U, old & new & WASP, old & new \\
\midrule
JFNK \texttt{info} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
iterations & 7 & 9 & 8 & 12 \\
cell-max, mass & 3.100e-05 & \textbf{2.021e-07} & 3.232e-07 & \textbf{4.374e-08} \\
cell-max, energy & 2.174e-03 & \textbf{2.002e-06} & 6.397e-05 & \textbf{9.764e-06} \\
cells above $10^{-5}$ & 7 & \textbf{0} & 70 & \textbf{0} \\
$\log_{10}\dot M$ & 10.34 & 10.34 & 13.21 & 13.21 \\
3000-step p2p at $r{=}1.03$ & 0.5333 & 0.5334 & 0.0103 & 0.0104 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\subsection{Both numbers, every time a residual is reported}

Acceptance is the cellwise maximum, because that is the statement ``no cell of
any row is out''; it is not the statement ``the column's budget is closed'',
which is what the integrated norm says, and the external review of 2026-09-03
(\S4) asks for both to be visible before either is used alone.
\texttt{write\_residual\_breakdown} prints, at the \texttt{EXHALE\_RESIDUAL}
diagnostic, the JFNK hand-back and every marching stop: per row the cellwise
maximum with its cell and radius and the integrated ratio with its numerator and
denominator; the numerator and denominator contributions of $r<1.03$,
1.03--1.10, 1.10--1.20 and $r\ge1.20$; and for the worst cell the signed
dimensional residual with every term of its row.

\subsection{A marching stop says that it is one, and the $du$ window is not
unified}

The review (\S5, item 7) judges the marching $du$ stop, the JFNK hand-off
threshold and the acceptance gates to be three concepts with three roles.
\textbf{The proposal to unify the $du$ window with the flux gate's window is
withdrawn}, and the census that measured the cost of it is kept as the reason:
unifying changes no answer ($\log_{10}\dot M$ within 0.01--0.02 dex wherever both
builds stop) but costs three WASP-121b Newton cases a factor 13.2 in steps and
stops three other cases converging at all within 60000 steps.

Instead, every $du$, $dtu$, plateau and step-cap stop now prints \textsc{this is
a marching stop, not an accepted steady state} with the three gates
\emph{measured} on the state being stopped at. Measured on a hot-Uranus run that
used to print ``converged: mass flux constant'' at $du=1.454\times10^{-4}$: its
cellwise residual is \textbf{1.282} in the energy row of cell~7.

\subsection{The complete update-map diagnostic, and what it decides}

Review B2 asks for a diagnostic that applies one production step and compares
$G_{\delta t}=[\Phi_{\delta t}(q)-q]/\delta t$ with the steady residual at three
decreasing time steps, and says ``this test decides item 3''.
\texttt{EXHALE\_UPDATE\_MAP} does it, with $\Phi_{\delta t}$ the marching loop's
own body and not a copy. $|G_{\delta t}+R|$, max over cells:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccc@{}}
\toprule
$\delta t/\delta t_{\rm CFL}$ & hot U mass & momentum & energy & WASP mass & momentum \\
\midrule
1 & 6.52e-01 & 5.33e-01 & 9.60e-01 & 9.63e-02 & 1.33e-01 \\
0.1 & 8.93e-02 & 5.27e-02 & 1.40e-01 & 1.09e-02 & 1.69e-02 \\
0.01 & 9.23e-03 & 5.17e-03 & 2.34e-02 & 1.10e-03 & 1.73e-03 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{$G_{\delta t}$ approaches the steady residual at first order in
$\delta t$ on both planets. The production map and the residual share a fixed
point, and the 42 percent discrepancy \S\ref{sec:p55-restart} measured at a CFL
step is the splitting truncation error of an explicit step, not an operator
mismatch.} The stage breakdown says where the rest is: \texttt{Apply\_BC}'s
conservative-primitive round trip moves the interior by a relative
$4.2\times10^{-16}$, the semi-implicit energy step is a rate to five digits, and
the composition pressure projection is a rate that converges on the hot Uranus
and is 1.124 against a residual of 1.133 on WASP-121b.

\textbf{With the Shapiro filter on the two provably cannot share a fixed point.}
With \texttt{Shapiro filter: 0.5 1} the filter's contribution to $\delta u$ is
the same at every time step --- it is applied per step, not per unit time --- so
as a rate it is 1.187e+01, 1.189e+02, 1.188e+03 at the three $\delta t$, and
$|G_{\delta t}+R|$ follows it exactly instead of converging.

A third trap cost the regression outright, and it is worth its own
subsection: the snapshots were first placed between the \emph{statements} of
one RK3 stage. See below.

\subsection{Provenance: what produced a profile file}

Every profile file carries three further \texttt{\#} lines: the revision and
dirty flag stamped in by the Makefile into a generated
\texttt{build/build\_stamp.f90} (\emph{the run never calls git}) together with
the \emph{run} time from \texttt{date\_and\_time} --- a build time compiled into
the executable would make two builds of the same source different files, and the
md5 of the binary is how a bitwise verdict is tied to a revision; the Makefile
writes the stamp at parse time and only when its content changes, so \texttt{make}
has a fixed point and \texttt{run\_check.sh} can and now does run \texttt{make -q}
after its \texttt{make} and refuse the matrix if anything is still out of date;
checksums of
the input files as read, by \texttt{file\_rolling\_checksum}, two modular rolling
sums that are exact in \texttt{integer(8)} on every compiler and deliberately not
called a digest; and the discretization, lower boundary model, carrier model,
restart schema version, residual definition version and grid size. Review \S5,
item 12.11.

\subsection{The regression failed for a reason that was not the code}

The tree binary built at 19:01 failed all ten regression cases at a relative
$3\times10^{-14}$ to $9\times10^{-11}$, with $du$ and $dtu$ at the stop agreeing
to every printed digit. The first hypothesis was a stale object linked by an
incremental build. It was not: \texttt{make distclean \&\& make} reproduced the
failure exactly. A bisect over clean builds --- the pre-145 tree, the norm and
gate group, the provenance group, and all of \S145 without the update map ---
reproduced the goldens bitwise in every case, leaving one patch.

\textbf{The arithmetic.} The update-map snapshots were placed between the
statements of one RK3 stage:

\begin{verbatim}
u1(k,:) = u(k,:) - dt_loc*(dF(k,:) - S(k,:))
if (upmap_n .gt. 0) u_umBCin = u1        ! <- here
call Apply_BC(u1)
\end{verbatim}

\noindent $a-bc$ is a fused multiply-add candidate and
\texttt{-ffp-contract=fast} is gfortran's default, so inserting a statement
changes the scheduling and with it whether the FMA is taken. An FMA rounds once
where a multiply and a subtract round twice: one ulp per step, $10^{-11}$ over
eleven thousand. \textbf{Every inserted statement was inside \texttt{if (upmap\_n
.gt.\ 0)} and did nothing with the diagnostic off.} The contraction setting is
not being changed --- it is the default the goldens were made under, and it is
the faster and the more accurate of the two. What changes is where
instrumentation may go: the boundary contribution is now taken once, out of line,
in \texttt{update\_map\_begin\_step}, the remaining snapshots sit between
operator-split stages and never between the statements of one, and a comment at
the first of them in \texttt{EXHALE\_main.f90} says why.
\textbf{Instrumentation that has to sit inside a stage must be measured out of
line; an \texttt{if} that does nothing at run time is not guaranteed to leave the
floating-point result alone, and the bitwise regression is what says so.}

\textbf{The binary had stopped being a function of its source.} \S145's first
build stamp compiled the BUILD TIME into a constant, so two \texttt{make
distclean \&\& make} of identical source produced different executables,
differing in exactly one object (\texttt{utilities.o}) in exactly that string.
Three workers comparing md5s therefore read ``different program'' from what was
the same program. The stamp now carries the git revision and dirty flag only, and
the run time is reported from \texttt{date\_and\_time} in the provenance header
instead. Two clean builds of one source now give one binary.

\textbf{And nothing checked that the binary matched the sources.} The stamp had
been generated by a rule with a phony prerequisite, so \texttt{make} never
reached a fixed point and \texttt{make -q} reported ``out of date'' immediately
after a successful \texttt{make} --- the one cheap check that would catch a stale
binary was useless. The Makefile now writes the stamp at parse time and only when
its content changes, and \texttt{run\_check.sh} runs \texttt{make -q} after its
own \texttt{make} and refuses the matrix with exit code 2 if anything is still out
of date. A bitwise verdict can no longer be taken from a binary the sources have
moved past.

\textbf{What an md5 of the binary identifies.} Two measurements, because the
guard leans on them. A comment does not change the code: same file name, one
added comment line, the \texttt{-S} output is identical apart from the
\texttt{.file} directive and the object bytes match. But a \emph{shifted line
number} does change the object, because every I/O statement carries its own
source line as an immediate for runtime error reporting --- adding one comment
line above a \texttt{write} turns \texttt{movl \$0x4} into \texttt{movl \$0x5}.
The eight-line comment added to \texttt{EXHALE\_main.f90} at the end of this work
moved the binary from \texttt{e83b4ab4} to \texttt{62cc6c64} with no numerical
change at all; both are bitwise identical to the goldens. \textbf{The md5 is a
fingerprint of one source text, which is what the \texttt{make -q} guard and the
\texttt{\# provenance:} header need. It is not a semantic fingerprint, and two
binaries with different md5s are not thereby different programs.}

\textbf{Not established.} Whether \texttt{fortdep.py} and the Makefile could ever
have missed a rebuild before \S145. Reading them found no mechanism: no duplicate
source basenames, no module provided by two files, the dependency file remade
whenever any source or \texttt{fortdep.py} changes, and a flag change forcing a
full rebuild through the flag stamp. A recurrence test --- a module-signature
edit, an incremental build, then a clean build of the same source --- gives
identical binaries. No instance has been demonstrated, and because no earlier
build recorded what it was built from (which is what the provenance header now
fixes), the earlier builds of 2026-09-03 cannot be reconstructed either way.

\subsection{What is not settled}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The hot Uranus root is still not a fixed point of the marching},
      by the same excursion as before any of this. What \S145 removes is the
      possibility that the measure was hiding it. Item (AD), now pointing at the
      base boundary (review Phase C).
\item \textbf{Cells 1--3.} The cellwise norm forces the solve to bring them
      below $10^{-5}$ and succeeds on both cases; nothing here says the state it
      reaches there is physical. Item (V).
\item \textbf{The accepted state's residual is not reproducible.} Re-running the
      ionization sweep on the same conserved state moves cells 1 and 2 from
      $10^{-5}$ to order unity, in the \emph{mass} row, which reads no radiative
      term: what moves is $\rho$, which \texttt{ioniz\_eq} rewrites through
      \texttt{calc\_rho}. Every number above is therefore taken from the solver's
      own residual vector. This is the next thing to diagnose.
\item \textbf{The energy row of the update map on WASP-121b}, where the
      composition pressure projection is a rate as large as the residual itself.
\item Goldens are NOT refreshed here and \texttt{run\_fcheck.sh} is not run:
      items (AB) and (AF) follow immediately and do both once.
\end{itemize}

\texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_newton.f90},
\texttt{src/EXHALE\_main.f90}, \texttt{src/modules/init/parameters.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/input\_read.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/functions/utilities.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/write\_output.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/write\_setup\_report.f90}, \texttt{Makefile}.

\texttt{docs/input\_schema.md}, \texttt{docs/EXHALE\_user\_manual.tex},

\section{The boundary condition writes the boundary, and the residual is a
state function (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:bc-writes-boundary}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{Judgement first, in three parts. (1) \texttt{Apply\_BC} was
rewriting the interior it was called to leave alone.} Its round trip ---
primitive out, boundary condition, conservative back over the WHOLE array ---
recomputed every interior cell's energy as \texttt{0.5*W(1)*W(2)**2} where the
input held \texttt{0.5*u(2)*u(2)/u(1)}. In an atomic gas that costs the last
bit; in a molecular one the two conversions use different heat capacities and
the projection is real: \textbf{measured, one step of \texttt{mol\_metals}
moves the interior pressure by $1.26\times10^{-3}$} while the density it does
not touch moves by $8.4\times10^{-16}$. It now writes the ghost indices and
returns the interior bit for bit. \textbf{(2) The steady residual filled the
ghosts before its ionization sweep}, so the conservative ghost state the fluxes
read carried the previous evaluation's composition
(\S\ref{sec:base-ghost-composition-lag}, item (AB)). It now fills them after,
which is the order the marching loop has always had --- state, then that
state's composition, then the ghosts, then the fluxes --- and the two are the
same discrete operator, which \S\ref{sec:p55-restart} requires of them. This
was only possible once (1) made a second call free. \textbf{(3) Neither of
those is what makes the residual a state function, and the measurement that
says so is new}: evaluate $F$ at a state, at another state, then at the first
again through one shared composition workspace and \textbf{1406 of 1500 entries
differ, by $3.0\times10^{-3}$ of the row scale --- 300 times the acceptance
tolerance}. Seed the sweep from one composition instead and the three
evaluations are \textbf{bitwise identical}. The equilibrium sweep's starting
guess is the whole of it, every call site in the solver already resets it, and
what was missing is a test that says so.

On the 1~microbar hot-Uranus root the ordering fix moves the 3000-step marching
departure at $r=1.03$ from \textbf{0.4526 to 0.2517}, and at $r=1.005$ from
1.6384 to 0.4443 --- the first change in this campaign that moves item (AD) at
all. $\log_{10}\dot M$ does not move on any case measured.

\noindent\textbf{A note on which flatness number is quoted where.} The
departure figures above and in \S\ref{sec:bc-ghost-item-ad} were measured
before \S\ref{sec:acceptance-conserved} made the flux gate read the signed
Riemann face flux; they are peak-to-peak excursions of that same face flux, so
they carry over unchanged. The steady-state spreads in
\S\ref{sec:bc-ghost-cases} are quoted in BOTH measures, because the gate's
meaning changed under this work and item (AA) is written in the older one.

\subsection{\texttt{Apply\_BC} writes the ghosts}
\label{sec:apply-bc-ghosts}

\begin{lstlisting}[language=Fortran,basicstyle=\ttfamily\footnotesize]
   call U_to_W_interior(u,W)      ! interior only; ghosts are outputs, not inputs
   call Apply_BC_W(W)             ! the boundary condition, in primitive variables
   do k = 1,Ng                    ! WAS: call W_to_U(W,u), the whole array
      call W_to_U_comp(W(:,1-k), u(:,1-k), 1-k)
      call W_to_U_comp(W(:,N+k), u(:,N+k), N+k)
   enddo
\end{lstlisting}

\noindent \texttt{W\_to\_U\_comp} is the arithmetic \texttt{W\_to\_U} performs
cell by cell, and for a gas with no molecules in it
\texttt{energy\_density\_from\_pressure} returns
$p/(\gamma_{\rm ad}-1)$ verbatim, so an atomic ghost is the double it always
was.

Two things follow. \texttt{Apply\_BC} is \emph{idempotent}, which is what item
(AB) recorded as the obstruction to fixing the ghost lag. And the interior of a
state stops changing under a routine whose subject is the boundary --- a
property nothing should have had to reason about, and one the caloric EOS of
\S\ref{sec:caloric-eos-and-reaction-heat} turned from a rounding curiosity into
a $1.26\times10^{-3}$ projection.

\subsection{The residual's order}
\label{sec:residual-order}

\begin{lstlisting}[language={},basicstyle=\ttfamily\footnotesize]
   unpack Y -> u(1:N)
   get_species_densities            ! interior composition of Y (n_part_cell1)
   Apply_BC(u)                      ! provisional ghosts: U_to_W needs a density
   U_to_W; get_species_densities; comp_T_from_p; excited_H; ioniz_eq
   get_species_densities            ! the composition the residual will use
   Apply_BC(u)                      ! NEW: the ghosts, with THAT composition
   assemble_residual                ! Reconstruct + RK_rhs read those ghosts
\end{lstlisting}

\noindent What is still one sweep behind, and deliberately: the ghost cells'
own composition was solved at the pressure the first \texttt{Apply\_BC} wrote,
not at the one the second writes. Iterating that pair to a ghost fixed point
would make the residual something the marching loop is not, and being the same
operator is the stronger requirement (\S\ref{sec:p55-restart}). No extra
ionization sweep is needed; the cost is one call.

\subsection{Is the residual a state function? Only because every call site is
careful}
\label{sec:residual-state-function}

\texttt{EXHALE\_RESID\_DETERMINISM=1} evaluates $F(Y_0)$, then $F(Y_1)$, then
$F(Y_0)$ again, then $F(Y_2)$, then $F(Y_0)$ again, and compares the three
$F(Y_0)$.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}}
\toprule
how the sweep is seeded & entries differing (of 1500) & max, in row-scale units \\
\midrule
one shared workspace, as \texttt{newton\_residual}'s interface allows
   & 1406 and 1400 & \textbf{2.968e-03}, 2.973e-03 \\
the same, with this section's ordering fix & 1412 and 1399 & 4.239e-03, 4.280e-03 \\
\textbf{seeded from one composition every time} & \textbf{0 and 0} & \textbf{0} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent Measured on the converged 1~microbar hot Uranus, single-threaded. The
tolerance these residuals are judged against is $10^{-5}$.

\textbf{So the carrier is the equilibrium sweep's starting composition, and
nothing else.} That is a strong statement and the third row is what makes it:
with the seed held fixed the residual reproduces to the bit, so no other module
is holding state between evaluations.

\textbf{The solver is already correct, by convention.} Every one of the five
places that call \texttt{eval\_residual} copies the adopted composition into a
workspace first (\texttt{f\_sp\_j = f\_sp} in the line searches,
\texttt{fwork = f\_sp\_base} in the banded Jacobian, the Gauss--Newton escape
and the Krylov directional derivative), so what a solve compares are residuals
seeded alike. The invariant holds and nothing about it is written down or
tested. \texttt{src/tests/residual\_determinism/} is the test that pins it; it
is what stops the sixth call site from being written without the reset.

\textbf{What it does not license.} \texttt{newton\_residual(Y, f\_sp, F)} still
takes the composition as \texttt{intent(inout)}, so the invariant is a property
of the callers and not of the routine. Making it structural --- the residual
seeds from an adopted composition it owns, and returns the new one separately
--- is a change to a public interface and is left as item (AF).

\texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner} & 7.1e-05 / 8.0e-05 / 1.1e-04 / 4.4e-05 & 12000, 5.5044e-01 / 5.5038e-01 & 10.47 both \\

\noindent\textbf{All ten move and none of them changes an answer.} The two
atomic cases stop on \texttt{du} at the same step with the same \texttt{du} to
five digits and the same rate: their trajectory changes only at the last bit,
and after 11,289 steps that has grown to $10^{-13}$. \texttt{mol\_carrier} and
\texttt{lower\_profile} are the same story. The six molecular cases with the
caloric EOS live move by $10^{-6}$ to $8\times10^{-4}$, which is not rounding:
it is the projection of \S\ref{sec:apply-bc-ghosts} removed.

That the molecular numbers are not monotone in step count is worth stating,
because it says which they are. On \texttt{mol\_metals} from its cold start:

and the last is the relaxation contracting it again. A golden refresh is
required and no quoted number moves.

\textbf{The named Newton cases.} Both re-solve and both converge, at a cost:
