\noindent\textbf{Two different flatness measures appear in that table and both
belong there.} The gate is the signed Riemann face flux
(\S\ref{sec:acceptance-conserved}); on the hot Uranus this section improves it
by a factor 49 at $r\ge1.03$ and 24 at the gate window. The cell-centred
product does not move, because it is not what the solve is driving --- and it
is the quantity item (AA) was written about, so it is quoted beside the gate
rather than instead of it.

The hot-Uranus accepted residual falls by a factor 3.1 when the ghosts are
consistent with the composition, which is the lag being removed. The iteration
count rises by 47 per cent there and by 91 per cent on WASP-121b.

\subsection{Does it move item (AD)? On the hot Uranus, yes}
\label{sec:bc-ghost-item-ad}

Each root reloaded and marched 3000 steps with the JFNK hand-off removed.
Peak-to-peak excursion of the face mass flux, in units of the root's own $F_0$:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccc@{}}
\toprule
root marched with & 1.005 & 1.03 & 1.10 & 1.20 & \texttt{du} at 3000 \\
\midrule
pre-146 root, pre-146 binary & 1.6384 & 0.4526 & 0.1010 & 0.0190 & 3.2256e-04 \\
pre-146 root, this section's binary & 1.6384 & 0.4526 & 0.1010 & 0.0190 & 3.2256e-04 \\
\textbf{this section's root}, pre-146 binary & 0.4443 & 0.2517 & 0.0403 & 0.0084 & 3.2250e-04 \\
\textbf{this section's root}, this section's binary & 0.4443 & 0.2517 & 0.0403 & 0.0084 & 3.2250e-04 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent Read the rows in pairs: \textbf{the departure is a property of the
root and not of the marching binary}, to four digits. The root this section
produces departs \textbf{44 per cent less at $r=1.03$ and 73 per cent less at
1.005}. \S\ref{sec:p55-restart} measured \S\ref{sec:row-scales-own-terms}'s row
scales at 0.06 per cent and P55's restart handling at 0.7 per cent on the same
quantity; this is the first change that moves it.

\textbf{What the two roots differ by is cell 1, and almost nothing else.} Every
column agrees to $10^{-3}$ or better except the base cell's velocity, $-15.0$
cm~s$^{-1}$ before and $-251.9$ cm~s$^{-1}$ after; the flux spread over
$r\ge1.03$ is the same to five digits and $\log_{10}\dot M$ is the same. So the
solve is landing at a different point along the near-null direction item (V)
owns, and that point is the one whose ghosts the marching loop would have
written anyway --- which is what the ordering fix is for. \textbf{Whether the
44 per cent is that consistency or the cell-1 displacement is not separated
here}, and the honest statement is that the two arrived together.

On WASP-121b there is nothing left to move: $0.0102 \to 0.0099$ at $r=1.03$, a
3 per cent change on an excursion that P55's restart handling had already
reduced to one per cent of the hot Uranus's.

\subsection{What is not settled}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The interface, not the invariant.} \texttt{newton\_residual}
      still takes the composition as \texttt{intent(inout)}; the state-function
      property is a discipline its five callers keep. Item (AF).
\item \textbf{The banded Jacobian's directional derivative} disagrees with the
      finite-difference ray by $1.0261\times10^{-1}$ on the hot-Uranus
      hand-off, unchanged by this section (\texttt{EXHALE\_JAC\_TEST=1},
      identical in both builds). It is a property of the banded model, and
      \S\ref{sec:p51-pseudo-time-and-flux-windows} is where it belongs.
\item \textbf{The ghost cells' own composition} is still solved at the pressure
      the provisional \texttt{Apply\_BC} writes, not at the final one.
      Deliberate; \S\ref{sec:residual-order}.
\item \textbf{Which half of the hot-Uranus improvement is the consistency and
      which is cell 1} (\S\ref{sec:bc-ghost-item-ad}).
\item \textbf{The cost.} 36 per cent more iterations on the hot Uranus and 118
      per cent on WASP-121b, not investigated. The residual is a different
      function now, so a different iteration count is expected; whether the
      extra iterations are the solve doing more work or the line search being
      handed a harder problem was not measured.
\end{itemize}

\noindent Files: \texttt{src/modules/states/Apply\_BC.f90}
(\texttt{Apply\_BC} writes the ghosts),
\texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_newton.f90} (\texttt{eval\_residual}
re-fills the ghosts after its sweep). Test:
\texttt{src/tests/residual\_determinism/}. Documentation:
\texttt{docs/p\_ab\_ghost\_order.md}, \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} ((AB) closed,
(AF) opened, (AD) narrowed again).

\section{The equilibrium sweep's seed is an argument (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:eq-sweep-seed-argument}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{Judgement first. The steady residual was a function of its
argument only because five call sites remembered to make it one.}
\texttt{eval\_residual} took the composition as one \texttt{intent(inout)}
array that was both the seed the equilibrium sweep starts from in each cell and
the place its answer is written, so whatever the caller's workspace last held
became the next evaluation's initial guess. Measured
(\S\ref{sec:residual-state-function}): evaluate $F$ at a state, at two others,
then at the first again through one shared workspace and \textbf{1406 of 1500
entries differ, by $3.0\times10^{-3}$ of the row scale against an acceptance
tolerance of $10^{-5}$}. Every call site in the solver defended against that by
copying the adopted composition into a workspace first ---
\texttt{f\_sp\_j = f\_sp}, \texttt{fwork = f\_sp\_base}, five times --- and
nothing said so, tested it, or stopped a sixth call site from being written
without it. \textbf{The seed is now an argument.}
\texttt{eval\_residual(Y, f\_sp\_seed, f\_sp, ...)} takes the seed
\texttt{intent(in)} and writes the swept composition to a separate
\texttt{intent(out)} dummy; the copy happens once, inside; and because the two
may not be the same array a caller cannot hand the sweep its own previous
answer even by accident. The five copies are deleted. \textbf{The test now
passes structurally}, the residual moving no more when another state is
evaluated in between than it moves when nothing is
(\S\ref{sec:seed-argument-test}), and the solve is bitwise unchanged on every
case measured --- the convention was being kept, and it is now kept by the
interface.

It is the same rule the chemistry of a single cell already states one level
down: a cell's root may not depend on the cell solved before it
(\texttt{seed\_species\_of\_cell},
\texttt{constrained\_chemical\_equilibrium.f90}). This raises it from the cell
to the sweep, and does not define it a second time.

\subsection{The interface}

\begin{lstlisting}[language=Fortran,basicstyle=\ttfamily\footnotesize]
   subroutine eval_residual(Y, f_sp_seed, f_sp, Fvec, heat, cool, n_part, ...)
      real*8, ..., intent(in)  :: f_sp_seed     ! where the sweep starts
      real*8, ..., intent(out) :: f_sp          ! where its answer goes
      ...
      f_sp = f_sp_seed                          ! the first thing it does
\end{lstlisting}

\noindent \texttt{newton\_residual} takes the same pair. Fortran forbids
aliasing an \texttt{intent(in)} dummy with an \texttt{intent(out)} one, so the
failure mode the measurement found is not expressible.

\textbf{What the call sites look like now.} The three that evaluate the iterate
the solve is standing on read

\begin{lstlisting}[language=Fortran,basicstyle=\ttfamily\footnotesize]
   call eval_residual(Y, f_sp, f_sp_j, F, heat0, cool0)
   f_sp = f_sp_j
\end{lstlisting}

\noindent and that copy is an \emph{adoption}, not a seeding convention: the
seed is named in the call, and the assignment afterwards says the solve has
taken the result as its new composition. The line searches and the damped
Gauss--Newton escape pass \texttt{(Ytry, f\_sp, f\_sp\_j, ...)} --- seed from
what is adopted, write somewhere else --- and adopt only when the step is
accepted, which they already did. The banded Jacobian, the
Levenberg--Marquardt descent and the Krylov directional derivative pass
\texttt{(Y, f\_sp\_base, fwork, ...)}: those three already declared their seed
\texttt{intent(in)} and copied it by hand, and now they simply hand it over.

\subsection{What it changes: nothing numerical}

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}}
\toprule
 & hot Uranus gate rung & WASP-121b \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} \\
\midrule
\texttt{info} & $0 \to 0$ & $0 \to 0$ \\
iterations & $25 \to 25$ & $109 \to 109$ \\
$\lVert R\rVert$ accepted & 3.176e-06 $\to$ 3.176e-06 & 8.138e-06 $\to$ 8.138e-06 \\
gate flux spread & 2.466e-14 $\to$ 2.466e-14 & 1.153e-11 $\to$ 1.153e-11 \\
$\log_{10}\dot M$ & $10.34 \to 10.34$ & $13.21 \to 13.21$ \\
\texttt{Hydro\_ioniz.txt}, \texttt{Ion\_species.txt}
   & \textbf{byte identical} & \textbf{byte identical} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent and the ten-case matrix is byte identical as well. That is the
expected outcome and it is the point: the solver was keeping the convention, so
moving it into the interface can only remove a way to break it.

\subsection{The test}
\label{sec:seed-argument-test}

\texttt{src/tests/residual\_determinism/} drives
\texttt{EXHALE\_RESID\_DETERMINISM=1}, which evaluates $F(Y_0)$ twice with
nothing in between (the control), then $F(Y_0)$, a trial, $F(Y_0)$, another
trial, $F(Y_0)$, \textbf{reusing one output workspace throughout} so that it
carries each evaluation's composition into the next call, and compares the
three $F(Y_0)$ bit for bit.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}}
\toprule
 & entries differing (of 1500) & max, row-scale units \\
\midrule
before \S\ref{sec:eq-sweep-seed-argument}, one shared workspace
   & 1406 and 1400 & 2.968e-03, 2.973e-03 \\
before, with \S\ref{sec:bc-writes-boundary}'s ghost ordering
   & 1412 and 1399 & 4.239e-03, 4.280e-03 \\
\textbf{\S\ref{sec:eq-sweep-seed-argument}}
   & \textbf{6 and 3, within the control} & \textbf{1.374e-12, 6.253e-14} \\
the control itself (nothing in between) & 6 & 1.624e-12 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{The test is judged against its control, and that took a
correction.} As first written it demanded bitwise agreement, and on the tree it
was installed in it therefore failed while the invariant held. The control ---
$F(Y_0)$ twice with nothing in between --- differs in \textbf{6 entries, all in
cells 1 and 2, row-scale max $1.62\times10^{-12}$}: the first call through a
run builds tables the later ones reuse, the H$_2$ rovibrational table among
them, and that is a one-time cost of the first evaluation rather than history
passing between states. Re-evaluating $F(Y_0)$ after each of two trial states
then differs by $1.37\times10^{-12}$ and $6.25\times10^{-14}$ --- no more than
the control, and seven orders below the $10^{-5}$ the solver accepts at. So the
test asks the question it exists to ask: does $F$ move MORE because another
state was evaluated in between than it moves when nothing is? A $10^{-9}$ floor
keeps that comparison meaningful when the control comes out clean, and the
control line is printed rather than absorbed so that a future change which
makes the first evaluation differ for a different reason stays visible.

\subsection{What is not settled}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The marching loop's \texttt{ioniz\_eq} call is untouched}, and
      correctly so: there the seed IS the run's stored composition, which is
      what the sweep should start from, and \texttt{f\_sp\_io} being both is the
      honest contract. What this section removes is a caller passing a
      workspace and getting the last state's answer as its guess.
\item \textbf{The 6-entry control difference} is attributed to first-call table
      building by its signature --- cells 1 and 2 only, $10^{-11}$, identical
      after the first evaluation --- but the specific table was not identified.
\item \textbf{Nothing here makes the sweep's root seed-independent.} A Newton
      solve in one cell, started from a different guess, may land on different
      bits, and the invariant this section establishes is that the guess is a
      stated function of the caller's argument, not that the root is
      independent of it. How far the root moves with the seed is not measured.
\end{itemize}

\noindent Files: \texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_newton.f90}
(\texttt{eval\_residual} and \texttt{newton\_residual} take the seed as an
argument; the five copies deleted), \texttt{src/EXHALE\_main.f90} (two call
sites). Test: \texttt{src/tests/residual\_determinism/}. Documentation:
\texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} ((AF) closed).

\section{The PLM to WENO3 hand-off is a continuation between two discrete
problems, not a switch (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:plm-weno-continuation}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{Judgement first, and it is two-sided.} On the two cases that
could be measured, the shipped one-step hand-off is a \textbf{harmless
transient}, and that is a measurement rather than an assumption: the
\texttt{dtu} excursion it causes is quantitatively the fixed-state operator
difference (1.83 predicted against 1.71 measured on the first step), it decays
below its pre-hand-off value within about fifty steps, \texttt{du} never stops
descending, and no positivity guard fires. \textbf{But the two discretizations
do not share a solution near the boundaries}, which is the part that matters
for the physics: over the wind PLM and WENO3 agree to a part in $10^2$ to
$10^4$, while in the first two or three cells above the base the WENO3 mass-row
residual is \textbf{6.7 times the largest PLM residual anywhere on the grid},
and in the outermost cells the momentum rows differ by 62 per cent. A
\texttt{wasp\_full} run held on PLM does not converge in 15,000 steps and
settles on a base 400--700~K hotter and up to 2.4 times denser, with the
opposite sign of base velocity and $\log_{10}\dot M$ 0.08 higher. So the
two-stage recipe is a continuation between two different discrete problems, and
treating it as one is right even where the transient it produces is benign. The
continuation is implemented and \textbf{default off}; $\lambda=1$ reproduces
the shipped code to the bit.

\subsection{The instrument: an operator difference on a fixed state}

\texttt{EXHALE\_OPDIFF} assembles the PLM residual and the WENO3 residual for
the same interior cells, each with its own ghosts and pressure split, and
stops. On \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion} at the hand-off step (11,861):

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccclc@{}}
\toprule
row & max PLM $/s$ & max WENO3 $/s$ & max difference $/s$ & at & difference / PLM \\
\midrule
mass     & 1.519 & 10.245 & 10.232 & $r = 1.00019$ & 6.74 \\
momentum & 1.678 & 2.379  & 1.036  & $r = 4.681$   & 0.618 \\
energy   & 1.924 & 1.925  & 1.202  & $r = 1.00077$ & 0.625 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The difference lives at the two boundaries and nowhere else, so its
origin is the base ghost and pressure split at one end and the outer
extrapolated ghost at the other, not the reconstruction over the wind.
Predicted against measured across the hand-off, on the \texttt{dtu} window
($r\ge r_{\rm esc}$):

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}}
\toprule
 & predicted & measured \\
\midrule
PLM step \texttt{dtu}   & 5.979e-4 & 5.948e-4 (step 11,861) \\
WENO3 step \texttt{dtu} & 1.095e-3 & 1.015e-3 (step 11,862) \\
ratio & 1.831 & 1.706 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\subsection{The continuation}

\texttt{reconstruction\_continuation\_rhs} assembles the whole right-hand side
under each flag and combines them,
\begin{equation}
R_\lambda = (1-\lambda)\,R_{\rm PLM} + \lambda\,R_{\rm WENO3},
\end{equation}
blending the outer ghosts of \texttt{Apply\_BC\_W} with the same $\lambda$.
Both the three-stage marching step and \texttt{assemble\_residual} go through
it, so the marching map and the residual continue together. At $\lambda=0$ and
$\lambda=1$ it is a single evaluation and bitwise equal to the pure scheme; on
reaching $\lambda=1$ it disarms itself and hands the flag to WENO3, \textbf{so
the final gates are evaluated with the pure WENO3 operator}.

Input key, refused rather than ignored where it cannot apply:

\begin{lstlisting}[language={},basicstyle=\ttfamily\footnotesize]
Reconstruction continuation: <dlambda> [<dtu_tol>] [fixed|adaptive]
\end{lstlisting}

\noindent \texttt{dlambda} $\le0$ or an absent key is the shipped one-step
hand-off; \texttt{dtu\_tol} (default 1.2) halves the $\lambda$ step instead of
advancing when a step exceeds that multiple of the \texttt{dtu} at the start of
the ramp; \texttt{fixed} turns that control off. The two optional fields are
told apart by content rather than position, the mode being a word and the
tolerance a number. Resolved at the end of \texttt{input\_read} once
\texttt{Reconstruction scheme:} and both \texttt{du\_th} values are known: a
run that is not two-stage, or whose PLM stage is empty
(\texttt{du\_th\_plm} $\le$ \texttt{du\_th}), gets the key cleared and a
WARNING. The four \texttt{EXHALE\_RECON\_LAMBDA\_*} environment variables of
the measurement build are gone; \texttt{EXHALE\_OPDIFF} stays one, with the
other diagnostic probes that measure a state and change no result.

\subsection{What the ramp does to the transient}

\texttt{mol\_sec\_ion}, whose \texttt{dtu} before the hand-off is 5.948e-4:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccc@{}}
\toprule
run & ramp steps & $\lambda=1$ at & back-offs & \texttt{dtu} peak & vs before \\
\midrule
shipped, one step & --- & 11,861 & --- & 1.060e-3 & 1.763 \\
\texttt{dlambda = 1} & --- & 11,861 & --- & 1.060e-3 & 1.763 \\
\texttt{0.02}, fixed & 49 & 11,910 & 0 & 7.501e-4 & 1.248 \\
\texttt{0.02}, adaptive & 58 & 11,919 & 2 & 7.213e-4 & 1.200 \\
\texttt{0.002}, adaptive & 499 & 12,360 & 0 & 5.948e-4 & 0.990 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent A 500-step ramp removes the excursion entirely, and the cost is below
the scatter of a shared machine (14,000 steps: 10~m~37~s shipped, 9~m~36~s with
the ramp).

\subsection{Why it is default off, and what would justify turning it on}

Adopting a default ramp is not justified by these two cases: it buys a 20--25
per cent smaller \texttt{dtu} excursion that decays on its own within fifty
steps. It would be justified by the configuration item (S) reports ---
HD~189733~b with molecular and oxygen chemistry, transport and IR bands, where
the same hand-off is recorded as taking \texttt{du} to $\sim10^5$ within 2000
steps --- and that case was out of reach here (it is not in the matrix and one
trajectory to it costs tens of thousands of steps). What this work supplies is
the instrument to settle it in one run: \texttt{EXHALE\_OPDIFF=2} on that state
measures $R_{\rm WENO3}-R_{\rm PLM}$, and if the ratio is the $\sim7.5$ its
reported \texttt{dtu} jump implies then the hand-off is the cause, while
$\sim1.8$ like here would mean a WENO3 instability the hand-off merely
uncovers, which a continuation will not fix.

\subsection{A provenance defect, fixed at its single definition}

The tree wrote \texttt{recon=trim(rec\_method)} in two places, the coupling
header and the provenance header, so a run stopped inside a ramp would have
reported \texttt{recon=PLM} while its equations were part WENO3.
\texttt{reconstruction\_operator\_label()} in \texttt{parameters.f90} is now the
one definition and both headers call it:

\begin{lstlisting}[language={},basicstyle=\ttfamily\scriptsize]
# coupling: sec_ion=T sec_ion_step=0 valve=-1.00000E+00 recon=PLM+WENO3(lambda=0.0400) fluxconst=-1.00000E+00
# provenance: recon=PLM+WENO3(lambda=0.0400) base_bc=isothermal carrier=local restart_schema=3 resid_def=145 N=500
\end{lstlisting}

\noindent Snapshots before the hand-off read \texttt{recon=PLM} and after the
ramp \texttt{recon=WENO3}, in the same run.

\subsection{Verification}

\texttt{dlambda = 1} is the stronger equivalence test than an absent key, since
it drives the blended right-hand side, the blended ghosts, the
$\lambda$-weighted face-pressure term, the controller and the disarm and still
lands on the shipped result: \texttt{wasp\_full} and \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion} are
byte-identical to the unpatched control with the \texttt{du}/\texttt{dtu}
traces agreeing digit for digit, and so is an absent key. The parse dump gains
the three values \textbf{only when the key is used}, following the
\texttt{if (do\_read\_sed)} precedent in the same file, so the 1122 files of
\texttt{parse\_golden/} do not move. The ten-case matrix is byte-identical: the
key is off, and six of the ten never leave the PLM stage in the first place.

\noindent\textbf{Files.} \texttt{src/modules/init/parameters.f90} (the
continuation state and \texttt{reconstruction\_operator\_label}),
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/input\_read.f90} (the key and its refusal),
\texttt{src/modules/files\_IO/write\_setup\_report.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/functions/utilities.f90} (both headers, one label),
\texttt{src/modules/states/Apply\_BC.f90} (the blended outer ghost),
\texttt{src/modules/time\_step/RK\_rhs.f90},
\texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_residual.f90}
(\texttt{reconstruction\_continuation\_rhs}), \texttt{src/EXHALE\_main.f90}
(the controller). Documentation:
\texttt{docs/f\_plm\_weno\_continuation.md}, \texttt{docs/input\_schema.md}.

\section{One routine counts the elements, and it is asserted around every
refresh that moves them (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:element-census}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{Judgement: the code had no single statement of how many nuclei
of each element a composition holds.}
\texttt{utilities.f90::hydrogen\_helium\_nuclei\_density} covers H and He; C, N,
O and the other metals had no counterpart, and their closure existed only in
\texttt{src/utils/element\_budget.py}, which reads a finished run. A run could
therefore break an element budget in one refresh and only be found out several
thousand steps later, by a post-processor that says a run failed but not which
refresh failed it. \texttt{element\_census.f90} is that statement, and the
assertions built on it name the refresh.

\subsection{What the routine counts, and from where}

\texttt{element\_nuclei\_and\_charge(rho, f\_sp, n\_nuc, n\_chg, rho\_comp)}
returns the nucleus density of H, He and the ten metal elements, the positive
charge density (the free electron density under neutrality), and the mass
density the composition implies through \texttt{calc\_rho}'s own weights.

No multiplicity is written in the module. It reads \texttt{bsp\_nH},
\texttt{bsp\_nHe}, \texttt{bsp\_nO}, \texttt{bsp\_nC}, \texttt{bsp\_charge},
\texttt{bsp\_mass}, \texttt{bsp\_is\_excited\_level}, \texttt{mion\_elem},
\texttt{mion\_stage} and \texttt{melem\_A} from \texttt{species\_table}, so
H$_2$ and H$_2^+$ carry two H nuclei, H$_3^+$ three, HeH$^+$ one H and one He,
OH one H and one O, H$_2$O two H and one O, CO one C and one O, each metal ion
stage one nucleus of its element, and the He 2$^3$S column is skipped because
it is a level of He\,I and not an independent species. Adding a carrier is
adding a row to \texttt{species\_table}; this module follows without being
edited.

\texttt{hydrogen\_helium\_nuclei\_density} is left where it is. Its statement
order is the floating-point add order the goldens were snapshotted with, and it
is called from three places that must not disagree. The new routine is the
metal counterpart it never had, and the two are held together by test E1, which
requires the charge the census returns to equal \texttt{calc\_ne} on the same
state.

\subsection{Where it is asserted, and what the statement is at each site}

Off unless \texttt{EXHALE\_ELEMENT\_ASSERT} is \texttt{1} (report and continue)
or \texttt{2} (report and stop), the convention
\texttt{EXHALE\_CARRIER\_DEBUG} and \texttt{EXHALE\_DIFFUSION\_CHECK} already
use. When off, nothing is allocated and nothing is computed.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}l p{0.55\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
site & statement \\
\midrule
around \texttt{carrier\_write\_back} & absolute nucleus density of every
   element, per cell \\
around \texttt{photochemical\_transport\_step} & the same: the write-back
   restores the entry element totals cell by cell, so the whole step is
   element-neutral \\
around every \texttt{ioniz\_eq} sweep, tagged marching / steady iterate /
   steady candidate & every ratio $n_{\rm El}/n_{\rm H}$ \\
around \texttt{relax\_photochemical\_composition} & absolute nucleus density of
   every element \\
around the restart equilibration & every ratio $n_{\rm El}/n_{\rm H}$ \\
the accepted state of each steady outer pass, and immediately before each final
   \texttt{write\_output} & against the reservoirs the run resolved \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{Why the ratio and not the density across \texttt{ioniz\_eq}.}
\texttt{n\_io} is \texttt{intent(inout)} and the sweep rewrites it from its own
\texttt{calc\_rho}, so every density it returns may move by one common
mass-closure factor. That factor is reported separately --- and the distinction
matters, because ``every element off by the same amount'' is a moved
$n_{\rm H}$ denominator while ``one or two elements off'' is a repartition
defect. The failure report prints the worst departure of each of the twelve
elements so the two read differently at a glance.

\textbf{The tolerance is round-off, not abundance.} Default $1.0\times10^{-9}$
(\texttt{EXHALE\_ELEMENT\_ASSERT\_TOL} overrides). These are exact bookkeeping
identities: the operators rescale stage populations onto element totals, so the
only error is floating point. Measured on \texttt{mol\_carrier} at 300 steps,
every operator closes at 3.5e-16 to 6.2e-16; the accumulated round-off of a
finished marching state is $\le10^{-12}$; the cell solver's own
$\texttt{xtol} = \sqrt{\epsilon} = 1.5\times10^{-8}$ is the largest departure a
converged cell solve can leave. $10^{-9}$ sits between the two.

On failure it prints the element, the cell, its radius, the before/after element
and hydrogen totals, \texttt{rho*n0} and \texttt{rho(composition)} before and
after, and every species carrying that element in that cell with its
multiplicity.

Cost, \texttt{mol\_carrier} at 300 steps single-threaded: 11.96~s with the
assertions off against 11.77~s with them on and fatal (898 checks). Within
noise.

\subsection{Item 12.8 does not reproduce on the path it was reported on}
\label{sec:element-census-item-t}

\texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} item (T) records the first converged A2 wind failing
its element budgets near $r = 1.003$--$1.006$, carbon by $+90.6$ per cent and
oxygen by $+49.0$ per cent, with the carrier nuclei counted once inside the
carriers and once inside the free-stage columns ``somewhere in the JFNK/Picard
state refresh''.

Run with the assertions on, the A2 oxygen configuration restarted into the
steady solver --- 42 steady-iterate sweeps, 1230 probe sweeps, and, with the
outer loop forced to take its carrier pass from an unconverged solve, 20 passes
of \texttt{relax\_photochemical\_composition} --- \textbf{breaks no element
budget}. Every sweep, every write-back, every transport step and the restart
equilibration close inside $10^{-9}$, and the finished output closes H, He, C, N
and O at $1.77\times10^{-10}$.

This is not the state item (T) was measured on: that state is a converged A2
wind reached from a $\sim$25000-step march plus a JFNK finish at
$\texttt{info} = 0$, and it does not exist in the tree. So this is a \emph{not
reproduced on the same code path}, not a \emph{fixed}. The likeliest reading is
that the carrier rework of \S\ref{sec:molecular-carrier-transport} removed it:
that section is dated after item (T) was opened, it is in the same two
routines, and what it repaired was exactly two disagreeing definitions of the
element budget the carriers are held against.

What does survive: the steady/Picard path closes at $1.77\times10^{-10}$ where
the marching path closes at $2.6\times10^{-13}$, and the departure is the same
number for all five elements --- the hydrogen denominator, not the elements.
Three decades inside the gate; reported, not chased.

\subsection{A restart dump reported a molecular run as atomic, and under the
wrong coupling}
\label{sec:element-census-dump-ic}

Both found by the new restart round-trip fixture, both in the
\texttt{EXHALE\_DUMP\_IC} diagnostic rather than in \texttt{load\_IC}:

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{write\_output} takes the H$_2$ / H$_2^+$ / H$_3^+$ / HeH$^+$ / OH
      / H$_2$O / CO columns from \texttt{nmol\_eq} and \texttt{nox\_eq}, which
      only the equilibrium sweep fills. The dump hook runs before the first
      sweep, so on \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff} all four molecular columns came
      out \emph{exactly zero} against the $5.34\times10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ of
      H$_2$ the restart file carried.
      \texttt{molecular\_carrier\_densities\_from\_state(rho, f\_sp)} fills them
      from the loaded composition first: a state a diagnostic writes has to be
      the state it was given.
\item The rule that adopts the file's \texttt{\# coupling:} state runs about 280
      lines after the dump hook, so the dump wrote
      \texttt{sec\_ion=F sec\_ion\_step=-1} over a file that stated
      \texttt{sec\_ion=T sec\_ion\_step=40}. The same rule is now applied inside
      the dump block.
\end{itemize}

\noindent Neither touches a production path: both are inside the
\texttt{EXHALE\_DUMP\_IC} block, which ends in \texttt{stop}.

\subsection{Tests}

\texttt{make element\_census\_tests} builds
\texttt{element\_census\_tests.x}, on the \texttt{diffusion\_tests.x} pattern:
synthetic columns the driver sets itself, no \texttt{input.inp},
\texttt{stop 1} on failure. 20 tests, 20 passing.

\begin{itemize}
\item E1 --- the census reproduces the species-table stoichiometry on a
      hand-computed state, and its charge equals \texttt{calc\_ne} on the same
      state.
\item E2 --- element closure through one carrier write-back: \texttt{0.0} for a
      generic perturbation and $1.9\times10^{-16}$ for the configuration item
      12.8 reports, a cell whose transported CO collapses by 2.5 decades and
      hands its carbon back to the free stages.
\item E3 --- the H$_2$ photoevent ledger. Over 15--200~eV of the Chung et al.\
      (1993) branching, every final state the code applies carries two H nuclei
      and zero net charge once its electron is counted. The two channels the
      branching does \emph{not} resolve are measured rather than assumed small
      and printed beside the result: double ionization is inside \texttt{f\_di}
      and is about 4.3 per cent of the H$_2$ ionizations above 80~eV with its
      co-product mis-assigned, and neutral dissociation over 33--41~eV (up to 7
      per cent of \texttt{sigma\_H2} at 37.5~eV) is handed to the H$_2^+$ branch
      by $1 - f_{\rm di}$, which creates one H$_2^+$ and one electron the event
      does not make. Both are item 12.1's stated approximation; the gate for
      them belongs with explicit cross sections resolved by channel.
\item E4 --- the chemical-equilibrium branch of the base H$_2$ fraction (item
      12.6): with no handoff, $q_{\rm H_2} = 0.838401$ from the fit at
      $(p_{\rm base}, T_0)$ and the ghost H$_2$ nucleus fraction is $0.984428$
      at He/H $= 0.0793$; with a handoff, the handoff value and an imposed base
      composition; and the fit exceeds the attainable ceiling
      $0.5/(0.5 + \mathrm{He/H})$ at He/H $= 0.2$, which \texttt{input\_read}
      refuses.
\end{itemize}

The restart round trip is a shell fixture rather than a Fortran test, because
it needs two runs of the binary. \texttt{backup/regression/roundtrip} is
rebuilt in place around it (item 12.4). The case that carried this name could
not run at all --- \texttt{output/Hydro\_ioniz\_IC.txt} was zero bytes, there
was no \texttt{Ion\_species\_IC.txt}, \texttt{Load IC? True} made it abort in
\texttt{load\_IC}, its logs were from the ATES era, and it was in no
\texttt{DEFAULT\_CASES} list --- because it had been built from a converged
product that no longer exists.

It now builds its own state, in two halves that need no coordination:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{stage A is an ordinary named case.} 40 deterministic steps of the
      hot-Uranus molecular gate (\texttt{input.inp}, \texttt{base.inp},
      \texttt{maxsteps}), so \texttt{run\_check.sh check roundtrip}
      bitwise-compares it exactly like a matrix case. 40 steps is short enough
      to run in seconds and long enough that the state is not the initial
      condition: the molecular network has solved and the \texttt{\# coupling:}
      line carries \texttt{sec\_ion=T sec\_ion\_step=40} rather than its
      default.
\item \textbf{stages B and C are \texttt{roundtrip/roundtrip\_check.sh},} run
      after that. It hands the stage-A outputs back as the \texttt{\_IC} pair,
      reloads with \texttt{EXHALE\_DUMP\_IC=1}, and requires every species
      column --- matched BY LABEL, so a schema change reports a missing column
      instead of a numeric mismatch --- together with \texttt{rho},
      \texttt{v}, \texttt{p} and the \texttt{\# coupling:} header to round-trip
      to $10^{-12}$. It restores \texttt{input.inp} and the stage-A outputs on
      exit, so \texttt{run\_check.sh golden roundtrip} still snapshots the right
      state.
\end{itemize}

The case stays OUT of \texttt{DEFAULT\_CASES} and is described in the
\texttt{run\_check.sh} header, because its second half is not a bitwise
comparison and needs its own invocation.
\texttt{check\_roundtrip\_state.py} replaces \texttt{check\_roundtrip.py}, which
compared columns by POSITION and had this case as its only consumer; the
retired contents are kept in \texttt{roundtrip/.superseded\_20260903/} rather
than deleted, since \texttt{backup/} is not in the git remote.

Measured: the rebuilt case FAILS on a binary without
\S\ref{sec:element-census-dump-ic} (all four molecular columns zero, and the
coupling header written as \texttt{sec\_ion=F sec\_ion\_step=-1}) and PASSES
with it, so it guards exactly the two defects it found.

\subsection{Verification}

\begin{itemize}
\item Byte-identical \texttt{output/Hydro\_ioniz.txt} and
      \texttt{output/Ion\_species.txt} against a build of the unmodified tree on
      \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff}, \texttt{mol\_carrier} and
      \texttt{wasp\_full}, 300 steps each single-threaded. The new module is
      inert unless the environment variable is set; the two restart fixes are
      inside a block that ends in \texttt{stop}.
\item \texttt{element\_census\_tests.x}: 20/20.
\item The rebuilt \texttt{backup/regression/roundtrip}:
      \texttt{run\_check.sh check roundtrip} byte-identical against its own
      golden, and \texttt{roundtrip\_check.sh} passing every species column,
      \texttt{rho}, \texttt{v}, \texttt{p} and the \texttt{\# coupling:} header
      at $10^{-12}$, leaving the case directory unchanged. The same case fails
      on a binary without \S\ref{sec:element-census-dump-ic}.
\item The A2 steady/Picard runs of \S\ref{sec:element-census-item-t}, with
      \texttt{EXHALE\_ELEMENT\_ASSERT=1}.
\end{itemize}

\section{E2: the Lyman--Werner geometry measured, and the one dayside factor a
run is allowed to have (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:lw-geometry-dayside}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{Judgement first, in two parts.} (i) The plane-parallel
trapping inside the H$_2$ self-shielding table is \textbf{physically wrong for
a spherical layer, in a known direction and by a known amount: it
over-traps.} Measured against a matched spherical calculation on the same line
data, it over-predicts $p_{\rm eff}$ by 0.2 per cent at $r/H = 41$ and by up to
20 per cent at $r/H = 16$, one-signed, 6.5 per cent weighted by the
dissociation rate over a hot-Uranus molecular layer. It is \emph{not} rebuilt,
because two escape-probability methods in the \emph{same} slab differ by 20--40
per cent and not with one sign, so the method is the leading term and the
geometry is not. The headers now carry the number instead of the words ``an
open item of TO\_BE\_DONE.md'', and the trapping carries the provenance name
\texttt{slab\_surrogate}. (ii) A separate defect found while measuring it:
\textbf{a run could carry three dayside conventions at once.}
\texttt{set\_energy\_vectors} halved $F_{\rm XUV}$ on an exact string match,
\texttt{lya\_rt} and \texttt{excited\_hydrogen} halved the stellar Ly$\alpha$
beam on a substring test, and \texttt{fuv\_band\_flux} halved none of the five
FUV bands --- and the H$_2$ dissociation rate did not even read that function,
taking \texttt{F\_LW\_star} directly. Under \texttt{Rate/2 + Mdot/2}, the
setting of the whole molecular matrix, the Lyman--Werner rate stood \textbf{a
factor 2 above the run's own convention.} That is fixed: one definition,
\texttt{global\_parameters dayside\_dilution()}, read by every stellar beam the
code has.

\noindent Full account, design and figures:
\texttt{docs/e2\_lw\_geometry.md},
\texttt{docs/e2\_lw\_geometry\_factors.png},
\texttt{docs/e2\_lw\_geometry\_rays.png}.

\subsection{What the table's geometry is, read out of the code}

\texttt{sigma\_pump} and \texttt{p\_single} come from
\texttt{lbl\_table.absolute\_curves} through
\texttt{src/utils/h2\_shielding\_table\_line\_by\_line.py}: a plane-parallel
slab with one normally incident beam,
\begin{equation}
\tau(\nu,N) = N \sum_i x_i \sigma_i(\nu),
\end{equation}
with $N$ the column between the illuminated face and the point.
$p_{\rm eff}/p_{\rm single}$ is read node by node from the 27 CLOUDY decks,
whose geometry is plane-parallel and illuminated on one face. The column the
code hands the table, \texttt{calc\_column\_dens\_one(nH2, NH2col)}, is
\emph{purely radial} --- accumulated from the outermost cell inward, no stellar
zenith angle anywhere in the path.

\textbf{That last identification is exact, not an approximation.} For a
parallel beam the substellar ray column \emph{is} the radial column, in a
sphere as in a slab. The slab table is therefore right for the substellar ray,
and the geometry question is only about (a) the fluorescent trapping and (b)
which ray a 1-D shell should carry.

\subsection{The matched calculation}

Slab and sphere are evaluated from one kernel built on the Abgrall, Roueff \&
Drira (2000) line list, LTE populations and the Voigt profiles that generated
the installed table --- \texttt{lbl.py} is imported directly, so no molecular
datum can differ. An escape probability averaged over directions is linear in
the transmission, so with
\begin{equation}
\sum_l A_{ul}\,\langle P_{ul}\rangle_\Omega
   = \sum_k w_k\,A_{\rm esc}[u, N_k]
\end{equation}
the two geometries differ \emph{only} in the set of ray columns
$\{N_k, w_k\}$. $P_{ul}$ is a single-flight escape probability under complete
redistribution against the full overlapping-line opacity.

Slab limit: \texttt{sigma\_pump} and \texttt{p\_single} reproduce
\texttt{lbl\_table.absolute\_curves} to \textbf{seven significant digits}, and
the installed Fortran table's \texttt{p\_single} to 0.1--0.5 per cent from
$10^{16}$ to $2\times10^{21}$ at 700--2700~K. Resolution: angle 8 to 96
Gauss--Legendre points, $<10^{-4}$; path sampling 500 to 16000,
$<3\times10^{-5}$; frequency window 2000 to 20000 Doppler widths,
$<2\times10^{-5}$; frequency grid $4\times10^5$ to $8\times10^5$ points,
$<10^{-5}$.

\subsection{The numbers}

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}ccccccc@{}}
\toprule
$r/R_{\rm p}$ & $N({\rm H_2})$ & $p_{\rm eff}$ slab & sphere &
   $f_{\rm trap}$ & $f_{\rm curv}$ & $f_{\rm shell}$ \\
\midrule
1.0002 & 3.90e20 & 0.2092 & 0.2088 & 0.998 & 1.058 & 0.204 \\
1.0544 & 8.29e18 & 0.2540 & 0.2321 & 0.914 & 0.993 & 0.295 \\
1.0710 & 1.21e18 & 0.2453 & 0.2210 & 0.901 & 0.992 & 0.320 \\
1.1288 & 3.38e15 & 0.3016 & 0.2648 & 0.878 & 0.994 & 0.261 \\
1.3629 & 9.91e12 & 0.2163 & 0.1728 & 0.799 & 1.201 & 0.589 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent H$_2$-column weighted / dissociation-rate weighted over the layer:
$f_{\rm trap}$ 0.968 / 0.935, $f_{\rm curv}$ 1.034 / 1.013, $f_{\rm shell}$
0.229 / 0.261.

The mechanism: escape is dominated by the near-radial directions, where the two
geometries have the \emph{same} column --- which is why the effect is small ---
and the difference is the near-tangential rays, which a sphere caps at
$\sqrt{\pi r/2H} = 8$--12 times the radial column where a slab lets them
diverge, plus the lit sliver past the terminator. The controlling parameter is
$r/H$, not the column, which is why the effect vanishes at the base
($r/H = 41$, the escape hemisphere closes exactly at $\mu = 0$) and is largest
at the top of the layer ($r/H = 16$) where H$_2$ is already negligible.

$f_{\rm shell} = 0.20$--0.33 is \emph{not} a slab error. It is the ratio of the
shell average a 1-D spherically symmetric H$_2$ budget needs to the substellar
value the code evaluates. Its optically thin limit is 1/2, because the night
side is dark; it falls below that because the slant columns away from the
substellar point shield.

\subsection{One dayside factor}

\texttt{global\_parameters} gains \texttt{dayside\_dilution()}.
\texttt{set\_energy\_vectors}, \texttt{lya\_rt}, \texttt{excited\_hydrogen} and
\texttt{fuv\_band\_flux} all read it, and
\texttt{lyman\_werner\_dissociation\_rate} is called with
\texttt{fuv\_band\_flux(ib\_LW)} instead of \texttt{F\_LW\_star}, so the band
has one owner again. The keys keep their meaning --- the flux \textbf{at the
planet's orbit}, whether stated or integrated from the spectrum file --- and
the dilution is applied where the beam is used, so the setup report and the
resolved dump still state the number the run was given. The setup report gains
one line naming the factor, and \texttt{output/Lyman\_Werner.txt} a header line
giving the beam that actually drove $k_{\rm LW}$.

Two stale statements found in the same files and corrected:
\texttt{write\_output} described the \texttt{f\_shield} column as ``the
Richings, Schaye \& Oppenheimer (2014) temperature-dependent fit'', which
\S\ref{sec:h2-shield-table} replaced by the level-resolved table; and the
generator's docstring used a forbidden naming form.

\subsection{What moved}
\label{sec:lw-geometry-moved}

\textbf{Nothing that does not carry an FUV band flux.} \texttt{wasp\_full}
(He 2$^3$S, metals, \texttt{Stellar Lya flux: 1.0e5},
\texttt{Rate/2 + Mdot/2}, 400 steps) and \texttt{mol\_base\_handoff} (the
molecular gate with no FUV band flux, 12000 steps) are
\textbf{byte-identical} in every output file, \texttt{Excited\_H.txt} and the
\texttt{\_adv} profiles included. The XUV refactor, the two $\xi$ call sites and
the new Ly$\alpha$ B2 dilution therefore cost nothing:
\texttt{fuv\_band\_flux} reaches the solution only through the oxygen
photolysis, which those runs do not have, and
$F_{\rm XUV} = \xi_{\rm day}\cdot\ldots$ reproduces the old literals exactly.
The only change in those runs is one line of the setup report.

\textbf{\texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner}} is the one matrix case that moves, and it
moves by more than the factor 2 on the rate suggests, because the H$_2$ front
is where the rate and the chemistry balance:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
quantity & before & after & ratio \\
\midrule
H$_2$ front, $x({\rm H_2}) = 0.1$ & 1.04763 $R_{\rm p}$ & 1.05546 $R_{\rm p}$ & 1.0075 \\
H$_2$ front, $x({\rm H_2}) = 10^{-3}$ & 1.07299 $R_{\rm p}$ & 1.08122 $R_{\rm p}$ & 1.0077 \\
$N({\rm H_2})$ through the layer & 2.857e20 & 3.241e20 & 1.134 \\
$x({\rm H_2})$ at the base & 0.4715 & 0.4808 & 1.020 \\
$T$ at the base & 1124.5 K & 1134.4 K & 1.009 \\
$\dot M$ at 2 $R_{\rm p}$ & 8.252e10 g~s$^{-1}$ & 7.917e10 g~s$^{-1}$ & 0.959 \\
$\log_{10}\dot M$ (run report) & 10.47 & 10.44 & $-0.03$ dex \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent $x({\rm H_2})$ rises by 1.02 at the base, 1.41 at $r = 1.039$ and
\textbf{4.28 at $r = 1.081$}, right through the front, and falls back to
1.04--1.38 in the wind above it. Halving the beam moves the front out by 0.8 per
cent of $R_{\rm p}$ and puts 13 per cent more H$_2$ under it, and the extra
molecular cooling and mass in the layer takes 4 per cent off the mass-loss
rate.

\textbf{The SED-derived branch moves the same way} and by much less, for a
reason that is about the star and not about the code. A hot-Uranus gate rerun
with \texttt{Spectrum type: Load from file..} and the LHS 1140 SED (no
\texttt{Stellar LW flux} key) integrates
$F_{\rm LW} = 0.598$~erg~cm$^{-2}$~s$^{-1}$ out of the spectrum --- 570 times
weaker than the 343 of the regression case --- so Lyman--Werner is a minor
H$_2$ sink there: after 3000 steps the front moves by 0.04 per cent and
$N({\rm H_2})$ by 0.18 per cent. What the case establishes is that the stated
key and the integrated value take the \emph{same} path:
\texttt{input\_read} assigns the SED value to \texttt{F\_LW\_star} and the
dilution is applied downstream in \texttt{fuv\_band\_flux}, so neither can
drift from the other. \textbf{The matrix has no case that exercises this
branch}; the one above is a scratch construction.

\textbf{The gate rung's converged state is not re-established here.}
\texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner} is a fixed-step relaxation snapshot
(\texttt{maxsteps 12000}), and uncapped runs of it from both binaries are still
marching toward the JFNK hand-off at $du < 10^{-2}$: the baseline is at
$du = 0.090$ after 30171 steps and the patched run at $du = 0.199$ after 15830,
both falling at about $8.5\times10^{-6}$ per step. On that trend the hand-off is
thousands of steps away for the baseline and tens of thousands for the patched
run. \textbf{The front and $\dot M$ above are therefore snapshot values at a
common step count, not converged ones}, and a quantitative $\dot M$ for this
case still needs the Newton finish.

\subsection{Not done, deliberately}

The trapping cube is not rebuilt in spherical geometry. No $r/H$ axis is added:
over the H$_2$-bearing layer it would span 0.90--1.00. The shell average is
available as a \textbf{default-off} closure and is not the default, because it
is calibrated on one planet and changes the meaning of a converged solution.

\subsection{The golden refresh}

Measured on the eleven-case matrix with the change in: \textbf{ten cases
byte-identical, \texttt{mol\_lyman\_werner} alone moved}, which is the case
list the grep of \S\ref{sec:lw-geometry-moved} predicts, since it is the only
one carrying an FUV band flux. Re-measured against the golden it replaces:
$\rho$ 7.3 per cent and $T$ 4.5 per cent at their worst cells, $p$ 10.8 per
cent, $\log_{10}\dot M$ $10.47 \to 10.44$. The two large relative changes in
velocity are both at velocity zeros and are not what they look like: at
$r = 1.0093$ the old value is 63.9~cm~s$^{-1}$, which is $5.7\times10^{-5}$ of
the domain maximum and the 46th smallest of 500 cells, and the change of
851~cm~s$^{-1}$ is $7.6\times10^{-4}$ of the wind speed; the other, at
$r = 1.200$, sits on the flux-gate window edge. Away from those, the wind above
1.5 $R_{\rm p}$ moves by 7 per cent in $\rho$, 11 per cent in $v$ and 4 per
cent in $T$, all of it at $r \sim 2.8$.

These are positions along a transient, not converged physics: the case is a
fixed-step snapshot, so what the numbers establish is the sign and the reach of
the change, not its value at a steady state. The previous eleven goldens are
preserved as \texttt{backup/regression/golden\_blockI\_20260904/}.

\section{H$_2$ photoabsorption is a sum of four mutually exclusive channels,
and the cross section they share is the measurement rather than a fit that does
not meet itself (E1, E1b) (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:h2-photo-channels}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{Judgement first. The code carried one H$_2$ photoabsorption
cross section and split it with one branching fraction, and three different
reactions were inside that split.} Written as four mutually exclusive channels
with one stoichiometric table, the H$_2$ destruction rate is unchanged --- it
always was right, because absorption destroys the molecule whatever it leaves
behind --- and the FRAGMENTS change: above 51.4~eV a double ionization makes two
protons, two electrons and no H atom where the code made one proton, one
electron and one H atom, and over 33--41~eV up to 7.4 per cent of the
absorptions make two neutral H atoms and no ion at all where the code made an
H$_2^+$ and an electron. Both new channels default ON, because both reactions
are measured and the code was making fragments that the events do not make. The
channel split leaves the opacity untouched by construction --- the four cross
sections sum to \texttt{sigma\_H2} to $4.4\times10^{-16}$, machine precision,
at every energy and under every model.

\noindent\textbf{E1b is the second half and it is the larger one.
\texttt{sigma\_H2} itself did not meet itself}: the three-piece Yan fit steps by
a factor 1.719 at 18~eV and 0.619 at 85~eV, a 72 per cent discontinuity in an
opacity that the JFNK residual differentiates. It is now a MEASUREMENT
everywhere the wind absorbs --- Backx, Wight \& Van der Wiel (1976) Table 1 over
15.4--18~eV and Samson \& Haddad (1994) Table 1 over 18--300~eV --- and no piece
of the analytic fit survives below 300~eV. The worst of it was at the
ionization threshold, where the fit fell to 0.17 against a measured 14.2, a
factor 85. Three independent experiments now bound the cross section: they agree
to a few per cent below 30~eV and diverge by 10 to 20 per cent above it, which
is the real uncertainty and is wider than any one paper quotes. \textbf{The
molecular goldens move and the atomic ones do not.}

\subsection{What was wrong}

\texttt{sigma\_H2} (Yan, Sadeghpour \& Dalgarno 1998, Eqs.\ 17--19) is one
number per photon energy, and \texttt{set\_energy\_vectors} split it in two:

\begin{lstlisting}[language=Fortran,basicstyle=\ttfamily\footnotesize]
s_h2_di = sigma_H2(E) * frac_H2_dissociative_ionization(E)   ! H + H+ + e-
s_h2    - s_h2_di                                            ! H2+ + e-
\end{lstlisting}

\noindent with \texttt{frac\_H2\_dissociative\_ionization} the Chung, Lee,
Masuoka \& Samson (1993) Table II ratio. Three reactions were folded into those
two branches.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Double ionization},
      ${\rm H_2} + h\nu \to {\rm H^+} + {\rm H^+} + 2e^-$, threshold 51.4~eV.
      Chung et al.'s eqs.\ (3)--(4) state it: ``The branching ratio
      H$^+$/(H$^+$+H$_t$) is understood to include both single and double
      ionization where appropriate'', and their Fig.\ 4 discussion: ``by 80 eV
      about 20\% of a(H$^+$) comes from double ionization. This percentage
      remains fairly constant towards higher energies.'' Their
      $\sigma({\rm H^+})$ is a PROTON count and a double event yields two, so
      the single dissociative branch was standing in for two reactions. Catalog
      item 12.2, \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} (P31b).
\item \textbf{Neutral dissociation},
      ${\rm H_2} + h\nu \to {\rm H} + {\rm H}$, over 33--41~eV.
      \texttt{sigma\_H2} there follows Samson \& Haddad's ABSORPTION cross
      section, whose photoionization yield drops to 0.926 at 37.5~eV, so the
      $1 - f_{\rm di}$ branch handed the neutral share to H$_2^+$. Catalog item
      12.3, (P31c).
\item \textbf{The extrapolation above 124~eV}, where Chung et al.'s table stops
      and $f_{\rm di}$ was held flat. Catalog item 12.1, (P31a). This one is not
      closed here; it is now NAMED instead of silent
      (\S\ref{sec:h2-di-model}).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The four channels}
\label{sec:h2-four-channels}

\texttt{src/modules/functions/h2\_photo\_channels.f90}. One routine returns all
four cross sections at a photon energy, and one table gives what each event does
to the species counts. Nothing downstream writes those numbers out by hand.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}clcrrrrr@{}}
\toprule
 & channel & threshold & H$_2$ & H$_2^+$ & H & H$^+$ & $e^-$ \\
\midrule
M & ${\rm H_2} + h\nu \to {\rm H_2^+} + e^-$ & 15.4 eV & $-1$ & $+1$ & 0 & 0 & $+1$ \\
S & ${\rm H_2} + h\nu \to {\rm H} + {\rm H^+} + e^-$ & 18.076 eV & $-1$ & 0 & $+1$ & $+1$ & $+1$ \\
D & ${\rm H_2} + h\nu \to {\rm H^+} + {\rm H^+} + 2e^-$ & 51.4 eV & $-1$ & 0 & 0 & $+2$ & $+2$ \\
N & ${\rm H_2} + h\nu \to {\rm H} + {\rm H}$ & 33 eV (window) & $-1$ & 0 & $+2$ & 0 & 0 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent Every row conserves H nuclei
($2\,d{\rm H_2} + 2\,d{\rm H_2^+} + d{\rm H} + d{\rm H^+} = 0$) and charge
($d{\rm H_2^+} + d{\rm H^+} - de = 0$); that is the ledger test of review item
A3, and it is checked for all four channels in \texttt{src/tests/e1\_h2/}.

\textbf{How the split is built.} With $f_n(E)$ the neutral share and
$r_{pm}(E)$ the Chung Table II proton-to-H$_2^+$ ratio, and $d(E)$ the share of
the released protons that comes from the double channel,
\begin{align}
\sigma_N   &= f_n\,\sigma_{\rm H_2}, \\
\sigma_{\rm ion} &= (1 - f_n)\,\sigma_{\rm H_2}, \\
\sigma_M   &= \sigma_{\rm ion} / \left[\,1 + r_{pm}(1 - d/2)\,\right], \\
P          &= r_{pm}\,\sigma_M \qquad \text{(the proton count)}, \\
\sigma_S   &= (1 - d)\,P, \\
\sigma_D   &= d\,P/2 .
\end{align}
With $d = 0$ and $f_n = 0$ this collapses to
$\sigma_S = f_{\rm di}\sigma_{\rm H_2}$ and
$\sigma_M = (1 - f_{\rm di})\sigma_{\rm H_2}$, the previous arithmetic exactly,
which is why the default build does not move.

\textbf{A note on Chung et al.'s own normalization, because it does not close.}
Their Eqs.\ (3)--(5) set
$\sigma({\rm H^+}) + \sigma({\rm H_2^+}) = \sigma_i = Y\sigma({\rm abs})$, which
equates $(N_s + 2N_d) + N_m$ to an event count $N_m + N_s + N_d$ and so
over-counts by $N_d$. This module does not adopt that identification: it takes
their RATIO column as the measurement and imposes the event count separately.
That is the only way four mutually exclusive channels can sum to the
absorption.

\textbf{Cross-check against the size bound \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} (P31b)
predicted.} That entry worked out, for $N_d/N_i = 0.0225$ above 80~eV, that the
old arithmetic was low by 2.2 per cent in protons, H$_2^+$ and free electrons and
high by 22 per cent in H atoms. Measured on the new construction at 500~eV with
the \texttt{chung80} model: protons $+2.1$ per cent, H$_2^+$ $+2.1$ per cent, H
atoms $-18.3$ per cent. Same signs, same size.

\subsection{Against the Phase A photoevent ledger}

Item A3 of the review asks for ``an H2 photoevent ledger, requiring
conservation of H nuclei and charge for every final-state channel''. Phase A
implements it as test E3 on the TWO-way branching, and its own comment defers
the gate here: ``These are REPORTED, not gated: they are the known
approximation of item 12.1, and the gate belongs with the explicit-channel cross
sections of phase E1, not here.'' So the two tests are a pair, not a duplicate
--- E3 sizes the two unresolved channels on the old branching, and
\texttt{src/tests/e1\_h2/} gates them once they are resolved. The invariants are
E3's; this section does not restate them.

E3 prints two numbers. Both are reproduced by the channel construction, and one
of them needs its weighting said out loud.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrl@{}}
\toprule
 & Phase A E3 & E1 channels & note \\
\midrule
double ionization at 100 eV & 0.04259 & 0.02176
   & E3's is PROTON-weighted, $0.20 f_{\rm di}$; E1's is the EVENT share \\
the same, as an event share & 0.02129 & 0.02176
   & $0.10 f_{\rm di}$ against $\sigma_D/\sigma_{\rm H_2}$; $+2.2$ per cent \\
double ionization, proton share & 0.20 (stated) & \textbf{0.20000}
   & E1 reproduces Chung's 20 per cent exactly \\
neutral dissociation at 37.5 eV & ``up to 7\%'' & 0.07398
   & $\sigma_N/\sigma_{\rm H_2}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{The factor 2 between the first two rows is the defect itself,
not a disagreement.} Chung et al.'s 20 per cent is a share of
$\sigma({\rm H^+})$, which counts PROTONS, and a double event yields two of
them; the share of the EVENTS is therefore half of it. E3 prints the
proton-weighted figure because that is the form the source states; E1 has to
carry the event form because its four channels are mutually exclusive events.
The residual $+2.2$ per cent between 0.02129 and 0.02176 is the renormalization
of the H$_2^+$ channel that appears once the event count is imposed separately
from Chung et al.'s own closure (\S\ref{sec:h2-four-channels}), and it is the
same 2.2 per cent \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} (P31b) predicted for H$_2^+$.

Under \texttt{yan\_rho} instead, the double channel is 0.03055 of the events at
100~eV and 0.278 of the protons --- against 0.02176 and 0.200 under
\texttt{chung80}. That factor 1.4 is the model spread of
\S\ref{sec:h2-di-model}.

\subsection{What each channel is charged, and where its electrons go}

The rows are only half of a channel; the other half is the energy. Each of the
four is charged its own threshold and partitioned according to whether it makes
a photoelectron.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule
channel & charged & photoelectron? & secondary ionization \\
\midrule
M & 15.4 eV & yes, one & yes, \texttt{iabs\_H2} partition \\
S & 18.076 eV & yes, one & yes, \texttt{iabs\_H2\_di} partition \\
D & 51.4 eV & yes, \textbf{two} sharing the excess
   & yes, \texttt{iabs\_H2\_di} partition (see below) \\
N & $D_0({\rm H_2}) = 4.478$ eV & \textbf{no} & none \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{N carries no \texttt{fhv} factor and no secondary term.} It is not
      an ionization. The bond energy is spent breaking the molecule and the
      whole remainder of the photon becomes kinetic energy of two H atoms, i.e.\
      heat. This makes the 33--41~eV band heat MORE than it did before, because
      that share used to be charged the 15.4~eV ionization potential and then
      reduced by \texttt{fhv}.
\item \textbf{D is partitioned like the other two ionizing channels, and it must
      be.} The channel exists only above 51.4~eV, which is where the
      secondary-ionization share is largest; charging its excess whole as local
      heat would overstate the heating and lose the ionizations its fast
      electrons make. $D_0({\rm H_2})$ is taken from \texttt{mol\_rates}, not
      redefined here.
\end{itemize}

\noindent\textbf{The approximation in D, stated with its range.}
\texttt{photoelectron\_shares} is indexed by absorber and returns the partition
of ONE electron carrying the whole excess; D makes TWO that share it. The
dissociative absorber's shares are used at that photon energy --- the closest
tabulated one, same molecular target, adjacent threshold. Because the partition
varies slowly with electron energy above $E_{\rm sec\,ion} = 30$~eV, the error
is second order in the difference between the mean electron energy and the full
excess. \textbf{It is not zero}, and it biases toward too little heating and too
much ionization, since a slower electron heats more. Removing it needs a
partition evaluated at $(E - 51.4)/2$, which needs its own absorber row in
\texttt{electron\_energy\_degradation}. That is not done here.

\subsection{The double-ionization branching is a MODEL, and it is named as one}
\label{sec:h2-di-model}

Nothing in the code's sources measures $d(E)$. Two published statements bracket
it and they disagree, so both are implemented and neither is the default.

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{chung80} --- Chung et al.\ (1993), discussion of their Fig.\ 4: 20
      per cent of $\sigma({\rm H^+})$ above 80~eV, ramped from zero at the
      51.4~eV threshold, held above 80~eV. The ramp is NOT in the source;
      ``small'' near threshold is all it says.
\item \texttt{yan\_rho} --- Yan et al.\ (1998) section 4: ``At 110 eV, the
      measured ratio of double to single ionization is 0.038. The asymptotic
      ratio is predicted to be 0.0225 (Sadeghpour \& Dalgarno 1993).'' The ratio
      is ramped from zero at 51.4~eV to 0.038 at 110~eV and relaxed to 0.0225 by
      300~eV, then inverted to $d$ at that energy's measured $r_{pm}$. Both the
      ramp and the relaxation are interpolations between two published numbers.
\end{itemize}

\noindent\textbf{They differ by a factor 1.6 at 110~eV} (\texttt{chung80} gives
a double-to-single ratio of 0.023 there, \texttt{yan\_rho} 0.038). That is the
uncertainty, and running both is how it gets reported. The review's requirement
was to ``either obtain a defensible model or expose the constant branching as an
uncertainty option; do not silently present it as measured''; this is the second
of those.

\textbf{Above 124~eV} the ratio $r_{pm}$ is still held at its 124~eV value,
0.2048, because Chung et al.\ stop there. That extrapolation is unchanged by
this work and remains catalog item 12.1 (P31a). What has changed is that it is
now one named input to a documented construction instead of a property of an
undifferentiated branching fraction.

\subsection{What the channels are worth, measured with both switches}
\label{sec:h2-channels-ab}

Both channels default ON, so the A/B is run by switching each OFF.
\texttt{mol\_base\_handoff} at its pinned 12,000 steps,
\texttt{OMP\_NUM\_THREADS=1}, on the final \texttt{sigma\_H2}. \textbf{All five
configurations print $\log_{10}\dot M = 10.43$}, so the table is the profile.
Maximum relative difference against the default over the physical cells:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrrrrrr@{}}
\toprule
switched off & $\rho$ & $v$ & $T$ & heat & H$_2$ & H$_2^+$ & H$^+$ & H\,I \\
\midrule
double ionization off & 2.2e-4 & 1.0e-3 & 1.1e-4 & 7.1e-4 & 3.0e-3 & \textbf{2.0e-2} & 2.7e-3 & 1.6e-3 \\
neutral dissociation off & 3.5e-5 & 2.5e-5 & 2.7e-5 & 4.0e-5 & 8.3e-4 & 2.2e-4 & 6.5e-6 & 2.7e-5 \\
both off (the pre-E1 split) & 2.2e-4 & 1.0e-3 & 8.7e-5 & 7.1e-4 & 3.3e-3 & \textbf{2.0e-2} & 2.7e-3 & 1.6e-3 \\
\texttt{yan\_rho} instead of \texttt{chung80} & 8.3e-5 & 1.6e-4 & 4.8e-5 & 3.2e-4 & 2.2e-3 & 8.2e-3 & 7.8e-4 & 3.1e-4 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{The double channel carries the effect and it lands on
H$_2^+$.} Turning it off moves $n({\rm H_2^+})$ by $2.0\times10^{-2}$ at the
base, and turning the neutral channel off as well adds nothing to that
($3.3\times10^{-3}$ against $3.0\times10^{-3}$ in $n({\rm H_2})$ is the only
visible change). The sign is the one the construction requires: resolving the
double channel makes the H$_2^+$ share LARGER, because the event count is
imposed separately from Chung et al.'s own closure
(\S\ref{sec:h2-four-channels}), and it is the same 2.2 per cent
\texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} (P31b) predicted.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrrr@{}}
\toprule
 & $r = 1.00$ & 1.02 & 1.05 & 1.10 & 1.20 \\
\midrule
$n({\rm H_2^+})$, both off vs default & -1.95e-2 & -1.57e-2 & -1.39e-2 & -8.0e-4 & +5.6e-5 \\
$n({\rm H^+})$ & -2.44e-3 & -2.57e-3 & -2.32e-3 & +7.2e-6 & +5.2e-6 \\
$n({\rm H\,I})$ & -1.56e-3 & -1.44e-3 & -8.6e-4 & -8.1e-5 & -4.4e-5 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{The proton source moves by 0.26 per cent}, against the ``at
most 0.5 per cent'' bound \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} (P31b) derived for the
shielded molecular base. The bound holds and the measurement is inside it.

\textbf{The neutral channel is small here and that is a property of this
atmosphere, not of the channel.} It lives only over 33--41~eV, and in the
shielded base that band carries little flux; its largest effect is
$8.3\times10^{-4}$ in $n({\rm H_2})$. It would matter more where the 33--41~eV
band is not shielded.

\textbf{The model choice is worth 41 per cent of the double channel's own
effect.} \texttt{yan\_rho} against \texttt{chung80} moves $n({\rm H_2^+})$ by
$8.2\times10^{-3}$ where switching the channel off entirely moves it by
$2.0\times10^{-2}$. That is the uncertainty of \S\ref{sec:h2-di-model},
measured on a run rather than on a cross section.

\textbf{Everything is below 1.10 $r_{\rm base}$}: $T$ moves by under
$1.1\times10^{-4}$, $v$ by under $1.0\times10^{-3}$, and $\log_{10}\dot M$ not
at all to the printed digit.

\subsection{Range of validity, stated at the code site}

\begin{itemize}
\item $f_n$ is measured over 33--41~eV only, twelve rows of Chung et al.\
      Table 1, whose yields come from Backx, Wight \& van der Wiel. It is set to
      zero outside that window. \textbf{That zero is the source's assumption,
      not a measurement}: ``No yield measurements were made above 28 eV because
      it was assumed that the ionization yield would be unity at higher
      energies.''
\item A zero anchor is carried at 32.0 and 41.5~eV so $f_n$ is continuous. Those
      two points are continuity anchors resting on the source's own sentence
      that the Backx et al.\ yields ``drop from 100\% to 92\%'' between 32 and
      41~eV; they are not measurements. Without them $f_n$ would step from 0 to
      0.0078 at 33~eV, and a discontinuous cross section is differentiated by
      the JFNK residual.
\item $r_{pm}$, the proton-to-H$_2^+$ ratio, is measured over 18.076--124~eV
      (Chung et al.\ Table II) and held flat above. That extrapolation is item
      12.1 (P31a) and is unchanged by this work. It IS independently confirmed
      over 20--30~eV by Backx et al.'s own H$_2^+$ column, to 0.1--0.5 per cent
      (\S\ref{sec:h2-sigma-measurement}).
\item $d$, the double-ionization share of the protons, is a MODEL. Default
      \texttt{chung80}; the two implementations disagree by a factor 1.6 at
      110~eV (\S\ref{sec:h2-di-model}) and by 41 per cent of the channel's own
      effect on a run (\S\ref{sec:h2-channels-ab}).
\item \texttt{sigma\_H2} is a measurement over 15.4--300~eV and a rescaled
      sum-rule tail above it (\S\ref{sec:h2-sigma-measurement}). Its real
      uncertainty is the spread between three experiments: a few per cent below
      30~eV, 10 to 20 per cent above.
\item The uncertainty Chung et al.\ quote on their own data: ``An estimate of
      the total uncertainty in the data is about $\pm$4\%--5\%.''
\end{itemize}

\subsection{A separate defect this work measured, and then fixed (E1b)}

Building the continuity test exposed something that is not E1 and is larger than
E1: \textbf{\texttt{sigma\_H2} itself is discontinuous at two of the three joins
of the published piecewise fit.}

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrr@{}}
\toprule
join & below & above & ratio \\
\midrule
18 eV (Eq.\ 17 / Eq.\ 18) & 5.693 & 9.787 & \textbf{1.719} \\
85 eV (Eq.\ 18 / Eq.\ 19) & 0.1281 & 0.0793 & \textbf{0.619} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent Both formulas were re-derived by hand from the coefficients in
\texttt{references/Yan\_1998\_ApJ\_496\_1044.pdf} and both are transcribed
correctly, so this is a property of the published fit as published, not a
transcription error. Against Chung et al.'s Table II absorption column, Eq.\ 18
is right at its lower end (9.665 against their 9.75 at 18.1~eV, 7.659 against
7.65 at 20~eV) and drifts high toward its upper end, while Eq.\ 19 is right at
85~eV (0.0793 against their 0.08). So the 72 per cent step at 18~eV is Eq.\ 17
undershooting, and the 38 per cent step at 85~eV is Eq.\ 18 overshooting.

It changes the H$_2$ opacity directly and moves every molecular result, so it
was first reported here as its own item.
\textbf{\S\ref{sec:h2-sigma-measurement} fixes it}: over the range Chung et al.\
measured, the measurement replaces the fit.

\subsection{E1b: \texttt{sigma\_H2} is a measurement everywhere it is absorbed}
\label{sec:h2-sigma-measurement}

\noindent\textbf{The preceding subsection reported two joins in
\texttt{sigma\_H2} as a defect. This subsection removes them, and it does so by
reading the sources. No piece of the Yan analytic fit survives below 300~eV.}

\begin{lstlisting}[language={},basicstyle=\ttfamily\footnotesize]
15.4 <= E < 18 eV : k_bx * Backx, Wight & Van der Wiel (1976) Table 1
18 <= E <= 300 eV : Samson & Haddad (1994) Table 1
E > 300 eV        : k_hi * Yan Eq. 19    (E^-7/2 sum-rule tail)

all tables interpolated in log sigma against log E
k_bx = 9.85    / Backx(18) = 1.016415
k_hi = 0.00154 / Eq19(300) = 0.885805
\end{lstlisting}

\subsubsection{18--300 eV: Samson \& Haddad (1994) Table 1}

``Recommended Total Photoabsorption Cross Sections of H2 from 18 eV to
300 eV'', 72 rows. Stated accuracy \textbf{$\pm$2 to $\pm$3 per cent over
18--113~eV}, the measured range, and \textbf{$\pm$3 to $\pm$4 per cent from 113
to 300~eV}. Yan Eq.\ 18 is not used at all.

The first version of E1b took this column from Chung et al.\ (1993) Table II. It
is the same data --- Chung's text says ``Values for a(abs) were taken from the
data of Samson and Haddad'', his reference 31 being this paper as ``submitted''.
\textbf{At the 50 energies the two tables share, 49 agree exactly and one
differs in its last digit} (62~eV, 0.237 against 0.236). The original is used
because it reaches 300~eV where Chung's stops at 124. It also settles the
earlier draft's 113~eV question: Chung's rows at 115, 120 and 124~eV are Samson
\& Haddad's own recommended values, not his extrapolation.

\subsubsection{15.4--18 eV: Backx, Wight \& Van der Wiel (1976) Table 1}

J.\ Phys.\ B, 9, 315, ``Oscillator strengths (10--70 eV) for absorption,
ionization and dissociation in H2, HD and D2, obtained by an electron-ion
coincidence method'', their Table 1, column $f^0(E)$. This is the experiment the
other two normalize to: Chan et al.\ (1992) place their own spectrum ``on an
absolute scale by normalization at 18 eV'' to it, and Chung et al.\ (1993) take
the photoionization yields of their Table 1 --- which set the neutral channel of
\S\ref{sec:h2-four-channels} --- from it.

\textbf{Units and normalization, from the paper.} Their Fig.\ 2 plots $f^0(E)$
in eV$^{-1}$ with a $\times10^{-1}$ axis multiplier and the table is in
$10^{-2}$~eV$^{-1}$; the absolute scale is the TRK sum rule, ``normalized on an
integral value of two (TRK sum rule) with a 1\% correction for energies beyond
80 eV''. The conversion is the standard
$\sigma[{\rm Mb}] = 109.75\,df/dE[1/{\rm eV}]$, and it is \textbf{confirmed
against the other measurement rather than assumed}: it puts Backx at 7.628~Mb at
20~eV and 2.700 at 30~eV against Samson \& Haddad's 7.650 and 2.710, i.e.\ 0.3
and 0.4 per cent. A factor 100 instead would put them 9 per cent low.

\textbf{The join.} Backx gives 9.691~Mb at 18~eV where Samson \& Haddad give
9.850, so the branch is scaled by 1.0164. \textbf{That 1.6 per cent is a
measured difference between two independent experiments}, inside both quoted
accuracies, and not a fitted constant.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}rr@{}}
\toprule
$E$ [eV] & $\sigma$ [$10^{-18}$ cm$^2$] \\
\midrule
15.4 & 14.20 \\
15.5 & 14.06 \\
16.0 & 13.05 \\
16.5 & 12.05 \\
17.0 & 11.27 \\
17.5 & 10.69 \\
18.0 & 9.85 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{How big the correction is.} The branch this replaced was Yan
Eq.\ 17 scaled by a continuity constant. \textbf{Eq.\ 17 falls to 0.10 (0.17
after scaling) at 15.4~eV, where the measurement is 14.2}: the analytic fit went
to zero at the ionization threshold, which no photoionization cross section
does. The error ran from \textbf{a factor 85 at threshold} to 1.7 at 18~eV.

\subsubsection{The digitization, kept as a check and not used}

Before Backx et al.\ arrived, this branch was digitized from Fig.\ 1 of Chan,
Cooper \& Brion (1992) --- whose Tables 1--4 give only the discrete Lyman and
Werner transitions, the continuum being in that figure alone. Method: page
rendered at 600~dpi, energy axis calibrated on the 11, 17 and 19~eV ticks
(residuals 0.3--1.2~px, 1~px $= 0.0046$~eV), trace height read per column
outside the legend box and the H$_2^+$ threshold marker, \textbf{the read
repeated 18 times} over three binarization thresholds, two search windows and
three averaging widths.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}rrrr@{}}
\toprule
$E$ [eV] & digitized from Chan Fig.\ 1 & Backx et al.\ Table 1 & digitized / table \\
\midrule
16.0 & 13.11 & 13.05 & 1.005 \\
16.5 & $\sim$10.9 & 12.05 & 0.90 \\
17.0 & 10.38 & 11.27 & 0.921 \\
17.5 & $\sim$10.3 & 10.69 & 0.96 \\
18.0 & 9.85 (anchored) & 9.85 & 1.000 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{The digitization was good to 0.5 per cent at 16~eV and 8 per
cent at 17~eV}, against a quoted reproducibility of 1--4 per cent, so its stated
error was optimistic in the middle of the band --- a figure read cannot see a
systematic tilt in its own axis calibration. It is recorded here because it was
the evidence before the table existed, and it is not in the code. \textbf{A
table beats a figure.}

\noindent Read the last two columns. \textbf{Below about 31~eV the three agree
to a few per cent} --- Backx within 1.6 per cent of Samson \& Haddad, Lee 4 to 8

high, Lee 1 to 43 per cent high, and the disagreement grows with energy as the
cross section falls. So \texttt{sigma\_H2} is good to a few per cent below 30~eV
and to 10--20 per cent above it, \textbf{whatever any single paper's quoted
accuracy says}. Samson \& Haddad's $\pm$2 to $\pm$3 per cent is the accuracy of
one experiment, not of the quantity.

\subsubsection{An independent check on the branching, from the same table}

Backx et al.\ tabulate a second column, $f^{(i)}({\rm H_2^+})$, the oscillator
strength for producing H$_2^+$ specifically. Where the photoionization yield is
unity, that column divided by the absorption column must be $1 - f_{\rm di}$,
and $f_{\rm di}$ in this code comes from an entirely different experiment (Chung
et al.\ Table II).

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}rrrr@{}}
\toprule
$E$ [eV] & Backx $f({\rm H_2^+})/f_{\rm abs}$ & $1 - f_{\rm di}$ (Chung) & ratio \\
\midrule
20 & 0.9813 & 0.9804 & 1.0009 \\
22 & 0.9800 & 0.9785 & 1.0016 \\
24 & 0.9817 & 0.9770 & 1.0048 \\
25 & 0.9770 & 0.9764 & 1.0007 \\

\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{The two experiments agree on the dissociative branching to
0.1--0.5 per cent over 20--30~eV.} That is an independent confirmation of
$f_{\rm di}$, which \S\ref{sec:h2-four-channels} uses to split three of the four
channels. Above 32~eV the yield falls below unity and the identity no longer
holds, and below 20~eV Backx's ionization column carries their superexcitation
feature, so the check is quoted only where it is valid.

\textbf{What could NOT be checked this way.} Chung's Table 1 photoionization
YIELDS, which set the neutral-dissociation channel, come from Backx's ionization
efficiency curve --- their Fig.\ 4, which is not tabulated. So the neutral
fraction $f_n$ still rests on Chung's transcription of a figure of Backx's, and
this work could not go behind it.

\subsubsection{The high join is a real tension between a measurement and a sum
rule}

Eq.\ 19 agrees with Samson \& Haddad to \textbf{0.33 per cent at 113~eV}
(0.033270 against 0.033160), so over the measured range the sum-rule tail and
the measurement are the same curve. They part above it: at 300~eV the table
reads 0.00154 and Eq.\ 19 gives 0.00174. Yan et al.\ say why in their section 4
--- they \textbf{raised} the 300~eV point from $1.54\times10^{-21}$ to
$1.75\times10^{-21}$~cm$^2$ ``to achieve agreement with the sum rules''. So
$k_{\rm hi} = 0.886$ carries the measured normalization into the tail and gives
up 12 per cent of their correction. \textbf{Continuity is chosen over the sum
rule} because a step in an opacity is what this change exists to remove, and
because $\sigma_{\rm H_2}(300)$ is $1.5\times10^{-3}$ against 14.2 at threshold.
The 12 per cent is recorded, not resolved.

\noindent Read down the last column: \textbf{$+204$ per cent at 16~eV and $+74$
to $+79$ per cent over 17--18~eV} (the measured continuum against a fit that
collapsed toward threshold), within 5 per cent over most of 18--85~eV,
\textbf{$-37.9$ per cent in the last few eV below 85}, and $-11.4$ per cent at
300~eV. The large numbers are the two joins being removed; the small ones are
the measurement disagreeing with the fit inside its own range by about its
stated $\pm$2 to $\pm$3 per cent.

\subsubsection{Continuity, gated}

\texttt{src/tests/e1\_h2/} scans \texttt{sigma\_H2} from 15.5 to 2000~eV in
$10^{-3}$~eV steps and reports the largest fractional step. It is
\textbf{$1.7\times10^{-4}$, at 17.501~eV}, i.e.\ a smooth cross section; either
surviving join would have shown $4\times10^{-1}$ or $6\times10^{-1}$, the
scaled-shape version of this branch showed $8.6\times10^{-3}$ and the digitized
one $6.1\times10^{-4}$. The 15.4~eV ionization threshold itself is now a real
step from 0 to \textbf{14.20}, as an ionization threshold must be --- the fit
stepped to 0.17 and then climbed, which was the wrong shape as well as the wrong
size.

\subsubsection{What this does not address}

\begin{itemize}
\item The log--log interpolation between table rows is an assumption about the
      shape between measured points, not a measurement. Backx's grid is 0.5~eV
      below 20~eV; Samson \& Haddad's is 1~eV to 40~eV and coarser above.
\item Nothing here revisits the 33--41~eV window as an ABSORPTION cross section.
      It still is one; that is what makes the neutral channel of
      \S\ref{sec:h2-four-channels} necessary, and the two changes are consistent
      because the neutral share is taken as a fraction of whatever
      \texttt{sigma\_H2} is.
\item Above 124~eV the proton/H$_2^+$ ratio is still held flat (item 12.1,
      P31a). E1b changes the cross section there but does not touch the
      branching.
\item Chung's Table 1 photoionization yields, which set the neutral channel,
      come from a FIGURE of Backx's (their Fig.\ 4) that is not tabulated, so
      $f_n$ was not checked against the original.
\item The 12 per cent measurement/sum-rule tension above 300~eV is recorded, not
      resolved.
\end{itemize}
