\noindent\textbf{The two atomic cases are bitwise identical}, which is the
acceptance test for them: \texttt{sigma\_H2} is only evaluated where there is
H$_2$. The molecular cases move, and this is not a default-off change --- E1b
changes the cross section itself, so their goldens are refreshed rather than
defended.

\textbf{Where the movement lands.} $n({\rm H_2^+})$ moves the most, up to 24 per
cent, which is the same place the channel A/B of \S\ref{sec:h2-channels-ab} puts
it and the same place the cross section changed most (the 15.4--18~eV band, where
H$_2^+$ is made). $n({\rm H_2})$ moves 2 to 13 per cent, $n({\rm H\,I})$ 1.5 to
4.5 per cent, the heating up to 2 per cent, and $\rho$, $v$ and $T$ by under 0.5
per cent. \textbf{The wind barely notices; the molecular layer does.}

\textbf{The one entry that needs a word.} \texttt{mol\_sec\_ion} shows a maximum
relative change in $v$ of 3.35, at $r = 1.181$ --- which is the velocity ZERO of
that snapshot, the smallest $|v|$ of all 500 cells (14~cm~s$^{-1}$, against
$2.9\times10^5$~cm~s$^{-1}$ at 2 $R_{\rm p}$). A relative measure at a zero
crossing is not informative. Over the wind window $r\ge1.2$ the same case moves
$v$ by $9.9\times10^{-2}$, and its $\rho$ and $T$ move by $1.4\times10^{-3}$ and
$5.6\times10^{-4}$ like every other case.

\section{The lower boundary is a characteristic condition at the face
(2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:characteristic-base-bc}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent\textbf{Judgement first. The ghost-cell closure was not inaccurate, it
was inconsistent: it left a momentum imbalance at cell 1 that does not go away
when the grid is refined.} It wrote three primitive components into a ghost CELL
and \texttt{Rec\_BC} then reused the same three numbers as the state at the
FACE, half a cell higher. That half cell is $\delta r/(2H)$ of hydrostatic
stratification --- $3.8\times10^{-3}$ on the hot-Uranus base grid --- and a
state error of $\delta r$ divided by $\delta r$ to make a flux difference is a
fixed fraction of the local weight at every resolution. \textbf{Measured, on an
isolated Euler-plus-gravity probe that links the production grid,
reconstruction, Riemann flux, source and boundary modules verbatim:
$R_{\rm mom}(1)/(\rho g)$ reads 0.2514, 0.2507, 0.2503, 0.2502 over an
$8\times$ refinement, against an interior truncation error of
$4.9\times10^{-6}$.} The velocity it drives is first order in $\delta r$:
$-247.1, -123.2, -61.3, -30.5$~cm~s$^{-1}$, which is
\texttt{docs/p44\_base\_sawtooth.md} section 7's production ladder
($-248.3, -122.2, -60.0$) reproduced to within 1--2 per cent \textbf{with no
chemistry, no radiation, no molecules and no wind}. The base sawtooth was never
a molecular-layer phenomenon; it was this boundary.

\noindent\textbf{The replacement states two conditions at the face and takes one
from the interior}, which is the characteristic count for a subsonic inflow. The
two are the lower atmosphere's pressure and specific entropy at the base level;
the one is the outgoing acoustic invariant of cell 1,
\begin{equation}
p_b - \rho_i c_i v_b = p_i - \rho_i c_i v_i,
\end{equation}
with $c_i$ at cell 1's own $\gamma_{\rm eff}$. The ghost cells become the volume
averages of the hydrostatic isentrope through the face state continued below it.
\textbf{On the same probe $R_{\rm mom}(1)/(\rho g)$ falls to
$1.75\times10^{-4}$ and becomes first order in $\delta r$, and $v(1)$ falls from
$-247$~cm~s$^{-1}$ to $-0.28$~cm~s$^{-1}$ and converges away.}

\noindent\textbf{Four keys are retired and now REFUSED at startup}:
\texttt{Valve eps}, \texttt{Hydrostatic base},
\texttt{Base ghost temperature}, \texttt{Base velocity}. Each selected one
component of a closure that no longer exists.
\texttt{Base BC: density|pressure} is kept --- it states the base LEVEL, not the
closure --- and its level is now carried to the face by the boundary itself, so
refining the grid no longer moves the level the user stated.

\noindent Design note, every measurement, and the decisions:
\texttt{docs/phaseC\_characteristic\_base\_bc.md}. Patch:
\texttt{docs/phaseC\_base\_bc.diff}.

\subsection{What the count is, and what the code had}

At \texttt{r\_edg(0)} the speeds are $v-c$, $v$, $v+c$, and a wave enters when
its speed is positive (radius increases outward, so base inflow is $v>0$).

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
base state & entering & reservoir conditions & interior relations \\
\midrule
subsonic inflow $0 < v < c$ & 2 & 2 & 1 \\
flow reversal $-c < v < 0$ & 1 & 1 & 2 \\
supersonic inflow $v > c$ & 3 & 3 & 0 \\
supersonic outflow $v < -c$ & 0 & 0 & 3 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The old default branch pinned $\rho$ and $p$ and valved the velocity,
so its count was right; \texttt{Base velocity: massflux} pinned all three, which
for subsonic inflow is one too many and is the combination Carlson (2011,
NASA/TM-2011-217181, Table 1 footnote) names as inadmissible. What the code had
none of was the reversal row: $\max(v_1, 0)$ clips a velocity, it does not
change how many conditions are imposed.

\subsection{The two defects were independent, and only one of them was the
valve}

Two probe measurements separate them, and they separate cleanly.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Hydrostatic maintenance is the pinned numbers.} Holding the same
      pair $(\rho_{\rm bc}, p_{\rm bc})$ with the interior-velocity copy REMOVED
      reproduces the legacy $R_{\rm mom}(1)$, $R_{\rm mass}(1)$ and $v(1)$ to
      six digits. The valve contributes nothing.
\item \textbf{Acoustic reflection is the velocity.} The legacy boundary reflects
      $|R| = 0.953$ of a pulse leaving through it; freezing the ghost velocity
      gives 0.031.
\end{itemize}

\noindent \texttt{docs/p44\_base\_sawtooth.md} section 9 reached the same
separation from the other side (raising $T_0$ closes the thermal gap and leaves
the flux error untouched), and \texttt{TO\_BE\_DONE.md} item (W) records it.

\subsection{What was built}

One new module, \texttt{src/modules/states/base\_boundary.f90}, with one entry
point. \texttt{base\_boundary\_states} takes the first interior CELL AVERAGE and
returns the face state, the ghost cell averages and the state at the face below
the ghost, all at once; \texttt{Apply\_BC\_W} calls it and writes the ghosts,
\texttt{Rec\_BC} reads the face state. \textbf{That is the whole of the ``one
kind, one rule'' repair}: the old code called
\texttt{BC\_component\_constrho} from both paths, and the two paths handed it
different data --- the valve read the cell-1 average in \texttt{Apply\_BC\_W}
and the velocity reconstructed at \texttt{r\_edg(1)}, a full cell higher, in
\texttt{Rec\_BC}.

The interior state at the face is cell 1 continued along \textbf{cell 1's own
hydrostatic isentrope}, not extrapolated linearly and not taken from the
reconstruction stencil, which reaches into the ghost and would make the boundary
read its own output. Continuing along the isentrope is what makes the condition
well balanced: at rest the interior face pressure equals the reservoir's and the
compatibility relation returns $v_b = 0$ exactly, at any resolution.

The reversal handover is a cubic smoothstep of width
\texttt{base\_face\_mach\_blend} $= 10^{-6}$ in face Mach number --- the one
designed-in constant, justified at its declaration by the physical base Mach
number of the gate ($\rho_b v_b r^2 = F_{\rm wind}$ gives
$v_b \sim 1.6$~cm~s$^{-1}$ against $c \sim 2.6\times10^5$, i.e.\
$6\times10^{-6}$), so every intended operating point lies wholly inside the
inflow branch. There is no \texttt{valve\_eps} to arm: the residual is
differentiable because the branch is a blend, not because a kink was rounded
off.

Supersonic inflow is \textbf{reported, not repaired}. It would need three
reservoir conditions and a $(p, s)$ reservoir states two; the model has no
lower-atmosphere velocity, so \texttt{check\_base\_inflow\_is\_subsonic} says
the state is outside the stated problem rather than a velocity being invented
for it.

\subsection{Validation}
\label{sec:characteristic-base-bc-validation}

Three tests on the probe, all new. (a) and (b) have baselines for the closure
this replaces; (c) is new.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
test & old closure & Phase C \\
\midrule
(a) $R_{\rm mom}(1)/(\rho g)$ at rest, $\delta r_c = 2\times10^{-4}$
   & 2.5135e-1, \textbf{zeroth order} & 1.749e-4, \textbf{first order} \\
(a) $v(1)$ at rest, $\delta r_c = 2\times10^{-4}$
   & $-247.1$ cm~s$^{-1}$ & $-0.278$ cm~s$^{-1}$ \\
(a) ladder $\delta r_c = 2\times10^{-4} \ldots 2.5\times10^{-5}$
   & $-247, -123, -61, -30$ cm~s$^{-1}$ & $-0.28, -0.04, -0.007, -0.0001$ \\
(b) acoustic $|R|$ & 0.953 & 0.956 \\
(c) manufactured steady inflow, cell 1 vs interior
   & not run & mass 1.8$\times$, momentum 0.68$\times$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{(c) is the test that earned its place.} It drives an EXACT
steady spherical isentropic solution ($\rho v r^2 = F$,
$v^2/2 + h + \phi = B$, a solution of the Euler equations with gravity, so
nothing is forced) through the boundary at base Mach $10^{-3}$ and reads the
residual of that exact solution: cell 1 comes out at 1.8 times the interior
truncation error in the mass row and 0.68 of it in the momentum row. The
boundary is no longer a distinguished cell.

\textbf{(b) did not improve, and section 7.3 of the design note shows it could
not.} Two characteristics enter a subsonic inflow face; if the reservoir states
two STATIC quantities then the incoming acoustic amplitude is pinned and a wave
arriving from inside is reflected. That is true of $(p, s)$, $(\rho, s)$ and
$(\rho, p)$ alike --- the pair does not matter, the staticness does. The
alternative was implemented and measured
(\texttt{base\_incoming\_invariant\_weight}, state $p + \rho c v = p_{\rm res}$
instead of $p$): $|R|$ falls to 0.0024, but on test (c) the cell-1 momentum
residual rises to $1.32\times10^{-1}$, \textbf{460 times the interior}, because
$p + \rho c v = p_{\rm res}$ puts the face pressure below the reservoir's by a
fraction $M$ of the pressure where a real reservoir's Bernoulli drop is $M^2$.
It buys transparency by corrupting the steady state and is rejected; the
constant stays at 0 with the measurement recorded at its declaration. A boundary
that is transparent to sound without that cost needs a relaxation form, which is
not a function of the instantaneous state and so has no fixed point the steady
residual can express. That is an open item, in the design note as D6.

\texttt{-fcheck=bounds,do,mem} on the bounded HD~209458~b case: clean,
$\log_{10}\dot M = 9.61$.

\subsection{Production}
\label{sec:characteristic-base-bc-production}

\textbf{The hot-Uranus gate rung, reloaded} --- the case (AB) measured, so the
one comparison with a baseline. $\texttt{info} = 0$ both; \textbf{19 JFNK
iterations $\to$ 14}; $\lVert R\rVert$ 8.961e-06 $\to$ 7.848e-06; the flux gate
2.501e-04 unchanged to four figures, $r\ge1.03$ 3.432e-03 $\to$ 3.402e-03,
$r\ge1.10$ 2.375e-03 $\to$ 2.372e-03; $\log_{10}\dot M$ $10.34 \to 10.34$;
H$_2$ front 1.0449 $R_{\rm p}$ unchanged; H$_3^+$ column $-0.9$ per cent;
$T({\rm cell}\,1)$ $1116.68 \to 1116.72$~K. And \textbf{$v({\rm cell}\,1)$
$-251.88 \to +14.40$~cm~s$^{-1}$}: the sawtooth is gone in the production code,
and what replaces it is outward and of the size the wind's own mass flux through
the base density gives.

\textbf{The same rung from a cold start} reaches the same root:
$\texttt{info} = 0$ at $\lVert R\rVert = 1.405\times10^{-6}$, the same three
gate numbers to four figures, the same $\log_{10}\dot M$, and a state agreeing
with the reloaded root to \textbf{$3.9\times10^{-5}$ in $\rho$,
$1.9\times10^{-4}$ in $v$, $1.3\times10^{-5}$ in $T$}, $v(1) = +14.393$ against
$+14.395$, and $T$ at $r - R_{\rm p} = 8\times10^{-3}$ equal to 818.01~K in
both. \textbf{That repairs the reproducibility defect of
\texttt{docs/p44\_base\_sawtooth.md} section 8.4}, which measured three
$\texttt{info} = 0$ states of this configuration on this same default base grid
putting the H$_2$ front anywhere in 1.053--1.089 $R_{\rm p}$ and that
temperature anywhere in 583--949~K. The cold start costs 820 JFNK iterations
across three attempts against the reload's 14; whether that is worse than the
same cold start under (AB) is \textbf{not established}, because (AB) did not run
one.

\textbf{WASP-121b \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton}}: $\texttt{info} = 0$ both,
$\lVert R\rVert$ 9.026e-06 $\to$ 9.910e-06, flux gate 5.242e-05 $\to$
5.238e-05, $\log_{10}\dot M$ $13.21 \to 13.21$, state moving by
$5.9\times10^{-3}$ in $\rho$ and $3.2\times10^{-3}$ in $T$,
$v({\rm cell}\,1)$ $1372.5 \to 1705.9$~cm~s$^{-1}$, 96 $\to$ 108 iterations.
Base Mach stayed subsonic at 0.331.

\textbf{The reload-and-march departure is the negative result, and it is the one
to read first.} Peak-to-peak face mass flux over 3000 steps, in units of the
root's own $F_0$:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccc@{}}
\toprule
root, binary & 1.005 & 1.03 & 1.10 & 1.20 & \texttt{du} at 3000 \\
\midrule
(AB), rerun here as a control & 0.4443 & 0.2517 & 0.0403 & 0.0084 & 3.2250e-04 \\
\textbf{Phase C} & \textbf{0.9284} & \textbf{0.3074} & \textbf{0.0473} & \textbf{0.0096} & 3.2904e-04 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The control reproduces \S\ref{sec:bc-ghost-item-ad} exactly, so the
harness is the same one. \textbf{Phase C does not repair item (AD) and makes it
worse}, $2.09\times$ at $r = 1.005$ and $1.22\times$ at 1.03. That is consistent
with \S\ref{sec:characteristic-base-bc-validation} (b): the boundary still
reflects what the base layer launches at it. One mechanism for the increase is
that the retired one-way valve, by clipping $v$ at zero, was also a nonlinear
amplitude limiter on that oscillation; \textbf{that is a hypothesis, not a
measurement.}

\textbf{The complete update map says what the increase actually is, and it is
not the boundary.} On each build's own root (\texttt{EXHALE\_UPDATE\_MAP=1},
three steps at 1, 0.1, 0.01 of the CFL step): the accepted root's residual falls
9.916e-3 $\to$ 6.067e-6 (mass), 7.473e-3 $\to$ 5.453e-6 (momentum),
1.486e-2 $\to$ 8.462e-6 (energy) --- \textbf{the base-cell residual floor, three
orders of magnitude, measured on the production root} --- while the defect
$|G_{\delta t} + R|$ at $\delta t/100$ moves only 2.460e-5 $\to$ 1.351e-5,
2.643e-5 $\to$ 9.840e-6, and \textbf{1.892e-4 $\to$ 1.891e-4: the energy row
does not move at all}, and it stops falling with $\delta t$ in both builds, in
the operator-split chemistry/energy columns. The root became $1600\times$ more
accurate and the splitting error did not, so it now dominates: defect over
residual at $\delta t/100$ goes from $2.5\times10^{-3}, 3.5\times10^{-3},
1.3\times10^{-2}$ to 2.2, 1.8, 22. The departure grew because the residual
shrank, and what is left is Phase B's B2. \texttt{Apply\_BC} moves the interior
by a relative 0.000E+00 in both builds.

\textbf{Regression matrix}, ten cases against (AB), single-threaded, same caps:
all ten move, and all ten flip the sign of $v({\rm cell}\,1)$ ---
$-726, -756, -139, -139, -114, -139, -139, -601, -140, -582$~cm~s$^{-1}$ become
$+2383, +2380, +49, +54, +43, +49, +54, +7, +30, +543$. Read the rest of that
table with three qualifications: the eight molecular rows are step-12000
snapshots of a relaxation (\texttt{du} 0.4--1.3 in both builds), so their
$\log_{10}\dot M$ $10.43 \to 10.52$ is a different point in a transient and not
a rate; the two WASP rows are \texttt{du}-stops, whose several-per-cent path
dependence covers $13.26 \to 13.24$ and whose Newton-finished sibling gives
$13.21 \to 13.21$, though their 60 per cent longer march
($11289 \to 18026$) is a real cost; and \texttt{lower\_profile} is not converged
in either build (\texttt{du} 28.2 and 819) so its row compares two transients.
Full table: \texttt{docs/phaseC\_characteristic\_base\_bc.md} section 7.4.

\subsection{What this does not do}

\textbf{This is a boundary repair, and the scope is exactly that.} What it
removes is the base cells' residual floor --- the place every coupled finish has
been stopping at $\lVert R\rVert \sim 1$ --- together with the hydrostatic
inconsistency that put it there. What it does NOT touch:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The H$_2$ front creep.} P51 measured, on the 200k-step marching
      state of the new physics, that FREEZING cells 1--5 at every step leaves
      the front's creep (1--3 cells per 20000 steps) unchanged to the fourth
      decimal (\texttt{.../scratchpad/p51/docs/p23\_transport\_on\_state.md}
      section 9, read only, not remeasured here). The creep is therefore not
      driven by the base cells and no boundary condition addresses it; whether
      it is a numerical bias or physical is under separate diagnosis.
\item It does not damp the base-layer ringing of item (AA):
      \S\ref{sec:characteristic-base-bc-validation} (b), and the marching
      departure of \S\ref{sec:characteristic-base-bc-production} gets worse, not
      better.
\item It does not change PLM's base layer, whose density drift is set by the
      second-order reconstruction and not by the boundary ($6.5\times10^{-3}$
      against the old closure's $9.7\times10^{-3}$, and growing with refinement
      in both).
\item It does not give the model a supersonic-inflow base.
\item Goldens are not byte-identical, for any case. This is a model change.
\end{itemize}

\section{Reserved: the coupled solve's step control (measured, not landed)}
\label{sec:reserved-step-control}
% ===================================================================== %

\noindent Two sections are reserved rather than written, so that the numbering
matches the drafts they belong to. Both are step-control work on the COUPLED
carrier solve, both are measured, and neither is in the tree:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{153} --- a scaled trust region (Powell dogleg on the Krylov and
      Cauchy legs, predicted reduction from the same Arnoldi relation the solve
      already builds, admissibility enforced inside the step). It works as a
      method: the ratio of actual to predicted reduction has median 0.93 with 42
      of 47 iterations in $[0.5, 2]$, the finite-difference ray test refuses no
      model, and it never violates the element budget where the line search does
      18 times.
\item \textbf{154} --- the merit and the predicted reduction measured in the
      ACCEPTANCE measure (the row scales of
      \S\ref{sec:row-scales-own-terms}) rather than in the state scales, at
      which the model becomes exact to three or four digits on the first
      iterations.
\end{itemize}

\noindent Neither closes the coupled solve, and the reason is why they are
reserved and not applied: with both in place the two controls bottom out at the
same place and the same number, $\lVert R\rVert = 1.00$ in BASE CELL $j = 1$,
which is one cell's row off by 100 per cent of its own terms. That is the
boundary imposing a cell instead of solving it, so the obstruction had left the
solver before either section was written, and
\S\ref{sec:characteristic-base-bc} is where it went. They are kept default-off
pending a re-measurement on top of the characteristic boundary. Drafts and every
measurement: the P51 notes under \texttt{docs/}.

\section{The base cells reproduce, and the residual is not a function of the
state alone (2026-09-03)}
\label{sec:selfconsistent-residual}
% ===================================================================== %

Measured 2026-09-03 on two builds:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Phase C} --- \texttt{.../scratchpad/phaseC/src} copied read-only
      into \texttt{.../p55base/pc155} and rebuilt; the clean build reproduces
      Phase C's own binary bit for bit (\texttt{583aaa98}), so the boundary
      being measured is theirs. Roots: \texttt{phaseC/hotU\_root} and
      \texttt{phaseC/wasp\_newton}, restarted from their own output.
\item \textbf{Pre-Phase-C} --- the tree as of
      \S\ref{sec:acceptance-conserved}, copied into \texttt{.../base123}.
      Roots: the two accepted states of \S\ref{sec:p55-restart}
      (\texttt{s11/hotU\_cellmax}, \texttt{s11/WASP\_cellmax}).
\end{itemize}

\noindent Probes (scratch only, both env-gated, both off by default):
\texttt{EXHALE\_SWEEP\_CONSERVE} reports what one sweep does to $\rho$,
$n_{\rm H}$ and $n_{\rm He}$; \texttt{EXHALE\_RESID\_REPRO=<n>} repeats
\texttt{eval\_residual} on one accepted $Y$ (negative $n$ restores the
composition before each repetition). Patch:
\texttt{p155\_selfconsistent.diff}.

\subsection{The premise of item (4) does not reproduce}

\S11.6 of \texttt{docs/p55\_base\_mode.md} recorded that re-running the
ionization sweep on an accepted state moves the mass residual of cells 1 and 2
from $9\times10^{-6}$ to $2.7\times10^{-1}$ and $8.6\times10^{-1}$, and
attributed it to \texttt{ioniz\_eq} rewriting $\rho$ through
\texttt{calc\_rho}. \textbf{Neither half of that survives measurement.}

\textbf{\texttt{calc\_rho} does not move $\rho$.} Over every sweep of both roots
on both builds, the density the sweep writes back and the density it was handed
differ by at most:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccc@{}}
\toprule
build & state & max abs $\delta\rho/\rho$
   & max abs $\delta n_{\rm H}/n_{\rm H}$
   & max abs $\delta n_{\rm He}/n_{\rm He}$ & sweeps \\
\midrule
Phase C & hot Uranus & 8.13e-16 & 4.67e-16 & 4.32e-16 & 57 \\
Phase C & WASP-121b  & 1.71e-15 & 2.22e-16 & 3.04e-16 & 86 \\
pre-C   & hot Uranus & 9.68e-16 & 3.64e-16 & 4.42e-16 & 346 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent This is roundoff, and it is roundoff for a reason: the sweep's
unknowns are fractions of the element totals $n_{\rm H}$, $n_{\rm He}$ and
$n_{\rm M,tot}$ that it computes from the state it is handed, and every
write-back is one of those totals times a fraction. Because the code's masses
are the nucleus counts exactly (H$_2 = 2m_{\rm H}$ with 2 H nuclei,
H$_3^+ = 3$ with 3, HeH$^+ = 5 = 4 + 1$), conserving nuclei conserves mass
identically. The \texttt{max(...,0.0d0)} clamps on \texttt{nhi} and
\texttt{nhei} in the molecular write-back CAN break this --- they are the one
place the element budget is not closed by construction --- but on these states
they do not bite.

\textbf{The base cells' residuals are not $O(1)$.} Repeating
\texttt{eval\_residual} on one accepted $Y$, cells 1--3, first evaluation
against the twentieth:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccc@{}}
\toprule
build & state & cell & mass row, eval 1 & eval 20 & ratio \\
\midrule
Phase C & hot Uranus & 1 & 7.904e-05 & 7.765e-05 & 0.982 \\
Phase C & hot Uranus & 2 & 2.521e-05 & 2.470e-05 & 0.980 \\
Phase C & WASP-121b  & 1 & 1.1725e-07 & 1.1725e-07 & \textbf{1.000} \\
Phase C & WASP-121b  & 2 & 1.6359e-07 & 1.6359e-07 & \textbf{1.000} \\
pre-C   & hot Uranus & 1 & 2.553e-07 & 2.491e-07 & 0.976 \\
pre-C   & hot Uranus & 2 & 8.154e-08 & 7.762e-08 & 0.952 \\
pre-C   & WASP-121b  & 1 & 9.476e-09 & 5.163e-09 & \textbf{0.545} \\
pre-C   & WASP-121b  & 2 & 2.177e-08 & 2.010e-08 & 0.923 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The largest excursion anywhere is a factor two, at WASP-121b cell 1
before Phase C. \textbf{Under Phase C that same cell is reproducible to four
significant figures.} The base cells are not the problem, and to the extent they
were one, Phase C's boundary closed it: it is the prescription that removed the
base cell's dependence on the previous sweep's composition (no
\texttt{n\_part\_cell1}, no valve).

\subsection{What is real: the residual is a function of (state, composition)}

\texttt{f\_sp} is \texttt{intent(inout)} in \texttt{ioniz\_eq} and the residual
mutates it. It is not part of the Newton unknown $Y$. So
\texttt{eval\_residual(Y, f\_sp)} is a function of two arguments, only one of
which the state carries.

\textbf{It is deterministic in both.} With the composition restored before every
repetition (\texttt{EXHALE\_RESID\_REPRO=-4}), all four states give bitwise
identical residuals on every repetition. Nothing else --- not the frozen
chemical background, not the excited-hydrogen populations, not the stored WENO
smoothness factors --- contributes anything at all. That was worth establishing
before looking further.

\textbf{But the number reported at acceptance is evaluated at the WRONG
composition.} In the line search the accepted trial is evaluated as
\texttt{eval\_residual(Ytry, f\_sp\_j)} with \texttt{f\_sp\_j} copied from the
PREVIOUS iterate, and \texttt{rnorm} is taken from that $F$. The state handed
back and written to disk carries the composition the accepted trial LEFT.
Evaluating the same $Y$ at its own composition, and iterating the sweep at fixed
$Y$ until it stops moving:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}llccccc@{}}
\toprule
build & state & reported $\lVert R\rVert$ & own composition, 1 sweep
   & at the composition fixed point & sweeps & factor \\
\midrule
Phase C & hot Uranus & 2.211e-06 & 1.283e-05 & 1.257e-05 & 3 & \textbf{5.7} \\
Phase C & WASP-121b  & 6.287e-06 & 3.865e-05 & 3.593e-05 & 9 & \textbf{5.7} \\
pre-C   & hot Uranus & 4.141e-06 & 1.762e-05 & 1.722e-05 & $\sim$10 & \textbf{4.2} \\
pre-C   & WASP-121b  & 6.264e-06 & 1.737e-04 & 3.539e-04 & $\sim$14 & \textbf{56} \\
pre-C   & \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton} & 8.873e-06 & 1.851e-04 & 3.412e-04 & $\sim$10 & \textbf{38} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The composition at fixed $Y$ has its own fixed point and reaches it in
3 to 14 sweeps; one evaluation is still short of it by up to a factor two.
\textbf{Phase C cuts the WASP-121b factor from 56 to 5.7 and leaves the hot
Uranus at about 5.7.}

\textbf{What this does and does not change about acceptance.} It does not,
today, change which states are accepted. Only 7 of the 63 regression cases set
\texttt{Resid tol} at all; without it \texttt{resid\_th} $= -1$, the residual
gate is off ($\lVert R\rVert < -1.000{\rm E}+00$ in the acceptance line), and
every one of the roots measured here was accepted on the FLUX GATE alone. The
flux gate reads the conserved face mass flux of \texttt{u} and is
composition-independent, so it is untouched by all of this.

What it changes is what the reported number means. $\lVert R\rVert$ is quoted in
run logs, in \texttt{docs/}, and in item (AD)'s own measurements, and on these
states it understates the residual of the state that was written by 4 to 56
times. Every one of the five states above is above $10^{-5}$ at its own
composition, so a run that DID set \texttt{Resid tol: 1.0e-5} would be accepting
a state that does not meet it.

\subsection{Prescription}

\noindent\textbf{(a) The gate and the report read the residual of the state that
is written, at the composition that state carries.}
\texttt{p155\_selfconsistent.diff} adds \texttt{resid\_at\_own\_composition}
(default \texttt{.false.}, \texttt{n\_selfconsistent\_max = 25}): at hand-back,
re-evaluate at $(Y, \texttt{f\_sp})$ and iterate the sweep at fixed $Y$ until
$\lVert R\rVert$ changes by less than $10^{-3}$ relative. Measured cost: 3
sweeps on the hot Uranus, 9 on WASP-121b, one-off. The coupled route already
does a single re-evaluation for its carrier half
(\texttt{nvar\_jac} $\ge$ 4); this is the same idea taken to the fixed point and
applied to all routes.

Default off because turning it on makes every root accepted under
\texttt{Resid tol} report a residual 4 to 56 times larger, which is a physics
decision about what ``converged'' means, not a refactor. The recommendation is
to turn it on: a steady state is a joint fixed point of the hydrodynamic balance
and the chemical equilibrium, and a measure that reads the hydro balance under
last iterate's chemistry is not measuring that.

\noindent\textbf{(b) $\rho$ should be an input to the sweep, not an output.} The
measurement says this changes no number today --- the write-back is
element-conserving on every state tested, to $10^{-15}$. It is still the right
shape: the sweep determines the composition at a given $(\rho, T)$ and the
particle count that follows; mass is the hydrodynamics' variable. Making
\texttt{n\_io} \texttt{intent(in)} and normalizing \texttt{f\_sp} by the input
density would make that structural instead of accidental, and it would turn the
\texttt{max(...,0.0d0)} clamps in the molecular write-back --- the one place the
element budget is NOT closed by construction --- into a detectable condition
rather than a silent mass adjustment. It is a golden-refreshing change at the
$10^{-15}$ level, so it belongs in a change series that is refreshing them
anyway.

\noindent\textbf{Not adopted here:} anything that would make the composition
part of $Y$. That is the coupled route's design and it exists
(\texttt{nvar\_jac} $\ge$ 4, the carrier unknown); extending it to the full
composition is a much larger question than this measurement supports.

\subsection{Contact with Phase C}

The patch touches \texttt{src/modules/time\_step/steady\_newton.f90} (the
hand-back block, after \texttt{unpack\_carrier}/\texttt{Apply\_BC} and before
\texttt{steady\_gates\_met}) and adds two parameters in
\texttt{src/modules/init/parameters.f90}. \textbf{No boundary code is touched}:
\texttt{Apply\_BC.f90}, the new \texttt{base\_boundary.f90}, \texttt{init.f90}
and \texttt{utilities.f90} are exactly Phase C's. The one place the two meet is
the hand-back \texttt{Apply\_BC(u)} call, which Phase C rewrites and this patch
only calls; if Phase C changes the call signature there, this patch follows it
and nothing else.

The probes are separable and belong in scratch:
\texttt{EXHALE\_SWEEP\_CONSERVE} in \texttt{ionization\_equilibrium.f90} and
\texttt{EXHALE\_RESID\_REPRO} in \texttt{steady\_newton.f90}. The conservation
probe is worth keeping in some form --- as a cheap assertion that the sweep's
write-back closed the element budget, reported once per run rather than printed
per sweep.

\subsection{What is not established}

\begin{itemize}
\item One accepted state per planet per build, all with the residual gate off. A
      case that actually sets \texttt{Resid tol} and converges under it has not
      been re-measured at its own composition.
\item Whether the composition fixed point at fixed $Y$ always exists and is
      unique. It was reached in 3 to 14 sweeps on all five states,
      monotonically on the two that start below it and with one overshoot on the
      three that do not (WASP-121b under Phase C: 3.86, 4.36, 3.79, \ldots
      $3.59\times10^{-5}$), but nothing here proves existence or uniqueness.
\item Whether accepting on the self-consistent residual changes the mass-loss
      rate. It cannot change the state that is written --- the patch only
      measures --- but a run that keeps solving instead of stopping will end
      somewhere else.
\item The \texttt{max(...,0.0d0)} clamps: shown not to bite on these five
      states, not shown never to bite. The conservation probe is what would say.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{What landed, and what the measure did to the one case that tests it}

\noindent\textbf{The own-composition residual is the DEFAULT}
(\texttt{resid\_at\_own\_composition}), not an option to be opted into: the
burden of a reason is on turning it off, and the only reason is reproducing a
number from before this section. The fixed point is iterated explicitly through
a separate output array, because \S\ref{sec:eq-sweep-seed-argument} forbids the
seed and the result of \texttt{eval\_residual} being the same array --- the
patch as drafted assumed the older five-argument signature and did not build.

\textbf{Two halves of the drafted patch were deliberately not taken}, both being
a second copy of a facility that had landed in the meantime: the
\texttt{EXHALE\_SWEEP\_CONSERVE} probe in
\texttt{ionization\_equilibrium.f90}, which measures element conservation
through the sweep that \S\ref{sec:element-census}'s \texttt{element\_census}
assertions already measure at every refresh that moves nuclei; and
\texttt{residual\_reproducibility\_probe} (51 lines in
\texttt{steady\_newton.f90}), which asks the question
\texttt{src/tests/residual\_determinism/} answers as a test with a verdict. One
facility, one rule.

\textbf{Measured on \texttt{wasp\_full\_newton}, the only default case that runs
a steady solve.} It is the only one of the eleven that moves, which is the case
list this change predicts:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}}
\toprule
 & before & after \\
\midrule
reported $\lVert R\rVert$ at hand-back & 9.927e-06 & \textbf{5.677e-04} \\
sweeps to the composition fixed point & --- & 7 \\
flux spread (the gate that accepted it) & 1.961e-11 & 1.961e-11 \\
$\log_{10}\dot M$ & 13.21 & 13.21 \\
state: $\rho$ / $v$ / $T$ max relative change & --- & 1.4e-15 / 0 / 4.2e-5 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent So the number the solver reports as the accepted root's residual was
\textbf{57 times too small}, and the state itself is untouched to roundoff ---
which is what this section claims: it does not move the solution, it stops
misreporting it. The case still converges because it sets no
\texttt{Resid tol} ($\lVert R\rVert < -1.000{\rm E}+00$ in its log), so the
residual gate was never tested and the flux gate accepted it; a run that does
set one will now fail a tolerance it used to pass, and that is the intended
consequence rather than a regression.

\textbf{Not done.} The other half of the prescription --- making $\rho$ an
\texttt{intent(in)} of the sweep so that element conservation is structural
rather than a property the arithmetic happens to have --- is not implemented. It
is worth doing and it changes no number (the sweep's rewritten $\rho$ differs
from the one it was handed by $1.7\times10^{-15}$ over 489 sweeps), so it
belongs with the next change that refreshes goldens rather than on its own.
